## How to read this report

**The measurement rig.** Phase 1 took pictures; Phase 4 measured the same screens.
- **Size.** `audits/tools/phase4/measure.mjs` (rig v2) runs every screen definition in `audits/tools/areas/*.mjs`, with the same states and helpers as the Phase 1 capture, in three runs: **themes** (1,721 jobs: the typical state on the iPad portrait in seven theme keys, System light, System dark, Hearth on a dark OS, Parchment, Frost, Midnight and Forest), **devices** (1,424 jobs: the other devices in System light and dark) and **states** (517 jobs: empty, overflow, loading, offline and error). That is **3,662 jobs, all 3,662 ok and 0 failed** (`audits/evidence/p4/measure/coverage.json`). Each named theme was applied as a person preference through the API and `localStorage`, and what actually applied is recorded per document.
- **What it records**, per document (the shell page and the app frame): every visible text box with its computed style and the contrast of its colour against the pixels behind it with the text hidden (10th percentile and median), behind an occlusion grid that defers text another element covers; icons, controls and information-bearing graphics (rings, bars, dots, strokes: 88,726 graphics measured); the resolved tokens; box sizes, margins, radii and shadows; glass layers; declared motion; tap targets; and the web tells. The named themes also get 1× screenshots. `aggregate.mjs` turns the raw files into the committed summaries in `audits/evidence/p4/measure/` (`pairs`, `failing-pairs`, `nontext`, `type`, `radii`, `shadows`, `spacing`, `glass`, `motion`, `targets`, `tells`, `tokens-resolved`).
- **Independent verification.** A first rig check (`rigcheck-1.mjs`, evidence `audits/evidence/p4/RIGCHECK/rigcheck-1.json`) found three faults in rig v1 (text sampled through covering overlays, icon-only controls over-counted as boundary failures, graphics not measured); rig v2 fixed all three and re-measured every job in place. A second check (`rigcheck-2.mjs`) re-measured 105 data points with its own code (its own PNG decoding, text hiding and WCAG maths) on 22 jobs covering all 11 areas and all seven theme keys: 88 of 93 text p10 values and 91 of 93 medians agree within 0.3, 92 of 93 AA verdicts agree (the 93rd is a tiny compass "N" whose edge sampling differs), 19 values measured in Phases 2 and 3 were checked (16 of them re-measured in the run) and reproduced, and the aggregates were recounted from all 3,662 raw files (`audits/evidence/p4/RIGCHECK/rigcheck-2-measure.json`, `rigcheck-2-agg.json`, `rigcheck-2-hero.json`). It left four secondary discrepancies, none of which changes a verdict: `nontext.json`'s headline `iconFail` counts include emoji and `<img>` icons, whose contrast is informational (cite the SVG figures); a ring's `ratioInside` is wrong for translucent rings; stroke samples 3 px out can land in a drop-shadow glow; text-labelled pill fills are not measured.
- **Limits.** Playwright WebKit on Windows paints no backdrop blur and renders fallback fonts (Segoe UI for the system faces, Palatino for the serif), so text on glass is measured against the unblurred fill and the identity of SF Pro, SF Pro Rounded and New York is not seen. Only resting states are measured by the rig (the MOTION and TELL scripts force hover, press and focus separately; after the completeness critic, `audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/states-sweep.mjs` measured text contrast in hover, press and focus states and all pseudo-element text on the desktop in the seven theme keys, COLOR Unresolved 8). Graphics are found by heuristics. The Windows WebKit port paints a `<select>` over any author background, so every select figure from the rig describes the port, not an iPad (DARK "Checked and not a bug" 1). Real devices were not used (see Not verified).

**One investigator per dimension, two skeptics per defect.** Each of the ten dimensions had one investigator, who read the code and the Phase 1 captures, used the rig data and ran its own experiments. Every bug, accessibility, security or perf finding came with a rerunnable script. Each candidate defect went to **two independent skeptics** who re-read the code and wrote their own scripts; a third skeptic broke a split vote (P4-GLASS-02, P4-GLASS-04 and P4-DARK-03). A defect is **CONFIRMED** only with at least two confirmations and more confirmations than refutations. No filed finding was refuted; the investigators' claims that did not survive (for example the Larder and Dollywood select contrast, a rig artefact) are recorded under each section's "Checked and not a bug", and open questions under "Unresolved".

**An independent re-measure of each investigation.** A separate script per dimension, written from scratch, re-measured the headline numbers: 172 numbers in all, 150 agreed and 22 did not. Every disagreement is corrected in its section, which says what changed (TOK 18/16, TYPE 14/12, SHAPE 17/16, ICON 15/14, GLASS 14/12, MOTION 20/17, DARK 17/14, ACCENT 20/17, TELL 15/13, COLOR 22/19; checked/agreed).

**The scorecard method.** Phase 3's calibration notes asked for the shared Hearth base and the shared Dollywood template to be scored once, with each app's own failures deducted on top (`audits/03-apps.md:419`).
1. **Shared bases.** Two bases were scored per rubric dimension: `hearth-shared` (the shell and every app on design.css, including the non-`.ds` F260, Prayer and Larder, which still take its colour, dark, glass and bootstrap) and `dollywood-template` (the build guide and the park map). A system-level defect is counted once, in the base, and never per area.
2. **Calibration rules.** 58 written rules (TYP-1 … DEL-4) each add or deduct a fixed amount when an area meets a stated condition. An area's cell is its base plus the rules that apply; the net adjustment per dimension is clamped to ±2, the cell to 1-10, in 0.5 steps.
3. **Row scorers and checkers.** One scorer per row applied the bases and rules with evidence. A separate checker per row re-checked every cell against the screenshots (378 opened in all). One-point differences take the checker's score; a gap of two points or more would go to a judge (none arose).
4. **A consistency pass** read all ten rows for the same rule applied differently. It raised 11 flags, and a ruling settled each one (all 11 accepted).

**The token proposal method.** Three independent proposals (Apple fidelity first; access and legibility first; migration first) were written and scored by a panel of three judges. The judges split (migration 142, fidelity 140, access 133). Because of an orchestration error, the synthesis was handed fidelity as the winner. It built on fidelity and grafted migration's compatibility and delivery layer, which is one judge's recommendation, plus ideas from access. See "How the set was assembled". Independent verifiers then checked contrast (their own cascade and WCAG code), completeness and coherence (a two-engine scope probe), and the house and CLAUDE.md constraints (a runtime check on the rig), in six rounds (round 6 had a contrast and a coherence verifier only). Rounds 1 to 4 found 23, 23, 20 and 17 issues (0, 0, 4 and 4 of them blocking), and every verifier in each of those rounds returned "not ok". Revisions 1 to 4 each answered the round before, and each later round re-checked the earlier fixes: round 3 found one of round 2's fixes (GLASS-7) half done, and round 5 found two of round 2's completeness issues open again. Round 5 checked revision 4 and found 17 issues, 1 of them blocking. Its constraints verifier returned "ok"; its contrast verifier (0 failing pairs in 431,954 evaluations, 3 minor wording errors) and its coherence verifier (the blocking issue plus 9 minor) did not. Revision 5 answered four of those 17: the blocking one (the Me hero's Switch button now has an exact batch-1a row) and the three wording errors; it left the other 13 open. Round 6 checked revision 5 with two verifiers, each with its own two-engine script. Both found all four fixes holding, the button painting exactly its tokens in WebKit and Chromium (≥ 6.58 in light, ≥ 6.86 in dark), and no blocking issue; the contrast verifier returned "ok", the coherence verifier "not ok" for minor issues only. Round 6 raised 4 new minor issues, plus one that both verifiers named (this report still held revision 4), which this assembly answers. **17 minor issues are open (13 from round 5, 4 from round 6), none blocking**; they are listed at the top of the Proposed token set section. Revision 5's own gate runs 102,583 evaluations with 0 failing and catches all 26 planted faults. **Phase 5 update (2026-09-25):** revisions 6 and 6b apply the household's decisions and settle the 17 open issues; the figures in this paragraph are revision 5's. See "Revision 6" in the Proposed token set's assembler's note for the current file, gates and verification.

**Severity** follows the Phase 2 rule (`audits/02-shell.md:25-37`) and its design-system clause: critical = household data lost or overwritten, an account or private content exposed, or an app unusable on the iPad, iPhone or TV; high = a core daily flow broken or wrong for a household member, or a privacy or safety issue for kids; medium = a secondary flow broken or misleading; low = cosmetic or an edge case. Text a household member needs that fails WCAG AA on a primary surface or control is at least medium (high when it is the main content or the primary action of a daily flow); decorative or secondary failures are low. A narrow trigger adds an Exposure line; it does not lower severity.

**IDs.** `P4-<DIM>-NN` are adversarially verified defects. A **primary** ID owns a defect and its severity; a **pointer** keeps its number and evidence but is counted under its primary (four pointers, listed under the register). CONS (consistency), VIS (house-style deviation), GAP (missing token or capability) and OK (done well) items describe the design and were **not adversarially verified**; each carries its own evidence, and the investigator's rating is shown on each. P2-* and P3-* IDs, and the UX-/VIS-/GAP- items in `audits/03-apps/*.md`, are pointers to earlier phases: a defect they already recorded is cited as related and not re-filed.

**Order of the report.** Summary, scorecard and register first. Then one section per dimension, each with its cross-area tables up front, then its confirmed defects, consistency, visual and gap findings, what works, what was checked and is not a bug, what is unresolved, its token gaps and its method. Then the proposed token set, what was not verified, and the scripts and evidence.

## Summary

- **Totals.** 44 defects were confirmed across the ten dimensions (42 by the investigations, 2 more from the completeness critic: P4-TELL-07 and P4-SHAPE-04), and none was refuted. After merging duplicates between sections, **40 primary defects: 0 critical, 0 high, 8 medium, 32 low**; four IDs are pointers counted under their primaries (P4-ACCENT-02, P4-ACCENT-03, P4-DARK-01, P4-DARK-03). Beside them sit 75 consistency, house-style and gap items and 39 positive items, none adversarially verified. No design-system defect loses household data: the costs are legibility, consistency, feel and battery.
- **Scorecard.** The shell scores **4.1** and the apps average **4.1** out of 10 (Phase 2 gave the shell 4.9, Phase 3 the apps 4.8). Rows range from **3.3** (the build guide) to **4.6** (Tally and Verses). Every row fell, most of all the park map (5.6 → 4.0) and Kid Verse (5.2 → 4.2), because the shared Hearth and Dollywood defects are now priced once in a base and each area's own measured failures are deducted by written rules. The weakest dimension across apps is Colour & palette (3.1); the strongest is Delight (5.2). Every row sits nearer the rubric's "clean but obviously a web page" anchor (4) than its "polished App Store app" anchor (7).
- **The system splits along `.ds`.** Where it is used, it works: the shell tokenises 88-89 % of its type and spacing, Tally, Timer, Kid Verse and Verses 92-100 % of their spacing, radius and colour, and all of them keep 98-100 % of their spacing on the 4 px grid. F260, Prayer, the Larder and both Dollywood exports use **0 spacing tokens and 0-7 % font-size tokens** (34-84 % on the grid), so the kid, kiosk and any future iPad scale cannot reach them, including two apps kids use (TOK, TYPE, SHAPE).
- **Colour: one token confusion explains most failing text.** The contrast gate checks 15 pair kinds; design.css's own components paint 27 more that nothing checks, and 18 of those fail somewhere (GAP-TOK-1). In the light palettes apps ink text and icons with the mid tones instead of the `-ink` tokens (**P4-COLOR-01**, medium): in Hearth 57.9 % of F260's text, 40.5 % of the park map's and 28.4 % of the build guide's is below AA. Six rules ink with the raw profile colour where `--accent-deep` already passes (**P4-COLOR-02**, medium), and Me → Switch is 1.76-2.48:1 in every dark scheme (**P4-COLOR-03**, medium).
- **The person's colour is one light-theme hex.** `apps/hub.js:80` writes it raw in every scheme, so every raw use fails somewhere while `--accent-deep` passes for every colour in every theme (0 of 77 cells). The selected tab, Prayer nav item and Timer preset differ from their neighbours only by a 1.0-1.35:1 fill and a hue shift (**P4-ACCENT-01**, medium), and icon inks from `apps.json` and profile hex are never lifted for dark, putting kid tiles and Home card heads at 1.90-2.95:1 (**P4-ICON-01**, medium).
- **Native feel.** Four tells pass everywhere (tap highlight, tap latency, no focus ring after a touch, no blue links). The rest fail wherever design.css scopes them to `.ds`, sets them where they cannot apply, or loses them in the cascade. The worst: keyboard focus is invisible on every `.ds .btn`, 26 of 26 Tab stops (**P4-TELL-01**, medium), and on every Apps-grid tile and picker card, whose own shadows beat the shared ring, with the chat composer removing its ring outright (**P4-TELL-07**, medium); the `--focus` token itself is under 3:1 everywhere (P4-TOK-01). A named dark theme on a light-OS device flashes paper-white Hearth until `hub.js` runs (P4-TELL-03).
- **Motion and glass cost.** The glass's biggest cost is not the blur but the `--sheen-x` drift, which restyles the whole document on every scroll step; F260 on the iPad drops frames for it (p95 24-32.5 ms against 17-18 ms without it; P4-GLASS-01). The Apps grid blanks and re-pops every 30 s (P4-MOTION-01), taps are lost in the 220 ms viewer exit (P4-MOTION-02), and there are no springs, 93 literal durations and no shared loading state. Five areas put live glass on content in most screens while four keep it on the control layer; no glass surface in any area responds to Reduce Transparency or Increase Contrast (GAP-GLASS-1).
- **Dark mode.** The dark blocks are complete and drift-free, and dark text is better than light in 8 of 11 areas. Dark's weaknesses are in the shared base: soft fills 1.01-1.22:1 from the card, a flat depth ladder, inverted toasts and an art set with no dark form. Hearth on a dark OS (P2-VIS-03) was measured app by app: the park map's pane tabs, the build guide's labels and F260's Reset fall to 2.6-3.9:1 (**P4-DARK-02**, medium).
- **Type, shape and icons.** There is no iPad type tier (the shell renders 160 of 163 selectors at the same size on the iPad as on the iPhone) and no text-size preference. Ten areas set their large titles eight ways and none is a 34 bold tracked title. Concentric corners are impossible by construction (at least 58 of 99 pairs off). Kid mode keeps adult-sized controls wherever a control is sized in px (P4-SHAPE-01), and the shared toast is capped at half the viewport, so ordinary messages wrap to two or three lines on the iPhone (P4-SHAPE-04). There are eleven icon families, no app uses the shell's set, and the sprite duotone never renders (P4-ICON-02).
- **Corrections to earlier phases.** P2's tab label "Apps" at 3.78 and VIS-PRAYER-1's dark nav "Record" at 3.40-3.56 are no-blur artefacts (4.91-5.60 with a real blur). The park map's family labels are 11.0 px, not 8.7. P2's "one icon language with 20 % duotone" holds only for inline SVGs. P2's scrollbar pass and P3's scrollbar rows came from Playwright's `--hide-scrollbars`. P3's claim that the park map keeps animating under Reduce Motion is withdrawn. Earlier reports are not edited; the sections record each correction.
- **The proposed token set** (`audits/tools/phase4/tokens/proposed-tokens.css`, 672 lines, no build step, with two component rules: `glass7-component.css` for GLASS-7 and `identity-component.css` for faces and app tiles) keeps every name design.css defines today that anything reads (three unread names are retired), adds the eight house pastels as theme-aware fill/ink families, per-person hue families stored as a name, "on" colours for every fill, an iPad type tier, a text-size preference, kid and kiosk scales that also reach `--fs-xs` and every legacy size, concentric radii, elevation roles, composite glass tokens and springs. Its gate runs 102,583 evaluations with 0 failing, catches all 26 planted faults, and resolves 7,560 values identically in WebKit and Chromium, where both component rules are also checked against today's components and the Me hero's Switch button is rendered with its batch-1a row; the TV board still fits 1920×1080 exactly as today, and with the named batch rows big numerals are ui-rounded for everyone, kid mode is fully rounded, and no text falls under 11 px (16 px for a kid), the Dollywood pair included. Its gap table has 127 rows (49 closed by a token, 59 by a token plus a Phase 6 change, 14 by a rule, 3 partly, 2 open), and it leaves 18 decisions for the household (D1-D18). **Verification is not finished.** Six rounds of independent verifiers (three per round in rounds 1-5, two in round 6) found 23, 23, 20, 17, 17 and 7 issues (0, 0, 4, 4, 1 and 0 blocking; round 6's 7 are 5 distinct). Revisions 1-4 answered rounds 1-4. Round 5, against revision 4, passed the constraints check but not the contrast check (0 failing pairs, three minor wording errors) or the coherence check, and its one blocking issue was the Me hero's Switch button (`apps/design.css:423`), in no batch row and 1.19-1.29:1 in every dark palette after batch 1a. Revision 5 answered 4 of round 5's 17 issues: that rule now has an exact batch-1a row on `--hero-btn-bg` / `--hero-btn-ink`, so ACCENT-4 and COLOR-3 are closed as T+R, and the three wording errors are corrected. Round 6's two verifiers, with their own two-engine scripts, found all four fixes holding (the button paints exactly its tokens in both engines, ≥ 6.58 in light and ≥ 6.86 in dark) and no blocking issue; the contrast verifier returned "ok", the coherence verifier "not ok" for minor issues only. **17 minor issues are open**: 13 from round 5 (among them, GLASS-9 needs a Phase 6 row for the literal blur recipes, and the table holds 126 source gaps, not 127) and 4 from round 6 (among them, in dark the Switch capsule is the colour of the hero's end stop, so only its label and a hairline shadow mark its edge). All are listed at the top of the Proposed token set section. **Phase 5 update (2026-09-25):** revisions 6 and 6b apply the household's decisions and settle the 17 open issues; the figures in this paragraph are revision 5's. See "Revision 6" in the Proposed token set's assembler's note for the current file, gates and verification.
- **After the completeness critic.** Two defects were added, each confirmed 2/2 with the skeptics' own scripts: **P4-TELL-07** (medium: focus invisible on the Apps-grid tiles, the picker cards and the chat field, which also corrects P4-TELL-01's statement that controls outside `.ds .btn` ring) and **P4-SHAPE-04** (low: the shared toast capped at half the viewport, settling SHAPE Unresolved 3). COL-1 no longer exempts a blink that lasts its whole state, so the Timer's Colour falls from 5 to 4 (row 4.4; apps mean 4.1). The consistency pass nets −1.5 points, not −2. A states sweep measured text in hover, press and focus states and all pseudo-element text in the seven theme keys: nothing new fails in the `.ds` areas, pseudo-element text passes, and five state-only failures (4.06-4.46:1: F260, the build guide, Prayer's Copy for Elizabeth, a shell soft button for Kiara) are recorded for Phase 5 to verify (COLOR Unresolved 8). Three screenshots saved at device scale were re-saved at 1x, and uncited PNGs are kept out of git (Scripts and evidence).

Each cell is its shared base plus the calibration rules the area meets (the net adjustment per dimension clamped to ±2, in 0.5 steps), then checked against the screenshots by a separate checker and a consistency pass. Dimensions marked * are provisional: the rig renders fallback fonts and no backdrop blur, so the identity of the Apple faces and the look of the blur are neither credited nor deducted. The TV board has no row of its own; it is part of the shell row.

- **Reading it.** The shell averages 4.1 and the nine apps 4.1 (4.15 before rounding; 4.16 before the Timer's Colour correction below). The lowest row is the build guide (3.3); the highest are Tally (4.6) and Verses (4.6). Across the apps the weakest dimension is Colour & palette (3.1), then Motion & feedback (3.6); the strongest are Delight (5.2) and Dark mode (4.6). - **Where the evidence is.** Each row's rules and screenshots are listed under "Rules behind each score" and "Screenshots the scores rest on" below; the measurements behind each rule are in the dimension sections that follow.

- **Direction.** Of the 110 cells, 65 went down, 39 stayed and 6 went up. Every row average fell, by 0.3 (the Larder, Tally) to 1.6 (the park map).
- **Why the scores fell.** Phase 3's calibration notes found the same fault scored anywhere from 4 to 7 (`audits/03-apps.md:419`). Phase 4 priced each shared Hearth and template defect once, in a base that is lower than the holistic scores assumed, and deducted each area's own measured failures by written rules. It also measured what earlier phases judged from stills: contrast in seven theme keys (not System only), rendered press states, cold-load layout shift, idle cost, glass placement and real hit areas.
- **Changes of two points or more, and the rules that moved them.** The park map: Colour 6 → 2 (COL-2, COL-3, COL-4 on a base of 4; Phase 3 measured only the MIN label and never dark or per-person text), Iconography 6 → 3.5 (the template base carries the text glyphs and literal compass Phase 3 did not price; ICO-4), Dark mode 7 → 4.5 (base 5 with the daylight map priced; DRK-4), Typography 5 → 3 (base 4; TYP-1 for the 9.5 px MIN), Ease of use 5 → 3 (EOU-2 and EOU-3 from measured hit areas). Kid Verse: Typography 5 → 3 (TYP-1, TYP-3, TYP-6), Colour 5 → 2.5 (COL-2, COL-4), Iconography 6 → 4 (ICO-2). F260: Typography 5 → 3 (TYP-1 halved, TYP-2, TYP-3), Colour 4 → 2 (COL-2, COL-3, COL-4, clamped). The build guide: Colour 4 → 2 (COL-2, COL-3). The shell: Iconography 6 → 4 (the base carries the duotone that never renders, the dead icon attributes and the licence gap; ICO-2 for text glyphs beside the drawn set), Ease of use 6 → 4 (the base carries the missing text-size preference, the hue-only tab and the placeholder-only fields; EOU-6 for the one-tap reminder delete).
- **What went up.** Tally's Dark mode (4 → 5: Hearth on a dark OS now sits in the base, and its discs are glass, not the soft fill) and Native feel (5 → 5.5), the Larder's Colour and Shape (4 → 4.5 and 5 → 5.5, COL-5 and SHP-2), F260's Ease of use (5 → 5.5) and the shell's Delight (6 → 6.5, the TV board and the household's faces).

### How the scores were checked

- **Row scorers.** One scorer per row applied the bases and the rules, with evidence for every adjustment and a reason for every rule not applied.
- **Checkers.** A separate checker per row re-checked all 11 cells against the screenshots and the evidence files (378 screenshots opened across the ten rows). Of the 110 cells, **97 were agreed** and **13 adjusted**. Eleven adjustments corrected how a rule was applied: the shell's Colour (COL-5 not earned: most card heads take the raw app hex), Iconography (ICO-2 added: text stars and checks beside the drawn set) and Ease of use (EOU-6 added: the Home reminder check deletes a shared reminder in one tap, UX-HOME-8); F260's Layout (LAY-5 added for its two-pane layout at 1024 px and wider); the Larder's Colour (COL-4 dropped: the age text and chip also carry the bar's meaning), Iconography (ICO-1 dropped: three stroke weights) and Ease of use (EOU-1 dropped: its primary actions are 48 and 52 px); Prayer's Motion (MOT-1 dropped: 12 of 19 controls do press); Kid Verse's Layout (LAY-2 added: the 686 px column, as charged to Verses) and Ease of use (EOU-1's first-screen condition fails on three device classes; the checker gave half credit, which the consistency pass removed); Verses' Native feel (NAT-2 added: a draggable image). Two adjustments were the checker's own judgement (the park map's and Kid Verse's Colour, +½ each); the consistency pass returned both to the rule result. The checkers also flagged two rows whose written rules differed from their result without changing it (F260's Typography: TYP-1 halved and an unwritten +½ dropped; the Larder's Layout: the clamp, now written as policy).
- **Judge.** A gap of two points or more between a row and its checker would have gone to a judge; none arose.
- **Consistency pass.** One reviewer read all ten rows for the same rule applied differently and raised 11 flags; a ruling settled each, and all 11 were accepted (net −1.5 points over the table: −4 from six rulings, +2.5 from five). It settled two policy questions for every row: where a rule's text and the list of areas its author expected disagree, the text wins; and the ±2 clamp is policy.

| Area | Dimension | Before → final | Ruling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shell | Typography | 5.5 → 4.5 | TYP-4 withdrawn: the kiosk clock is clamp(72px, 9vw, 190px), 73.8 px on an iPad in portrait, under the rule's 80 px (`index.html:142`); the TV clock is already credited by GLA-5. |
| Shell | Dark mode | 3.5 → 4 | DRK-2 withdrawn: the raw-hex icons also fail in light (the gold tile and bell at 2.76 in Hearth), and COL-4 already charges that component; DRK-1 stays. |
| Prayer | Iconography | 5.5 → 4.5 | ICO-1 withdrawn: four computed stroke weights (1.75, 2, 2.2, 2.4; `audits/evidence/p4/ICON/rollup.json`), a wider spread than the Larder's, which lost ICO-1 for three. |
| Dollywood park map | Colour | 2.5 → 2 | COL-2, COL-3 and COL-4 apply and clamp to −2 from a base of 4, as in F260; COL-3 is one threshold, so 40.5 % against 57.9 % earns nothing. |
| Kid Verse | Colour | 3 → 2.5 | The checker confirmed COL-2 and COL-4 and withheld COL-5; 4 − 1 − ½ = 2.5. |
| Kid Verse | Ease of use | 5.5 → 5 | EOU-1 not met: the Done star is on the first screen only in iPad portrait (`audits/screens/kidverse/kid-typical-ipad-landscape-light.png`), and the rule has no half credit. |
| Kitchen timer | Native feel | 5.5 → 5 | NAT-2 applies: the header art (`apps/timer.html:53`) can be dragged; `user-select:none` does not stop an image drag (Tally's art has `pointer-events:none`). |
| Kitchen timer | Colour | 4.5 → 5 | COL-4 withdrawn: the digits carry the time the arc shows, the same test that excused the Larder bar, the Verses histogram and Prayer's dots. The arc stays filed as P4-ACCENT-04. |
| Tally counter | Dark mode | 4.5 → 5 | DRK-3 withdrawn: the discs are glass (`apps/tally.html:68-78`), not the soft fill, and carry no state. |
| Tally counter | Ease of use | 3.5 → 4 | EOU-4 withdrawn: the who pill spells the owner's name, a non-hue cue (`apps/tally.html:113-120`). |
| Verses | Dark mode | 4 → 4.5 | DRK-2 withdrawn: the who-pill ring also fails in light (Kiara in Parchment, about 2.57) and the pill prints the name beside it. |

**After the completeness critic, one further ruling** (not one of the 11 flags): **Kitchen timer, Colour 5 → 4.** COL-1 exempted "a transient blink", but the time's-up 0:00 blinks `1s steps(2) infinite` for the whole done state, until someone taps Reset or a preset (`apps/timer.html:38-39, 102, 120, 123`), so half the time the key fact of that state reads 2.42:1 (terra at opacity .65, the second of the two steps toward .3, over the danger-tinted page; Table COLOR-10), under 3:1 even as large text. A state-long blink is not transient. COL-1 now says so, and is withdrawn from the Timer: its Colour is its base, 4, and its row average 4.4. The same test was applied to every other state animation in the hub: the only other infinite animations pulse an icon or a background while speech or dictation runs (`apps/kidverse.html:57, 139`, `apps/verses.html:54`, `apps/leftovers.html:61`, `apps/prayer.html:389`, `index.html:76, 256, 265`) or are the skeleton shimmer (`apps/design.css:543`); none dims text a person needs, and Tally, the other COL-1 area, has none. COL-2 is not applied to the Timer either: the 0:00 reads at full contrast every other half-second, so its information is never absent, and the fault is priced by withdrawing the bonus.

### The bases

Two bases were scored once per dimension. `hearth-shared` is the base for the shell, F260, the Larder, Prayer, Tally, the Timer, Kid Verse and Verses, including the non-`.ds` apps, which still sit in the Hearth chrome and take its colour, dark and glass tokens and the theme bootstrap. `dollywood-template` is the base for the build guide and the park map; the template's shared components (fonts never loaded, 0 tokens, the compass, native controls, confirm(), missing press states, the pulses, the smooth scrolls, the daylight map) are priced there and never deducted again.

Against: SF Pro Rounded as the body face everywhere, serif display titles at 400, no weight tokens, `--fs-xs` never scales for kids or the kiosk, kid display type serif. | **4** | A ui-rounded body and tabular figures; family labels hold 11.0 px at every zoom. Against: Fraunces and Archivo named but never loaded, 149 literal px sizes and 0 type tokens, a 9 px compass N, label and value told apart by ink alone, no kid scale. |

Against: earthy fills at a third of the house chroma, one mid-tone hex per person, 18 of 27 unchecked component pairs fail somewhere, `--muted` on wells. | **4** | The chrome remaps the Hearth tokens; the accent reaches pressed chips without failures. Against: 56 chrome colour literals, no semantic ramp, UA placeholders at 1.35-1.77, the compass N on `--danger` at 1.0-1.45. Map colour is exempt. |

Against: phone margins on the iPad, a literal 880 px column, nine column widths, 11 % of targets tokenised, nine z-index ladders, 16 breakpoints. | **4** | Floating controls 10 px from the edges, a sheet with a grabber. ### The calibration rules

Each rule applies at most once per area however many components meet it. "Applied to" is the final set, after the checkers and the consistency pass (where a rule's own text and the list of areas its author expected disagreed, the rule text won).

| Rule | Δ | Condition | Applied to (½ = halved) |

| TYP-2 | −1 | Fewer than half the area's font sizes use design.css tokens, or 15 or more distinct sizes including fractional px, or web fonts outside the system stack. | F260, Larder Ledger, Prayer |
| TYP-3 | −½ | The primary numerals (count, time, progress, star total) are proportional or not in the rounded numeral face. | Shell, F260, Prayer, Tally counter, Kid Verse |
| TYP-4 | +1 | The centrepiece numerals follow the house: rounded or system face, tabular, tight tracking, at least 80 px on the iPad. | Kitchen timer |
| TYP-5 | +½ | Kid-mode type is sized for arm's length: a 14 px floor and titles of 28 px or more. | Prayer |
| TYP-6 | −½ | A kid-visible, tokenised area leaves half or more of its kid-mode text boxes at 12 px or less (not with TYP-2). | Kid Verse |
| COL-1 | +1 | Every resting text pair passes AA in every palette for every household profile. A blink or dim phase that ends on its own within a few seconds is not counted; one that lasts as long as its state (until someone acts) is a resting pair and is judged at its dimmest phase. | Tally counter |
| COL-2 | −1 | Needed text on a primary surface or control falls below AA in any palette in normal use, including the raw person colour as text and white on a mid tone. | Shell, F260, Prayer, Dollywood build guide, Dollywood park map, Kid Verse, Verses |

**Policies (compact).**
- **Scoring.** Cell = base + the rules that apply; the net adjustment per dimension is clamped to ±2 and the cell to 1-10, in 0.5 steps; the average is the mean of the 11 dimensions. Three cells hit the clamp (F260 Colour, Larder Layout, park-map Colour, each −2½ → −2).
- **Counted once, in the base.** P2-VIS-03, P4-TELL-03, the P4-COLOR-04 mechanism, P4-TELL-01, P4-TELL-07 and P4-TOK-01, P4-TELL-04 on `#views`, P4-TELL-06, GAP-GLASS-1, GAP-TELL-1 / CONS-MOTION-4, GAP-TYPE-1, GAP-TYPE-2, CONS-TYPE-4, P4-ICON-02, P4-ICON-05, P4-GLASS-01, P4-GLASS-02, GAP-DARK-1/-2, GAP-TOK-3, P4-ACCENT-01 on the shell `.tab`, P4-COLOR-05 on `.ds` placeholders, P4-TOK-02, P4-DARK-04, VIS-DARK-1, CONS-DARK-1, VIS-GLASS-2 and VIS-SHAPE-1. Where an area puts information on a token defect, or paints a raw hex where a safe token exists, that choice is the area's and is deducted.
- **One fault, one dimension.** Contrast that fails in a light palette or in both schemes goes to Colour; a failure only in dark, or only under Hearth on a dark OS, to Dark mode; text under 11 px to Typography; targets, error prevention and the kid route to Ease of use; presses, layout shift, Reduce Motion, idle cost and undo to Motion; dialogs, default controls, selectable chrome, loading tells and OS scrollbars to Native feel; glass placement and wasted blur to Shape; 2-3 m and 10-foot legibility to Glanceability.
- **Halving.** A deduction is halved for a narrow trigger (one orientation or device class, one profile in one non-default palette, Hearth on a dark OS) or when only secondary controls or screens meet it. Transient phases, disabled controls and other WCAG-exempt cases are not counted.
- **Maps.** Cartographic colour and text over map art inside the Dollywood canvases earn nothing and lose nothing under Colour; SVG label size is still graded under Typography. Everything drawn in HTML over or beside the map is chrome.
- **Audiences.** The shell row carries the 24/7 iPad Home and the TV board (GLA-5, GLA-6). Apps are judged by the measured readable distance of their key fact on the iPad, kid-visible areas by the kid's key fact at 1.5 m, and the park map at arm's length. Every kid-visible area must pass the pre-reader route as well as the adult rules (EOU-3 is a full point).
- **Evidence.** Phase 4 re-measured values first, then Phase 3, then Phase 2. Rig artefacts (the Windows WebKit select colours) and refuted or unresolved items never drive a rule; plausible-only items (GAP-MOTION-3) stay out. Missing features are Phase 5 material, and the declined features (a kid routines/stars app, a shared grocery list) are never counted.

What the investigators claimed and the skeptics or the re-measure did not accept is recorded under each section's "Checked and not a bug" (for example the Larder and Dollywood select contrast, a Windows WebKit artefact); open questions are under each section's "Unresolved" and are grouped under Not verified below.

P4-TOK-01 (the token) and P4-TELL-01 (the `.ds .btn` cascade that removes the ring) are two causes of the same symptom and stay separate.

## What design.css defines versus what the apps use (TOK)

**Scope.** This dimension covers:
- `apps/design.css`: its token, theme and kind blocks, and its own `.ds` component layer.
- The shell: `index.html`, including the TV board.
- The nine apps.
- `docs/design.html` and `apps/hub.js`.

The baseline is fe6041d (the working tree; app code unchanged).

**How the findings were checked.**
- **Bugs (P4-TOK-NN).** Two were sent to two skeptics each, and both were confirmed 2/2.
- **Gap, consistency and positive items (GAP-TOK, CONS-TOK, OK-TOK).** These describe the design, not malfunctions, so they were **not adversarially verified**. Each carries its own evidence.
- **Re-measure.** 18 headline numbers were re-measured from scratch by a separate script. 16 agreed. The two that did not (breakpoints, `color-mix()` counts) are corrected below, and so are three smaller points.

### Summary

- **Tokens.** design.css defines **121 tokens**: type 18, spacing 10, radius 6, target 2, layout 6, colour 52, glass 10, shadow 9, motion 8. There are no weight, z-index, opacity or breakpoint tokens. All five palettes override the same 47 tokens, and **no area references an undefined token** (all re-measured).
- **Adoption splits in two.** Colour is tokenised almost everywhere (83-100 %), but type, spacing and motion are tokenised only in the shell and the four small `.ds` apps.
  - F260, Prayer, the Larder and both Dollywood files use **0 spacing tokens** and **0-7 % font-size tokens**.
  - So the kid and TV scales cannot reach them. That includes the Larder and the park map, which kids use.
- **The contrast gate covers a third of what is painted.** docs/design.html and scripts/test-design.mjs check 15 pair kinds, and every checked case passes (180/180).
  - design.css's own components paint **27 more pair kinds that nothing checks, and 18 of them fail somewhere** (229 of 486 cases).
  - The failures: placeholder text 2.49-2.79, the Larder "to eat" badge on the Apps grid 2.55-2.61 in dark palettes, the focus ring, the switch, sync dots, bar and skeleton tracks, and profile/app colours used as glyphs.
- **Two confirmed low bugs.**
  - **P4-TOK-01:** the `--focus` ring is under 3:1 in every palette for every profile colour.
  - **P4-TOK-02:** the on/off `.switch` in Me → Notifications nearly disappears when off in the light palettes, and its knob is about 2:1 when on in the dark ones.
- **The root causes are missing kinds of token:**
  - no "on" colour per fill (only `--on-accent` exists);
  - the person and app colours are each stored as one light-theme hex that never re-tunes (17 of 19 fall under 3:1 as glyphs in Midnight and Forest);
  - the derived accent tokens cannot be scoped to one component;
  - there are no composite glass tokens (the glass filter is retyped 25 times).
- **Each area invents its own scales:**
  - 16 distinct breakpoint values;
  - nine unrelated z-index ladders;
  - literal font weights 300-800 in all 11 areas;
  - 168 `color-mix()` recipes, with the person colour mixed at 27 ratios;
  - four naming vocabularies, in which "ink" means text, deep text on a soft fill, the page background, or a light surface.
- **The system works when it is used.** Tally, Timer, Kid Verse and Verses are 92-100 % tokenised for spacing, radius and colour. Verses is the only area that re-points the accent correctly.

### Confirmed defects

#### P4-TOK-01 — The `--focus` ring is under 3:1 in every palette for every profile colour

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Rule clause:** information-bearing non-text below 3:1 counts as a bug, but a secondary failure is low. Keyboard focus is secondary in a touch-first hub.
  - **Exposure:** keyboard users only (desktop, or an iPad with a hardware keyboard). Touch never triggers `:focus-visible`.
- **Areas:** design.css; the shell (tab bar, `.ds` inputs); Prayer (the kid "Prayed" button); both Dollywood files (hub and live buttons).
- **What happens.**
  - `--focus` is `0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 38%, transparent)` (apps/design.css:102).
  - It is the only focus indicator: `:focus { outline: none }` (:313), then `:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--focus) }` (:314).
  - The same token is the ring on `.ds` inputs (:446), Prayer's kid `.prayed` button (apps/prayer.html:426), and the Dollywood hub/live buttons (apps/dollywood.html:226; apps/dollywood-live.html:226).
  - At token level, a 38 % tint over the surface is 1.25:1 (Forest, TV colour) to 1.90:1 (Hearth and Frost, TV colour). All 60 of 60 cases are under 3:1.
  - Rendered on the glass tab bar in the dark palettes it is 1.10-1.21.
  - Because `--focus` resolves on `:root`, a component that scopes `--accent` never changes its ring (GAP-TOK-6).
- **Expected.** A focus indicator at 3:1 or better against its surroundings, in every palette and for every profile colour (WCAG 1.4.11).
  - For the token proposal: the raw `--accent` does not reach 3:1 either in the dark palettes for the dark swatches (2.11-2.57 over `--surface` for Eli and David in Midnight and Forest).
- **Why it matters.** Anyone on a keyboard cannot see where focus is: on the tab bar, the Prayer kid button, the park-map buttons, and (faintly) the inputs.
- **Evidence.**
  - `audits/evidence/p4/TOK/token-pairs.json`, pair "--focus ring (accent 38%) over surface vs surface": 60/60, lowest 1.25.
  - `audits/evidence/p4/TOK/verify-tok-focus-ring-1.json`, with `verify-tok-focus-ring-1-<theme>-<eli|dad>.png`.
  - `audits/evidence/p4/TOK/verify-tok-focus-ring-2-webkit.json`, `verify-tok-focus-ring-2-chromium.json` and `verify-tok-focus-ring-2-webkit-hearth-eli.png`.
  - Code: apps/design.css:102, 313-314, 446.
- **Reproduction.** From the repo root:
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/pairs.mjs` (the "--focus ring" line);
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/verify-tok-focus-ring-1.mjs`;
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/verify-tok-focus-ring-2.mjs webkit` (or `chromium`).
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** wrote its own script with independent sRGB and WCAG maths: `verify-tok-focus-ring-1.mjs`, WebKit, desktop 1440×900.
    - Setup: 6 themes (the 5 palettes plus System on a dark OS) × 5 adults. Each theme was set as that person's preference through `PUT /api/data/hub/theme` plus `hub.theme`.
    - Token maths: 30/30 cases under 3:1 (1.29-1.87 over `--surface`, 1.31-1.84 over `--bg`).
    - Painted: pressing Tab lands on the tab bar's Home button. Its computed box-shadow is the 38 % ring, so the ring does render there.
    - Pixels were read 2 px and 9 px outside the border box. The ring measured 1.72-1.87 in the light palettes and **1.10-1.21 in Midnight, Forest and System dark**, lower than the token maths because it sits over the glass tab bar. That is 12/12 painted cases under 3:1.
  - **Skeptic 2** wrote `verify-tok-focus-ring-2.mjs` and ran it in **both WebKit and Chromium**, with identical results.
    - Setup: the real shell as Eli; 5 palettes × 10 swatches; real keyboard `:focus-visible` on a plain button, plus `:focus` on a `.ds .input`.
    - The ring pixel was read from screenshots: 1.25-1.91, 50/50 cases under 3:1. For example, Hearth/Eli: ring #BCBFCF on #FFFCF8 = 1.79.
    - On inputs, the 1 px border also turns full `--accent`, and that border reaches 3:1 in 41/50 cases.
    - The border fails in 9: Parchment/Kiara 2.69, and Midnight and Forest with Eli, David, TV or guest-plum (1.92-2.76).
- **Corrected claim.** The investigator's numbers and code citations hold. The corrections:
  - **Rendered it is worse.** On the dark tab bar the ring is 1.10-1.21.
  - **Inputs are narrower than claimed.** A `.ds` input also gets a full-accent border, which is adequate in 41/50 cases, so "keyboard users cannot see focus" is true for buttons the ring reaches, not for most inputs.
  - **Where the ring renders:** the tab bar, plain buttons, Prayer kid `.prayed` and the Dollywood hub buttons.
  - **Kid Verse is not a focus use.** `apps/kidverse.html:69` uses `--focus` as the today-dot ring and is already filed as VIS-KIDVERSE-2, so Kid Verse is dropped from the areas.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - Phase 2 UX "Keyboard focus is invisible on buttons" (medium; `audits/02-shell.md:5931-5935`). On `.ds .btn` the ring is removed by specificity.
  - VIS-KIDVERSE-2 (`audits/03-apps/kidverse.md:704`).
  - The new facet here is the token itself, wherever it does render.

#### P4-TOK-02 — The on/off `.switch` nearly vanishes when off in the light palettes, and its knob is about 2:1 when on in the dark ones

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Rule clause:** non-text below 3:1 on a secondary settings control. No text fails, nothing is lost, and it is not a daily flow.
  - **Exposure:** all six switches are in Me → Notifications (index.html:1262-1269):
    - the master "Reminders on this device", which is off by default;
    - five per-kind switches, which appear only once the device is subscribed and default to on.
  - So the off state people mostly see is the master switch, on a push-capable device that has not subscribed yet. That is the moment someone comes looking for it.
  - Where push is unsupported, the master is disabled at opacity .4 (apps/design.css:462), which is exempt as an inactive control.
- **Areas:** design.css; the shell (Me). The F260 and Prayer `.switch` classes are different components (segmented controls; CONS-TOK-2) and are not affected.
- **What happens.** The track is `var(--line)` when off and `var(--ok)` when on; the knob is a hardcoded `#fff` (apps/design.css:455-462). The switch sits on a `.card.glass` (index.html:1262), not on `--surface`. The two skeptics' pixel measurements against that card:

| Palette | Off track vs card | Off knob | On track vs card | On knob vs track |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hearth | 1.30-1.31 | 1.0-1.04 vs card, 1.36 vs track | 4.32 | 4.50 |
| Parchment | 1.41-1.50 | 1.26 vs card, 1.78 vs track | 4.50-4.55 | 5.68 |
| Frost | 1.32-1.34 | 1.06 vs card, 1.39 vs track | 4.70 | 4.96 |
| Midnight (= System dark) | 1.02-1.23 | 13.7 vs track, 16.85 vs card (clearly visible) | 8.15-8.33 | **2.02** |
| Forest | 1.08-1.30 | 12.8 vs track, 16.6 vs card (clearly visible) | 8.23-8.42 | **1.97** |
| Hearth on a dark OS | 1.23 | as Midnight | as Midnight | 2.02 (token) |

The token-level figures (investigator, and confirmed by the re-measure) are: off track vs `--surface` 1.33 / 1.45 / 1.34 / 1.20 / 1.27, and 1.20 for Hearth on a dark OS; knob on `--ok` 4.50 / 5.68 / 4.96 / 2.02 / 1.97 / 2.02.

The skeptics' dark off-track ranges differ (1.02-1.08 against 1.23-1.30) because they sampled different points on different devices: 6 px outside the switch on the iPad, and the composited card on the iPhone. Both are far under 3:1.

- **Expected.** The switch's track boundary and its knob reach 3:1 against their surroundings in every palette, judged against the card the switch actually sits on.
- **Why it matters.** This is the control that turns push reminders on. In Hearth, the default, a switched-off switch is barely visible as a control. In the dark palettes the "on" knob fades, though the green track still shows the state.
- **Evidence.**
  - `audits/evidence/p4/TOK/token-pairs.json`: pairs "--line track vs surface (.switch off)" and "#fff knob vs --ok track".
  - `audits/evidence/p4/TOK/verify-tok-switch-state-1.json`, with `verify-tok-switch-state-1-{system-light,system-dark,hearth-light,parchment-light,frost-light,midnight-dark,forest-dark}.png`.
  - `audits/evidence/p4/TOK/verify-tok-switch-state-2.json`, with `verify-tok-switch-state-2-{hearth,parchment,frost,midnight,forest,hearth-darkos}-enabled-off.png` and `-midnight-enabled-on.png`. The Hearth off crop shows only the knob's drop shadow outlining the control.
  - Code: apps/design.css:455-462; index.html:1262-1269.
- **Reproduction.** From the repo root:
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/pairs.mjs`;
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/verify-tok-switch-state-1.mjs`;
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/verify-tok-switch-state-2.mjs`.
  - Both verify scripts un-hide `#notif-prefs` and enable `#notif-toggle` in the test page only, because the rig has no push.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** (`verify-tok-switch-state-1.mjs`; WebKit, iPad portrait, Eli on Me, 7 theme runs set through the API and `hub.theme`).
    - It set one switch off and five on, then sampled 1× screenshot pixels: the track, the card 6 px outside, and the knob centre.
    - The token maths matched the investigator exactly.
    - On the card: off track 1.31 / 1.50 / 1.34 / 1.02 / 1.08; off knob about 1.0 against the Hearth card; on-knob 2.02 / 1.97 in dark.
  - **Skeptic 2** (`verify-tok-switch-state-2.mjs`; WebKit, iPhone PWA, typical seed).
    - It measured three states: as shipped (disabled), enabled-off and enabled-on.
    - Off track vs card 1.23-1.41; off knob vs card 1.04-1.26 in the light palettes, 16.6-16.85 in dark; on track 4.32-8.42; on knob vs track 4.50 / 5.68 / 4.96 / 2.02 / 1.97.
    - As shipped, the master is disabled at opacity .4 with the help text "This browser cannot receive push notifications."
- **Corrected claim.**
  - **Placement.** The switch sits on the Notifications glass card, and its six uses are all there: there are no admin toggles, and F260's and Prayer's `.switch` are other components.
  - **The on track vs card is 4.32 in Hearth**, not "4.40 or more". It still passes 3:1.
  - **Which state fails depends on the palette.** In practice the off state fails only in the light palettes, where the track and the white knob both nearly vanish. In the dark palettes the off switch still shows by its knob, and the failing part is the on-state knob, at about 2:1.
- **Related:** no P2 or P3 ID covers this control; both skeptics grepped. The Prayer item at `audits/03-apps/prayer.md:986` is about a different control.

### Consistency, visual and gap findings

These describe the design and were not adversarially verified. Each carries its own evidence. No house-style (VIS) item is filed in this dimension: how these tokens look is scored in the colour, type and material dimensions.

#### GAP-TOK-1 — The contrast gate checks 15 pair kinds; design.css's components paint 27 more, and 18 of those fail somewhere (medium)

- **Areas:** design.css, docs, the shell, Kid Verse, Dollywood, Verses.
- **What the gate checks.**
  - docs/design.html:285-307 builds 36 rows per theme: 7 neutral pairs, 4 chip ink-on-soft pairs, the opaque toast, and 3 accent pairs × 8 household colours.
  - scripts/test-design.mjs:47-53 and 101-112 asserts them for System light and dark, and per palette **only on a light-OS page**.
  - Every checked case passes: 0 fails in 12 runs of the guide's own `window.__contrast` (6 themes × light/dark OS), lowest 4.72 (Parchment, Kiara) (`guide-contrast.json`).
- **What it misses.** 27 further pair kinds that design.css's components paint (Table TOK-I). 18 of them fail somewhere, 229 of 486 cases:
  - text: the placeholder (2.49-2.79, all six scenarios);
  - text: `.badge` #fff on `--danger` in the dark palettes (2.55-2.61);
  - text: `--muted` on `--surface-2`, 4.37 in Parchment and 4.45 in Hearth. The token comment claims AA "on paper and cards" only (apps/design.css:47);
  - text: `--accent-deep` on `--accent-tint`, 4.23-4.30 for Kiara in the light palettes (the kid Home date kicker);
  - text: `--on-accent` on the hue mid-tones (gold 3.22, terra 4.41, olive 4.40);
  - large text: `--gold` as a large numeral, 2.96;
  - non-text: switch, focus, sync dots, bar and skeleton tracks, tint rings (13/60) and app-icon glyphs (32/60).
- **The gate also never runs:**
  - Hearth on a dark OS. The guide's `setTheme` copies hub.js, so on a dark-OS page `__setTheme('hearth')` paints exactly the Midnight numbers with `data-scheme="light"`. That is P2-VIS-03, invisible to the test.
  - The 2 guest-only swatches #8C4F7A and #4C7B6A (index.html:449, against the 8 at docs/design.html:253).
  - The 9 apps.json tile colours.
  - Every app's own pairs.
  - WebKit (the family's devices).
- **Caveat.** `.person-chip` (17/60) is used by no area today, and the tab-indicator row is not a failure by itself (U-TOK-1). The other 16 failing pairs are painted by shipped components.
- **Expected.** The gate enumerates every foreground/background pair the shared components render:
  - text 4.5, large 3, non-text 3;
  - in every palette, including Hearth on a dark OS;
  - for all 10 swatches;
  - in WebKit.
- **Why it matters.** CLAUDE.md tells future changes that the palette is proven AA ("WCAG AA on every text pair for all eight family colours in all five palettes"). The proof covers about a third of what is painted, so regressions in placeholders, badges, switches, rings and focus ship green.
- **Evidence:** `token-pairs.json` (summary and byPair), `guide-contrast.json` (12 runs; `dark-os/hearth` has `--bg` rgb(26,21,18) with scheme light), docs/design.html:253, 285-316.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/pairs.mjs && node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/guide-contrast.mjs`.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - P2-VIS-03;
  - P2-VIS-06;
  - VIS-VERSES-3;
  - Phase 2 UX, placeholder-only labels (`audits/02-shell.md:5803-5806`, 2.66/2.79);
  - Phase 2 VIS, dark skeletons (`audits/02-shell.md:5851`, 1.04 on bg);
  - the Phase 2 theme-card blurbs (4.45, measurement table).

#### GAP-TOK-2 — Only `--accent-deep` has an "on" colour; every other filled surface picks white or `--on-accent` by hand (medium)

- **Areas:** design.css, the shell, F260, Verses, the park map.
- **What happens.** `--on-accent` is the only "on" token (apps/design.css:92), and it is tuned for `--accent-deep`. Everything else is hand-picked:
  - **The badge.** `.ds .badge` paints `#fff` on `var(--danger)` (:515-516). But `--danger` (= `--terra`) is re-tuned light in the dark palettes. So the Larder "N to eat this week" badge on the Apps grid (index.html:703; 12 px bold) is 4.51 in Hearth, 5.66 Parchment and 4.94 Frost, but **2.61 in Midnight, 2.55 in Forest and 2.61 for Hearth on a dark OS**.
  - **The switch knob** is `#fff` on `--ok`: 1.97-2.02 in dark (P4-TOK-02).
  - **F260** defines `--on-solid: white` (apps/f260.html:26). It uses it on `--olive` for the daily Done (:144; 4.50 in Hearth, exactly at the edge) and on `--terra` (:392).
  - **Verses** pairs `--on-accent` with `--olive` for "Got it" (apps/verses.html:59; 4.40, VIS-VERSES-3).
  - **The park map** puts white on its wait tiles (apps/dollywood-live.html:500-501).
  - **Across the light palettes**, `--on-accent` on the hue mid-tones is: gold 3.22 / 4.27 / 3.96, terra 4.41, olive 4.40, teal 4.74.
- **Expected.** Each fill token has a paired, theme-tuned "on" token that passes 4.5:1 in every palette, and no component hardcodes `#fff`.
- **Why it matters.** The badge is the Apps grid's at-a-glance cue, on the Larder tile, that food must be eaten. In the dark palettes, and in System at night, a household member cannot read it. This meets the rule's "text a household member needs … on a primary surface": at least medium.
- **Evidence:** `token-pairs.json` pairs "#fff on --danger", "#fff knob vs --ok track" and "on-accent on --olive/--gold/--terra/--teal"; apps/design.css:459-460, 515-516; apps/f260.html:26, 144, 392; apps/verses.html:59; index.html:703.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/pairs.mjs`.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - Phase 2's unnumbered VIS item "The accent and tile icons are not lifted for dark" (medium; `audits/02-shell.md:5840-5846`) recorded the badge at 2.61. New here: Forest 2.55, Hearth on a dark OS, and the missing token as the root cause.
  - VIS-VERSES-3.

#### GAP-TOK-3 — Profile and app colours are single light-theme hex values that never re-tune; as foregrounds in Midnight and Forest, 17 of 19 fall under 3:1 (medium)

- **Areas:** the shell, design.css, hub.js, the park map, the build guide.
- **What happens.** design.css re-tunes every hue family per palette (for example `--olive` #5B8143 → #9DC183 in Midnight). The person and app colours, though, are each one hex, stored in:
  - the profile row (worker/seed.sql:4-11);
  - the 10 guest swatches (`SWATCHES`, index.html:449);
  - the 9 apps.json tile colours;
  - the fallbacks `#8A6A4B` (apps/hub.js:461; index.html:450; ×9 in the park map's JS).

  hub.js writes the colour inline as `--accent` (apps/hub.js:80).

  As a foreground (tile glyph, ring, avatar ring, timer ring) it sinks in the dark palettes (Table TOK-J):
  - glyph on its own tile under 3:1 for 17/19 in Midnight and Forest, 8 of 9 app tiles;
  - ring on `--surface` under 3:1 for 7/19 (Eli 2.57, David 2.14, TV 1.95).

  9 of the 19 entries use one of 7 hex values that are not design.css values at all.
- **Expected.** Profiles and apps reference a hue family or a person-palette token whose fill, ink and foreground values are defined per theme. The accent then lifts in the dark palettes the way the hue tokens do.
- **Why it matters.** Pre-readers find apps by icon and colour, and System goes dark every night. The TV and the dark palettes lose the per-person colour cue.
- **Evidence:** `appcolours.json`, `tokens-resolved.json` (the default `--accent` is the theme's `--mocha`; a profile's accent is fixed), apps/hub.js:80, 461; index.html:449-450; `audits/screens/shell/apps-typical-ipad-portrait-dark.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/tokens.mjs && node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/appcolours.mjs`.
- **Re-measure.** The counts agree exactly. They use the tile gradient's 22 % stop, its worst case (apps/design.css:607). At the 15 % mid-tone the counts are 13/19 in Midnight and Forest and 3/19 in Parchment.
- **Related (not re-filed):** the Phase 2 unnumbered VIS item (`audits/02-shell.md:5840-5846`), which covers the rings and 6 of 9 tile icons at 1.95-2.93.
  - New here: all 19 colours × 5 palettes, including Forest; 8 of 9 tiles at token level; the 7 hex values (9 of 19 entries) outside design.css; and the data-model root cause (a hex per person and per app).

#### GAP-TOK-4 — Kid and kiosk scale only the tokenised subset; every literal size escapes them (medium)

- **Areas:** design.css, the shell, F260, the Larder, Prayer, the park map.
- **What the kind blocks scale** (apps/design.css:280-289):
  - kid overrides `--tap`/`--tap-lg`, `--fs-sm`…`--fs-hero` and five radii;
  - kiosk overrides only `--fs-*` and `--blur`.
- **What they miss:**
  - `--fs-xs` stays 12 px for both;
  - spacing and line-height never scale;
  - the TV keeps 44 px targets.
- **Everything literal escapes as well** (Table TOK-D):
  - font sizes: F260 0/122, Larder 0/16 (kid-visible), Prayer 5/65 (its kid block), park map 0/72 plus 45 base-rule literals (kid-visible);
  - target sizes: shell 17, F260 50, park map 30, Prayer 14;
  - the shell's `[data-kind=kid]` rules restate 64/84 px by hand instead of using `--tap`/`--tap-lg` (index.html:60, 124, 188).
- **Expected.** Every size a kid or the TV sees comes from a token that the kind blocks scale: type including `--fs-xs`, targets, spacing and radii.
- **Why it matters.** Kid mode and the 10-foot TV depend on the kind scale, but the Larder and the park map keep adult type for pre-readers.
- **Evidence:** `adoption.json`, `literals-shell.json` (cat targetSize), `tokens-inventory.json`, apps/design.css:280-289.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/usage.mjs && node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/literals.mjs && node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/adoption.mjs`.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - Phase 2 VIS, `--fs-xs` stays 12 in kid and kiosk (`audits/02-shell.md:5771-5773`);
  - `audits/03-apps/leftovers.md:995`;
  - `audits/03-apps/dollywood-live.md:817`.
  - New here: the cross-area measure, and the kiosk's missing target, spacing and radius scaling.

#### GAP-TOK-5 — There are no weight, z-index, opacity, breakpoint, press-scale, fluid-type or composite-glass tokens, so each area invents its own (medium)

- **Areas:** all 11.
- **What each area invents** (Table TOK-F):
  - **Weights:** literal weights in all 11 areas: design.css 20 (600 ×10, 700 ×7, 400 ×3), shell 26, F260 87 (800 ×16), Prayer 52, park map 40, Kid Verse 16.
  - **z-index:** nine unrelated ladders, from design.css 1/20/50/60 to Prayer 10-40.
  - **Breakpoints:** **16 distinct values**, or 18 counting min/max direction; none is shared by every area.
  - **Fluid display sizes:** one-off `clamp()`s (shell ×6, Tally, Timer, Kid Verse, Verses); nothing beyond `--fs-hero`.
  - **Press scales:** .86 to 1.06 across areas.
  - **Glass filter:** `saturate(1.4)` is retyped 25 times outside design.css (F260 6, Tally 6, Larder 2, Prayer 2, the Dollywood template 9).
  - **Glass shadow:** its five-part box-shadow is restated in the shell (index.html:261), Timer (:36), Prayer (:283-300), the Larder (:32-45) and Tally ×3.
  - Only the Dollywood template has composite glass tokens (`--lv-glass*`, apps/dollywood.html:215).
- **Expected.** design.css defines weight, layer, opacity, breakpoint, press and fluid display scales plus composite glass tokens, and the areas reference them.
- **Why it matters.** Without shared layers, overlays from different areas can collide; without shared weights, hierarchy drifts from app to app. Hand-copied glass diverges from the recipe the moment the recipe changes.
- **Evidence:** `literals-summary.json`, `literals-<area>.json` (fontWeight, zIndex, glassFilter hits with lines), `tokens-inventory.json` → `byCategory`, `remeasure.json` → `breakpoints`, `saturate14`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/literals.mjs`.
- **Corrected** from the investigator's "21 distinct breakpoints". Its own list and its own `literals-summary.json` give 16 values (18 with direction); no reading gives 21.

#### GAP-TOK-6 — design.css cannot scope the accent to one component, because the derived accent tokens resolve once on `:root` (low)

- **Areas:** design.css, Kid Verse, Prayer, Verses.
- **What happens.** `--accent-soft/-tint/-deep/-glow`, `--glow-accent` and `--focus` are declared on `:root` (apps/design.css:86-102) and inherit as computed values. A component that sets `--accent` therefore has to restate each derived token by hand. Three areas tried:

| Area | Derived tokens restated | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Kid Verse | none | The Done ★ paints Ezra's teal: local `--accent` rgb(180,134,27), fill rgb(14,91,86) (P3-KIDVERSE-14) |
| Prayer | one of three (`--accent-soft`) | On the Family list the nav text is slate-deep rgb(57,67,101) on teal-soft rgb(220,236,234), while Pray now and + stay slate (VIS-PRAYER-4) |
| Verses | three (apps/verses.html:56-58) | Correct, but its `.btn-primary` glow and focus ring still use the person's colour |

- **Expected.** A scoping hook: a selector that re-declares the derived tokens, so that setting `--accent` on a component re-derives soft, tint, deep, glow and focus.
- **Why it matters.** Two of the three attempts in the codebase got it wrong, and every future per-component colour will hit the same trap.
- **Evidence:** `accent-repoint.json`, `accent-repoint-kidverse-ezra.png`, `accent-repoint-prayer-eli-family.png`, apps/design.css:86-102, apps/kidverse.html:55, 137, apps/prayer.html:39, apps/verses.html:56-58.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/verify-accent-repoint.mjs`.
- **Re-measure.** The Kid Verse fill reproduced exactly on the rig (the local `--accent` is gold; the inherited `--accent-deep` resolves to rgb(14,91,86)).
- **Related:** P3-KIDVERSE-14 and VIS-PRAYER-4 own the two app instances. Only the system rule is new.

#### GAP-TOK-7 — The "every colour is a token" rule fails only on `#hex` in the first `<style>` (low)

- **Areas:** the shell, design.css, F260, the Larder, Prayer, both Dollywood files.
- **What the rule tests.** scripts/screens-apps.mjs:41-49 and scripts/screens-shell.mjs:114-115 test `/#[0-9a-f]{3,8}/` in the first `<style>` only. For the Dollywood pair, only line 212 (the remap line) is tested.
- **What passes today:**
  - **Shell:** 6 rgba/white/black in its CSS, plus the JS `SWATCHES` ×10 and `FALLBACK`.
  - **design.css:** 18 colour literals outside the token blocks, which are never checked. They include `#fff` ×2 (:459, :516), `#FFFCF8` (:429) and the URL-encoded chevron `#7D6F62` (:449).
  - **Park map:** 56 chrome colour literals: the wait bands (apps/dollywood-live.html:496-508), the meeting flag (:517), the stamp (:519), and `#8A6A4B` ×9 in JS style strings.
  - **Other areas:** F260 and Larder `white`; Prayer's JS hex (apps/prayer.html:1537); inline-style hex (apps/dollywood.html:664).
- **Expected.** The gate covers every colour literal: hex, rgb/hsl and named colours, in CSS, inline styles and JS style strings, and all the Dollywood chrome rules.
- **Why it matters.** CLAUDE.md's "every colour in every app is a token" is enforced for one syntax only.
- **Evidence:** scripts/screens-apps.mjs:41-49, scripts/screens-shell.mjs:114-115, `literals-shell.json`, `literals-design_css.json`, `literals-dollywood-live.json` (cat colour, status violation).
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/literals.mjs`.

#### GAP-TOK-8 — Each dark palette is stored two or three times in design.css (low)

- **Where the copies are:**
  - Midnight's 47 values are byte-identical in three places: `:root[data-theme=midnight]` (apps/design.css:156-175), the `@media` dark `:root:not([data-theme])` block (:176-197) and `.tp-half` (:257-276).

  - Hearth has two (42 values at :238-256).

- **Why it matters.** A palette fix has to be made in two or three places, or the System-dark and swatch copies drift.

- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/tokens.mjs`.
- **Related:** P2-VIS-03, which the `@media` copy makes possible.

#### GAP-TOK-9 — 3 tokens are unused, 3 are used only by the style guide, and 5 are exact aliases (info)

- **Unused anywhere:** `--info`, `--shadow-sm`, `--dur`.
- **Style guide only:** `--sp-12`, `--sp-16` (docs/design.html:11, 18) and `--bg-2` (through the guide's NEUTRALS template).

- **Reachable only through a class no area uses:** `--info-soft` and `--info-ink`, via `.chip-info`.

#### CONS-TOK-1 — Four local token vocabularies, in which "ink" means four different things (low)

- **The duplicated alias sets.** F260 and Prayer each define the same nine aliases for design tokens (apps/f260.html:16-20; apps/prayer.html:24-34).
- **What "ink" means where:**
  - In the Dollywood template, `--ink` is the **page background** (`--ink: var(--bg)`, apps/dollywood.html:212).
  - In the Larder, `--ledger-ink` is `--surface`, a light colour (apps/leftovers.html:14).
  - In design.css, the `-ink` suffix means deep text on a soft fill (apps/design.css:73-78).
- **Other names that clash:** in the Dollywood template `--cream` is the text and `--dim` = `--muted`, while in Prayer `--dim` = `--text` (apps/prayer.html:27).
- **Expected.** One vocabulary: areas use design.css names directly.
- **Why it matters.** The same word points to opposite roles, so a change made by name lands on the wrong surface.
- **Evidence:** `local-tokens.json`; Table TOK-H.

#### CONS-TOK-2 — The non-`.ds` apps reuse design.css class names for different components, and the segmented control exists four ways (low)

- **The names collide.** F260 (`.btn` ×35, `.row` ×10, `.seg` ×8, `.switch`, `.sheet`, `.toast`), Prayer (`.chip` ×10, `.small` ×25, `.pill`, `.sheet`, `.toast`, `.switch`) and the Dollywood template (`.btn`, `.badge`, `.pill`, `.stat`) have no `body.ds`. So these are their own components, which design.css would restyle the moment `.ds` was added.
- **The segmented control four ways:**

| Where | Class | Shape | Height | Label size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| design.css (apps/design.css:465-468) | `.ds .seg` | radius 16 | 44 px | weight 600 |
| F260 (apps/f260.html:60) | `.switch` | pill | 52 px | 15 px |
| Prayer (apps/prayer.html:66) | `.switch` | pill | 44 px | 13.5 px |
| Dollywood | `.tabs` | radius 0 | — | 13 px |

  Meanwhile design.css's own `.switch` is an on/off toggle.
- **Primary-button radius:** design.css 16, F260 999, Prayer 12, Dollywood 12 (hub) or 3 (base).
- **Expected.** Each shared component has one name; app-specific ones are namespaced.
- **Why it matters.** It blocks a gradual move to `.ds`, and the same control looks different from app to app.
- **Evidence:** `components.json`; apps/f260.html:60; apps/prayer.html:66, 192; apps/dollywood.html:25, 56, 224; apps/design.css:349-370, 455-468.

#### CONS-TOK-3 — 168 `color-mix()` recipes, with the person colour mixed at 27 different ratios (low)

- **Counts.** 168 occurrences and 99 distinct recipes (re-measure):
  - design.css 55;
  - the Dollywood template 58;
  - F260 11, Prayer 11, Tally 11;
  - shell 6, Larder 6;
  - Timer 5, Verses 3, Kid Verse 2.
- **The person colour** (`var(--accent)` or `var(--tint)`): 86 occurrences, 39 distinct recipes, at 27 numeric ratios: 0, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 22, 26, 30, 32, 34, 35, 38, 40, 45, 52, 55, 58, 60, 62, 66, 70, 72, 74, 75 and 84 %.

Its "37" also counted distinct recipes against a total of occurrences. The 27 ratios agree.

#### CONS-TOK-4 — The shell's eight off-scale radii are one ratio (size × 0.32) typed eight times (info)

- **What happens.** The app-icon radii are 13/14/11/20/15/28/10/18 px, for sizes 40/44/36/64/48/88/30/56 px (index.html:109, 139, 167, 188, 226, 240, 247; apps/design.css:606). Each is round(size × 0.32).
