### What works

- **OK-TOK-1 — No undefined tokens, and full palette parity.**
  - **Undefined tokens:** 0 in all 13 areas. Every `var()` resolves to a design.css token, a component-local, a hub.js runtime variable or a local definition.
  - **The only names without a static definition all have fallbacks:** design.css's consumer inputs `--p`, `--tabs` and `--i`; F260's runtime `--g-${…}`; and the Dollywood `--cc/--cw/--cd` (set in JS).
  - **Palette parity:** all five palettes override the same 47 tokens (`overriddenByOnlySomeThemes` is empty), and all 121 tokens resolve without an invalid value in WebKit in 10 scenarios.
  - Evidence: `usage-matrix.json`, `tokens-inventory.json`, `tokens-resolved.json`, `remeasure.json` → `undefinedTokens`.
- **OK-TOK-2 — The small `.ds` apps are almost fully tokenised.**
  - Tally, Timer, Kid Verse and Verses are 92-100 % tokenised for spacing, radius and colour. The shell is 95 % for colour, 88 % for spacing and 89 % for type.
  - Outside the Dollywood pair, the shell's and the apps' first `<style>` contains no hex.
  - The guide's own 36 rows pass AA in every palette on either OS scheme.
  - Evidence: `adoption.json`, `guide-contrast.json`.
- **OK-TOK-3 — Verses re-points the accent the right way.** It restates `--accent`, `--accent-soft` and `--accent-deep` together on its rating buttons (apps/verses.html:56-58). It is the working pattern for GAP-TOK-6. Evidence: `accent-repoint.json`.

### Checked and not a bug

No finding was refuted: two were sent to skeptics and both were confirmed 2/2. The following points were corrected on review and the re-measure. They are not skeptic verdicts.

- **`--cc`, `--cw` and `--cd` are not undefined.** The template sets them in JS with `setProperty` on the coaster layer: apps/dollywood.html:807 and apps/dollywood-live.html:807, from ../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:804.
  - That runs when the flavour is not `live`, and the only rules that read them apply only outside the live flavour (template.html:204).
  - The fallbacks 7/3/.8 cover the moment before the script runs.
- **The Kid Verse `--focus` use is not a focus ring.** apps/kidverse.html:69 draws the today dot with it, and that is already VIS-KIDVERSE-2 (1.70/1.51).
- **The skeleton figures of 1.14 (here) and 1.04 (Phase 2) do not disagree.** 1.14 is `--surface-2` on a card surface; 1.04 is `--surface-2` on the page background. Both are right.
- **The design.css `.switch` is not used by F260 or Prayer.** Their `.switch` classes are their own segmented controls. The shell's six uses are all in Me → Notifications; there are no admin toggles.

### Unresolved

- **U-TOK-1 — Does the tab bar's selected state meet WCAG 1.4.11?**
  - The `.tab-ind` fill (`--accent-soft`) is 1.10-1.24 against the glass tab bar in every case. But `.tab.on` also changes the label from `--muted` to `--accent-deep` (apps/design.css:564), so fill is not the only cue.
  - To settle it: measure the rendered contrast between the selected and idle label and icon colours, per palette and swatch, on the real tab bar.
- **U-TOK-2 — Is `--muted` on `--surface-2` in Parchment (4.37) shipped anywhere?** Phase 2 measured the Me theme-card blurbs at 4.45 in Hearth. To settle it: capture the Me theme cards and any `.well` or `.seg` with muted text in Parchment and measure the pixels.
- **U-TOK-3 — Kiara's kid Home kicker (4.23-4.30) is token-level only.** To settle it: capture Kiara's kid Home in Hearth, Parchment and Frost on iPad portrait and measure the date kicker's pixels.
- **U-TOK-4 — How many of the Dollywood base-rule literals survive?** The 186 per file are an upper bound. To settle it: compute the cascaded value per element in both flavours, from the sibling template.
- **U-TOK-5 — Rendered contrast and engine parity.**
  - The pair ratios are token-level on a blank WebKit page: no photos and no real blur, with glass composited over `--bg` only. Rendered-pixel contrast belongs to the COLOR dimension.
  - `tokens.mjs` and `pairs.mjs` ran in WebKit only. Skeptic 2 of P4-TOK-01 found WebKit and Chromium identical for the ring.
  - Real devices (SF fonts, real blur, Dynamic Type) were not seen.
- **U-TOK-6 — Kiara's Kid Verse and Prayer's kid mode (always the Family list) were not captured for the accent re-point.** To settle it: rerun `verify-accent-repoint.mjs` as Kiara, and as a kid on Prayer.
- **U-TOK-7 — Dollywood JS colours.** The Dollywood JS colour split (123 in the guide and 86 in the map classed as "map or data") is a context heuristic that was spot-checked only.

### Token gaps for the proposal

**Colour**
1. **"On" tokens per fill.** Add `--on-danger`, `--on-ok`, `--on-warn`, `--on-info` and `--on-<hue>` per theme, each at 4.5 or better. Retire the literal `#fff` in `.badge` (apps/design.css:516) and in the `.switch` knob (:459), and F260's `--on-solid` (GAP-TOK-2).
2. **A theme-aware person palette.** `--person-<hue>` with fill, ink and foreground-on-dark per theme, covering the 2 guest-only swatches. Profiles and apps store a hue name, not a hex, and hub.js sets `--accent: var(--person-x)` (GAP-TOK-3).
3. **A scope selector for the derived accent tokens** that re-declares `--accent-soft/-tint/-deep/-glow`, `--glow-accent` and `--focus`, plus per-element `--tint-soft`, `--tint-deep` and `--tint-ink`. The shell already computes `--tint-ink` inline at index.html:955 and 1070 (GAP-TOK-6).
4. **A named tint scale** of 5-6 steps (for example wash, soft, tint, ring, deep, glow), replacing 27 ad-hoc ratios (CONS-TOK-3).
5. **Non-text control tokens that meet 3:1:**
   - an off-track (`--line` is 1.20-1.45 today);
   - a solid per-theme `--focus-ring` (1.25-1.90 today; raw `--accent` is also under 3:1 in the dark palettes);
   - a bar and skeleton track (1.14 today);
   - an offline sync dot (2.49-2.79 today).
6. **A `--placeholder` text token at 4.5 or better,** instead of the "decorative only" `--muted-decor`. Also a stated contract for `--muted` on `--surface-2` (4.37-4.45).
7. **A highlight and shade scale** to replace the literal `rgba(255,255,255,a)` and `rgba(0,0,0,a)`: 13 in design.css components, 5 in the shell, 13+ in the park map.
8. **A categorical and semantic-ramp palette.** Today each app invents one: F260 `--g-*`, Prayer `--d0…--d7`, the Larder's freshness ramp (in JS) and the park map's wait bands (apps/dollywood-live.html:496-508).

**Type**
9. **Font-weight tokens** (literal weights in all 11 areas) and **a fluid display scale** beyond `--fs-hero` (shell ×6, and the Tally, Timer, Kid Verse and Verses numerals).
10. **Kind scales that reach everything:** kid and kiosk `--fs-xs`, line-heights, and every literal px size (F260 0/122, Larder 0/16, Prayer 5/65 and park map 0/72 tokenised today).

**Spacing**
11. **Adopt the spacing scale** in F260 (213 literals, 66 values), Prayer (139, 57 values), the Larder (33) and the Dollywood template. Either snap their 6, 10 and 14 px to the 4-pt scale or add half-steps. Also let kid and kiosk scale spacing.

**Radius**
12. **An icon-radius ratio** (size × 0.32) and **a control-radius role**: primary buttons are 16 / 999 / 12 / 3 px across areas today. Also let the kiosk scale radii.

**Shadow**
13. **Ring-width, pressed/inset and coloured-glow elevation tokens.** design.css alone has 15 bespoke shadow geometries (avatar rings 2/2.5/3.5/4/5/8 px, hover and hero glows, the switch).

**Glass**
14. **Composite glass tokens** `--glass-bg`, `--glass-shadow` and `--glass-filter`. `saturate(1.4)` is retyped 25 times and the five-part shadow restated in 6 areas. The Dollywood `--lv-glass*` shows the shape.

**Motion**
15. **A press-scale token** (.86-1.06 across areas today) and **long-duration tokens** (.8 s ring and bar, 1.4 s shimmer, 1-1.2 s pulse and blink). Retire the dead aliases `--dur` and `--ease-out`. The areas' own springs are F260 `cubic-bezier(.3,1.6,.5,1)`, Prayer `(.22,.9,.3,1)` and Dollywood `(.2,.8,.2,1)`.

**Layout**
16. **A z-index layer scale** (nine unrelated ladders today) and **a documented breakpoint scale** (16 distinct values today).
17. **Targets through `--tap`/`--tap-lg`** instead of literals (shell 17 including the kid 64/84 px, F260 50, park map 30, Prayer 14), so that they follow the kind scale.

**Structure and gates**
18. **One source per palette.** Today Midnight is stored 3×, Forest 2× and Hearth 2×, and the `.tp` copies miss the glass-edge tokens, `--accent-tint`, the semantic aliases and `--focus` (GAP-TOK-8).
19. **Contrast gates that cover what is painted.**
    - The contrast table iterates every component pair: the 27 unchecked kinds, Hearth on a dark OS, all 10 swatches, in WebKit.
    - The token rule covers rgba, named, JS and inline colours and all the Dollywood chrome (GAP-TOK-1, GAP-TOK-7).
20. **One vocabulary.**
    - Retire the F260/Prayer alias set and the Dollywood `--ink/--cream/--dim` names.
    - Namespace app-local components whose names collide with `.ds` (`.btn`, `.row`, `.chip`, `.switch`).
    - Keep one segmented control (CONS-TOK-1, CONS-TOK-2).
21. **Prune.** Remove `--info`, `--shadow-sm` and `--dur`; decide on `--sp-12`, `--sp-16` and `--bg-2`; deprecate the aliases `--ease-out`, `--accent-strong`, `--shadow` and `--shadow-lg` (GAP-TOK-9).

### Method, scripts and evidence

All scripts are under `audits/tools/phase4/TOK/`, and the evidence is under `audits/evidence/p4/TOK/`. Everything ran on the local instance; nothing contacted production, and no app code was changed.

| Script | What it does | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `lib-tok.mjs` | Shared parser: a real CSS tokenizer that tracks selector, at-rule stack and line per declaration; inline `style=""`, JS style strings, `.style.x=` and `setProperty`; colour maths (WCAG, OKLab) | — |
| `tokens.mjs` | Every custom property in design.css's token, theme and kind blocks, with its value per block and a duplicate-block check. Then every token resolved in WebKit in 10 scenarios (5 palettes, System light and dark, Hearth on a dark OS, kid, kiosk) | `tokens-inventory.json`, `tokens-resolved.json` |
| `usage.mjs` | `var()` references per area × token, classified as design, component-local, hub.js, local or undefined (with fallbacks) | `usage-matrix.json`, `local-tokens.json` |
| `literals.mjs` | Every hardcoded value in 16 categories, each with the token it should use or "no token exists", with false-positive and exemption rules | `literals-<area>.json`, `literals-summary.json` |
| `adoption.mjs` | Token refs / (token refs + literals) per area × category | `adoption.json` |
| `mixes.mjs` | Every single-level `color-mix()` and the ratios applied to the person colour | `mixes.json` (a lower bound; see CONS-TOK-3) |
| `components.mjs` | `.ds` on `<body>`, design.css classes used per area, and each area's own component rules | `components.json` |
| `pairs.mjs` | Every foreground/background pair design.css's components paint, resolved in WebKit in 6 scenarios × 10 swatches, each flagged as guide-checked or not | `token-pairs.json` |
| `guide-contrast.mjs` | docs/design.html's own `window.__contrast`, for every theme on a light and a dark OS page, served read-only on a random port | `guide-contrast.json` |
| `appcolours.mjs` | The 9 tile colours and 10 swatches as glyph-on-tile and ring-on-surface in every palette | `appcolours.json` |
| `verify-accent-repoint.mjs` | A runtime proof on the rig (WebKit, iPad portrait) that re-pointing `--accent` does not re-point its derived tokens | `accent-repoint.json`, `accent-repoint-kidverse-ezra.png`, `accent-repoint-prayer-eli-family.png` (1× CSS) |
| `verify-tok-focus-ring-1.mjs`, `verify-tok-focus-ring-2.mjs` | The P4-TOK-01 skeptics (WebKit; the second also Chromium) | `verify-tok-focus-ring-*.json/png` |
| `verify-tok-switch-state-1.mjs`, `verify-tok-switch-state-2.mjs` | The P4-TOK-02 skeptics (WebKit; iPad portrait and iPhone PWA) | `verify-tok-switch-state-*.json/png` |
| `remeasure.mjs` | An independent re-measure written from scratch: it imports only `lib/local.mjs`, does its own static parse, and uses WebKit on a read-only static server plus the rig | `remeasure.json` |

| rgb/named | 6 |

| shadows | 6 |

**Not verified in this dimension.**
- scripts/test-design.mjs itself was not run, because it binds port 8765 and writes to docs/screens outside audits/. Its contrast table was reproduced independently with `guide-contrast.mjs`.
- `audits/evidence/p4/measure/tokens-resolved.json` did not exist when this ran, so this dimension's own WebKit resolution was used.
- See *Unresolved* for the rest.

**Processes.** Every script closes its browser and the local rig in a `finally` block. Playwright/WebKit processes seen running at the end belonged to parallel Phase 4 investigators (for example the ICON dimension's verify script), so they were not killed.

## Every hardcoded value that should be a token (TOK)

This part of the TOK dimension counts every literal the areas use where a design.css token exists or should exist. It uses the same scripts and the same verification as the section above; the re-measure's results for these counts are in that section's "Method, scripts and evidence". The findings that rest on these tables are filed there: GAP-TOK-4 (the kid and kiosk scales reach only the tokenised subset), GAP-TOK-5 (no weight, z-index, opacity, breakpoint, press-scale, fluid-type or composite-glass tokens), GAP-TOK-7 (the hex gate), CONS-TOK-1 (four local vocabularies), CONS-TOK-3 (168 `color-mix()` recipes) and CONS-TOK-4 (the shell's radii). Each later dimension also tables its own literals: Table TYPE-3 (font sizes), Tables SHAPE-2 and SHAPE-8 (spacing and radii), Table GLASS-2 (glass recipes), Table MOTION-1 (durations and curves) and Table ICON-2 (strokes and sizes). Every hit, with its file and line, is in `audits/evidence/p4/TOK/literals-<area>.json`; the other bare file names in these tables are in `audits/evidence/p4/TOK/` too.

## Type (TYPE)

Baseline: the working tree at fe6041d (no app file has changed since). Every number comes from one of four sources: the rig-v2 raw files (`audits/evidence/p4/measure/raw/`, 3,662 jobs), code, the targeted local runs listed under Method, or the independent re-measure. No request went to production, and no PIN or pairing code was read or used. The rig renders Windows fallback faces: ui-rounded and system-ui become Segoe UI, ui-serif becomes Palatino Linotype, the generic `serif` becomes Times New Roman, and Manrope loads from Google Fonts. Face identity on Apple devices is therefore argued from the declared stacks. Sizes, weights, tracking and line heights are computed values and do not depend on the face.

**Summary**

- **One defect confirmed, 2/2, low (P4-TYPE-01).** At the build guide's default whole-park view, three groups of map labels render below the 11 px floor:
  - section names are 6.14 px on the iPhone PWA (5.51 px in iPhone Safari);
  - listing marker numbers are 6.82 px on every device;
  - contour heights are 9.5 px at every zoom.
  The template's zoom code sets these sizes (`../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:800-802`). The rig's type inventory cannot see SVG text, so no earlier phase recorded them.
- **The type tokens reach only part of the hub.**
  - Well tokenised: the shell (51 token sizes, 0 bare px; 6 `clamp()` declarations have px bounds), Verses (99 % of text boxes on a token value) and Timer (90 %).
  - Literal px only: F260 (0 tokens, 122 px), Prayer (5 tokens, 64 px), the Larder (0, 16) and both Dollywood exports (0, 149).
  - A change at the token level (kid mode, an iPad tier, a text-size setting) therefore skips five of the nine apps (CONS-TYPE-7).
- **No iPad tier and no text-size setting.**
  - Between the 430 px iPhone and the 820 px iPad, 160 of 163 shell selectors keep the same size, and so do 173/181 in F260, 131/132 in Prayer, 31/31 in the Larder and 146/146 in the park map. Only display text, plus a few F260 and build-guide controls, grows (GAP-TYPE-1).
  - No `-apple-system-*` text style, no `rem`-based font size and no hub text-size preference exist in the code. F260's Large text zooms its page by 1.15, which still leaves its WEEK label at 10.92 px (GAP-TYPE-2).
- **Each role is set differently in each area.**
  - Titles: 10 areas, 8 treatments, and none is 34 px bold with tight tracking. F260, the Larder and Timer repeat the viewer bar's name as a second title (CONS-TYPE-1).
  - Section headers are set 7 ways, buttons run 13-18 px at weights 400-700, and body text 14.5-22 px (CONS-TYPE-2).
  - Big numerals use four faces, and F260, Prayer and Kid Verse have no tabular figures (CONS-TYPE-3).
- **Kid mode is only partly larger, and serif.**
  - The kid block never re-maps `--fs-xs`, so kickers, tab labels and captions stay 12 px. 52 % of Kid Verse's kid text boxes are 12 px or less.
  - The kid tokens reach 5 of the 8 kid-visible areas. The Larder (0/15 selectors grow) and the park map (0/43) set sizes in literal px (CONS-TYPE-4).
  - Kid display type is serif everywhere except Prayer (CONS-TYPE-5).
- **The TV board (extends P2's UX-HOME-2, not re-filed).** Names, star counts, feed times and bylines are 18 px, and the date is 12 px. On a 55-inch set at 3 m, those look the way 7.9 px and 5.3 px text looks on an iPad at 40 cm (VIS-TYPE-1).
- **Corrections to earlier phases.**
  - The park map's family and meeting labels measure 11.0 px on screen at every zoom, not "about 8.7 px".
  - The build guide's axis labels have a 4.46 px font size; 5.7 px is their glyph height.
  - The park map's pane headings fall back to the generic serif (Times on Apple devices), not Georgia.
  - P3's "about 6 px at the whole-park phone fit" did not reproduce for any label the rig could see, and stays open (Unresolved 1).
- **Re-measure.** 14 key numbers were re-measured with independent code (its summary says 13, but it lists 14 results). 12 agree. 2 disagree:
  - The build guide's iPad count is 107/113, not 107/123.
  - The kid growth counts were undercounts: the investigator's report read only each combination's top 5 selectors.
  Both are corrected below, along with smaller corrections to wording.

### Confirmed defects

The one confirmed defect was adversarially verified: two skeptics re-read the code, wrote their own scripts and re-ran the measurement on the local instance. Its severity follows the Phase 2 rule (`audits/02-shell.md:25-37`) and its design-system clause.

#### P4-TYPE-01 — Build guide map labels render below 11 px at the default whole-park view: section names 6.1 px on the iPhone (5.5 px in Safari), listing numbers 6.8 px on every device, contour heights 9.5 px at every zoom

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low. Not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** a measurable text-size failure (below 11 px) on a secondary surface. The text is map annotation, not the main content or a primary action. The design-system clause makes decorative or secondary failures low.
  - **Why not higher:** the same information is elsewhere. Section names are on the chips above the map, listing numbers are in the Listings tab and the marker pop-ups, and pinch or + zoom brings section names to 15 px.
  - **Exposure:** everyone who opens the build guide sees the whole-park view first. The iPhone is worst (section names 6.14 px in the PWA, 5.51 px in Safari); on the iPad portrait they are 10.23 px. Listing numbers are 6.82 px on all five devices. The build guide is adult-only.
- **Areas:** dollywood (build guide). The park map ships the same code. Its measured screens showed none of these three groups, because the illustrated basemap hides `#seclabels` and `#contour` (`apps/dollywood-live.html:526`); see Unresolved 1.
- **What happens.**
  - **The cause** is the template's `apply()`, which runs after every pan and zoom (`../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:799-802`, exported to `apps/dollywood.html:802-805`). `k` is metres per CSS px (`mpp()`, `template.html:788`), so the map's own drawing scale is 1/k.
  - **Listing markers** are scaled by `ms = k × (k > 0.75 ? 0.62 : k > 0.45 ? 0.8 : 1)` (`template.html:800`). Their 11 px numbers (`[data-flavor=hub] .mk .onum`, `apps/dollywood.html:281`) therefore draw at 11 × 0.62 = 6.82 px. Only at k ≤ 0.45, zoomed far in, do they reach 11 px.
  - **Contour heights** are set to `9.5 × k` user units (`template.html:801`), which draws at a constant 9.5 px at every zoom.
  - **Section names** are set to `15 × min(k, 1.1)` user units (`template.html:802`). Once zoomed in they draw at 15 px. At the whole-park view k is above 1.1, so they draw at 16.5/k px: 6.14 px on the iPhone PWA (CTM 0.3723), 5.51 px in iPhone Safari (0.3341) and 10.23 px on the iPad portrait (0.6199).
  - **In the screenshot,** "WILDWOOD GROVE", "ENTRANCE & PLAZA" and the haloed marker numbers are small, faint text on the whole-park map (`audits/evidence/p4/TYPE/verify-build-guide-svg-labels-under-11-1-iphone-pwa.png`).
  - **Why it went unrecorded:** the rig's type inventory records HTML text only, so none of these labels is in `type.json`. P3 recorded only the cross-section axis labels (VIS-DOLLYWOOD-4).
- **Expected.** House style: never below 11 px. Map labels should keep a constant on-screen size at or above 11 px, as the park map's family labels already do with `${11*k}` (`template.html:1339, 1349`; they measure 11.0 px at every zoom), or be hidden below a zoom threshold instead of shrinking.
- **Why it matters.** On a phone the section names and listing numbers are how the map is read, and at 5.5-6.8 px they cannot be read.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `audits/evidence/p4/TYPE/hidden-text.json`. Build guide map, iPhone PWA: `text.seclab` 6.14 (9 labels), `text.onum` 6.82 (44), `text.clab` 9.5 (22). iPad portrait: 10.23, 6.82, 9.5. Cross-section: `svg#prof > text` 4.46 on the iPhone PWA, 9.1 on the iPad.
  - Skeptics: `verify-build-guide-svg-labels-under-11-1.json` and `-1-iphone-pwa.png`, `verify-build-guide-svg-labels-under-11-2.json` (all in `audits/evidence/p4/TYPE/`).
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-live-guide-svg.json` (text box height against an HTML reference span: 0.93-1.08).
  - Code: `apps/dollywood.html:111, 131, 133, 277, 281, 802-805, 936`; `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:788, 799-802` (read-only).
  - Phase 1 captures: `audits/screens/dollywood/map-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`, `audits/screens/dollywood/cross-section-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `cd "C:/Users/ex_bo/OneDrive/Claude Related/App Hub" && node audits/tools/phase4/TYPE/hidden-text.mjs --only dollywood`. The console shows `map iphone-pwa svg min eff 6.14`. Per-label detail is in `hidden-text.json` `runs[].docs[frame].svg`: `text.seclab` 6.14, `text.onum` 6.82, `text.clab` 9.5.
  - Skeptics: `node audits/tools/phase4/TYPE/verify-build-guide-svg-labels-under-11-1.mjs` (five devices) and `… -2.mjs` (four + taps and a section chip).
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** wrote their own WebKit probe (local instance, typical household, Eli, System light), reusing only the navigation from `audits/tools/areas/dollywood.mjs`. For every visible SVG `<text>` it took the computed font size × √|det(getScreenCTM())|, the glyph box height and the app's own `window.MK` and `window.MS`, on five devices.
    - Section names: 6.14 px on the iPhone PWA, **5.51 on iPhone Safari**, 10.23 on the iPad portrait. They pass on the iPad landscape (14.92) and desktop (13.15).
    - Listing numbers: 6.82 px on all five devices. Contour heights: 9.5 on all five.
    - Axis labels: 4.46 px on both iPhones, glyph box 5.7; 9.1 on the iPad portrait, 13.42 on the iPad landscape, 11.78 on desktop.
    - Zoomed to a section: section names 15 px everywhere; listing numbers 8.8 px on phones and 11 px on the iPad and desktop.
    - Every value matches `apply()`. A grep of `audits/*.md` and `audits/03-apps/*.md` found no earlier record of the map's section, marker or contour labels.
  - **Skeptic 2** re-read the label CSS and `template.html:788, 800-802`, then wrote their own WebKit script (iPhone PWA and iPad portrait, Eli, System light). It measured six states: the default view, each of four + taps, and a section chip.
    - iPhone. Default (MK 2.686): 6.14 / 6.82 / 9.5. After one tap (MK 1.79): section names 9.21. Two taps: 13.82. Three taps: 15. Four taps (MK 0.53): listing numbers 8.8. Section chip (MK 0.59): 15 / 8.8 / 9.5.
    - iPad. Default (MK 1.61): 10.23 / 6.82 / 9.5. One tap: section names 15. Two taps: listing numbers 8.8. Four taps (MK 0.32) and the section chip: listing numbers 11.
    - They confirmed it is not a rig artefact: the size arithmetic does not depend on which face loads.
  - **Re-measure (independent code):** `.seclab` 16.5 × 0.3723 = 6.14 (iPhone) and 16.5 × 0.6199 = 10.23 (iPad); `.onum` 11 × 0.62 = 6.82 on both; `.clab` 9.5 on both; axis 12 × 0.372 = 4.46 (iPhone PWA) and 12 × 0.758 = 9.1 (iPad). Agrees.
- **Corrected claim.** Accurate at the default whole-park view, with four refinements:
  - It is worse in iPhone Safari (430×740): section names are 5.51 px there.
  - "Everywhere" overstates it. Section names reach 15 px once zoomed in: one + tap on the iPad, three on the iPhone. Listing numbers step from 6.82 to 8.8 to 11 px, and reach 11 only at k ≤ 0.45. A section chip on the iPhone still leaves them at 8.8 px.
  - Contour heights are a deliberate constant (9.5 × k): a floor violation by design, not a scaling slip.
  - The axis-label facet (4.46 px) is VIS-DOLLYWOOD-4 and is not re-filed. It adds only a reconciliation: 4.46 px is the font size, and P3's 5.7 px is the glyph box height.
  - The fix belongs in the sibling template's `apply()` (the 0.62 / 0.8 marker factors, the `min(k, 1.1)` cap, the 9.5 base), then a rebuild and export. `apps/dollywood.html` is generated.
- **Related (not re-filed):** VIS-DOLLYWOOD-3 (the toolbar's 10.5 px caps and the off-scale sizes), VIS-DOLLYWOOD-4 (the axis labels).

### Consistency, visual and gap findings

These items were not adversarially verified. The evidence is the investigator's code scan and rendered inventory, spot-checked by the section writer against the cited lines and the raw JSON, with the re-measure's corrections applied. Severities are the investigator's ratings.

#### GAP-TYPE-1 — No iPad type tier: body, secondary, button and tab text is the same size on the 820 px iPad as on the 430 px iPhone, in every area (investigator rating: medium)

- **What happens.**
  - Of the selectors seen on both devices, the same size on both: shell 160/163, F260 173/181, Prayer 131/132, Larder 31/31, park map 146/146, Verses 51/53, Kid Verse 55/57, Tally 8/10, Timer 10/12, build guide 107/113. Table TYPE-4 lists what grows.
  - What grows is display text, apart from a few controls:
    - display: the hero 30.1→44, the gate title 34→46, F260 titles 23-26→26-30, verse refs 38.7→56, Prayer's pray-mode line 30→42.6, the Tally count 111.8→162, the Timer digits 76.5→87.8;
    - controls: F260's journal-bar buttons 11→12 and labels 11.5→13, and the build guide's toolbar buttons 12.5→14 and 13→15. The build guide's zoom buttons shrink 20→15.
  - No design.css media query changes a type token. The only other width change is the shell's tab labels, 12→16 px in the ≥ 1024 px sidebar (`apps/design.css:573`).
- **Expected (house style).** Base on Dynamic Type and scale up for across-the-room reading on the iPad, the primary, always-on device. Body, secondary text and controls should step up at regular width, the way the kid and kiosk blocks already re-map the `--fs` tokens.
- **Why it matters.** The iPad is read from 2-3 m, yet reminders, Larder meta, prayer rows and captions stay at 12-16 px.
- **Evidence:** `roles.json` (`areas.*.scale`); `remeasure-raw.json`; `apps/design.css:22-24, 573`; `audits/screens/shell/home-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png` against `audits/screens/shell/home-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TYPE/report.mjs ipad`.
- **Related (not re-filed):** UX-HOME-1 (P2, investigator only). It measured the iPad Home's key numbers at 2.3-3.1 mm and noted that "there is no iPad or ambient type scale" (`audits/02-shell.md:546-549`). This item is the cross-area measurement: the same holds in every app.

#### GAP-TYPE-2 — No text-size preference and no Dynamic Type hook; F260's page zoom is the only control, and it leaves its 9.5 px label at 10.92 px (investigator rating: medium)

- **What happens.**
  - Every size is a px literal or a px token, and `html` sets `text-size-adjust: 100%` (`apps/design.css:293`).
  - NOT FOUND IN CODE, in `index.html`, `apps/*.html`, `apps/design.css` and the template: `font: -apple-system-body` or any `-apple-system-*` text style, `rem`-based font sizes (F260 and Prayer use `rem` only for max-widths, `apps/f260.html:44`, `apps/prayer.html:50`), or a hub text-size preference. As far as the code shows, iOS Larger Text never reaches the hub; this was not tested on a device.
  - F260 alone offers Large text, as `body.big { zoom: 1.15 }` (`apps/f260.html:50, 2034`; person scope `f260.big`). It zooms the layout as well as the text:
    - 17 → 19.6 px and 25 → 28.8 px;
    - the WEEK ring label 9.5 → 10.92 px, still under 11 (the re-measure read it from the rendered box: 28.11 × 9.5 → 32.33 × 10.92, a ratio of 1.150);
    - on the iPhone it wraps the meta line (VIS-F260-10), and it stops at the F260 frame.
- **Expected.** Grandparents are in the audience, and nothing important may hide behind small type. A person-scope text-size preference, like the theme, should scale the type hub-wide, and ideally follow the OS setting.
- **Why it matters.** A grandparent who needs larger text cannot get it outside F260, and inside F260 some text is still below the floor.
- **Evidence:** `apps/design.css:293`; `apps/f260.html:50, 2034`; `hidden-text.json` (f260 large-text: body zoom 1.15, smallest `span#todayRing > span.rn > small` at 10.92); `remeasure-live-f260-zoom.json`; `code-scan.json` (px or `--fs` tokens only, no `rem`).
- **Reproduction:** `grep -rn "apple-system-body\|-apple-system-headline\|font: *-apple" index.html apps/*.html apps/design.css` (no output); `node audits/tools/phase4/TYPE/hidden-text.mjs --only f260`.
- **Related (not re-filed):** VIS-F260-10 (the wrap). No earlier phase recorded the missing hub-wide setting (a grep of `audits/*.md` for "Larger Text", "text size" and "apple-system-body" finds nothing).

#### VIS-TYPE-1 — TV board: the kiosk block uses its phone-sized steps for information text; names, star counts, times and bylines are 18 px and the date 12 px (investigator rating: medium; extends P2's UX-HOME-2, not re-filed)

- **Owner.** Phase 2 already recorded the defect: UX-HOME-2 ("On the TV the board's news is its smallest text", medium, investigator only; `audits/02-shell.md:556-558`) and the VIS note "TV text is below 10-foot sizes" (`:5973-5977`). This item adds measurements and the token-level cause. It is not a second defect.
- **New facts.**
  - Re-measured live in System and Midnight, as eight size tiers (Table TYPE-6). Only the clock, verse refs and greeting are 10-foot sizes.
  - As iPad equivalents at 3 m on a 55-inch set: 18 px reads like 7.9 px on an iPad at 40 cm (9.35 px on a 65-inch), the 26 px feed lines like 11.4 px, the 22 px reminders like 9.7 px, and the 12 px date like 5.3 px.
  - The cause is the kiosk block (`apps/design.css:286-289`). It sets `--fs-sm` to 18, which the board uses for its information text (`index.html:153, 163`), and it does not re-map `--fs-xs` at all (`apps/design.css:417`). On a kiosk viewport 1050 px tall or less, the feed lines shrink further, to 22 px (`index.html:175`).
  - P2's own glance heuristic found that on a 65-inch set everything except the date reaches its bare-threshold test (H2), while on a 55-inch set the date and the 18 px text fail it (`audits/02-shell.md:543, 557`). The severity therefore depends on the set, which is not known (Not verified).
- **Expected (house style).** The kiosk is a 10-foot UI. Its smallest information text should subtend at least what the iPad floor does at arm's length, about 28-32 px at 1080p, and the date and names should never use the 12 and 18 px steps.
- **Why it matters.** The kids look for their stars and the parents look for who prayed, from across the room.
- **Evidence:** `remeasure-live-tv-board.json`; `remeasure-tvmath.json`; `report.mjs tv`; `audits/screens/tv/board-typical-tv-light.png`; `index.html:142-163, 175`; `apps/design.css:286-289, 417`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TYPE/report.mjs tv`.
- **Related:** UX-HOME-2 (owner), P2-VIS-02 (the board's overflow; must be solved by layout, not by smaller type).

#### CONS-TYPE-1 — Ten areas, eight large-title treatments, none 34 bold with tight tracking; three apps repeat the viewer bar's title (investigator rating: low)

- **Titles by area** (iPad portrait, re-measured live):
  - shell: view h1 36/400 ui-serif, tracking normal; Home hero 44/400 serif;
  - F260: h1 30/700 rounded, −0.9 px;
  - Larder: h1 28/700 ui-serif, −0.28 px;
  - Prayer: h1 31/600 Manrope, −0.99 px;
  - Timer: h1 18/600 ui-serif, +0.18 px;
  - build guide: h1 28/400 ui-serif, tracking normal (42 on desktop);
  - no title: Tally (a 12 px caps pill), Kid Verse and Verses (a 56 px serif reference), the park map (a 15.5/700 pill).
- **Tracking.** The shell and the Dollywood pair explicitly reset serif titles to 0 (`apps/design.css:331-332, 418`; `apps/dollywood.html:223`).
- **The viewer bar.** Every app sits under the shell's 14/600 viewer-bar title (`index.html:335, 409`). F260 ("F260 Reading Plan"), the Larder ("The Larder Ledger") and Timer ("Kitchen timer") repeat that name as a second title. The build guide's and Prayer's titles are different text.
- **Expected.** One large-title role (system-ui 34/700, about −0.02em; smaller inline on the phone) used by every app that needs a title, and no second copy of the viewer-bar name.
- **Why it matters.** The one element that should identify a screen changes face, weight and size in every app, so moving between apps feels like moving between websites.
- **Evidence:** `audits/evidence/p4/TYPE/titles-ipad-portrait.png` (ten areas cropped from the Phase 1 captures); `remeasure-live-titles.json`; `report.mjs titles`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TYPE/report.mjs titles && node audits/tools/phase4/TYPE/montage.mjs`.
- **Related (not re-filed):** P2 VIS "Rounded body and serif titles" (`audits/02-shell.md:5764-5770`), VIS-TIMER-2 (Timer's repeated title), VIS-VERSES-5, VIS-DOLLYWOOD-3.

#### CONS-TYPE-2 — The same role is set differently in every area: section headers seven ways, buttons 13-18 px at weights 400-700, body 14.5-22 px (investigator rating: low)

- **Section headers:** shell 18/700; F260 15/700; Larder 13/700 caps; Prayer 19/600; Verses and Kid Verse 18/700; build guide 16/400 serif; park map 15/600 generic serif.
- **Buttons:** shell 16/600 (large 18/600); F260 15.5/600; Prayer 16.5/600; Larder 16/600, with Copy at 14/400; Timer and Verses 18/600; park map 13-15/700; build-guide toolbar 15/400. iOS uses 17 semibold.
- **Body:** shell 16, F260 17, Prayer 17-17.5, Verses 16, Larder lede 14 serif, build guide 13-14.5, park map 12.5-15.
- **Captions and kickers:** captions 11-12.5 px at weights 400-600; kickers 12 px at 400 (mono), 700 or 800, tracked .05-.08em.
- **Expected.** One role table used by every app through tokens: Headline 17/600, Body 17/400, Callout 16, Subheadline 15, Footnote 13, Caption 12/11, button 17/600.
- **Why it matters.** Hierarchy has to be relearned in each app, and a heading of the same kind means something different in each.
- **Evidence:** Table TYPE-2; `roles.json` (combos per area); `apps/design.css:306-309, 333, 354, 366`; `apps/f260.html:55-125`; `code-scan.json` (Prayer: 64 px literals).
- **Related (not re-filed):** P2 "The type scale sits 1-2 px off Dynamic Type" (`audits/02-shell.md:5771`), VIS-F260-8, VIS-DOLLYWOOD-3.

#### CONS-TYPE-3 — Big numerals in four faces; tabular figures missing in F260, Prayer and Kid Verse (investigator rating: low)

- **Four faces** (Table TYPE-7):
  - ui-rounded 300: the Timer;
  - ui-rounded 700-900: the TV clock, the Verses stats and the shell's star counts;
  - ui-serif 400 or 700: the Tally count, the Kid Verse star count and balance, the build-guide stats;
  - Manrope 700: Prayer's counts.
- **Tabular figures.** `font-variant-numeric` appears 0 times in `f260.html`, `prayer.html` and `kidverse.html`, so their counts use proportional figures. So does the shell's kid Home star count (`.star-big`, `index.html:197`). The Dollywood template has the opposite problem: it applies tabular figures to all text, prose included (`apps/dollywood.html:14-15`).
- **Expected (house style).** ui-rounded for big numerals (timer, tally, progress counts), tabular, in every app.
- **Why it matters.** Counts are the most glanced-at text in the hub, and one numeral face would tie the apps together.
- **Evidence:** `report.mjs numerals`; `code-scan.json`; `apps/tally.html:58`; `apps/kidverse.html:62, 78`; `apps/timer.html:32`.
- **Related (not re-filed):** VIS-TALLY-3, VIS-KIDVERSE-7, VIS-DOLLYWOOD-3.

#### CONS-TYPE-4 — The kid type scale reaches five of the eight kid-visible areas, and `--fs-xs` never scales, so kickers, tab labels and captions stay 12 px for kids (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens.**
  - Shared selectors that grow in kid mode (the re-measure's full sets): shell 36/42, Tally 4/5, Timer 4/5 (not the digits), Verses 12/13, Kid Verse 10/16.
  - None grow in the Larder (0/15) or the park map (0/43), because both set sizes in literal px. Prayer builds its own kid layout (2/4 shared selectors grow; its kid minimum is 14 px).
  - Share of kid text boxes at 12 px or less: Kid Verse 52.1 %, park map 44.4 %, Larder 29.4 %, shell 27.1 %, Tally 20.0 %, Verses 10.6 %, Prayer 0 %, Timer 0 %.
  - The cause: the kid block (`apps/design.css:280-284`) re-maps `--fs-sm` through `--fs-4xl` but not `--fs-xs`. Kickers, bylines, badge names and tab labels therefore stay 12 px (for example `span#kick.kicker`, `div.rem-by`, `div#who.who.kicker`).
- **Expected.** CLAUDE.md: kid mode has "bigger targets and type". Every kid-visible surface should follow the kid tokens, the caption step included.
- **Why it matters.** Kid mode is meant to be one consistent, larger world. In two apps it is simply the adult page.
- **Evidence:** `report.mjs kid`; `remeasure-raw.json`; `remeasure-live-scale.json` (Larder kid and adult on the iPad: 0/12 grow; Tally 4/5: count 162→168, minus 36→44, plus 48→60, reset 16→19); `audits/screens/kidverse/kid-rewards-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`; `audits/screens/dollywood-live/kid-typical-ipad-portrait-dark.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TYPE/report.mjs kid` prints the kid shares and minimums. Its grow counts are low, because it reads each combination's top 5 selectors. The full counts are in `remeasure-raw.json` (`areas.*.kid`).
- **Related (not re-filed):** UX-LEFTOVERS-2 (the Larder's adult-size type for kids), VIS-KIDVERSE-7, VIS-TALLY-8.

#### CONS-TYPE-5 — Kid display type is serif in every kid-visible area except Prayer (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens.** The largest kid text is ui-serif, which is New York on Apple devices:
  - shell: view title and hero 44/400 (30.1 on the iPhone);
  - Kid Verse: verse reference 64/400, star count 44/700, balance 44/400, story title 34/400;
  - Verses: reference 64/400, "All done" 44/700;
  - Tally: count 168/400; Larder: h1 28/700; Timer: h1 22/600; park map: card title 26/400.
  - Only Prayer (Manrope) avoids a serif. Body text is rounded only because `--font-sans` starts with ui-rounded for everyone (`apps/design.css:18`).
- **Expected (house style).** ui-rounded throughout kid mode, numerals included.
- **Why it matters.** The pre-reader's big type (their stars, their verse) is exactly where the friendly rounded face matters most.
- **Evidence:** `report.mjs kid` (the serif display list); `apps/design.css:19-20`; `apps/kidverse.html:36, 62, 78`; `apps/tally.html:58`.
- **Related (not re-filed):** VIS-TALLY-3, VIS-KIDVERSE-7.

#### GAP-TYPE-3 — The system has no 11 px floor and nothing checks for one: 10 components in 4 areas go below (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens.**
  - Table TYPE-5 lists the components: the compass N in both exports, the park map's MIN, F260's WEEK, Kid Verse's day letters and badge dates, the build guide's toolbar captions, and its four groups of SVG labels.
  - The only lint in the repo checks colour: `scripts/screens-apps.mjs` fails on a hex (CLAUDE.md, Tests), and nothing fails on a size.
  - The one component that looked below the floor and is not, the park map's family labels, uses the right pattern. It sizes text as `11 × k` user units, so it draws at 11.0 px at every zoom.
- **Expected (house style).** Never below 11 px, enforced the way the no-hex rule is.
- **Why it matters.** Sub-floor text keeps reappearing, app by app, because nothing in the system forbids it.
- **Evidence:** `report.mjs under11`; `report.mjs tokens` (line numbers of sizes under 11); `hidden-text.json`; `remeasure-code.json` (`under11` per file).
- **Related:** P4-TYPE-01; VIS-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-8, VIS-KIDVERSE-1, VIS-KIDVERSE-7, VIS-DOLLYWOOD-3, VIS-DOLLYWOOD-4. P3's calibration note records that only the build guide deducted for sub-11 text (`audits/03-apps.md:437`).

#### CONS-TYPE-6 — The park map's pane headings fall back to the generic serif (Times on Apple devices), and the Dollywood badges and marker numbers to generic sans, because the template names faces it never loads (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens.**
  - **The pane headings.** The hub flavour remaps `.tabbody h2` to `--font-display` (`apps/dollywood.html:223`). The live flavour remaps only `.pop h2` (`apps/dollywood-live.html:223`). Its own `.tabbody h2` rule changes the size to 15 px and nothing else (`:450`), so the park map's "Official listings" and "Layers" headings keep `Fraunces,serif` (`:59`).
  - **What renders.** 192 text boxes, all Fraunces → generic serif, 15/600 (153 in `#tab-list`, 39 in `#tab-layers`). The build guide's identical component is ui-serif 16/400.
  - **The badges and marker numbers.** The pop-up badge (`.pop .badge`, `:117`) and the marker numbers (`.onum`, `:131`) declare `Archivo,sans-serif` in both exports. The hub and live rules for `.mk .onum` (`apps/dollywood.html:281`, `apps/dollywood-live.html:544`) set size and weight but not the family, so they resolve to generic sans (Helvetica on iOS).
- **Expected.** Every family is a design.css token, and the template's standalone faces (Fraunces, Archivo) never reach the hub exports.
- **Why it matters.** One export shows Times headings next to SF Pro Rounded, and the two exports of one template disagree.
- **Evidence:** `apps/dollywood-live.html:59, 117, 131, 222-223, 450, 544`; `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:59, 117, 223` (read-only); `raw/devices/dollywood-live/search-typical-iphone-pwa-light-system.json` (`div#tab-list.tabbody > h2`: ff Fraunces, resolved serif); `remeasure-live-fraunces.json`; `audits/screens/dollywood-live/search-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `sed -n 59p apps/dollywood-live.html; sed -n 450p apps/dollywood-live.html | cut -c1-80; sed -n 223p apps/dollywood-live.html | cut -c1-240`.
- **Correction to P3.** P3 wrote "Fraunces falls back to Georgia" (`audits/03-apps/dollywood-live.md:729`). No stack that reaches these headings names Georgia; only `h1` and `.seclab` do (`:19, 111`). The re-measure's canvas test agrees: `600 15px Fraunces, serif` measured 303.04 px wide, the same as the generic serif and Times New Roman, and not Georgia (363.6).
- **Related (not re-filed):** VIS-DOLLYWOOD-3.

#### CONS-TYPE-7 — Five of nine apps size text in literal px and bypass the tokens: F260 122, the Dollywood template 149, Prayer 64, the Larder 16, against a fully tokenised shell (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens.**
  - Declared sizes, token against literal: design.css 29/0 and `index.html` 51/0 (bare px; six `clamp()` declarations carry px bounds). Verses 15/1, Kid Verse 27/4; Tally and Timer use tokens plus a clamp.
  - Literal-only: F260 0/122 (25 distinct), Prayer 5/64 (22 distinct), the Larder 0/16, the build guide and park map 0/149 each (23 distinct, plus 3 JS `fontSize` assignments).
  - At runtime, distinct adult sizes: shell 9 (100 % of text boxes on a token value), F260 26 (9 fractional), Prayer 25 (10 fractional), park map 18, build guide 17 (Table TYPE-3).
- **Expected.** CLAUDE.md already makes every colour a design.css token. Sizes need the same rule, or no kid, kiosk, iPad or text-size scale can reach these apps.
- **Why it matters.** Every hub-wide type change (kid mode, an iPad tier, larger text) silently skips F260, Prayer, the Larder and both Dollywood exports. Table TYPE-4 shows it already happens for kids in the Larder and the park map.
- **Evidence:** `code-scan.json`; `remeasure-code.json`; `report.mjs scale`, `report.mjs tokens`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TYPE/code-scan.mjs && node audits/tools/phase4/TYPE/report.mjs scale`.
- **Related:** P3's park-map compliance row (143 `font-size` literals, `audits/03-apps/dollywood-live.md:817`).

#### VIS-TYPE-2 — The Dollywood template tells labels from values by ink alone (dt and dd both 13/400; profile stats 12.5/700), and the difference shrinks to 1.62:1 in Midnight (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens.**
  - Sibling texts with the same family, size, weight and transform differ only in ink: 14 pairs in the build guide and 1 in the park map (Table TYPE-8).
  - The clearest is the key/value list: `dl.kv dt` and `dd` are both 13/400 ui-rounded, with ink `--dim` against `--text`. That is 2.75:1 apart in System light and **1.62:1 in Midnight**, a new measurement.
  - The shell, TV, Larder, Tally, Timer, Verses and Kid Verse have no such pairs.
- **Expected (house style).** Hierarchy through weight and size, not colour alone: label at Footnote 13/400 in the secondary ink, value at Subheadline or Body 15-17/600.
- **Why it matters.** Low-vision readers, and anyone in bright park sunlight, lose a distinction carried only by grey levels. In dark palettes it nearly disappears.
- **Evidence:** `colour-only.json`; `remeasure-live-kv.json`; `audits/screens/dollywood/cross-section-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TYPE/colour-only.mjs`.

### What works

- **OK-TYPE-1 — The shell's type is tokenised, with a 12 px floor and no colour-only hierarchy.**
  - `index.html` has 51 token font sizes and no bare px; six `clamp()` sizes carry px bounds (`:97, 100, 102, 142, 145, 175`).
  - Nine distinct adult sizes cover 100 % of the shell's text boxes, and the minimum is 12 px everywhere, kid mode and the TV included.
  - Six `tabular-nums` declarations cover the two clocks, the feed times, the kid chips' star counts and both timer pills (`index.html:100, 142, 196, 206, 350, 360`); only the kid Home's big star count is proportional.
  - No sibling texts differ by colour alone.
  - Verses (99 % on token values) and Timer (90 %) are almost as clean, which shows the token route works for apps.
  - Evidence: `code-scan.json`, `remeasure-code.json`, `report.mjs scale`, `colour-only.json`.
- **OK-TYPE-2 — The Timer and TV clock numerals, and Prayer's kid layout, are the best type in the hub.**
  - The Timer's digits are 87.8 px ui-rounded 300, tabular, −0.02em (`apps/timer.html:32`), and the TV clock is 172.8/700, tabular, −0.02em (`index.html:142`). Both look like the iOS Clock app.
  - Prayer's kid list sets titles at 34/600, the Prayed button at 22/700 and bylines at 19/500, with a 14 px minimum and no kid text at 12 px or less. It is the only kid surface sized for a child at arm's length.
  - Evidence: `report.mjs numerals`, `report.mjs kid`; `audits/screens/timer/running-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`; `audits/screens/prayer/kid-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png`.
- **OK-TYPE-3 — The park map's family and meeting labels hold 11.0 px at every zoom.** They are sized as `11 × k` user units (`template.html:1339, 1349`), so their on-screen size is constant:
  - iPhone: 16.64 units × CTM 0.661;
  - iPad: 8.72 × 1.261;
  - desktop: 7.53 × 1.461;
  - whole-park iPhone: 34.0 × 0.3235.
  An 11 px HTML reference span in the same face matches their width to 0.01 px (`remeasure-live-park-labels.json`, `remeasure-live-park-phone-fit.json`). This is the pattern P4-TYPE-01's labels should follow.
- **OK-TYPE-4 — F260 is the only app with a text-size control, and it follows the person** (`f260.big`, person scope; `apps/f260.html:2034`; `audits/00-inventory.md:3280`). GAP-TYPE-2 covers its limits.

### Checked and not a bug

No filed finding was refuted: the one confirmed defect survived both skeptics. The claims below were checked and corrected or dropped.

- **"Build guide, iPad vs iPhone: 107/123 the same."** A transcription error. The raw data gives 107/113 (4 larger, 2 smaller), and the investigator's own `roles.json` gives the same 113 (re-measure).
- **"Only display text grows on the iPad."** Not quite:
  - In F260 the journal-bar buttons (11→12), labels (11.5→13) and a stat (15→22) also grow.
  - In the build guide the toolbar buttons (12.5→14, 13→15), the step h3 (20→22) and the readout (12→12.5) grow, and the zoom buttons shrink (20→15).
  - The conclusion stands: body, secondary and caption text stays phone-sized (`report.mjs ipad`; `remeasure-raw.json`).
- **"Kid growth: shell 19/25, Verses 11/12, Kid Verse 9/15, park map 0/41".** Undercounts. `report.mjs kid` reads `combos[].sels`, which `roles.mjs` cuts to each combination's top 5 selectors. The full sets are 36/42, 12/13, 10/16 and 0/43, plus Prayer 2/4. The Larder, Tally and Timer matched. The conclusion holds: the kid tokens reach the shell, Tally, Timer, Verses and Kid Verse, but not the Larder or the park map.
- **"The shell is 100 % on tokens with 0 literals."** True only for bare px. Six `clamp()` sizes in `index.html` have literal px bounds (`:97, 100, 102, 142, 145, 175`), and the re-measure counts 51 token declarations, not 50: it counts `:145` as a token.
- **"The TV pane titles are 26/700."** The Reminders pane title is 22/700 (`remeasure-live-tv-board.json`).
- **"18 px on a 65-inch TV is 9.4 px on an iPad."** 9.35: the draft's script rounded the pixel pitch to 0.75 mm.
- **"Kid Verse's kid minimum is 12 px."** It is 10 px: the kid badge dates and hints (`apps/kidverse.html:86`; `report.mjs kid`, min 10).
- **"Every shell widget number is tabular."** The kid Home's big star count (`.star-big`, `index.html:197`) is proportional (`report.mjs numerals`: `normal`).
- **"The compass N is 9 px on every device" (build guide).** The rig saw the build guide's N on the iPad and desktop only; the park map's N on all four devices.
- **P3: "the park map's family labels are about 8.7 px"** (`audits/03-apps/dollywood-live.md:92, 729, 772`). 8.72 is the size in SVG user units. On screen they are 11.0 px at every zoom (OK-TYPE-3; re-measure agrees to 0.05 px).
- **P3: "profile axis labels render at 5.7 px on the phone"** (VIS-DOLLYWOOD-4). The font size is 4.46 px. 5.7 px is the glyph box height (both P4-TYPE-01 skeptics; re-measure).
- **P3: "Fraunces falls back to Georgia"** (`audits/03-apps/dollywood-live.md:729`). It falls back to the generic serif; see CONS-TYPE-6.
- **P3: "143 px literals" in the park map.** 143 `font-size` declarations; 149 counting the `font:` shorthand. A difference of definition, not an error.

### Unresolved

No filed finding is unresolved. These questions would refine or extend the findings.

The re-measure called this wrong because the family and meeting labels measure 11.0 px there. ### Method, scripts and evidence

**Investigator scripts** (`audits/tools/phase4/TYPE/`; evidence in `audits/evidence/p4/TYPE/`):

| Script | What it measures | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `code-scan.mjs` | Every font-size, `font:`, family, weight, tracking, numeric and transform declaration per file; token against literal; literal sizes under 11 px with line numbers. The Dollywood pair was also scanned through `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html` (read-only; identical counts) | `code-scan.json` |
| `roles.mjs [--out DIR]` | From the rig-v2 raw files: per area and profile kind, every combination of family, size, weight, line height, tracking, transform and numeric with devices and selectors; per-selector sizes by device; everything under 11 px; numerals and titles ≥ 24 px. Only the area's own document (the page for the shell and TV, the frame for apps) | `roles.json` (294 KB) |
| `report.mjs [ipad\|kid\|titles\|numerals\|under11\|scale\|tv\|tokens]` | Prints the cross-area tables from `roles.json` and `code-scan.json` | stdout |
| `colour-only.mjs` | Sibling texts with the same family, size, weight and transform whose inks differ by 1.5:1 or more | `colour-only.json` |

## Spacing, layout, radius and shadow (SHAPE)

Baseline: the working tree at fe6041d (no app file has changed since). Scope: the shell (`index.html` and `apps/design.css`, the TV board included) and the nine apps. Every number comes from one of four sources:
- the rig-v2 raw files (`audits/evidence/p4/measure/raw/`, 3,662 jobs), re-aggregated per area's own document by `analyze.mjs`;
- the investigator's targeted runs (`cards.mjs`, `crops.mjs`, `verify.mjs`);
- the skeptics' scripts, one pair per bug;
- the independent re-measure (`remeasure.mjs`).

All runs were on the local instance, in WebKit on Windows. No request went to production, and no PIN or pairing code was read or used. Box sizes, radii, paddings and shadows are computed CSS values and do not depend on the fallback fonts. The rig does not paint backdrop blur, so glass depth is judged here by shadow layers and fill only.

**Summary**

- **Four defects confirmed, each 2/2 and low. Three are tap targets; the fourth, added after the completeness critic, is the shared toast's width.**
  - **P4-SHAPE-01, kid mode.** Kid mode keeps adult-sized controls wherever a control is sized in fixed px. The kid `--tap` of 64 reaches only rules that read `var(--tap)`.
    - The Larder has 7 selectors at 44-52 px, identical for Ezra and for an adult.
    - The park map has every default-view control under 64, and 4 controls plus an inline link under 44.
    - The shell's sidebar tab is a fixed 48 px, so it measures 195×48 for kids on the iPad landscape and desktop (new; P2 measured only the 56 px bottom bar).
  - **P4-SHAPE-02, Prayer.** The toast action is 36×22 with `padding:0`. It carries Undo after "Mark answered" and "Open it" after an add, for 6 s.
  - **P4-SHAPE-03, park map.** About five control rules under 44 px beyond the five that VIS-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-5 recorded: the sheet handle (22), About the data (29), the layer-toggle rows (29), the kids' height stepper (40×40) and the directions-bar buttons (40). The investigator's "18 selectors" counts element boxes. By real hit area on a touch device the count is 13 selectors.
  - **P4-SHAPE-04, shared toast (added after the completeness critic).** `hub.toast` centres with `left: 50%`, so it is capped at half the viewport: 215 px on the iPhone, where ordinary shell, Kid Verse and Verses messages wrap to two or three lines.
- **The system splits in two along `.ds`.**
  - The areas built on `.ds` and the tokens hold the system: shell, TV, Tally, Timer, Kid Verse, Verses. They are 98-100 % on the 4 px grid for macro spacing (97-100 % on the re-measure's single screens), their large radii are on the scale (the shell 87.5 %, the TV kiosk 63.6 % because of its icon corners), and no adult target is under 44 except the shell's album ×.
  - The areas with their own component CSS (F260, Prayer, the Larder, the Dollywood pair) are 34-84 % on the grid. Prayer and the Dollywood pair also draw half their large radii as literals (Table SHAPE-1).
- **The same role is drawn differently in every area.**
  - The content card: six radii (12-36), five paddings, three border widths and three elevations (CONS-SHAPE-1).
  - The main action button: six corner shapes, 44-60 px tall (CONS-SHAPE-4).
  - Sheets: four radii, plus 18 on the Dollywood popover, and three elevations (CONS-SHAPE-5).
  - Content columns: nine widths, and only two apps use a layout token (CONS-SHAPE-2).
- **Concentric corners are impossible by construction.**
  - `.card` is R22 with a 21 px inset, and `.btn` is r16. Concentric would need r1, so every button in a card is 15 px off.
  - The rig's 55 of 95 off-concentric pairs is a floor. The re-measure found pairs the rig cannot see: pills are skipped, and the top-left radius stands in for all four corners. That makes at least 58 of 99, before counting pill containers (VIS-SHAPE-1).
- **The iPad keeps the phone's margins.**
  - The shell and the build guide sit 16 px from the edge of an 820 px iPad.
  - On the iPad landscape, opening an app moves the content edge from 252 px (in the shell) to anywhere from 22 px (F260) to 410 px (Tally).
  - F260's coloured week stripes paint 7 px from the iPhone edge (new; VIS-SHAPE-2).
- **Elevation.**
  - Consistent: toasts are `--e3`, and sheets and modals `--e4`. The one exception is the park map's popover, which is `--e3` (the build guide's is `--e4`).
  - Not consistent: cards and buttons use none, `--e1` or `--e2` depending on the app, and two bottom bars use literal upward shadows. There are no role tokens (GAP-SHAPE-1).
- **Re-measure.** 17 key numbers were re-measured with independent code, and 16 agree. The concentric totals disagree, because of the two blind spots in the rig's check. This section corrects them, along with four smaller points: the popover elevation, "want 1" not "want 2", F260's stripe margin, and the Prayer Rename size.
- **Evidence hygiene.** `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/verify-kid-targets-own-css-2-dollywood-live.png` is 1.47 MB, above the 1 MB evidence limit. This section does not cite it; at assembly it was kept on disk and listed in `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/.gitignore`.

#### Table SHAPE-9 · Concentric corners

The rig's rule: want = R − inset, and a pair violates when |r − want| > max(3 px, 25 % of R) (`audits/tools/phase4/measure/page-lib.mjs:477-492`). The re-measure scanned every corner on the main screens with the same rule, but it includes pills and uses each corner's own radius.

| Area | Rig: distinct pairs / off | Re-measure (main screen): pairs / off | Worst examples (R / inset / r → want) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shell | 42 / 25 | Home 13 / 11; Me 18 / 11 | Me `.card.glass` R22 / 21 / `#syncnow` r16 → 1 (off 15); Home `.gcard` R22 / 21 / `.btn-soft` r16 → 1; admin `.list` R22 / 17 / `.btn-ghost` r16 → 5; kid Reminders card R28 / 21 / `.list` r28 → 7. Same values in System and Midnight |
| TV (kiosk) | 14 / 3 | 8 / 1 | kiosk Me card R22 / 21 / r16 → 1 |
| F260 | 0 / 0 (rig blind: pills skipped) | **4 / 1** | Today card R22 / 19.5 (dx 19.5, dy 17.5) / Done capsule r30 → 2.5 |
| Larder | 4 / 4 | 5 / 4 | add bar `form#add` R16 / 13 / `#name`, `#size`, `#date`, Log r12 → 3 (off 9) |
| Prayer | 1 / 1 | 2 / 0 | sheet R26 / 23 / `.ask` r16 → 3 (possibly judged at a square corner; Unresolved 2) |
| Tally | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | circles only: not a meaningful pass (pills skipped) |
| Timer | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | circles and pills only: as Tally |
| Build guide | 19 / 11 | 5 / 3 | build card R20 / 15 / `#b-menu` r12 → 5; toolbar R16 / 11 / `#bmap` r12 → 5; map box R20 / 11 / readout r16 → 9 |
| Park map | 8 / 5 | 6 / 2 | **sheet R24 / 23 / tabs r14 → 1 (off 13), which the rig passed**; meeting bar R16 / 13 / field r10 → 3; route card R18 / 18 / glyph r12 → 0; amenity button R12 / 11 / icon r8 → 1 |
| Kid Verse | 3 / 2 | 6 / 5 | story card R28 / 21 / `#story-say` r28 → 7 (off 21); story art R28 / 28 / r22 → 0; who-pill R23 / 21 / avatar r14 → 2 |
| Verses | 4 / 4 | 1 / 1 (iPad); 2 / 2 (iPhone, after Show) | trainer R36 / 25 / buttons r28 → 11; kid R44 / 38 / Got it r36 → 6; who-pill R23 / 21 / avatar r14 → 2 |
| **All** | **95 / 55** | — | **at least 58 of 99** (see below) |

The per-pair geometry agrees wherever both methods saw the same pair. The totals do not, because the rig's check has two blind spots:
1. **Pills.** It skips pill children (`if (A && !pill)`) and pill containers (`R < min(w,h)/2 − 1`) (`page-lib.mjs:478-480`). F260's "0 of 0" is therefore wrong: the Done capsule sits inside the Today card's corner curve. Tally and Timer at 0 of 0 are the same blind spot, and so are the who-pill and avatar pairs in Kid Verse and Verses.
2. **Corners.** It reads `borderTopLeftRadius` for the container and applies it to whichever corner is nearest (`page-lib.mjs:472-481`). A sheet rounded only at the top (the park map's `24 24 0 0`) is judged at its square bottom corners. The re-measure measured the park map's sheet/tab pairs at the real top corner: R24 / 23 / r14, want 1, off 13.

Adding F260's four pairs (one off) and the park map's two corrected pairs gives at least 58 off out of 99. That is before the pill-container pairs, which neither total includes.

### Confirmed defects

All four were adversarially verified (P4-SHAPE-04 was added after the completeness critic). For each, two skeptics re-read the code, wrote their own scripts and re-ran the measurement on the local instance. Severity follows the Phase 2 rule (`audits/02-shell.md:25-37`) and its design-system clause. All four are low, rated low by both skeptics, with none raised or lowered. P4-SHAPE-01 to -03 are ordered by reach; P4-SHAPE-04 follows them.

#### P4-SHAPE-01 — Kid mode keeps adult-sized controls wherever a control is sized in fixed px: the Larder (7 selectors at 44-52 px), the park map (every default-view control under 64, four under 44) and the shell's sidebar tab (195×48 on the iPad landscape and desktop)

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** a measurable target-size shortfall against the kid-mode goal, where every control still clears the 44 px house minimum except the park-map items, and those are already filed for everyone (VIS-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-5). That makes it cosmetic or an edge case, not a broken core flow. It matches P2 PROF's low rating for the same class of defect in the shell.
  - **Not counted here:** a kid's tap on the Larder ✓ removes a family item for everyone. That data risk is owned by P3-LEFTOVERS-13 (critical); the small target does not raise this finding.
  - **Exposure:** Ezra and Kiara, on the apps they can see (CLAUDE.md lists the Larder and the park map for kids). The sidebar tab applies at 1024 px and wider: the iPad landscape and desktop.
- **Areas:** leftovers, dollywood-live, shell.
- **What happens.**
  - **The cause.** For kids, design.css sets `--tap: 64px; --tap-lg: 84px` (`apps/design.css:281`, under the comment "Kids: bigger targets", `:279`). Only rules that read `var(--tap)`, or that carry their own kid rule, change. Anything sized in literal px keeps the adult size.
  - **The Larder** sizes its controls in px: `#name` 52, `select, #date` 44, `.log` 52, `.mic` 52, `.done` 48×48 (`apps/leftovers.html:47, 52-53, 55, 58, 83`). It has no `data-kind="kid"` rule; its only `data-kind` rules are for the kiosk (`:18, :96`). For Ezra every control matches Mae's exactly:
    - ✓ 48×48;
    - `#size` and `#date` 263×44;
    - `#name` 378×52;
    - mic 52×52;
    - Log 88×52;
    - Copy for Hearth 181×52.
    That is 12 of 12 controls under 64 on the iPad portrait and 10 of 10 on the iPhone: 7 distinct selectors.
  - **The park map.** The template has no `data-kind` rule at all. In Ezra's default view:
    - the sheet handle is 820×22 (430×22 on the iPhone);
    - the sheet tabs are 197×46 (100×46 on the iPhone);
    - Find me and Whole park are 54×54, and North 50×50.
    In the Nearby pane, the segment is Nearby 67×32 and Waits 57×32, Set my spot is 96×36, and the Queue-Times.com link is 92×15. That is 12 of 12 under 64, with the handle, the segment, Set my spot and the link under 44.
  - **The shell.** It is a `.ds` area, but its tab rule hardcodes `min-height: 56px` (`apps/design.css:560`), and `min-height: 48px` in the sidebar at 1024 px and wider (`:573`). The kid tab is therefore 104×56 on the iPhone and 140×56 on the iPad portrait, both already recorded by P2, and **195×48 on the iPad landscape and desktop**, which is new. The other kid shell controls measure 64-117 px.
  - **Control group.** Kid Verse (smallest 84), Verses (84), Timer (smallest 64; Start 84), Tally (+ 168, − 116, Reset 64) and Prayer (Prayed 161×64) all clear 64. Prayer keeps its own CSS and still clears it, through its own `.kid .prayed{min-height:64px;min-width:64px}` (`apps/prayer.html:421`). So the dividing line is fixed px against `var(--tap)`, not own CSS against `.ds`.
- **Expected.** House style: "44x44pt minimum tap targets; larger in kid mode." CLAUDE.md promises "bigger targets" in kid mode. Every control a kid can reach should size from `--tap` (64) or `--tap-lg` (84).
- **Why it matters.** The kids are 4-5 years old. The kid scale was built for them, but it stops at the apps that size in px, and on the Larder the smallest kid target is also the one that changes family data.
- **Evidence.**
  - Skeptics: `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/verify-kid-targets-own-css-1.json`, `-1-leftovers-ipad-portrait.png`, `-1-shell-ipad-landscape.png`; `verify-kid-targets-own-css-2.json`, `-2-leftovers.png`, `-2-shell-landscape.png`.
  - Investigator: `verify.json` V4; `analyze.json → areas.leftovers.targets.kid`, `areas['dollywood-live'].targets.kid`, `areas.shell.targets.kid`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure.json → runs.kid` (40 entries).
  - Code: `apps/design.css:279-283, 560, 573`; `apps/leftovers.html:18, 47-58, 83, 96`; `apps/prayer.html:421`.
  - Phase 1: `audits/screens/leftovers/kid-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png`, `audits/screens/dollywood-live/kid-family-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png`.
- **Reproduction.** From the repo root:
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/verify.mjs` → `verify.json` V4 (profile ezra).
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/verify-kid-targets-own-css-1.mjs` (13 area/device cases, typical seed) or `… -2.mjs` (park seed, Ezra against Mae).
  - The full per-area list: `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/analyze.mjs` → `analyze.json → areas.<area>.targets.kid.list`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** ran `verify-kid-targets-own-css-1.mjs` (WebKit, typical seed, Ezra, light). It swept every visible interactive element whose centre hit-test lands on it, in 13 area/device cases, and it opened the park map's Nearby and Family panes. It saw:
    - `data-kind=kid` and `--tap` 64px everywhere;
    - the Larder 12 of 12 under 64 (iPad) and 10 of 10 (iPhone), nothing under 44;
    - the park map 7 of 7 on its first screen, plus the segment, Set my spot and the link in Nearby (5 under 44 with the handle);
    - the shell tab 195×48 (iPad landscape, desktop), 140×56 (iPad portrait) and 104×56 (iPhone);
    - Kid Verse, Verses, Timer, Tally and Prayer at 0 under 64.
    It deleted its two park-map PNGs, which were over 1 MB.
  - **Skeptic 2** ran `verify-kid-targets-own-css-2.mjs` (WebKit, park seed). It listed every button, link, input, select and role control for Ezra and for Mae on eight areas and four shell devices, and recorded body `.ds` and the resolved `--tap`. Ezra's Larder and park-map sizes were identical to Mae's (12 of 12 under 64 in each; 5 under 44 on the map). The shell and the control group matched skeptic 1. It confirmed that the template has no `data-kind` rules.
  - **Re-measure (independent code):** exact on every size (Larder `.done` 48×48, `#size`/`#date` 263×44, `#name` 378×52, `#mic` 52×52, Log 88×52, Copy 181×52; shell tab 140×56 and 195×48; `#lv-handle` 820×22, tabs 197×46; Kid Verse 338×84; Tally 168 / 116 / 162×64; Timer `#go` 298×84).
- **Corrected claim.** The claim is right in substance, with four corrections:

On a touch device the switch's hit area is its 60 px label row and the × is 44×44 (P4-SHAPE-03), so for a kid both are under 64 but not under 44.
  - **What is new.** The cross-area cause, the 48 px kid sidebar tab, and the Larder's measured kid sizes.

#### P4-SHAPE-02 — Prayer's toast action is a 36×22 target: Undo after "Mark answered" and "Open it" after an add, offered for 6 seconds

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** a measurable target-size failure (under 44×44) on a secondary safety-net action. The button works, and no data is lost if it is missed: the request is in the Record with the note just typed, and "Put back on the list" reopens it. That path erasing the note is P3-PRAYER-04, not re-counted here.
  - **Not raised:** the re-measure noted a case for medium, because this Undo is the only one-tap recovery after "Mark answered". This section keeps the skeptics' low, because it is not the primary action of a daily flow and nothing is lost.
  - **Exposure:** every adult who marks a request answered or adds one.
- **Areas:** prayer.
- **What happens.**
  - The toast is one element for every message (`apps/prayer.html:563`). Its button is styled `.toast button{background:none;border:none;…font-size:14px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;padding:0}` (`:260-261`), with no minimum size.
  - The button's height is the body line height, 1.55 × 14 px = 21.7 px (`:46`), and its width is the word: 36 px for "Undo".
  - `toast()` hides it after 6,000 ms (`:1142-1149`). It carries "Undo" after "Moved to the record." (`:1331`) and "Open it" after "Added to the family list." (`:1319`).
  - The only listener is on `#toastAct` (`:1426`). A tap 8 px above or below the word's centre still lands on the button; at 14 px it lands on the `#toast` div, which does nothing.
  - The toast is 236×49 on the iPad portrait. On the iPhone PWA it is 215×72.5, because the message wraps onto two lines (VIS-SHAPE-4).
  - Undo itself works: the status goes back to active.
  - An aside, not filed separately: the rotation-count chips have `min-height:44px` but no `min-width` (`:187`), and measure about 43×45.
- **Expected.** 44×44 pt minimum everywhere (house style; CLAUDE.md, Adding an app, step 6), and above all on an undo, since the house style prefers undo to a confirm.
- **Why it matters.** A grandparent who marks the wrong request answered has 6 seconds to hit a 22 px word.
- **Evidence.**
