#### P4-SHAPE-04 — The shared `hub.toast` is capped at half the viewport, so ordinary messages wrap to two or three lines on the iPhone in the shell, Kid Verse and Verses (added after the completeness critic)

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low. Not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** cosmetic. Every message is still shown in full, at the same contrast and for the same time; it is narrower and two or three lines tall, and a three-line pill covers more of what is behind it (in Kid Verse, the Read it to me button for about 2.2 s). No flow breaks and no contrast or target threshold is failed.
  - **Exposure:** every iPhone (430 px) and, for messages longer than about 30 characters at 14 px, the iPad in portrait. On screens 1024 px and wider the toast fits one line.
- **Areas:** shell, kidverse, verses (the three documents that call `hub.toast`); the kiosk nudge reaches every hub.js document but only for the display profile.
- **What happens.**
  - `hub.toast` (`apps/hub.js:431-434`) builds a `.ds > .toast#hub-toast` in whichever document calls it. `.ds .toast` is `position: fixed; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); … max-width: calc(100% - 32px)` (`apps/design.css:588-591`). A fixed box with `left: 50%` and an auto width shrinks to fit the remaining 50 % of the viewport, so it can never be wider than half the screen, whatever `max-width` says. `max-width: calc(100% - 32px)` shows the intent was the full width minus margins.
  - On the 430 px iPhone (PWA and Safari) the computed `left` is 215 px, and every toast wider than 215 px on one line is clamped to exactly 215 px (WebKit, measured 700 ms after it appears):
    - shell "That app is not available for this profile." (`index.html:715`): 215×67, 2 lines (one-line width 294);
    - shell "Notifications on for this device.": 215×67, 2 lines (241);
    - shell "Hub updated — it will use the new version next time it opens.": 215×87, 3 lines;
    - Verses and Kid Verse "This device cannot read aloud.": 215×67, 2 lines (235);
    - Kid Verse "You already have today's star — come back tomorrow!": 215×87-96, 3 lines (387-436), over the Read it to me button.
    - Short messages stay on one line ("Checked with the house." 197, "Could not save that." 169, "Great listening!" 153).
  - On the iPad in portrait the cap is 410 px, so only the 61-character messages wrap (410×67, 2 lines, with 788 px available). On the iPad in landscape and the desktop, `left: calc(50% + 110px)` at 1024 px and wider (`index.html:340-341`) leaves enough room for one line.
  - With the counterfactual centring (`left: 16px; right: 16px; margin-inline: auto; width: max-content`, no translate) every one of these fits one line on the iPhone except the 61-character strings, which take 2 lines at 398 px.
- **Expected.** A toast sized to its message up to the viewport minus the margins: one line for a short message, like the iOS banner it imitates.
- **Why it matters.** Toasts are the hub's only confirmation surface, and the iPhone is the device the family carries. A narrow two- or three-line pill near the tab bar is harder to read at a glance, and for a kid it covers the next button.
- **Evidence.**
  - Critic: `audits/evidence/p4/CRITIC/toast-wrap.json` (iphone-pwa: `w` 215 with 2-3 lines; ipad-portrait: 241-367 on 1 line, 410 on 2 lines) and `audits/evidence/p4/CRITIC/toast-shell-iphone-pwa.png` (1x: the two-line "Grandma Jo can now tap their name on any device." pill on Me).
  - Skeptic 1: `audits/evidence/p4/CRIT/verify-critic-shared-toast-half-viewport-wrap-2-1.json`, `-2-1-shell-iphone.png`, `-2-1-verses-iphone.png` (the two-line "This device cannot read aloud." pill in Verses).
  - Skeptic 2: `audits/evidence/p4/CRIT/verify-critic-shared-toast-half-viewport-wrap-2-2.json`, `-2-2-shell-iphone.png`, `-2-2-kidverse-iphone.png` (the three-line star message over Read it to me).
  - Code: `apps/design.css:588-591`; `apps/hub.js:248, 431-434`; `index.html:340-341, 715`.
- **Reproduction.** `node audits/tools/phase4/CRITIC/toast-wrap.mjs | grep iphone-pwa`: every message longer than about 30 characters prints `"w":215` with `"lines":2` or `3`. The skeptics' scripts, which fire only messages each document really sends: `node audits/tools/phase4/CRIT/verify-critic-shared-toast-half-viewport-wrap-2-1.mjs` and `node audits/tools/phase4/CRIT/verify-critic-shared-toast-half-viewport-wrap-2-2.mjs`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** called `hub.toast` with real message strings in the shell (`#me`) on the iPhone PWA and Safari, the iPad in both orientations and the desktop, and inside the Tally, F260, Kid Verse and Verses frames on the iPhone PWA and iPad portrait, and measured each box, line count, natural one-line width and the counterfactual layout. Two identical runs; the numbers above, and the critic's (215×67 on 2 lines, 241×46 on 1 line on the iPad, 215×87 on 3 lines, a 410 cap on 2 lines), match exactly.
  - **Skeptic 2** grepped every `hub.toast` caller (shell 30+, Kid Verse 11, Verses 4; F260, Tally, Timer, the Larder and Prayer 0; F260 and Prayer have their own toasts) and fired only messages each document sends, on the iPhone PWA and Safari, the iPad portrait and the desktop, as Eli (shell, Verses) and Ezra (Kid Verse). Same cap and wraps. The cap is ordinary CSS shrink-to-fit sizing of a fixed box with `left: 50%` and `right: auto`, the same on iOS Safari; the Windows fallback fonts only move the exact wrap point, so it is not a rig artefact.
- **Corrected claim.** The mechanism and the numbers are right; the critic's area list was too wide. Timer makes no `hub.toast` call (its "Timer done" toast belongs to the shell), the Larder, Tally and F260 reach it only through the kiosk nudge (`apps/hub.js:248`), which fires for the display profile on the 1920 px TV, where it fits one line, and Prayer has its own toast (VIS-SHAPE-4). Wrapping starts at about 29-30 characters at 14 px, not 25. F260's own `.toast` rule (`apps/f260.html:416-417`) also matches `#hub-toast`, which explains its slightly different height; not investigated further.
- **Related (not re-filed):** VIS-SHAPE-4 (Prayer's own toast, the same centring; this settles its Unresolved 3), SHAPE token gap 14 (the toast contract), P4-SHAPE-02 (Prayer's toast action), CONS-MOTION-3 (three toast systems). Nothing in the P2 or P3 reports records the wrap.
- **Token gap.** A toast layout rule in the shared component: `left: 0; right: 0; margin-inline: auto; width: max-content; max-width: calc(100% - 2 * var(--margin))` (or a `--toast-max` token), no `translateX`, with the desktop offset for the sidebar applied as `left: 220px` rather than `50% + 110px` (SHAPE token gap 14; Proposed token set, SHAPE-14).

### Consistency, visual and gap findings

These items were not adversarially verified. Their evidence is the investigator's rendered inventory and targeted runs, spot-checked by the section writer against the cited code lines and the raw JSON, with the re-measure's corrections applied. Every item is the investigator's low rating.

#### CONS-SHAPE-1 — The content card is built six ways: radii from 12 to 36, five paddings, three border widths, three elevations (low)

- **What happens.** The same role, a solid content card, is drawn as follows (Table SHAPE-4):
  - **Radii:** 12 (Larder), 16 (F260 Next up, Prayer ledger), 20 (build guide), 22 (shell, F260 Today), 28 (Kid Verse, Verses), 36 (TV panes).
  - **Padding:** 0, 14, 16×18, 18×16 or 20.
  - **Border:** 0 (Prayer's ledger), 1 px (`.ds`) or 1.5 px (F260).
  - **Elevation:** none (Prayer), `--e1` (Larder) or `--e2` (elsewhere).
  Even the `.ds` apps disagree with design.css's own `.card`, which is `--r-lg` 22, `--sp-5`, `--e2` (`apps/design.css:381-383`): Kid Verse and Verses override it to `--r-xl` 28 (`apps/kidverse.html:41, 61, 74, 95, 122`; `apps/verses.html:72`).
- **Code:**
  - the Larder: `.item` `var(--r-sm)` + `var(--e1)` (`apps/leftovers.html:71`);
  - F260: `.today` and `.hero`, 1.5 px borders, `--r-lg` / `--r` (`apps/f260.html:117, 100`);
  - Prayer: `.ledger{background:var(--gold-soft);border-radius:var(--r);padding:16px 18px}`, with no border and no shadow (`apps/prayer.html:151`);
  - the build guide: `border-radius:20px` (`template.html:234, 248`).
- **Expected.** One card recipe from design.css (radius, padding, border, elevation), used by every area, with variants only by role (grouped list, hero).
- **Why it matters.** Moving between apps, the same kind of surface changes its corner, weight and depth. The hub reads as separate web pages rather than one system.
- **Evidence:** `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/sheet-cards.png`; `cards-summary.json`; `remeasure.json → runs.boxes` (every card agrees).
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/cards.mjs && node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/cards-summary.mjs`, then read the `card ·` lines under `ipad-portrait`.
- **Related:** P2 VIS Shape (`audits/02-shell.md:5865`); the P3 Larder and F260 Shape rows (`audits/03-apps/leftovers.md:914`, `f260.md:774`).

#### VIS-SHAPE-1 — Concentric corners are impossible by construction; at least 58 of 99 container/child pairs are off (low)

- **What happens.**
  - **The root cause is in design.css.** `.card` is R22 with 20 px padding and a 1 px border, an inset of 21 (`apps/design.css:381-383`), and `.btn` is r16 (`:352`). Concentric would need r1, so every button in a card is 15 px off.
    - The re-measure read this in System and Midnight: Me `.card.glass` / `#syncnow` and Home `.gcard` / `.btn-soft`, R22 / 21 / r16 → want 1.
    - The draft's "want 2" is corrected to 1.
  - **The kid scale does not help.** It raises both radii by 6-8 px (`:283`) but not the padding, so kid cards stay off: the shell's kid Reminders card R28 / 21 / r28 (want 7), Verses kid R44 / 38 / r36 (want 6), and Kid Verse's story card R28 / 21 / `#story-say` r28 (want 7, off 21).
  - **Own-CSS areas repeat the pattern:**
    - the Larder's add bar R16 / 13 / r12 (want 3, off 9) on all four fields;
    - the build guide's build card R20 / 15 / r12, toolbar R16 / 11 / r12 and map box R20 / 11 / readout r16.
  - **New facets beyond P2/P3:**
    - in the park map: the sheet R24 / 23 / tabs r14 (want 1, off 13), the meeting bar R16 / 13 / field r10, the route card R18 / 18 / r12 and the amenity button R12 / 11 / r8;
    - the TV kiosk's Me card;
    - F260's Today card R22 / 19.5 / Done capsule r30 (want 2.5);
    - the who-pill R23 / 21 / avatar r14 (want 2) in Kid Verse and Verses.
  - **The count.** The rig's 55 of 95 is a floor, because its check skips pills and uses the top-left radius for all four corners (Table SHAPE-9). With F260's pairs and the park map's corrected pairs it is at least 58 of 99. Tally and Timer are not measured, not passing.
- **Expected.** House style: "an inner element's radius = outer radius minus padding." The shell's sheet (R36 / 20 / r16) and theme cards (R22 / 6 / r16) already do it.
- **Why it matters.** Mismatched nested corners are one of the clearest tells between the hub and first-party iPadOS surfaces, and design.css produces them by default.
- **Evidence:** `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/sheet-concentric.png`; `analyze.json → areas.*.concentric`; `verify.json` V1; `remeasure.json → runs.boxes` (`what: "conc …"` and `"concScan …"` entries); `audits/tools/phase4/measure/page-lib.mjs:472-492` (the rig's check).
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/verify.mjs` → V1 (four pairs); `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/remeasure.mjs boxes` (per-corner scans with pills).
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - P2 VIS "Cards are not concentric" (`audits/02-shell.md:5875`);
  - VIS-DOLLYWOOD-7 (`audits/03-apps/dollywood.md:736`);
  - VIS-KIDVERSE-8 (`audits/03-apps/kidverse.md:725`);
  - the Verses, Larder and Prayer Shape rows (`audits/03-apps/verses.md:582`, `leftovers.md:914`, `prayer.md:952`).

#### CONS-SHAPE-2 — Nine content column widths, and only two apps use a layout token (low)

- **What happens.** Content columns are 360 (Tally's dial), 484-528 (Prayer, 33rem), 560 (Larder), 608 (Timer), 660 or 704 and then 1204 (F260, 44rem / 78rem), 688 (Kid Verse and Verses, the only users of `--max-read`), 788-880 and then 1200 (the shell), 1400 (the build guide) and full bleed (the park map) (Table SHAPE-3).
  - On the iPad landscape the content edge moves from 252 px in the shell to 22 px (F260), 246 (Kid Verse, Verses), 286 (Timer), 310 (Larder), 348 (Prayer) or 410 (Tally) when an app opens.
  - `.ds .container` and `.container-wide` exist (`apps/design.css:341-342`), and no area uses them.
- **Expected.** A small set of named column widths (for example narrow, read and wide), chosen by app type and shared with the shell.
- **Why it matters.** On the always-on iPad the family flips between apps constantly. A jumping content edge and phone-width columns on a landscape iPad look unplanned.
- **Evidence:** `verify.json` V2; `remeasure.json → runs.margins` (agrees ±1 px); `index.html:68, 84`; `apps/f260.html:44, 447`; `apps/leftovers.html:19`; `apps/prayer.html:50`; `apps/tally.html:40`; `apps/timer.html:13, 22, 48`; `apps/kidverse.html:22`; `apps/verses.html:23`; `template.html:233, 385`; screenshots `audits/screens/{leftovers/main,prayer/today,f260/today,tally/main,shell/home}-typical-ipad-landscape-light.png` and `audits/screens/kidverse/kid-typical-ipad-landscape-light.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/verify.mjs` → V2 (e.g. ipad-landscape: leftovers 310/560, prayer 348/484, f260 22/1136, tally 410/360, shell 252/896).
- **Related:** VIS-PRAYER-6; VIS-HOME-3; the P3 Larder, Verses, Timer and Tally layout rows (`audits/03-apps/leftovers.md:913`, `verses.md:581`, `timer.md:479`).

#### VIS-SHAPE-2 — The shell and the build guide keep the phone's 16 px margins on the iPad; F260 drops to 22 px in landscape, and its week stripes paint 7 px from the iPhone edge (low)

- **What happens.**
  - **The shell.** `#views` pads with `--sp-4` at every width below 1024 px (`index.html:66-67`), so Home, Apps and Me sit 16 px from the edge of an 820 px iPad. Inside the same shell, the apps sit 66-230 px in.
  - **The build guide** also sits at 16 px on the iPad portrait and landscape.
  - **F260** is 80 px in on the iPad portrait and 22 px on the iPad landscape (its two-column layout).
  - **New (re-measure).** On the iPhone, F260's `.weeks{margin-left:-9px}` (`apps/f260.html:466`, at ≤ 480 px) and the week's 3 px left border (`:231`) hang the coloured stripes 9 px into the 16 px margin. The painted edge is 7 px from the screen edge, and the milestone rail's right edge is 14 px. On the iPad portrait the stripe starts at 67 against an 80 px text column.
  - Prayer's `.mark` buttons (margin −7) likewise paint at 15 px on the iPhone against a 22 px text margin.
- **Expected.** House style: 16-20 pt margins on the phone, wider on the iPad (for example 24-32 at regular width), with nothing painted inside the margin.
- **Why it matters.** On the primary device the shell looks like a stretched phone layout, while the apps inside it are inset. On the phone, F260's stripes nearly touch the screen edge.
- **Evidence:** `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/verify-margins-shell-ipad-portrait.png`; `verify.json` V2 (ipad-portrait shell 16/16; f260 80/80 against ipad-landscape 22/22); `remeasure.json → runs.margins` (iphone-pwa f260 left 7, right 14, `main#weeks.weeks > section#week-1`; ipad-portrait 67/78); `analyze.json → areas.dollywood.margins`; `audits/screens/dollywood/map-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png`; `audits/screens/f260/today-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/verify.mjs` → V2; `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/remeasure.mjs margins`.
- **Related:** P2 Layout & spacing, "the iPad keeps 16 px margins" (`audits/02-shell.md:5421, 5948`); the P3 F260 Layout row (`audits/03-apps/f260.md:773`). The painted-stripe facet is new.

#### CONS-SHAPE-3 — The spacing rhythm splits the system in two: `.ds` areas are 98-100 % on the 4 px grid, own-CSS areas 34-84 % (low)

- **What happens.**
  - Macro spacing on the 4 px grid (rig / re-measure): shell 99.7 / 99.7 %, TV 100 / 100, Tally 100 / 100, Timer 100 / 100, Kid Verse 98.4 / 97.2, Verses 98.6 / 96.9.
  - Against those: build guide 83.6 / 74.9, park map 65.5 / 54.5, Larder 46.9 / 45.5, Prayer 44.3 / 40.9, F260 36.4 / 34.1.
  - The off-grid values are literal paddings and gaps:
    - F260: week padding 10, header gaps 14;
    - Prayer: mark margin −7, history padding 13, row gaps 15, wrap 22 (`apps/prayer.html:50`);
    - Larder: list gap 10, body padding 14, status 11, group margin 18.
- **Expected.** A 4/8 pt rhythm everywhere (house style), through the `--sp-*` tokens.
- **Why it matters.** Uneven gaps make the large apps feel hand-assembled next to the small ones, and literal spacing is out of reach of any future iPad or kid spacing tier.
- **Evidence:** `analyze.json → areas.*.spacing` (`grid4`, `macroGrid4`, `offGrid`); `remeasure.json`; Table SHAPE-2.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/analyze.mjs` (prints `## <area> … g4= … macro g4=` per area).
- **Related:** the P3 Prayer Layout row (`audits/03-apps/prayer.md:951`); the P3 Larder Layout row (`audits/03-apps/leftovers.md:913`). This is the rendered side of TOK's source finding: spacing-token adoption is 0 % in those five areas.

#### CONS-SHAPE-4 — The main action of a screen has six corner shapes and heights from 44 to 60 (low)

- **What happens.** The main actions are (Table SHAPE-6):
  - F260's Done, a 60 px pill;
  - Timer's Start, 60 px, r22;
  - Verses' Show, 60 px, r28;
  - Kid Verse's Done, 84 px, r36 (kid);
  - Prayer's Pray now, 60 px, r12;
  - the Larder's Log, 52 px, r12;
  - the shell's `.btn`, 44 px, r16;
  - the build guide's tabs, 52 px, r0.
  design.css ties the radius to the size (`.btn --r`, `.btn-lg --r-lg`, `.btn-xl --r-xl`, `apps/design.css:352, 366-367`) rather than giving primary actions one shape, and the apps override it (`apps/verses.html:50`; `apps/kidverse.html:50, 134`; `apps/prayer.html:192-194`; `apps/leftovers.html:55`).
- **Expected.** One primary-button shape (iOS 26 uses capsules) at one or two heights, from a token.
- **Why it matters.** The one control each screen wants tapped looks different in every app, so pre-readers and grandparents get no learned "this is the button" shape.
- **Evidence:** `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/sheet-buttons.png`; `crops.json → buttons[]`; `remeasure.json` (every height and radius agrees).
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/crops.mjs` → `crops.json` `buttons[]`.
- **Related:** the P3 Timer "Shape: corner language" (`audits/03-apps/timer.md:477`); VIS-DOLLYWOOD-12; the P3 Prayer Shape row (`audits/03-apps/prayer.md:952`).

#### CONS-SHAPE-5 — Sheets and modals use four corner radii (five with the Dollywood popover) and three elevations (low)

- **What happens.** (Table SHAPE-7.)

  - Only the shell sheet is concentric with its content.
- **Expected.** One sheet radius and one overlay elevation for every sheet and popover.
- **Why it matters.** Sheets are the Liquid Glass surface the house style names, and four shapes make the same gesture feel different in each app.

- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/analyze.mjs` → `analyze.json → areas.shell.radiiSel['36/36/0/0']`, `areas.prayer.radiiSel['26/26/0/0']`, `areas['dollywood-live'].radiiSel['24/24/0/0']`.

#### GAP-SHAPE-1 — Elevation has no role tokens and no upward level, so each role gets a different depth and the bars use literals (low)

- **What happens.** (Table SHAPE-10.)
  - Content cards use none, `--e1` or `--e2`; buttons none, `--e1` or `--e2`; floating glass controls `--e2` or `--e3`.
  - The bottom-anchored bars use two literal upward shadows:

  - What is consistent: toasts (`--e3`), and sheets and modals (`--e4`, except the park-map popover).
- **Expected.** Named elevation roles (card, control, floating, overlay, toast, bottom bar) mapped onto the four e-levels, with an upward variant for bars.
- **Why it matters.** Without roles each app picks its own depth. The token proposal needs the roles to make depth consistent.

#### VIS-SHAPE-4 — Prayer's toast wraps a short message onto two lines on the iPhone, because its centring caps it at half the viewport (low; new, found by P4-SHAPE-02's skeptics)

- **What happens.** `.toast{position:fixed;left:50%;transform:translateX(-50%);…max-width:92vw}` (`apps/prayer.html:254-257`). A fixed box with `left: 50%` and an auto width shrinks to fit within the remaining 50 % of the viewport, so the toast can never be wider than 215 px on a 430 px iPhone, whatever `max-width` says.
  - "Moved to the record." plus Undo therefore wraps onto two lines, in a 215×72.5 box.
  - On the iPad the same toast is 236×49, one line.
  - The shell's shared `.ds .toast` uses the same `left: 50%` centring (`apps/design.css:588`). **Measured after the completeness critic:** it wraps the same way, at a 215 px cap on the iPhone, in the shell, Kid Verse and Verses; that facet is filed and verified as P4-SHAPE-04 (Unresolved 3 is settled).
- **Expected.** A toast sized to its message up to the maximum width: one line for a short message.
- **Why it matters.** A two-line pill with a small action beside it is harder to read at a glance, and it is less like the iOS banner it imitates.
- **Evidence:** `verify-prayer-undo-target-1.json` (toast 215×72.5 on the iPhone PWA), `verify-prayer-undo-target-1-iphone.png`; `verify-prayer-undo-target-2.json` (73×215; skeptic 2 identified the cause); code `apps/prayer.html:254-257`, `apps/design.css:588`. This was not adversarially verified as a finding in its own right; both skeptics measured it while verifying P4-SHAPE-02.
- **Related:** none. A grep of the P2/P3 reports finds no record of the toast wrapping.

### What works

- **OK-SHAPE-1 — The `.ds` apps and the TV hold the shape system.**
  - Tally, Timer, Kid Verse, Verses and the TV board are 97-100 % on the 4 px grid for macro spacing, and their large radii are 100 % on tokens, with the kid scale applied.
  - None has an adult target under 44. Every kid target is at 64 or above: Kid Verse's, Timer's and Verses' main kid actions are 84 px, and Timer's smallest kid control is 64.
  - They keep 16 px phone margins, except Tally's centred dial.
  - They show that the design.css tokens are enough to deliver the rhythm and the kid scale when an app uses them.
  - Tally's and Timer's concentric results are not measured, because the rig skips pills. They are not a pass.
  - Evidence: `analyze.json` (spacing, radii, targets for tally, timer, kidverse, verses, tv); `verify.json` V4 (Kid Verse `#done` 338×84, Tally `#plus` 168×168); `remeasure.json`.
- **OK-SHAPE-2 — Toasts share `--e3`; sheets and modals share `--e4`; the shell sheet and theme cards are concentric.**
  - Every toast measured (shell, F260, Prayer, Kid Verse, Verses) is `--e3`.
  - The sheets and modals in the shell, Prayer and F260, and the build guide's popover, are `--e4`. The park map's popover (`--e3`) is the one exception.
  - The e-levels are re-tinted per theme and resolve correctly in every document measured.
  - The shell sheet (R36 / 20 / r16) and theme cards (R22 / 6 / r16) pass the concentric check.
  - On the phone, seven areas keep 16 px text margins, and the park map's floating controls sit at 10 px, as Apple Maps does. Prayer (22) and Tally's centred dial are the exceptions, and F260's week stripes paint inside the margin (VIS-SHAPE-2).
  - Evidence: `analyze.json` (shadow classes; `concentric.examplesOk`); `audits/02-shell.md:5878`.
- **OK-SHAPE-3 — The shell's grouped list is the iOS idiom.** `.list` rows are 68-70 px (min `--tap-lg`) with 12/16 padding and hairline separators in an inset R22 container (Table SHAPE-5). It is the pattern the other list idioms should converge on.

### Checked and not a bug

No filed finding was refuted: all four bugs survived both skeptics. The claims below were checked and corrected or dropped.

- **"Park map: 18 control selectors under 44."** Measured by element box. By real hit area on a touch device the count is 13:
  - the Share-my-spot and kid-beacon switches are 60 px label rows (`template.html:435, 1429`);
  - the card × is 44×44 under `pointer:coarse` (`:130`);
  - the Queue-Times.com link is an inline link.
  "18, not the five P3 recorded" also compared selectors with rules: 8 of the 18 are P3's five rules (P4-SHAPE-03).
- **"Kid targets fall below 64 wherever an area keeps its own CSS."** Imprecise. Prayer keeps its own CSS and clears 64; the shell is `.ds` and misses it. The dividing line is fixed px against `var(--tap)` (P4-SHAPE-01).
- **"Timer's kid actions are 84."** Its Start is 84; its smallest kid control is 64.
- **"The Prayer toast is 49 px tall."** On the iPad. On the iPhone it is 72.5, because the message wraps (VIS-SHAPE-4).
- **"Rotation chips 42×44."** About 43×45 in skeptic 1's probe: `min-height:44px` holds, and only the width is short, by about 1 px.
- **"Rename/Remove 57×31."** VIS-PRAYER-3 records Rename 59×31 and Remove 57×31. The rig's 57 is the smaller of the two.
- **"F260: 0 of 0 concentric pairs; no rounded child near a rounded parent's corner."** Wrong. The rig skips pills. The Done capsule (r30) sits in the Today card's corner curve: R22 / 19.5 → want 2.5, a violation.
- **"Tally and Timer: 0 of 0 concentric."** Not measured, for the same reason. They are listed as "not measured", not as passes.
- **"The park-map sheet/tab pairs pass (R24 / 10 / r14, ok)."** The rig judged the sheet at its square bottom corner. At the real top corner the pair is R24 / 23 / r14, want 1, off 13.
- **"55 of 95 concentric pairs off."** A floor, not a total: at least 58 of 99 (Table SHAPE-9).
- **"Every button in a card sits 15 px off (want 2)."** The want is 1: 20 px padding plus a 1 px border is an inset of 21. The draft's own `verify.json` V1 agrees.
- **"The Dollywood popover is `--e4`."** Only in the build guide. The park map's resolves to `--e3` (`template.html:213, 228`).
- **"verify.mjs V2 agrees to the pixel."** True for the text columns. F260's week stripes and Prayer's mark buttons paint outside them (VIS-SHAPE-2).
- **"Shell spacing 79.1 % on the 4 px grid."** Pooled over every screen. Home alone is 63.7 %, the same as Phase 2's 64 %. Not an error, a difference of definition.
- **"Park map macro spacing 65.5 %."** The re-measure found 54.5 % on the main screen (33 values), outside its ±10 pp tolerance. Both are stated. The conclusion (own CSS, off the grid) is unchanged.
- **Skeptic 2's line references `:1301` and `:1473`** are line numbers in the export `apps/dollywood-live.html` (the share label row and the sheet's `pointerdown` drag handler), not in the template, where `:1301` and `:1473` are unrelated code. The template's share row is `:1429`. This section cites each line against the file it belongs to.
- **"The template promises 44 px targets" (skeptic 2).** The comment at `template.html:209` describes the hub (build-guide) flavour only. The expectation for the park map comes from CLAUDE.md.

### Unresolved

No filed finding is unresolved. These questions would refine or extend the findings.

### Method, scripts and evidence

**Investigator scripts** (`audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/`; evidence in `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/`):

| Script | What it measures | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `analyze.mjs` | Re-aggregates the 3,662 rig-v2 raw files per area's own document (`frame:<app>` for apps, `page` for the shell and TV), skipping a frame whose `offset.visible` is false. It covers spacing shares, margins, radii on and off the scale, concentric pairs, shadow classes against each document's own `--e1…--e4`, and targets (< 44 for adults and the kiosk, < 64 for kids). It exists because `aggregate.mjs` pools the shell page and the app frame (`audits/tools/phase4/aggregate.mjs:171-188`), which mixes the viewer bar into every app | `analyze.json` (225 KB) |
| `cards.mjs`, `cards-summary.mjs` | Every painted box of 100×40 or more on each area's main screen (typical household, System, light) on the iPad portrait and iPhone PWA, plus Ezra on the iPad portrait and the TV: radius, padding, border, elevation tokens, fill token, backdrop, max-widths and grids | `cards.json` (368 KB), `cards-summary.json` |
| `crops.mjs` | 1× CSS crops of cards, buttons and concentric pairs, with the measured values underneath | `sheet-cards.png`, `sheet-buttons.png`, `sheet-concentric.png`, `crops.json` |
| `verify.mjs` | The investigator's own independent check: V1 concentric pairs, V2 side margins (4 devices × 8 areas), V3 the Prayer toast action, V4 kid target sizes | `verify.json`, `verify-prayer-undo-toast.png`, `verify-margins-shell-ipad-portrait.png` |

**Skeptic scripts** (same folder): `verify-prayer-undo-target-1.mjs` and `-2.mjs`, `verify-kid-targets-own-css-1.mjs` and `-2.mjs`, and `verify-parkmap-targets-18-1.mjs` and `-2.mjs`. Their outputs are the matching `.json` and `.png` files in `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/`, and their verdicts are in the scratchpad (`p4/verify/SHAPE/*.json`). Every skeptic closed its instance with `L.close()`. Skeptic 1 on the kid targets deleted two park-map PNGs over 1 MB. **One file breaks the evidence limit:** `verify-kid-targets-own-css-2-dollywood-live.png` is 1,470,626 bytes. This section does not cite it; at assembly it was kept on disk and listed in `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/.gitignore`.

**Re-measure** (`audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/remeasure.mjs`, modes `margins | boxes | extra | kid | undo`; outputs `remeasure.json` (123 KB) and `remeasure-prayer-undo.png` (820×260, 1×)). It uses its own DOM scans on the local instance (WebKit, typical household, iPad portrait and landscape, iPhone PWA, the TV), none of the investigator's scripts and none of the rig raw data. Its tolerances:
- sizes, margins and radii: ±1 px;
- grid shares: ±10 pp (one main screen against 3,662 jobs);
- concentric: compared pair by pair, with counts only as a subset;
- themes: System (light) and Midnight (dark) for cards, buttons, sheets and concentric pairs.

16 of 17 agree; the disagreement (row 6) and the smaller points in rows 5, 7 and 12 are corrected in this section.

**Method caveats.**
- In the dark palettes `--e1` is a prefix of `--e2` (`apps/design.css:173`), so a substring-based elevation classifier matches both. The re-measure read those as `--e2`, and `analyze.mjs` classifies by whole drop layers.
- The rig's spacing counts include computed `auto` margins; the shares are occurrence-weighted and not corrected for them.
- The rig's concentric check runs once per selector (the first time it is seen), skips pills, and uses the top-left radius (`page-lib.mjs:470-492`).
- All cited screenshots are System theme. The named-theme shots were not cropped for this dimension.

## Icons (ICON)

Baseline: the working tree at fe6041d (no app file has changed since). Engine: Playwright WebKit on the local rig (`audits/tools/lib/local.mjs`, variant `typical`, demo clock); Chromium was used as a second engine where noted. Themes: Hearth, Parchment and Frost (OS light), Midnight and Forest (OS dark). Each theme was set as the profile's person preference (`PUT /api/data/hub/theme?scope=person`) and in `localStorage` `hub.theme`. System is Hearth by day and Midnight by night, so those two cover it. No request went to production.

**Summary**

- **Five defects confirmed, each 2/2 by the skeptics.** One is medium.
  - **P4-ICON-01 (medium).** Icon inks taken from the raw `apps.json` or profile hex are never lifted for dark. In Midnight and Forest this puts 4 of 7 kid tiles, 6 of 9 adult tiles, three Home card heads and the accent icons at 1.90-2.95:1. In Parchment the Kid Verse and Timer tiles are 2.35 and 2.99.
  - **Four low defects:**
    - **P4-ICON-03.** `--gold` is used as the ink for icons on gold tints: six icons at 2.76-2.78:1 in Hearth.
    - **P4-ICON-04.** The park map's compass needle is a fixed `#FF6B4A`, at 2.24-2.75:1 in the light palettes.
    - **P4-ICON-02.** The shell's 20 % duotone never renders through `<use>`.
    - **P4-ICON-05.** `.ds .icon` overrides every icon's own `stroke-width` and `fill` attributes.
- **Eleven icon families; no app uses the shell's own sprite.**
  - "Done" is drawn with five different SVG paths plus a text ✓. "Star" is drawn four ways and "add" four ways.
  - Six computed stroke weights are in use (1.75-2.6 viewBox units). For 14-26 px icons that renders at 1.02-2.86 px.
  - The shell alone renders 11 icon sizes, and `design.css` has no icon size, weight or ink tokens (CONS-ICON-1, GAP-ICON-1).
- **Two earlier conclusions are corrected.**
  - Phase 2's "one icon language … 20 % duotone" (`audits/02-shell.md:6005`) holds only for inline SVGs.
  - Phase 3 Verses' "mixed strokes 1.75 / 2 / 2.25" (`audits/03-apps/verses.md:583, 617`) never reaches the screen: every one of those icons renders at 1.75.
- **The shell already has three working ink patterns, applied in only a few places:**
  - `--gold-ink` on the Home Kids and Stars heads: 5.33 in Hearth, 7.9-8.0 in dark.
  - `--tint-ink` on the feed icons: 3.54 or better in every palette.
  - Theme-token tints on the TV heads: 4.86-6.16 in dark.
- **What works.**
  - All 42 icon-only controls in the Hearth re-measure have a name (0 unnamed; the investigator also found 0 on 28 surfaces in all five palettes).
  - Tab-bar icons are 5.21-7.80:1 in light and 5.32-6.18:1 in dark.
  - Larder, Prayer, Tally and Verses icons are ≥ 4.40:1 in every palette.
  - No SF Symbols and no SF Pro are shipped.
- **Re-measure.** 15 key numbers were re-measured: 14 agree (2 of them after corrected locations or counts) and 1 disagrees. The F260 week-done tick fails only in the light palettes (2.30-2.60) and passes in dark (4.17-4.23). The draft's formula counted the row's group opacity twice.

Corrections to the investigator's draft in this table:

- **Shell counts are distinct icons.** `report.mjs` de-duplicates. The raw instance counts on the 10 shell surfaces in Hearth are 133 / 108 / 54, and the investigator's raw `measure-hearth.json` and the re-measure give the same values.
- **F260 stroke range.** The rendered stroke is 1.5-6 px as in `rollup.json`, not "0.83-4.17". The 0.83 came from the excluded hidden-state marks.
- **F260 counts under 3:1.** These use the rendered-pixel (`peak`) field, not the draft's `declared` figure, because the finished-week row is dimmed as a group (see Table ICON-3). The draft's 80 / 77 / 76 / 76 / 76 and lowest 1.78 / 2.03 / 1.89 / 1.92 / 1.94 overstate the dark palettes.
- **F260 emoji artefacts removed.** The ⛰ readings (2.71 in Hearth, 2.97 in Parchment) are left out, because ⛰ renders as a colour emoji in the rig.
- **Build guide.** The minimap (1.02-1.22) is not an icon, so it is left out of the build guide row.

Other cross-area numbers:

- **Stroke weights.** Seven distinct computed weights are in use across the hub: 1.4 (map dots), 1.75, 2, 2.2, 2.4, 2.5 and 2.6 viewBox units. For icons of the same job at 14-26 px the rendered stroke runs from 1.02 px (the shell's 14 px feed icons) to 2.86 px (the F260 Today tick), a 2.8× spread.
- **Sizes.** The shell alone renders 11 icon sizes. `design.css` defines 24 and 32 px (`apps/design.css:602-603`), plus `.btn .icon` at 1.25em (`:371`), `.tab .icon` at 26 px (`:563`) and `.empty .icon` at 48 px (`:546`). Nothing scales the tab icons for kid or kiosk mode (no kid or kiosk rule for `.tab .icon` in `index.html` or `design.css`). The TV heads are 26.4 px on a 1920 px board.
- **Caps.** Linecaps are round everywhere except F260's progress rings (butt).

### Confirmed defects

All five were adversarially verified. For each, two skeptics wrote their own scripts, re-read the code and re-ran the measurement. Severities follow the Phase 2 rule (`audits/02-shell.md:25-37`) and the design-system clause of the Phase 4 brief.

#### P4-ICON-01 — Icon inks taken from `apps.json` or profile hex are never lifted for dark: kid tiles, Home card heads and accent icons fall under 3:1

- **Severity: medium.** Both skeptics rated it medium.
  - **Clause:** a measurable accessibility failure. Information-bearing non-text is below 3:1 on primary surfaces: the Apps grid, the kid Apps grid and the Home cards.
  - **Why not high:** every icon has an adjacent visible text label, so no adult flow breaks. The kid tile picture is the pre-readers' cue, which holds it at medium.
  - **Exposure:** Midnight and Forest. System resolves to Midnight at night, and the kitchen iPad stays open 24/7. In Parchment, two tiles are affected.
- **Areas:** shell (Apps grid, kid Apps grid, Home, kid Home, Chat); dollywood-live (selected tab, from the template).
- **What happens.** The inks are raw hex values set inline, and no palette can change them:
  - **Source of the inks.**
    - Tile glyphs are painted with the app's `apps.json` colour through `style="--tint:<hex>"` (`index.html:700`).
    - The Home card heads for Today's reading, In the fridge and Prayer get the same inline hex (`index.html:1165, 1176, 1188`).
    - `.ds .app-icon` paints `color: var(--tint)` (`apps/design.css:606-608`).
    - Where no `--tint` is set, it falls back to `--accent` (`apps/design.css:93`), which hub.js sets inline from the profile colour (`apps/hub.js:80`).
    - The park map strokes the selected tab with `var(--accent)` (`../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:429`).
  - **Midnight / Forest:**
    - Kid Apps grid (52.8 px glyphs): Larder 1.95 / 1.92, Prayer 2.84-2.87 / 2.82, Tally 2.93 / 2.88, park map 2.75 / 2.66. That is 4 of 7 kid tiles under 3:1; Timer 3.22, Verses 3.11 and Kid Verse 4.02 pass.
    - Adult Apps grid: 6 of 9 tiles at 1.95-2.93 in Midnight and 1.90-2.88 in Forest (F260, Larder, Prayer, Tally, build guide, park map).
    - Home card heads: Today's reading 2.29-2.30 / 2.25, In the fridge 1.95 / 1.92, Prayer 2.83-2.87 / 2.82-2.83.
    - Accent icons: the chat bot sparkle (Eli) 2.28-2.30 / 2.25; the park map's selected Nearby tab (Eli) 2.11-2.14 / 2.08-2.11; the kid "Let's play" sparkle (Ezra) 2.95 / 2.88. The investigator also measured Ezra's selected park-map tab at 2.70 in Parchment and 2.71 in Midnight.
  - **Parchment:** the Kid Verse tile 2.34-2.35 and the Timer tile 2.99.
  - **The contrast with the TV.** The TV board draws the same book and prayer meanings with theme tokens (`--tint:var(--slate|mocha|…)`, `index.html:1118-1125`), and they measure 4.86-6.16 in dark. On Home, the heads that use tokens also pass: Kids 7.89-8.01 and Reminders 6.08-6.16.
- **Expected.** Every icon on a tint reaches ≥ 3:1 in all five palettes, with app and person colours resolved through inks that have dark values.
- **Why it matters.** At night the pre-readers find their apps by the tile picture, and four of their seven pictures are below the non-text minimum. Adults lose the card-head cue on Home, though they keep the text.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator data: `audits/evidence/p4/ICON/measure-midnight.json`, `measure-forest.json` and `measure-parchment.json` (surfaces `shell-apps`, `shell-kid-apps`, `shell-home`, `shell-chat`, `shell-kid-home`, `dollywood-live`), plus `below3.json`.
  - Investigator screenshots: `shot-home-heads-midnight-ipad.png`, `shot-tv-heads-midnight.png`, `shot-apps-grid-midnight-iphone.png`, `shot-apps-grid-parchment-iphone.png`.
  - Skeptic screenshots: `verify-icon-ink-hex-not-lifted-dark-1-kid-apps-midnight.png` (faint Larder, Prayer and Tally glyphs), `verify-icon-ink-hex-not-lifted-dark-2-kid-apps-midnight-ipad.png`, `verify-icon-ink-hex-not-lifted-dark-1-adult-home-midnight.png`.
  - Phase 1: `audits/screens/shell/apps-typical-ipad-portrait-dark.png`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - Investigator: `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/measure.mjs midnight shell-apps,shell-kid-apps,shell-home,shell-chat,shell-kid-home,dollywood-live`, then `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/report.mjs`. Read `declared` for the `.ticon` and `h2 > span.app-icon` items, and repeat with `forest` and `parchment`.
  - Skeptics: `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/verify-icon-ink-hex-not-lifted-dark-1.mjs` and `-2.mjs`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** re-read `index.html:700`, `design.css:606-609` and `hub.js:80`, and the template's `:429`. Their own WebKit script set each theme as a person preference and confirmed `data-theme` and `data-scheme`. For each icon it recorded the computed ink and which inline `--tint`/`--accent` ancestor it came from, then hid the icon and took the median background from a CSS-scale shot.

#### P4-ICON-02 — The 20 % duotone never renders on sprite icons (`<use>`), so the one icon recipe renders two ways

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** cosmetic. A decorative 20 % fill is missing; no information, flow or contrast is affected.
- **Areas:** shell (also the style guide, `docs/design.html`).
- **What happens.**
  - **Why the selector misses.** `.ds .icon .duo { fill: var(--tint); fill-opacity: .2; stroke: none }` (`apps/design.css:605`; the comment at `:604` states the intent) needs the `.duo` path to be a descendant of `.icon`. In the sprite, the `.duo` paths sit inside `<symbol>` in an unclassed hidden `<svg>` (`index.html:416-438`; 13 of the 21 symbols carry one). Inside the `<use>` instance there is no `.icon` ancestor, so the rule never matches. The `.duo` path inherits `fill: none` from `.icon` (`:602`) and is stroked a second time on top of the outline.
  - **Where the duotone does render.** Only inline SVGs get the tint: the 9 tile icons, `ICON_STAR` and `ICON_PIN` (`index.html:886-887`).
  - **Surfaces with no duotone:** the tab bar, the pill, the Reminders, Today's reading, In the fridge, Prayer and Around the house heads, chat, Me, and five of the six TV heads.
  - **Surfaces with the duotone:** the Kids head (adult Home), the Stars head (kid Home), the Me Kids' rewards head and the TV "Stars this week" head.
  - **Visibility.** The mix is subtle at 1× (a maximum channel delta of about 40), which explains why Phase 2 recorded the language as consistent.
  - **Style guide.** The guide's only icon sample also goes through `<use>` (`docs/design.html:243`, symbol at `:247`), so it never shows the duotone either.
- **Expected.** One recipe that renders the same through `<use>` and inline, or a spec without a duotone.
- **Why it matters.** It corrects two earlier statements:
  - P2's "OK — One icon language … a 20 % duotone" (`audits/02-shell.md:6005`) holds for inline icons only.
  - The Timer checker's "its duotone is not discernible at 16 px" (`audits/03-apps/timer.md:443`): the duotone is absent, not small.

  The house's one icon recipe does not render as specified on most of the shell.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `audits/evidence/p4/ICON/duo-sprite-webkit.json` and `duo-sprite-chromium.json` (`duoRendersViaUse: false`, `duoRendersInline: true`, light and dark); `duo-sprite-webkit.png` (the same `#i-home` at 192 px, hollow via `<use>` and tinted inline).
  - Skeptic 1: `verify-duotone-missing-on-sprite-1-{webkit,chromium}.json` and `-webkit.png`.
  - Skeptic 2: `verify-duotone-missing-on-sprite-2-{webkit,chromium}.json`, `-shipped.png` and `-inlined.png`.
- **Reproduction.** `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/duo-sprite.mjs webkit`, then again with `chromium`. Also `verify-duotone-missing-on-sprite-1.mjs` and `-2.mjs`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** drew every real `svg.icon` on Home (light and dark), Apps, Chat, Me, kid Home and TV three times at 48 px, in WebKit and Chromium:
    - A: the shipped clone;
    - B: inline without `.duo`;
    - C: inline with `.duo`.

    In the region where C differs from B, the results were:
    - **`<use>` icons:** 0 of 20 on Home, 0 of 25 on Chat, 0 of 10 on kid Home and 0 of 13 on TV rendered the duotone. For example, the `#i-book` head had 384 of 454 fill pixels untinted.
    - **Inline icons:** every one rendered it (35 of 35 on Home; the TV Stars head included).
    - **Positive control:** the sprite geometry drawn inline always tinted.
  - **Skeptic 2** measured the icons in place, on shipped pages. They replaced each `<use>` with its symbol's content (A) and stripped `.duo` from the originally inline icons (B), against a noise baseline of 0 px, in both engines and both modes.
    - Home: 9 icons declare a duotone and 1 renders it (the inline Kids head). All 8 `<use>` icons changed by 81-250 px when inlined.
    - Me: 0 of 6.
    - TV: 1 of 6 (only the inline Stars head).
  - **Re-measure:** through `<use>` the `#i-home` interior stays pure `[255,255,255]`; drawn inline it is `[246,217,207]`. 13 of the 21 symbols carry `.duo`.
- **Corrected claim.** The mechanism and the fact that both engines agree are confirmed. Counts depend on the method, but the rule does not: every `<use>` icon renders 0 duotone and every inline icon renders it. The counts by method:
  - 75 declared / 31 rendered distinct icons (investigator, de-duplicated);
  - 108 / 54 raw instances in Hearth (investigator and re-measure);
  - 55 / 35 DOM-wide on adult Home (skeptic 1);
  - 9 / 1 visible on Home (skeptic 2).

  Corrections to the draft:
  - "TV heads never get it" is wrong for the TV "Stars this week" head, which is inline and does get it.
  - The Park head was not observed; it appears only on park days.
  - The style-guide sample is at `docs/design.html:243`, not `:244`.
  - The mix is subtle at 1×, not glaring.
- **Related (not re-filed).** P2 OK "One icon language" (`audits/02-shell.md:6005`) and the rubric row (`:5423`). No P2 or P3 ID records this defect.

#### P4-ICON-03 — `--gold` is used as icon ink on gold tints: six icons at 2.76-2.78:1 in Hearth, while the shell's `--gold-ink` override covers only two heads

> **Overlap (assembly).** The Kid Verse week-strip star (gold on gold-soft, 2.78 in Hearth) is also listed among the non-text facets of P4-COLOR-01. It is one defect instance, counted here.

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** a decorative or secondary non-text failure. Each heading icon repeats the text heading beside it. The earned Kid Verse day and the earned F260 milestone are also shown by the gold-soft fill, the border and full opacity.
  - **Exposure:** Hearth, which is also System by day.
- **Areas:** shell (Home, kid Home, Me, TV), kidverse, f260.
- **What happens.** Two recipes paint the base hue `--gold` (`#B4861B` in Hearth) on a gold tint.
  - **Recipe 1: `.app-icon` with `color: var(--tint)`** (`apps/design.css:606-608`) and `--tint:var(--gold)`, on a 22 %→8 % gold mix. Each measures 2.76-2.77, or 2.64-2.88 across the gradient:
    - the Reminders bell on Home (`index.html:1203`), kid Home (`:1153`) and the TV (`:1127`);
    - the Me "Kids' rewards" star (`:1272`);
    - the TV "Stars this week" star (`:1124`).
  - **Recipe 2: `--gold` on `--gold-soft`.** Each measures 2.78:
    - the Kid Verse week-strip star (`apps/kidverse.html:68`). The day number in the same element uses `--gold-ink` (`:67`).
    - F260's earned-milestone text glyphs ♥ ✓ ♪ ◐ (`apps/f260.html:196`).
  - **Not affected:** the adult Home Kids head and the kid Home Stars head. `index.html:199` sets `color: var(--gold-ink)` on them, and they measure 5.33-5.34.
  - **Other palettes:** Parchment 3.09-3.11 at the median (2.87 at the 22 % end), Frost 3.21-3.30 (2.97 at the 22 % end), Midnight and Forest 5.1-7.8.
- **Expected.** ≥ 3:1 for every gold icon in every palette. `--gold-ink` already exists in every palette (`apps/design.css:74, 124, 144, 164, 206`) and measures 5.32-5.37 on these backgrounds in Hearth.
- **Why it matters.** One ink repeats on the gold icons across the shell, the TV, Kid Verse and F260. The shell's own fix is applied in one place.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `measure-hearth.json` (surfaces `shell-home`, `shell-kid-home`, `shell-me`, `shell-tv`, `kidverse`, `kid-kidverse`, `f260`) and `below3.json`.
  - Skeptic 1: `verify-gold-icon-ink-hearth-1.json` and `-tv.png`.
  - Skeptic 2: `verify-gold-icon-ink-hearth-2.json`, `-2-parchment.json`, and crops including `-home-adult-reminders-bell.png`, `-home-adult-kids-card-head.png` (the passing `--gold-ink` head), `-me-adult-rewards-head.png`, `-tv-tv-stars-head.png` and `-kidverse-kid-days-on-star.png`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - Investigator: `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/measure.mjs hearth shell-home,shell-tv,shell-me,kid-kidverse,f260 && node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/report.mjs`, then filter `below3.json` for theme `hearth` and fg `[180,134,27]`.
  - Skeptic 1: `verify-gold-icon-ink-hearth-1.mjs`.
  - Skeptic 2: `verify-gold-icon-ink-hearth-2.mjs hearth` (and `parchment`).
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** selected each target by selector and sampled every background pixel (min, median, max). They also repainted each text glyph red, then blue, to see whether the ink applies at all, and computed the ratio analytically from the tokens for all five palettes.
    - **Hearth:** bell 2.76 on all three surfaces; Me head 2.76; TV Stars 2.76; week-strip star 2.78; F260 ♥ ✓ ♪ ◐ 2.78 (the repaint changed 49-115 px, so the ink is really drawn).
    - **Passing:** the Home Kids and Stars heads, 5.33 / 5.34.
    - **Emoji:** ⛰ 📖 🔥 💯 ✝ changed 0 px when repainted, so they render as colour emoji.
    - **Analytic, gold on gold-soft:** Hearth 2.78, Parchment 3.11, Frost 3.30, Midnight 7.79, Forest 7.55.
  - **Skeptic 2** used the median background under each hidden icon in Hearth and Parchment.
    - **Hearth:** bell 2.76 (adult Home, kid Home, TV); Me head 2.76; TV Stars 2.76; week-strip star 2.78; F260 text glyphs 2.78.
    - **Passing:** the Home heads at 5.33-5.34.
    - **`--gold-ink` instead:** would measure 5.32-5.37 on the same backgrounds.
    - **Parchment:** 3.09-3.11, which passes.
  - **Re-measure:** bell 2.77 on Home, kid Home and TV; Me head 2.77; TV Stars 2.77; week-strip 2.78; F260 milestones 2.78; the Home Kids and Stars heads 5.34 (`--gold-ink`).
- **Corrected claim.**
  - **Wrong location in the draft:** "Stars/Kids star heads 2.76 (Home, Me, TV)" is wrong for Home. The failing star heads are the Me Kids' rewards head and the TV Stars head only.
  - **⛰ is a rig artefact:** its "2.71" is not a gold-ink failure; it renders as a colour emoji.
  - **Parchment and Frost:** they fail only at the 22 % end of the gradient, which is not filed.
  - **Not a token gap:** `--gold-ink` exists in every palette. The defect is that `.app-icon` and these two rules use the base hue instead of the existing ink step. The draft's "add `--gold-ink`" is withdrawn.
- **Related (not re-filed).** The P2 Kid Verse tile at 2.77 in light (`audits/02-shell.md:5885`; its `apps.json` colour is the same `#B4861B`). VIS-F260-1 covers gold used as text (`audits/03-apps/f260.md:706, 805`), not the milestone glyphs.

#### P4-ICON-04 — The map compass's north needle is a fixed `#FF6B4A`: 2.24-2.75:1 in the three light palettes

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** a secondary information-bearing graphic below 3:1. North is also marked by a rotating "N" label at 4.37-4.77:1, so nobody is blocked.
  - **Exposure:** the park map in Hearth, Parchment and Frost (and System by day), for adult and kid profiles alike. In the build guide the button is dead (P3-DOLLYWOOD-10) and hidden below 700 px.
- **Areas:** dollywood-live, dollywood (generated). The fix belongs in `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:620`.
- **What happens.**
  - **The markup.** The north half of `#lv-north` is `fill="#FF6B4A"` as a literal attribute (`apps/dollywood-live.html:620`; identical at `apps/dollywood.html:620`, from `template.html:620`). It sits on the cream glass button (`var(--lv-glass-soft)`, `:417`).
  - **Measured:**

    | Palette | Contrast |
    |---|---|
    | Hearth | 2.70-2.75 |
    | Parchment | 2.24-2.29 |
    | Frost | 2.66-2.72 |
    | Midnight | 5.85-5.93 |
    | Forest | 5.76-5.83 |

  - **Against the grey south half** it measures only 1.13-1.41 in every theme.
  - **The other north cue.** A 9 px, weight 800 "N" in `var(--danger)` (`:418`) rotates with the button and reads 4.37-4.77 in the light palettes.
  - **Build guide.** The compass is hidden below 700 px by `[data-flavor=hub] .lv-northwrap{display:none}` inside `@media(max-width:699px)` (`apps/dollywood.html:313, 352`).
- **Expected.** The needle colour comes from a per-palette token at ≥ 3:1 on the control. `var(--danger)`, which the N label already uses, passes here.
- **Why it matters.** It is the colour cue for north on a rotated map, and it fails in the normal daylight themes. CLAUDE.md allows hex only for map colours, and this is control chrome.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `measure-{hearth,parchment,frost}.json` (surfaces `dollywood`, `dollywood-live`, `kid-dollywood-live`, selector `button#lv-north.lv-north > svg`) and `below3.json`.
  - Skeptic 1: `verify-compass-needle-hex-1.json` and `-1-parchment.png`.
  - Skeptic 2: `verify-compass-needle-hex-2.json`, `-2-webkit-parchment.png`, `-2-chromium-parchment.png` and `-2-webkit-midnight.png`.

- **Reproduction.**
  - Investigator: `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/measure.mjs parchment dollywood-live,dollywood && node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/report.mjs`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-compass-needle-hex-1.mjs` and `-2.mjs`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** (WebKit; all six themes; dollywood-live on iphone-pwa and dollywood on ipad-portrait and iphone-pwa):
    - Method: rotation and transition were disabled, and 6 points inside the north half were sampled at device-pixel scale, with the button's background taken from a shot with the needle hidden.
    - The computed fill was `rgb(255,107,74)` in every theme.
    - Results: Hearth 2.75, Parchment 2.29, Frost 2.72, Midnight 5.85, Forest 5.76.
    - The build guide on iPhone has `display: none`.
    - The N label measures 4.41-4.77 in light and 6.32-6.37 in dark.
  - **Skeptic 2** (WebKit and Chromium; Chromium paints the real backdrop blur):
    - Method: eroded `isPointInFill` samples of the north and south halves.
    - WebKit: 2.75 / 2.29 / 2.72 / 5.85 / 5.76.
    - Chromium: 2.73 / 2.27 / 2.70 / 5.85 / 5.76.
    - Needle against the south half: 1.13-1.41.

  - **Re-measure:** 2.70 / 2.24 / 2.66 / 5.93 / 5.81 (iPhone PWA).
- **Corrected claim.** The draft's "the only cue for north" is wrong: the rotating N label is also a cue. The build-guide exposure is iPad and desktop only, and there the button is dead. The inline hex itself was already counted in P3 (`audits/03-apps/dollywood.md:908`); the new facet is the contrast measurement.
- **Related (not re-filed).**

#### P4-ICON-05 — In the `.ds` apps every icon's own `stroke-width` and `fill` attribute is dead: all compute 1.75, and the "filled" Prayer-warrior heart renders as an outline

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** cosmetic. The stroke weights differ by 0.25-0.5 px, and one badge glyph draws as an outline instead of solid. No text, contrast, target or data is affected.
- **Areas:** kidverse, verses (both `<body class="ds">`: `apps/kidverse.html:144`, `apps/verses.html:99`).
- **What happens.**
  - **Why the attributes lose.** Any author CSS rule beats an SVG presentation attribute, and `.ds .icon { fill: none; stroke-width: 1.75 }` (`apps/design.css:602`) is such a rule.
  - **Stroke weights.** Each of these icons asks for its own weight and computes 1.75:
    - Verses' Not yet and Almost (`stroke-width="2"`) and Got it (`"2.25"`) (`apps/verses.html:113-115`);
    - Kid Verse's I heard it (`"2.2"`, `apps/kidverse.html:173`; kid view only);
    - the Story lover badge book (`"1.9"`, `:400`).
  - **The heart.** The Prayer-warrior heart is written `fill="currentColor"` (`:400`) but computes `fill: none` and draws a 1.75 outline.
  - **The star.** The badge star beside it is filled, because it has its own rule, `.ds .icon.star` (`:52`). The heart has no such rule.
- **Expected.** The markup and the rendering agree. Either the fill intent survives `.ds .icon`, or the dead attributes are removed.
- **Why it matters.** It corrects P3 Verses' "strokes 1.75 / 2 / 2.25 … mixed" (`audits/03-apps/verses.md:583, 617`). The rendered weights are uniform, and only the markup differs. The badge row pairs a filled star with an outline heart, against the code's intent.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `audits/evidence/p4/ICON/facets.json` (`attrStrokeWidth` vs `computedStrokeWidth`; `kidverse-ezra-heart`: `svgFillAttr "currentColor"`, `fill "none"`).
  - Skeptic 1: `verify-ds-icon-overrides-attributes-1-{webkit,chromium}.json`, `-1-badges-ezra-shipped.png` and `-1-badges-ezra-attr-honoured.png`.
  - Skeptic 2: `verify-ds-icon-overrides-attributes-2.json`, `-2-badges-shipped.png` and `-2-badges-intended.png`.
- **Reproduction.** `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/facets.mjs`, then inspect `facets.json`. Also `verify-ds-icon-overrides-attributes-1.mjs` and `-2.mjs`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** (WebKit and Chromium; Kid Verse as ezra and eli, Verses as eli after Show):
    - Every attributed icon computes 1.75px with `fill: none`, on both the `<svg>` and its shape.
    - A pixel test (copy the attributes into inline style so they win; noise 0 px) changed:
      - story-heard: 67 / 62 px
      - book: 59 / 125 px
      - heart: 130 / 134 px
      - Not yet: 94 / 93 px
      - Almost: 18 / 34 px
      - Got it: 50 / 42 px
    - Icons whose attribute already equals the rule changed 0 px.
    - The badge-row PNGs show an outline heart as shipped and a solid heart with the attribute honoured.
  - **Skeptic 2** (both engines):
    - The same computed values.
    - Control: with `body.ds` removed, each icon computes its own attribute (2px, 2.25px, 2.2px, 1.9px), and the heart fills.
    - Forcing the attributes changes 18-127 px per icon and 220 px on the heart (its ink ratio goes from 0.17 to 0.26).
  - **Re-measure:** Kid Verse attributes 1.75 / 1.9 / 2.2 and Verses 1.75 / 2 / 2.25 all compute 1.75px, for kid and adult. The `.bicon` heart computes `fill: none` with a 1.75 stroke.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - The claim is accurate.
  - Attributes that already say 1.75 or `none` are redundant, not visibly dead.
  - In the seed data the Prayer-warrior badge is unearned (muted). The same rule draws it as an outline once it is earned.
  - The stroke differences are sub-pixel, so the heart is the only visible mismatch.
- **Related (not re-filed).** VIS-KIDVERSE-9 (labels repeat their icon; text −/+) is a different defect.

### Consistency, visual and gap findings

These items were not adversarially verified. The evidence comes from the investigator's static and rendered inventory, spot-checked by the section writer against the cited lines.

#### CONS-ICON-1 — Eleven icon families; no app uses the shell's own set (investigator rating: medium)

- The shell (F1-F3) is one custom 1.75 recipe. Each app brings its own:
  - F260: Feather/Lucide-derived paths at 2 on 18 px, a 20-grid tick at 2.6, colour emoji, text glyphs and CSS chevrons.
  - The Larder: inlined Lucide at 2-2.4.
  - Prayer: hand drawn at 1.75-2.4.
  - Kid Verse and Verses: hand drawn, computing 1.75.
  - The Dollywood template: hand drawn at 2-2.6, plus text glyphs and emoji.
  - Tally and Timer: none.
- `<use href="#i-…">` appears only in `index.html` (30 uses of a 21-symbol sprite) and in F260's private 11-symbol sprite (`static.json`; the re-measure's static check).
- The same meaning is drawn in several ways (Table ICON-4):
  - "Done": 5 SVG paths at 5 computed weights, plus a text ✓ in 5 areas.
  - "Star": 4 ways. The SVG star head and the text ★ chips sit in the same Kids card (`index.html:913-916`).
  - "Add": 4 ways.
  - "Previous / next": chevrons and text −/+ inside F260 (`apps/f260.html:617-620` vs `:692-694`).
  - "Book": 5 drawings; "timer" 3; "map pin" 3.
- Rendered stroke for icons of the same job (14-26 px) runs 1.02-2.86 px. The shell renders 11 sizes (Table ICON-2).
- **Expected (house style):** "One open-source icon set … consistent stroke weight and optical size in every app."
- **Evidence:**
  - `static.json`, `rollup.json`, Tables ICON-2 and ICON-4.
  - `audits/screens/f260/milestones-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`: colour emoji, text ✎ and ♥, stroked printer and gear, text − and +, CSS chevrons and SVG ticks on one screen.
  - `shot-home-heads-midnight-ipad.png`: an SVG star head beside text ★ chips.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/static.mjs && node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/report.mjs`, then compare `strokeWidthsVbUnits`, `strokePxMin`/`strokePxMax` and `renderedSizesPx` per area.
- **Related (per-app mixes already noted, not re-filed):**
  - VIS-F260-12 and the F260 rubric row (`audits/03-apps/f260.md:775`).
  - VIS-KIDVERSE-9.
  - VIS-DOLLYWOOD-8.
  - The park map's icon-set row (`audits/03-apps/dollywood-live.md:778`).
  - Prayer (`audits/03-apps/prayer.md:953`) and Verses (`audits/03-apps/verses.md:617`).
  - P2 "Glyphs" (`audits/02-shell.md:5889`).

  New here: the cross-area count and the meaning-level duplicates.

#### CONS-ICON-2 — One drawing, several meanings (investigator rating: low)

Several drawings carry more than one meaning (Table ICON-5):
- Flame = the activity feed in the shell, but a streak in F260.
- Heart = a memorised verse, the Prayer warrior badge and an **AED**.
- ⊕ = the Tally counter and Prayer's Add.
- × = close / remove and **delete the last PIN digit**; ✕ = ride closed.
- Minus = subtract, zoom out, previous week and "Almost".
- Sparkle = "Let's play", the chat assistant and the unknown-app fallback.
- Circular arrows = reload and Copy.
- The strollers amenity uses a shopping-cart emoji.
- The Guests head is a bare plus.

- **Expected:** one meaning per glyph across the hub. Table ICON-6 maps each meaning to a distinct Lucide or Phosphor name (for example `activity` vs `flame`, `heart-pulse` for AED, `delete` for the PIN backspace, `ban` for closed).
- **Why it matters:** grandparents and pre-readers read icons literally.
- **Evidence:** Table ICON-5 with file:line; `audits/screens/dollywood-live/amenity-tap-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png` (♥ AED markers).
- **Reproduction:** `grep -n "i-flame\|i-sparkle\|i-x\|i-plus" index.html`; `grep -n 'data-go="add"' apps/prayer.html`; `grep -n "aed:" apps/dollywood-live.html | cut -c1-200`.
- **Related:** P2 ambiguous glyphs (`audits/02-shell.md:5889`), VIS-LEFTOVERS-9 and UX-PRAYER-5 (not re-filed). New: the cross-app collisions.

#### VIS-ICON-1 — Text glyphs and colour emoji stand in for icons in six areas (investigator rating: low)

Glyphs render in the OS text font and emoji in the platform's colour set, so they take no token colour, weight or dark variant. Even the split between glyph and emoji depends on the platform: in the rig's WebKit, ⛰ and ✝ render as colour emoji, and repainting them changes 0 px (skeptic 1 of P4-ICON-03).

Where they appear:

| Shell | ★ ✓ | `index.html:916, 1065, 1068, 1169, 1187, 1358, 1478` |
| F260 | 12 glyphs and 6 emoji kinds | `apps/f260.html:603-620, 704, 1219-1232, 1510, 1586` |
| Tally | + − | `apps/tally.html:137-140` |
| Kid Verse | − + ★ ✓ | `apps/kidverse.html:160, 359, 369, 663` |
| Both Dollywood exports | 21 glyphs and 5 emoji | `apps/dollywood-live.html:584, 588, 621, 647, 961, 1285, 1532, 1564` |

F260's unearned milestones mix colour emoji at opacity .55 with grey text glyphs (✎ at 1.98-2.01 in the light palettes).

- **Expected:** control and status icons come from the one SVG set, and emoji are used only for faces.
- **Evidence:** `static.json` (`<area>.glyphs`, `<area>.emoji`); `audits/screens/f260/milestones-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`; `measure-hearth.json` f260 `div.mi` items.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/static.mjs`, then inspect `static.json`.
- **Related:** VIS-F260-12, VIS-KIDVERSE-9, VIS-DOLLYWOOD-8, `audits/03-apps/dollywood-live.md:778` and `audits/03-apps/tally.md:675` (not re-filed). This entry adds only the cross-area count.

#### GAP-ICON-1 — The design system has no icon tokens, size scale, weight rule, ink rule or shared sprite, and the style guide shows one glyph (investigator rating: medium)

What `design.css` has:
- `.icon` at 24 / 32 px with a 1.75 stroke (`apps/design.css:602-603`);
- the `.duo` fill (`:605`, broken through `<use>`, P4-ICON-02);
- `.app-icon` (`:606-609`);
- `.btn .icon` at 1.25em (`:371`), `.tab .icon` at 26 px (`:563`) and `.empty .icon` at 48 px (`:546`).

What is missing:
- **A size scale.** The shell renders 14-53 px in 11 sizes; F260 renders 16-64 px.
- **A stroke rule.** Nothing keeps the rendered stroke constant: it runs 1.02-3.85 px in the shell.
- **An ink rule for icons on a tint.** `.app-icon` paints the base `--tint` (P4-ICON-01, -03).
- **Dark values for app and person colours.**
- **Kid and TV icon sizes.** The kid tab icons stay at 26 px.
- **A sprite apps can load.** The sprite lives inline in `index.html` only.
- **A themed select chevron.** The chevron is `#7D6F62` in a data URI (`:449`). It passes at 3.34-4.75 but never follows the theme.

The style guide's Icons section is four copies of `#i-plus`, each on a hex `--tint` (`docs/design.html:241-247`).

- **Evidence:** the cited lines; `rollup.json` `renderedSizesPx`, `strokePxMin`/`strokePxMax`.
- **Reproduction:** `grep -n "icon" apps/design.css`; `sed -n 241,247p docs/design.html`; `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/report.mjs`.

#### GAP-ICON-2 — A custom shell set rather than one open-source set; Lucide and Feather paths ship without their licence notice (investigator rating: low)

- **The shell set is custom.** The shell and tile icons are hand drawn, not Lucide or Phosphor.
- **Open-source paths ship without a notice.**
  - The Larder inlines Lucide ("Lucide glyphs, inlined", `apps/leftovers.html:148`).
  - F260's lock, book, book-open, edit-3, settings and chevron symbols match Feather / Lucide by visual inspection (`apps/f260.html:531-541`); they were not diffed against upstream.
  - Neither ships the ISC or MIT notice. A repo grep for Lucide, Feather, ISC and licence finds only that comment and the Dollywood 3D bundle's MIT header (`apps/dollywood.html:1744-1746`).
- **Clean on Apple assets.** No SF Symbols and no SF Pro are shipped.

### Checked and not a bug

No filed finding was refuted. The claims below were checked and dropped or corrected:

- **"Home Stars/Kids star heads fail at 2.76 in Hearth" (draft P4-ICON-03).** Refuted: `index.html:199` paints them with `--gold-ink`, at 5.33-5.34 (both skeptics, the re-measure and `measure-hearth.json`).
- **"F260 ⛰ milestone fails at 2.71 as gold ink."** A rig artefact: ⛰ (and 📖 🔥 💯 ✝) render as colour emoji in WebKit on Windows, and repainting the ink changes 0 px (skeptic 1 of P4-ICON-03).
- **"The F260 week-done tick is 1.78-2.59 in every palette" (draft §3, §4, §8).** It is under 3:1 only in the light palettes.
  - Measured on rendered pixels: 2.30 / 2.60 / 2.46 in light, 4.17 / 4.23 in dark.
  - The draft's formula mixed the tick colour into a disc that is already dimmed by the row's group opacity, so it counted the dimming twice.
  - The token calculation (`[26,23,20]` on `[106,129,90]`, 4.1:1) and the investigator's own `peak` field agree with the re-measure.
  - F260's under-3:1 counts in dark fall from 76 to 3.

- **"Gold icons fail in Parchment and Frost."** Not filed: at the median they pass (3.09-3.11 and 3.21-3.30). They dip under 3:1 only at the 22 % end of the `.app-icon` gradient (2.87 and 2.97).
- **"The compass needle is the only cue for north."** Wrong: the 9 px "N" label rotates with the button at 4.37-4.77:1 (both P4-ICON-04 skeptics).
- **"TV heads never get the duotone."** Wrong for the TV "Stars this week" head, which is inline `ICON_STAR` and renders it (both P4-ICON-02 skeptics and the re-measure).
- **"`--gold-ink` is a missing token" (draft token gap 3).** It exists in every palette (`apps/design.css:74, 124, 144, 164, 206`). The gap is the rule that `.app-icon` uses the base hue.
- **The select chevron `#7D6F62`.** Not a contrast defect: 3.34-4.75 in every palette. It is listed only as a theming gap (GAP-ICON-1).
- **The Hearth Kid Verse tile at 2.76 and the Midnight adult tiles at 1.95-2.93.** Already in Phase 2 (`audits/02-shell.md:5843, 5885`), so they are not re-filed and serve as the baseline for P4-ICON-01.
- **SF Symbols or SF Pro shipped.** None found (GAP-ICON-2 grep).

### Method, scripts and evidence

**Investigator scripts** (`audits/tools/phase4/ICON/`):

| Script | What it does | Output (`audits/evidence/p4/ICON/`) |
|---|---|---|
| `static.mjs` | Static inventory of every `<svg>`/`<symbol>`, `<use>` reference, stroke-width value, icon-like Unicode glyph and emoji in `index.html`, `apps/design.css`, `apps/hub.js` and the nine apps. Lines over 20 000 chars (the Dollywood payload and the 3D bundle) are scanned for counts only | `static.json` |
| `measure.mjs <theme> [surfaces]` | Rendered inventory on 28 surfaces (10 shell, 18 app; adult and kid; iPad portrait, iPhone PWA, TV). Records every visible SVG (size, viewBox, computed stroke, paint, cap, duotone declared/rendered, control name and size) and every icon glyph drawn as text. Contrast is the computed paint over the median background pixel with the icons hidden (`declared`), plus the strongest rendered pixel (`peak`) | `measure-{hearth,parchment,frost,midnight,forest}.json` |
| `report.mjs` | Roll-up: area × metric, every icon under 3:1 per theme, icon-only controls under 44 × 44 | `rollup.json`, `below3.json`, `small-targets.json` |
| `duo-sprite.mjs [webkit\|chromium]` | Draws `#i-home` at 192 px via `<use>` and inline, and samples the interior | `duo-sprite-{webkit,chromium}.json/.png` |
| `facets.mjs` | Presentation attributes vs computed style for every `svg.icon` in Kid Verse and Verses | `facets.json` |
| `shots.mjs` | The cited 1× screenshots | `shot-*.png` |

**Skeptic scripts:** `verify-<key>-1.mjs` and `verify-<key>-2.mjs` for each confirmed finding, in the same folder. Their outputs are `verify-*.json` and `verify-*.png` in `audits/evidence/p4/ICON/`.

**Re-measure** (`audits/tools/phase4/ICON/remeasure.mjs`; outputs `remeasure-{hearth,parchment,frost,midnight,forest}.json`) uses a different method from the investigator's:
- The icon colour is the computed paint.
- The background is sampled in bands outside the icon box, on the rendered chip or button, at device pixels; the fallback is the most common colour inside the box.
- `pix` is the contrast of the strongest pixel actually drawn inside the icon box.
- It also sweeps icon sizes and computed strokes, and pixel-tests the sprite duotone.
- It ran in WebKit only, with the theme applied and confirmed on every surface.

Tolerances: contrast within 0.15 and on the same side of 3:1; stroke within 0.05 px; counts and size sets must match exactly.

**Limits:**
- Real devices were not used. Emoji and SF glyphs render in Segoe on the rig, and the rig's WebKit has no backdrop blur.
- Kid profiles were measured as Ezra only.
- Sheets and dialogs were not swept.
- The rig's `nontext.json` does not exist, so no cross-check against Phase 1 was possible.
- This dimension did not use the shared Phase 4 measure dataset (`audits/evidence/p4/measure/`).

Every run was local, and `L.close()` ran in a `finally` block in every script.

## Glass and material (GLASS)

Baseline: the working tree at fe6041d (no app file has changed since). Everything ran on the local rig (`audits/tools/lib/local.mjs`, variant `typical`). No request went to production, and no PIN or pairing code was read or used. Where glass is and what it computes was read in WebKit, the iOS engine, and in Chromium. Anything that depends on the blur being painted (cost, legibility over a real blur, pixel diffs) was measured in Chromium only: the rig's WebKit on Windows computes `backdrop-filter` but does not paint it (`audits/01-capture.md` §3). Every cost figure is headless Chrome 154 on a Windows desktop with an RTX 4080 SUPER, so only the ratios between arms are claimed, never the iPad's absolute cost.

The bar (house style, `audits/HUB-AUDIT-PROMPT.md:80-87`): Liquid Glass on the navigation and control layer only (tab bars, toolbars, floating buttons, sheets, the profile switcher), content cards solid, content visibly scrolling beneath the glass, Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast honoured with an in-app toggle, and few layers, with frame rate and CPU measured.

The system (`apps/design.css:387-404`): one recipe shared by `.glass, .card.glass, .glass-strong, .btn-glass, .pill, .topbar, .tabbar, .sheet`. It has a specular gradient (`--glass-spec`), an accent pickup radial at `var(--sheen-x)`, a fill `--g` (`--glass` .62-.66 alpha or `--glass-strong` .84-.86), a 1 px `--glass-edge`, a five-part shadow stack and `backdrop-filter: blur(var(--blur)) saturate(1.4) brightness(1.02)`. `--blur` is 18 px, and 28 px in kiosk mode (`:285-288`). A perf guard strips the blur from `.ds .card.glass` and `.ds .glass-lite` (`:399-401`), and an `@supports not` fallback sets a 96 % surface (`:402-404`). hub.js drifts `--sheen-x` with scroll, and with tilt where no permission prompt is needed; it is off under Reduce Motion (`apps/hub.js:439-453`). Every palette sets its own glass tokens (`apps/design.css:120-273`).

**Summary**

- **The costliest thing about the glass is the sheen, not the blur (P4-GLASS-01, low, 2/2).**
  - hub.js writes `--sheen-x` on `<html>` from a scroll-driven rAF. Each write is an inherited custom-property change, so it restyles the whole document: 5,572 elements per write in F260, 731 on Home, 164 in Prayer.
  - Dropping only those writes cuts scroll CPU 31-57 % (re-measure 36-61 %) and main-thread time 2.0-4.1× in all 8 scrolling scenes. Turning every `backdrop-filter` off moves scroll CPU only −19 % to +10 % (re-measure −9 % to +12 %).
  - F260 Today, a document with no blurred glass of its own on screen, drops frames for it: p95 frame 24-32.5 ms and 8-14 % of frames over 20 ms, against 17-18 ms and 0-4 % with the sheen off.
  - A registered non-inherited `@property` does not fix it (both skeptics tested it).
- **The perf guard follows one class name, not the role (P4-GLASS-02, low, 2 of 3).** `.card.glass-strong` keeps its live blur, and the documented escape hatch `.glass-lite` has 0 uses anywhere. It bites where the guard's own trigger is met: the Verses trainer card is a live blur in a page that scrolls (VIS-VERSES-2 owns that instance).
- **Three live blurs sit under fills that hide them (P4-GLASS-03, low, 2/2).** They are Prayer's accent FAB (alpha 1) and the park map's north button (alpha 1), where removing the blur changes 0 pixels of the fill, and the build guide's 96 % steps sheet on phones. The north button is solid only because a generic button reset out-specifies its glass rule, so it also loses the look its sibling buttons keep.
- **Two small, measured glass costs (P4-GLASS-04, P4-GLASS-05, low).** The TV board's Switch is the only live blur on the board, against the board's own no-blur rule; the size of its cost is disputed (+7 % to +44 % of about 0.04 cores). Tally's five content-glass layers add 8-31 % to a burst of + taps, not the 52 % first measured; the press animation costs more than the glass does.
- **Across areas (not adversarially verified):**
  - The recipe is re-typed 17 times in 5 source files, in three filter variants (CONS-GLASS-1).
  - Tally, Kid Verse, Verses, Timer and the build guide put live glass on content in 48-100 % of their screens, while F260, the Larder, Prayer and the park map keep it on the control layer (CONS-GLASS-2).
  - Glass is nested in glass on the park map's ride card and in Prayer's sheet (VIS-GLASS-1), and the app viewer's bar is glass with nothing ever passing beneath it (VIS-GLASS-2).
  - No glass surface responds to Reduce Transparency or Increase Contrast, in any area (GAP-GLASS-1): 0 of 214 glass elements change with the preference emulated and matching.
- **What works.**
  - With a real 18 px blur, the tab bar's and Prayer's nav labels pass AA (worst decile 4.91-5.26), so Phase 2's "Apps" 3.78 and VIS-PRAYER-1's provisional dark nav-label figure are no-blur artefacts.
  - Static glass is free at idle.
  - The TV panes keep the look with no blur of their own.
  - Four areas place glass exactly as the house style asks.
- **Re-measure.** 14 key numbers were re-measured independently: 12 agree and 2 do not (Tally's tap cost and the style-recalc range). Seven more draft figures contradicted the investigator's own raw data. All of these corrections are applied below.
