Score the shared template once with the build guide (P3 calibration note). | `press.json`, `park-live.json`, `reduced-motion.json` |
| Kid Verse | 5 | **Hold at 5 (or 4).** Every kid control presses (.96), and confetti and the pulse respect Reduce Motion. New: CLS 0.073 / 0.163 when the story section collapses and the actions drop 23 / 85 px. That happens on every slow first pull and only sometimes at 150 ms latency. | `press.json`, `cls-held.json`, `remeasure-cls-kidverse*.json`, `reduced-motion.json` |
| Verses | 4 | **Hold at 4.** Both controls press (.96) and CLS is ≤ 0.003. A slow first pull shows a blank page (text length 0), and the next verse still replaces instantly (P3). | `press.json`, `cls-held.json` |
| Native feel, all areas | — | Supports P2's "spinners instead of skeletons: mixed". Only the shell shows skeletons (2 surfaces); every app shows a blank, a false zero or a finished-looking page while loading. | `cls-held.json` `loadingAt1200` |

### Confirmed defects

All four were adversarially verified: for each, two skeptics re-read the code, wrote their own scripts and re-ran the measurement. Severities follow the Phase 2 rule (`audits/02-shell.md:25-37`). All four are low under "cosmetic or an edge case", and neither skeptic of any of them rated it otherwise.

#### P4-MOTION-01 — The Apps grid blanks and pops back in every 30 s while it is on screen

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** cosmetic. No data is lost, no flow breaks, and every tile comes back within about 0.56 s and stays tappable.
  - **Exposure:** any device left on the Apps tab, adult or kid. A kid's Home points to Apps, so a kid's iPad is the likeliest. It does not show under Reduce Motion: design.css cuts the animation to 0.01 ms, although the grid is still rebuilt. Under Reduce Motion the shell is blank anyway (P2-STAB-01).
- **Areas:** shell (Apps tab).
- **What happens.**
  - **The entrance.** `#grid` is a `.stagger` container (`index.html:380`). `.ds .stagger > *` runs `hub-pop` from opacity 0 and scale .96 / translateY 8 px over 360 ms `--spring`, with delays of 40-200 ms (`apps/design.css:595-599`).
  - **The trigger.** hub.js sets `lastPull` on every successful pull, including pulls that change nothing (`apps/hub.js:311`), and pulls every 30 s (`apps/hub.js:342`). The shell's `onSync` calls `renderGrid()` whenever `lastPull` changes while Apps is showing (`index.html:1242-1243`). Its `onChange` does the same for any f260 or leftovers change (`index.html:1240`).
  - **The rebuild.** `renderGrid()` replaces the grid with `grid.innerHTML` (`index.html:706`). The new markup is byte-identical, but the nodes are new, so every tile restarts the entrance.
  - **What it looks like.** In the first frame after each rebuild every tile is at opacity 0. The later tiles stay at 0 until their delay runs out, and the whole replay lasts about 560 ms. Home and the TV board do not do this.
- **Expected.** Entrance motion runs once per mount or tab entry, never when the same content is re-rendered from a background pull. Unchanged tiles stay put.
- **Why it matters.** The iPad sits open all day. A grid that empties and refills twice a minute reads as a glitch and draws the eye from across the room.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator:
    - `audits/evidence/p4/MOTION/replay.json`: Apps 18 `hub-pop` starts at 28 s and 58 s of a 65 s idle; Home 0; TV 0.
    - `replay-shot.json`: before `[1×9]`, mid `[0×9]`, after `[1×9]`.
    - `apps-grid-replay-mid-ipad.png`: only the F260 and Larder tiles are faintly visible; seven tiles are gone.
  - Skeptics: `verify-apps-grid-replays-entrance-every-pull-1.json` and `-1-mid.png`, `verify-apps-grid-replays-entrance-every-pull-2.json` and `-2-mid.png` (the Apps page with a title and a tab bar but no tiles).
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-replay.json`, `remeasure-tiles.json`.
  - Code: `index.html:380, 706, 1240, 1242-1243`; `apps/design.css:595-599, 611-613`; `apps/hub.js:311, 342`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `node "audits/tools/phase4/MOTION/replay.mjs"`. Expect `apps {"count":18, … "hub-pop on tile":[28,58]}`, with home and tv at 0.
  - `node "audits/tools/phase4/MOTION/replay-shot.mjs"`. Expect all mid opacities 0.
  - Skeptics: `verify-apps-grid-replays-entrance-every-pull-1.mjs` and `-2.mjs`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** wrote their own WebKit script on the real clock: 65 s idle on `#apps`, with a MutationObserver on `#grid`, `hub.onSync`, a markup comparison, `animationstart` on `.tile` and per-frame opacities. They ran it as Eli on the iPad portrait and as Ezra on the iPhone PWA.
    - Pulls at 28.1 s and 58.1 s. Each time the grid was replaced with byte-identical markup.
    - 18 `hub-pop` starts on the iPad (9 per pull, staggered over 28.1-28.5 s and 58.1-58.5 s). Opacities 30 ms after a replacement were `[0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]`.
    - Ezra's iPhone: the same pulls, 7 tiles, 14 starts.
  - **Skeptic 2** wrote their own WebKit script that does not call `hub.pull()` and waits 66 s for hub.js's own timer. It logs `animationstart` on `#grid` children, node identity and the minimum tile opacity per frame. Three runs: Eli iPad on `#apps`, Ezra iPhone on `#apps`, and Eli iPad on `#home` as the control.
    - Pulls at 29 s and 59 s, with 18 starts. 9 of 9 tiles were near 0 in one frame, and the tile nodes were replaced.
    - Ezra: 14 starts, 7 of 7 tiles near 0.
    - The `#home` control: 0 starts on `#grid`, same nodes.
  - **Re-measure** (capture-phase listener, three devices in parallel, WebKit): 18 starts at 28 s and 58 s, 9 tiles; Home 0; TV 0. After a `hub.pull()`, 9 of 9 tiles were below 0.05 in the first frame that dipped (79 ms), and 20 frames dipped. Agrees.
- **Corrected claim.** Accurate as filed, with four refinements:
  - Each replay lasts about 560 ms (up to 200 ms of delay plus 360 ms).
  - It also fires on any f260 or leftovers change while Apps shows (`index.html:1240`).
  - It reproduces in WebKit on hub.js's natural timer, not only with a manual pull in Chromium.
  - It does not show under Reduce Motion.
- **Related (not re-filed).** No P2 or P3 ID covers it. P2-HOME-04 and P2-SYNC-15 are about cold-load wording, and the Phase 2 grid items (VIS-HOME-1, OK-HOME-6) are about density.

#### P4-MOTION-02 — Closing an app cannot be interrupted: a tap in the 220 ms exit opens nothing, and an app opened in that window is hidden again

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** an edge case. Both triggers are timing windows, nothing is written, and tapping again recovers.
  - **Exposure:** a second tap within 220 ms of leaving an app (Hub, or a tab tap that closes the viewer). Also a notification tapped, or a hash change, while an app is closing. Reduce Motion does not narrow it, because the `setTimeout` stays at 220 ms.
- **Areas:** shell (viewer).
- **What happens.**
  - **Taps are lost.** `closeViewer()` adds `.closing` (`viewer-out`, 220 ms) and schedules a 220 ms `setTimeout` that removes `on` and sets the frame to `about:blank` (`index.html:729-733`). Until then the fading viewer is still `display: flex` at z-index 30 (`index.html:326-328`) and still takes pointer events. A tile tap in that window lands on `iframe#frame`, and nothing opens.
  - **An open in the window is undone.** `openApp()` removes `.closing` and adds `on` (`index.html:721, 725`) but never clears the pending timeout, which then fires and hides the app it just opened.
    - The routes in: `hashchange` (`index.html:650-652`) and the service worker's notification `open` message, which sets `location.hash` (`index.html:1575`; `sw.js:62-69`).
    - The result: viewer class `''`, `display: none`, frame `about:blank`, while the hash still names the app.
    - The person is left on the Apps grid with the Apps tab highlighted (`verify-viewer-exit-not-interruptible-1-hash-during-exit-ipad.png`).
    - Skeptic 1 noted (not re-measured) that `current` stays set to the hidden app.
  - **A close during the open restarts from full opacity.** `viewer-out` has only a `to` keyframe (`index.html:330`), so a close during `viewer-in` starts again from opacity 1 / scale 1. The spring is nearly finished by 120 ms (opacity 0.87-0.93), so the snap there is 0.07-0.13. A visible snap (about 0.39) happens only when the close comes within about 70 ms of the open.
- **Expected.** Transitions are interruptible (house style): a tap during the exit reaches the grid, an open during the exit cancels the pending close, and a close during the open reverses from the current frame.
- **Why it matters.** A quick tap on the next app right after leaving one does nothing. A notification tapped just as an app closes shows the grid instead of the app it named.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `audits/evidence/p4/MOTION/viewer.json`.
    - `C_hitAt80ms`: `iframe#frame`.
    - `C_rawTapDuringExit`: nothing opened.
    - `D_hashDuringExit`: `{viewerClass:'', viewerDisplay:'none', frameSrc:'about:blank', hash:'#timer'}`.
    - `E_hashAfter400ms`: Timer opens.
    - `viewer-open-during-exit-ipad.png`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-viewer-exit-not-interruptible-1.json`, `-1-hash-during-exit-ipad.png`, `verify-viewer-exit-not-interruptible-2.json`, `-2-hash-ipad.png`, `-2-t4-chromium.json`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-viewer.json`, `remeasure-interrupt.json`.
  - Code: `index.html:326-330, 650-652, 711-733, 1575`; `sw.js:62-69`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `node "audits/tools/phase4/MOTION/viewer.mjs"` (WebKit, iPad). Read `C_*`, `D_hashDuringExit` and `E_hashAfter400ms`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-viewer-exit-not-interruptible-1.mjs` and `-2.mjs` (the latter with `--t4-chromium` for the mid-open close).
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** re-read `index.html:326-330, 634-635, 650-652, 712-733, 1575` and `sw.js:62-69`. Their own script ran WebKit on the iPad portrait as Eli, on the real clock, with two app pairs: Prayer → Leftovers and Tally → Timer.
    - Raw taps: 6 of 6 taps 72-196 ms into the exit hit `iframe#frame` and opened nothing. Controls at 306 ms and 321 ms opened normally.
    - Hash opens: 4 of 4 at 68-164 ms ended hidden (class `''`, `display: none`, `about:blank`, hash `#leftovers` or `#timer`). Controls at 313 ms and 317 ms opened.
    - Mid-open close (Chromium, with the values read synchronously around the close in one task): at 67 ms, opacity 0.606 / scale 0.961 → 1 / 1 (a jump of 0.394); at 133 ms, 0.931 / 0.993 → 1 / 1 (0.069); at 216 ms, no jump.
  - **Skeptic 2** re-read the same code plus `apps/design.css:107-109`, and computed `--spring` numerically. Their own script ran WebKit on the iPad.
    - Taps 60 ms and 150 ms after Hub landed on `iframe#frame[tally]` and opened nothing. At 260 ms Timer opened.
    - `location.hash='#leftovers'` 80 ms into the exit opened Leftovers (class `on`, src set at 140 ms). At 1 s it was hidden: class `''`, `display: none`, `about:blank`, hash `#leftovers`.
    - A same-app hash (`#tally`) inside the window also ended hidden.
    - A close at exactly 120 ms could not be landed: headless WebKit ran about 6 rAFs in 700 ms, and Chromium's first rAF after 120 ms came at about 390 ms. By the curve, `viewer-in` is at opacity 0.886 / scale 0.989 at 120 ms.
  - **Re-measure** (WebKit, and Chromium for the snap):
    - 80 ms: class `''`, `display: none`, `about:blank`, hash `#timer`; a hit test on a tile at 80 ms lands on `iframe#frame`. 400 ms: Timer opens. Agrees.
    - The snap: the close fired at 125 ms (iPad) and 129 ms (desktop): opacity 0.873 → 1.0 and 0.93 → 1.0, jumps of 0.127 and 0.07. **Disagrees** with the draft's 0.52.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - The first two facets reproduce exactly.
  - The third is overstated. The draft's "opacity 0.48 → 1, jump 0.52 at 120 ms" compared a sample at 55 ms with the close at 212 ms, a 157 ms gap with no samples in `interrupt.json`. The real snap is 0.07-0.13 at 120 ms and about 0.39 only within about 70 ms of the open.
  - "Lands on an empty screen" should read "lands on the Apps grid, with the hash naming the hidden app".
- **Related (not re-filed).** Phase 2 notes that the spring "cannot be interrupted" (`audits/02-shell.md:5895`) without an ID. P2-STAB-01 (Reduce Motion blanks the hub) is a different defect.

#### P4-MOTION-03 — Park map on a park day: four infinite pulses keep the main thread 17-28 % busy while the map sits open; the two `box-shadow` rings drive it

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** a cost only (battery and heat). Nothing is wrong on screen and no flow breaks. It matches the precedent P3-DOLLYWOOD-08, the build guide's pulse, filed low.
  - **Exposure:** park days, with the map located, sharing and in front.
    - Hidden pages do not tick, and the map releases its GPS watch and wake lock when hidden (`apps/dollywood-live.html:1475`).
    - While it watches, its wake lock (`:1400`, requested after `watchPosition` at `:1408`) keeps the screen on, so the cost runs for as long as the map is open.
    - Measured in headless Chromium on a desktop CPU. The rig's WebKit has no CPU metrics.
- **Areas:** dollywood-live; the build guide shares the template. The fix belongs in `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:400, 413` (the same line numbers as the export).
- **What happens.** Four infinite animations run while the person is located and sharing:
  - `mepulse` on two SVG rings: transform and opacity, 2.4 s (`:546, 561-562`).
  - `lvlive` on the live-sharing dot: `box-shadow`, 2 s (`:400-401`).
  - `fabring` on the pressed Find me button: `box-shadow`, 2.2 s (`:413-414`).

  Pausing them one group at a time shows where the cost comes from:
  - The `box-shadow` pulses cannot be composited and force a main-thread frame 60 times a second, at about 6-8 % together.
  - Once those frames run, the SVG rings are re-laid-out on every one. That is 60 layouts a second over a 3,067-node map, and it adds about 14 points.
  - On their own the SVG rings cost 0.1-0.5 % in Chromium, which composites them. WebKit does not composite SVG transform animations, so on an iPhone they probably cost something alone. That was not measured.
- **Expected.** Ambient indicators animate only compositor properties (transform and opacity on HTML layers) and stop after a few cycles or when idle. Pausing when hidden already happens.
- **Why it matters.** On a park day the map is open on phones for hours, with the screen held on. A constant 17-28 % main-thread load drains batteries when the family most needs them.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `audits/evidence/p4/MOTION/park-live.json` and `park-live-located-no-preference-iphone.png`.
    - No preference: 4 running (`mepulse 2400ms` ×2, `lvlive 2000ms`, `fabring 2200ms`), 22.8 % busy, 60 style recalcs a second.
    - Reduce: 0 running, 0.5 %.
  - Skeptics: `verify-park-map-located-idle-pulses-1.json`, `-1-crosscheck.json`, `-1-located.png`, `verify-park-map-located-idle-pulses-2.json`, `-2-chromium-iphone.png`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-park.json`. Not located: `idle.json` (0 %).
  - Code: `apps/dollywood-live.html:400-401, 413-414, 546, 561-562, 1400, 1408, 1475`; `apps/design.css:611-613`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `node "audits/tools/phase4/MOTION/park-live.mjs"` (Chromium, variant `park`, iPhone PWA, GPS granted at map point 762,842). Expect about 20 % busy with 4 infinite animations under no preference, and about 0.5 % with 0 under reduce.
  - Skeptics: `verify-park-map-located-idle-pulses-1.mjs` and `-2.mjs` (with the ablation arms).
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** re-read the CSS. Their own Chromium script used the `park` variant on the real clock, as Eli on the iPhone PWA, with the map standalone, geolocation granted at 762,842 and Find me tapped. It took CDP metric deltas over 8 s idle windows, with control arms for Reduce Motion and not located, and paused each group in turn. The full run was done twice.
    - All four running: 25.0 and 27.3 % (run 1), 17.4 and 21.1 % (run 2), 21.6 then 19.1 % (a fresh-page cross-check). Always 60 recalcs and 60 layouts a second.
    - `mepulse` paused: 5.7-7.8 % (60 recalcs, 0.1 layouts a second). Only `mepulse` running: 0.2-0.5 %.
    - Only `lvlive`: 7.6-7.9 %. Only `fabring`: 5.3-6.1 %. All paused: 0.1-0.6 %.
    - Reduce: 0.6 % with 0 running. Not located: 0.4-0.5 %.
  - **Skeptic 2** wrote their own Chromium script with five 10 s windows on one located page (GPS on, pill "good", Find me pressed, 3,067 SVG nodes).
    - As shipped: 21.1 % (a repeat 21.3 %; an earlier run 28.0 then 26.3 %), 60 recalcs and 60.1 layouts a second.
    - All paused: 0.3 %. `mepulse` only: 0.1 %, 0 recalcs a second. The two `box-shadow` pulses only: 8.3 %, 59 recalcs and 0.3 layouts a second.
    - Reduce: 0 running, 0.5 %.
    - A WebKit arm: the same four animations running, each `currentTime` advancing 3041 ms in 3 s.
  - **Re-measure:** no preference 19.4 %, 60 recalcs a second, 4 infinite (`mepulse` ×2, `lvlive`, `fabring`); reduce 0 %, 0 running. Agrees within the ±30 % tolerance, under a parallel load.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - The busy figure is 17-28 % across runs (22.8 % in the investigator's), against about 0.5 % when not located or under Reduce Motion.
  - The mechanism is narrower than filed: the two `box-shadow` rings are the driver. Replacing them with transform/opacity rings would bring the idle page back to about 0.5 % while keeping the SVG pulse.
  - "Pause when hidden" is already provided.
  - The battery claim holds for as long as the map is in front, which the wake lock keeps it.
- **Related (not re-filed).** P3-DOLLYWOOD-08 (the build guide's `hlring` pulse, `apps/dollywood.html`) and P3-DOLLYWOOD-09 (the 3D render loop) are different animations in a different file. Phase 3 mentioned these park-map animations only in its rubric, as a Reduce Motion problem (`audits/03-apps/dollywood-live.md:734, 782`), which the runtime contradicts (see Checked and not a bug).

#### P4-MOTION-04 — JS smooth scrolls still animate under Reduce Motion: F260 ×8, the build guide ×2, the park map ×1

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** an edge case. It is a comfort miss under an accessibility preference: each scroll still lands in the right place and lasts under a second, and WCAG 2.3.3 (animation from interactions) is AAA.
  - **Exposure:** people with Reduce Motion on. Today these scrolls run only with an app opened standalone, because the shell is blank under Reduce Motion (P2-STAB-01).
- **Areas:** f260, dollywood, dollywood-live.
- **What happens.**
  - The CSS Reduce Motion rules cover transitions and animations only (`apps/design.css:611-613`, `apps/f260.html:476`, `apps/dollywood*.html:139`).
  - These scrolls pass `behavior: 'smooth'` with no check:
    - F260 `apps/f260.html:1474` (Reflect, whose button is hidden on the typical seed until there are reflections, `:1437`), `1691`, `1693`, `1700`, `1704`, `1705`, `1736` and `1985`.
    - The build guide `apps/dollywood.html:1127, 1140`.
    - The park map `apps/dollywood-live.html:1127`. Its `:1140` `mapIntoView` never scrolls, because `PHONE()` requires `FLAVOR === 'hub'` (`:689`) and the live file sets `FLAVOR = 'live'` (`:688`).
  - Neither engine ties `behavior: 'smooth'` to `prefers-reduced-motion` (emulated).
  - The template's own `setView` does skip its tween under reduce (`:813`), so the intent is in the code.
  - The scrolls a household member reaches daily are F260's Today, week and read-mode jumps: 1691, 1693, 1704, 1705 and 1736.
- **Expected.** Under Reduce Motion a scroll jumps (`behavior: 'auto'`).
- **Why it matters.** Long animated scrolls are the motion most likely to trouble someone who turned Reduce Motion on, and F260 runs them on every week jump.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `audits/evidence/p4/MOTION/rm-smooth.json` (the WebKit reduce arm has 2 frames between 193 and 1302 px; Chromium reduce 35) and `static-motion.json` `detail.f260.js.smoothScroll` (8 lines).
  - Skeptics: `verify-smooth-scroll-ignores-reduced-motion-1.json`, `-2.json`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-smooth.json`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `node "audits/tools/phase4/MOTION/rm-smooth.mjs"` fires F260's Reflect jump under reduce. Expect intermediate scroll positions in both engines.
  - Skeptics: `verify-smooth-scroll-ignores-reduced-motion-1.mjs` and `-2.mjs`, each with a `behavior: 'auto'` control.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** re-read every cited line and the template (`template.html:1125, 1138`). Their own script opened F260 standalone as Eli on the iPhone PWA, in WebKit and Chromium, under reduce and no preference. It recorded every `scroll` event for three cases: a real tap on `#reflectBtn` (unhidden for the test), a window-top smooth scroll as at `:1736`, and an `overflow-x` scroll as the Dollywood chips do at `:1127`. Each case also ran with `'auto'` as the control.
    - `matchMedia` was true under reduce.
    - WebKit reduce: 3 events over 269 ms (Reflect), 228 ms (window top) and 220 ms (chips). The `'auto'` control: 1 event, 0 ms.
    - Chromium reduce: 23, 38 and 34 events over 367, 616 and 550 ms.
    - No preference had the same shape.
  - **Skeptic 2** re-read the same lines and grepped the other apps and `index.html` (no smooth scrolls there). Their own script sampled with rAF and a 4 ms interval over F260 Reflect, the F260 window-top scroll and the build-guide chips (`dollywood.html:1127`), with an `'auto'` control.
    - WebKit reduce: 0 → 83 → 1221 → 1302 px over 245 ms; 4920 → 4007 → 1744 → 320 → 0 over 257 ms; chips 0 → 14 → 1027 over 292 ms.
    - Chromium: 35, 51 and 29 intermediate positions over 593, about 880 and 524 ms.
    - `'auto'`: 0 intermediate positions, final in 0-16 ms.
    - They also found that the park map's `:1140` is unreachable.
  - **Re-measure** (a second code path, F260's year-grid jump at `:1700`, sampled every 8 ms): Chromium 48 intermediate positions under reduce (44 with no preference); WebKit 4 (3). Agrees qualitatively.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - **The park map.** It has one reachable ungated scroll, not two.
  - **The Dollywood facet.** It is not new. Phase 3 recorded it without an ID (`audits/03-apps/dollywood.md:867, 929`; `audits/00-inventory.md:4191`), and P3-DOLLYWOOD-08 (the pulse) is the wrong related ID.
  - **What is new.** The F260 facet (Phase 3 wrote that F260 "honours" Reduce Motion, `audits/03-apps/f260.md:776, 863`, which is true for CSS only), the cross-area pattern and the two-engine measurement.
  - **The WebKit frame counts.** They do not separate reduce from no preference on their own: the investigator's no-preference arm had 1. The `'auto'` controls do separate them, since a jump has 0 intermediate positions and takes 0-16 ms. The claim therefore holds in both engines.
- **Related (not re-filed).** `audits/03-apps/dollywood.md:867, 929` (prose). The Dollywood fix belongs in `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:1125, 1138`.

### Consistency, visual and gap findings

These items were not adversarially verified. The evidence is the investigator's static and rendered inventory, spot-checked by the section writer against the cited lines and the raw JSON. Where the re-measure disagreed, its correction is applied.

#### CONS-MOTION-1 — Press feedback is complete in the `.ds` areas, partial or absent elsewhere, with nine scales and no brightness shift anywhere (investigator rating: low)

- **Coverage.**
  - Complete in the `.ds` areas: Tally 3/3, Timer 8/8, Kid Verse 2/2, Verses 2/2, the kid Home 6/6, and the shell 65/68 (86-100 % per surface).
  - Partial or absent elsewhere:
    - F260 57/103 (0 ms; the Plan/Journal switch and the 43 journal-bar books have none).
    - The Larder 8/12, background only.
    - Prayer 12/19. The primary Pray now and More only move 1 px (`button.act:active { transform: translateY(1px) }`, `apps/prayer.html:196`), and Mine/Family and the 5 bottom-nav tabs have nothing.
    - The build guide 0/16.
    - The park map 2/9 (the two FABs, .92, `apps/dollywood-live.html:409-411`).
  - Table MOTION-3 has the per-surface detail.
- **Form.** Nine scales, three press durations (0 ms, 150-180 ms, 220 ms `--spring`), and no brightness shift on any surface. The rules live in `apps/design.css:359, 468, 562`, `index.html:45, 187, 225, 291, 336, 352` and `apps/prayer.html:94, 196`, with nothing shared outside `.ds`.
- **Expected (house style).** Every tappable control scales to about 0.97 with a slight brightness shift, immediately, from one shared rule.
- **Why it matters.** Taps with no visible response invite double taps, as with Prayer's main button and every build-guide control. Several apps punish double taps (P3-LEFTOVERS-01, P3-VERSES-12).
- **Evidence:** `press.json`, `remeasure-press.json`, `curves.json` (`pressAfterTap`).
- **Reproduction:** `node "audits/tools/phase4/MOTION/press.mjs"`. It prints `== <surface>: N controls, … with press feedback` and one line per control kind.
- **Related:** P2 press scales (`audits/02-shell.md:5896, 6038`); VIS-TALLY-7 (Tally's `:active`-only feedback).

#### CONS-MOTION-2 — F260, Prayer, the Dollywood template, Kid Verse and the Larder use no duration tokens: 93 literal durations, two different overshoot "springs" (investigator rating: info)

- **Token share of durations** (Table MOTION-1; exact in the re-measure):
  - Token areas: design.css 21/24, shell 19/23, Tally 5/5, Timer 5/7, Verses 2/3.
  - No tokens: F260 0/32 (14 durations, 0-3400 ms), Prayer 0/34 (11 durations, 160-1000 ms), each Dollywood export 0/22 (9 durations, 150-2400 ms), Kid Verse 0/3 and the Larder 0/2. Kid Verse and the Larder each use one easing token (`--ease-out`).
  - Totals: 88 literal durations in F260, Prayer and the template, 91 with Kid Verse and 93 with the Larder.
- **A second, stronger "spring".** `cubic-bezier(.3,1.6,.5,1)` (11 % overshoot) sits in F260 (`:137, 258, 274, 294`) and Prayer (`:98`) beside `--spring` (5.3 %).
- **The park-map FAB.** Its curve is the literal `cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1)`: `--ease`'s value written out, not the token. `curves.json` labels it "150ms --ease", and that label is wrong.
- **Dead or odd tokens.** `--dur` has 0 uses, `--ease-out` is identical to `--ease`, `--ease-in-out` has 1 use (`index.html:328`), and `--dur-3` (360 ms) sits outside the 200-350 ms house range.
- **Expected.** All durations and easings come from the token set (CLAUDE.md: every value a design.css token).
- **Why it matters.** The same gesture feels different app to app, and a retune of the tokens would reach only five areas.
- **Evidence:** `static-motion.json` summary, `remeasure-static.json`, `curves.json`; `apps/design.css:105-109`.
- **Reproduction:** `node "audits/tools/phase4/MOTION/static-motion.mjs"`.

#### CONS-MOTION-3 — Four sheet implementations and three toast systems; none follows the finger, and only one animates out (investigator rating: low)

- **Sheets** (Table MOTION-4):
  - The shell's `.ds .sheet` rises 24 px over 360 ms and is removed in one frame.
  - Prayer's sheet slides 28 px over 320 ms and vanishes.
  - F260's centred modal rises 6 px over 250 ms over an instant scrim, and vanishes.
  - The Dollywood pair use a persistent detent sheet that changes detent on a flick of more than 40 px at `pointerup` but never tracks the finger.
  - Grabbers are drawn with no drag in the shell (below 720 px) and in Prayer.
  - At 720 px and wider the shell's sheet is a centred card without a grabber that still rises from below (`apps/design.css:587`). The draft's "on iPad … with a grabber" is wrong: the grabber is hidden there.
- **Toasts:**
  - `hub.toast`: a bottom glass pill, spring in, no exit, no action, 2.2 s (`apps/hub.js:431-435`). Used by the shell, Kid Verse (11 calls) and Verses (4).
  - F260's own top dark pill fades in and out over 3.4 s (`apps/f260.html:416-418`).
  - Prayer's own bottom dark pill has an Undo action and no exit, 6 s (`apps/prayer.html:254-259, 1142-1150`).
- **Undo.** Only Prayer's toast can carry an action. F260's Undo is a separate button in the Today card (`apps/f260.html:574`), so undo exists in only two apps.
- **Expected (house style).** One sheet that slides up, drags to dismiss following the finger and animates out, and one toast with an optional Undo and an animated exit, both from the SDK.
- **Why it matters.** Grabbers that do nothing and dialogs that blink away are web tells. Every other app would have to build its own toast to offer undo.
- **Evidence:** `viewer.json` `F_sheet` (`hub-fade` 220 ms, `hub-rise` 360 ms, 0 backdrops after 16 ms), `remeasure-viewer.json` `sheetExit`, `static-motion.json`; `audits/screens/prayer/mark-answered-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`; `audits/screens/f260/done-toast-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png`.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - P2 VIS "Sheets have a grabber but no drag, and no exit animation" (`audits/02-shell.md:5898-5901`, the shell facet).
  - P2 GAP-02 (chat actions neither confirmed nor undoable, `audits/02-shell.md:4399`).
  - F260's "modals that fade and rise 6 px instead of sliding up" (`audits/03-apps/f260.md:776`).

#### CONS-MOTION-4 — No shared loading state: skeletons only in the shell; a slow first pull shows blanks, false zeros or finished-looking pages (investigator rating: low)

- **What shows** (Table MOTION-5), 1.2 s into a cold load with the first pull held:
  - Skeletons appear only in the shell: 1 on Home, 1 on Me. There are none in any app or on the TV.
  - Blank pages: Prayer's kid page and Verses (text length 0).
  - Chrome only: Prayer's adult page.
  - False values: Tally "0", Timer "5:00 … Start", F260 "0/5" and "0 of 260 readings", shell Home "All quiet in the house." and "Week 1 of 52", and the TV "Week 1".
  - Finished-looking: the build guide.
  - Placeholders: Kid Verse's "…".
  - No area shows a data spinner.
- **The primitive is missing.** hub.js has no public "this scope has been pulled" signal. The shell re-implements one privately (`cached()`, `index.html:888-889`), and `.ds .skeleton` (`apps/design.css:539-544`) is used by no app.
- **Expected (house style).** Skeletons at the final size until a scope has been pulled, then content in place: skeletons, not spinners or false empties.
- **Why it matters.** The false values are the visible face of the data-loss defects on a slow first load (P3-TALLY-02, P3-KIDVERSE-01 and -03, P3-VERSES-03, P2-SYNC-17). The screen invites a tap on wrong data.
- **Evidence:** `cls-held.json` `loadingAt1200`, `remeasure-cls.json` `at1200`; `audits/screens/prayer/kid-loading-iphone-pwa-light.png`, `audits/screens/verses/trainer-loading-iphone-pwa-light.png`, `audits/screens/tally/main-loading-iphone-pwa-light.png`, `audits/screens/shell/home-loading-ipad-portrait-light.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `node "audits/tools/phase4/MOTION/cls.mjs" held`. It prints `| 1.2s: skel N … pulled false "<text>"` per surface.
- **Related (not re-filed):** P2-SYNC-15, P2-HOME-04, P2-VIS-04, P2-VIS-07, P2-SYNC-17, UX-F260-5, P3-TALLY-07, P3-LEFTOVERS-05, P3-VERSES-07, P3-TIMER-01, P3-PRAYER-10, UX-KIDVERSE-6, UX-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-3. The new facet is the cross-area count and the missing SDK primitive.

#### CONS-MOTION-5 — Reduce Motion is handled five ways and converges only because design.css's rule is global (investigator rating: info)

- **The five approaches.**
  - design.css has a global rule: `*, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: .01ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; transition: none !important; }` (`apps/design.css:611-613`). Every file links design.css (`apps/*.html`, `<link rel="stylesheet" href="design.css">`; the Dollywood exports at `:683`).
  - F260 and Prayer kill everything again (`apps/f260.html:476`, `apps/prayer.html:384`).
  - The Larder, Tally, Kid Verse and Verses target a few selectors.
  - The Dollywood template kills transitions only (`:139`) and gates its map tween in JS (`:813`).
  - Timer and the shell add nothing.
- **JS gates.** Kid Verse gates its confetti in JS (`:317`). hub.js checks once, for the sheen, with no change listener (`apps/hub.js:442`).
- **Result.** Standalone, every app boots under reduce with 0 running animations and 0 button transitions. The shell and TV stay blank (P2-STAB-01).
- **The global rule also stops the Dollywood loops.** The park map's and build guide's infinite animations stop under reduce, contrary to Phase 3 (see Checked and not a bug).
- **No crossfade.** No area substitutes a crossfade for movement, as Apple's Reduce Motion does.
- **Expected.** One rule in design.css that replaces movement with short crossfades, one live `hub.reducedMotion` flag for JS, and no per-app copies.
- **Why it matters.** Five copies drift. The next app that does not link design.css, or scopes its rule, loses Reduce Motion silently, and JS motion is already missed (P4-MOTION-04).
- **Evidence:** `reduced-motion.json` (dollywood: no preference `['hlring@hl-ring']` → reduce `[]`; shell and TV boot false with the `hub.sheenFrom` TypeError), `park-live.json` (4 → 0), `remeasure-rm.json`.
- **Reproduction:** `node "audits/tools/phase4/MOTION/reduced-motion.mjs"` (WebKit); `node "audits/tools/phase4/MOTION/park-live.mjs"`.
- **Related (not re-filed):** P2-STAB-01 (and its pointer P2-VIS-01).

#### GAP-MOTION-1 — Cold-load layout shift: CLS reads near zero where views are rebuilt with `innerHTML` while blocks move hundreds of pixels, and F260, the Larder and Kid Verse fail CLS outright (investigator rating: low)

- **Undercounted by CLS** (first pull held 2.5 s, Table MOTION-6):
  - Shell Home: CLS 0.025 / 0 while "Around the house" moves 218 / 348 px (iPad / iPhone; 260 / 435 px at 150 ms latency, at CLS 0).
  - The build guide: 0.0001 with an 862 px move.
  - Prayer: 0.006 / 0.020 while Pray now moves 97 / 146 px.
  - The TV: 0.065, with a 155 px rise.
- **Real CLS failures.**
  - F260: 0.604 on the iPad and 0.324 on the iPhone. The iPhone value depends on the browser date, because the content differs by week: with the rig's frozen demo instant it is 0.240, exactly P3's VIS-F260-3. The iPad value is the same under both clocks. So the iPad figure is new and 2.5× P3's, not 3.5×.
  - With a fast pull F260 still moves "Jump to current week" 405 / 598 px at CLS 0.
  - The Larder: 0.086 / 0.159.
  - Kid Verse: 0.073 / 0.163 in every held run, at about 6.1 s.
    - At 150 ms latency it is a race. It fired on both devices in the investigator's run. The re-measure reports it in 2 of 6 runs, and its saved files hold one firing (iPad 0.0734 on the real clock).
    - The shift sources: `section#story` collapses to height 0, while `div.actions`, the Say button and the small line are pushed down 23 px (iPad) and 85 px (iPhone) by content above them. That is consistent with the "…" placeholders filling in. It is not "a story card inserted above the actions" (the draft's mechanism).
- **The system has no stable-height rule** and no placeholder sizing.
- **Expected (house style).** No block moves after first paint. Phase 5 must verify with block positions, not CLS alone.
- **Why it matters.** The primary buttons (Pray now, Kid Verse's action row with Say, the F260 stepper) move under the finger as data lands.
- **Evidence:** `cls-held.json`, `cls-lat150.json`, `remeasure-cls.json`, `remeasure-cls-kidverse.json`, `remeasure-cls-kidverse-realclock.json`, `remeasure-cls-kidverse-f260-realclock.json`; `audits/screens/kidverse/kid-loading-ipad-portrait-dark.png`, `audits/screens/f260/today-loading-iphone-pwa-light.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `node "audits/tools/phase4/MOTION/cls.mjs" lat150`; `node "audits/tools/phase4/MOTION/cls.mjs" held` (Chromium; per surface `CLS … landmark moves … max …px`).
- **Related (not re-filed):** P2-VIS-04, P2-SYNC-15, the P2 GAP "Stable card heights" (`audits/02-shell.md:5909-5912`), VIS-F260-3, UX-KIDVERSE-6, P3-LEFTOVERS-05.

#### GAP-MOTION-2 — There are no springs: every curve is a fixed-duration bezier, and keyframe entrances restart when interrupted (investigator rating: info)

- **The curves.** All 11 bezier curves in use are fixed-duration (Table MOTION-2). `--spring` overshoots 5.3 % and reaches 90 % at 34.4 % of its time; F260 and Prayer's (.3,1.6,.5,1) overshoots 11 %.
- **Keyframe entrances cannot be retargeted:** `viewer-in`, `hub-rise`, `hub-pop`, Prayer's `slide`, F260's `rise`.
  - A dismissal has no exit or replaces the keyframe from its un-animated value (P4-MOTION-02, third facet).
  - Transitions (the tab indicator) do restart from the current value, but with zero velocity.
- **The viewer is asymmetric.** It opens from the tapped tile in 360 ms `--spring` and closes with a 220 ms `--ease-in-out` fade to .94 around the same point, not back into the tile (`index.html:327-330, 718-720`). The duration, curve and path all differ.
- **Layout properties.** The tab indicator animates `left` and `top` (`apps/design.css:567, 575`). It measured fine: 19-23 frames per 360 ms and 0 long tasks (`tabswitch.json`).
- **The positive side.** Presses are fast-in: 79 % of the .96 depth within a 60 ms tap.
- **Expected (house style).** Spring-based, interruptible transitions of 200-350 ms.
- **Why it matters.** It is the most visible "web page" tell in motion. Apple's sheets and zooms follow the finger and reverse mid-flight.
- **Evidence:** `curves.json`, `remeasure-curves.json`, `interrupt.json`, `remeasure-interrupt.json`, `viewer.json` (`A_open` origin); `apps/design.css:105-109`.
- **Reproduction:** `node "audits/tools/phase4/MOTION/curves.mjs"`; `node "audits/tools/phase4/MOTION/interrupt.mjs"`.
- **Related (not re-filed):** P2 "an overshoot curve that cannot be interrupted" (`audits/02-shell.md:5895`); the P2 rubric row (`:5424`).

#### GAP-MOTION-3 — Press states may never show on iPhone or iPad in most areas: few documents register the touch listener iOS needs for `:active` (investigator rating: low; plausible, not verified on a device)

- **The quirk.** iOS Safari applies `:active` on touch only when a touch event listener exists on the element or an ancestor. Each app runs in its own iframe document, so each needs its own listener.
- **Where listeners exist** (`grep -n touchstart`):
  - The shell's `#views` (`index.html:664`).
  - F260's document (`apps/f260.html:2040`, plus the read-mode swipe at `:1742`).
  - Prayer's `#pray` (`apps/prayer.html:1716`).
- **Where they do not:**
  - The shell's picker (`#gate`), tab bar, timer pill and viewer, including its pill (`index.html:366, 393, 404, 406`), all sit outside `#views` (`:375`).
  - Tally, Timer, Verses, Kid Verse, the Larder and the park map register none.
  - The build guide's only two are in three.js, on the 3D canvas.
  - `apps/hub.js` registers none.
- **Expected.** hub.js registers one passive document `touchstart` listener, so every press state works on iOS.
- **Why it matters.** If the quirk holds, every press scale measured in this audit is invisible on the family's primary devices.
- **Evidence:** `grep -c touchstart index.html apps/hub.js apps/*.html` (index 1, F260 2, Prayer 1, build guide 2 in three.js, the others 0); `index.html:366, 375, 393, 404, 406, 664`.
- **Reproduction:** the grep above; then, on a physical iPhone, open `apps/tally.html` and hold "+" (no scale is expected if the quirk applies).
- **Related (not re-filed):** VIS-TALLY-7 (`audits/03-apps/tally.md:551, 744, 796`), the Tally facet. The new facet is the cross-area count.

No VIS-MOTION items: the motion house-style deviations are carried by the CONS and GAP items above.

### What works

- **OK-MOTION-1 — Idle cost is near zero on 12 of the 13 idle surfaces, the TV board included.**
  - 10 s idle in Chromium: 0 % main thread, 0 style recalcs and 0 rAF on shell Home (adult and kid), Apps, F260, the Larder, Prayer, Tally, Timer, the park map (not located), Kid Verse and Verses.
  - The TV costs 0.1 % over 60 s with its 1 s clock (1.2 style recalcs a second).
  - The re-measure: 0-0.01 % on every one, and the TV 0.17 %.
  - The only costs are the build guide's pulse (P3-DOLLYWOOD-08) and the located park-map state (P4-MOTION-03).
  - The draft's "11 of 13" undercounts its own `idle.json`.
  - Caveat: a 10 s window misses the Apps grid's 30 s replay (P4-MOTION-01).
  - Evidence: `idle.json`, `idle-tv-board-typical-60000.json`, `remeasure-idle.json`.
- **OK-MOTION-2 — Where the design system is used, press feedback is complete and fast, and tab switches hold about 60 fps.**
  - `.ds` controls (`.btn`, `.tab`, `.tile`, `.seg`, the theme cards, the kid CTA) press on 100 % of sampled controls in Tally, Timer, Kid Verse, Verses and the kid Home.
  - They reach 79 % of their depth within a 60 ms tap (`curves.json`, re-measure 79.1 %).
  - Tab taps cost 3-11 ms of script, 0 long tasks and 19-23 frames per 360 ms indicator move. The largest frame gap is 53-73 ms, on the first Me and Chat visits on the iPad (`tabswitch.json`, not re-measured).
- **OK-MOTION-3 — Every app honours Reduce Motion standalone, and the JS gates that exist are right.**
  - All nine apps boot under reduce with 0 running animations and 0 button transitions (`reduced-motion.json`; re-measure exact).
  - The Dollywood `setView` skips its tween under reduce (`apps/dollywood-live.html:813`), and Kid Verse skips its confetti (`apps/kidverse.html:317`).
  - The park map releases its GPS watch and wake lock when the page is hidden (`apps/dollywood-live.html:1475`).
- **OK-MOTION-4 — The viewer opens out of the tapped tile.** `transform-origin` comes from the tile's rect (`index.html:718-720`; `viewer.json` origin 745 px, 139 px), the one spatial transition in the hub that behaves like an iOS zoom. Phase 2 also lists it under "Works" (`audits/02-shell.md:5424`).

### Checked and not a bug

No filed finding was refuted: all four confirmed defects survived both skeptics. The claims below were checked and dropped or corrected.

- **Phase 3's "the park map's infinite animations keep running under Reduce Motion".** Refuted at runtime.
  - The claim: `audits/03-apps/dollywood-live.md:734, 782`; `audits/00-inventory.md:4467`.
  - design.css's global rule (`apps/design.css:611-613`) sets every animation to one 0.01 ms iteration, and both exports link design.css (`:683`).
  - The four park-day pulses go from 4 running to 0 (`park-live.json`, both P4-MOTION-03 skeptics, the re-measure), and the build guide's `hlring` stops (`reduced-motion.json`).
  - The same rule covers `lvmarch` (`:477`), which was not running in the measured state.
- **"Closing 120 ms into the opening snaps opacity 0.48 → 1 (a jump of 0.52)."** A sampling artefact. `interrupt.json` has no samples between 55 ms and the close at 212 ms. At 120-129 ms the snap is 0.07-0.13; about 0.39 is reached only at 67 ms (P4-MOTION-02).
- **"An app opened during the exit ends on an empty screen."** It ends on the Apps grid with the Apps tab highlighted, while the hash names the hidden app (skeptic 1's screenshot).
- **"The SVG `mepulse` rings cause the park map's main-thread cost."** In Chromium they cost 0.1-0.5 % alone. The two `box-shadow` pulses force the frames, and the rings' re-layout rides on those frames (both P4-MOTION-03 skeptics).
- **"The park map should pause its pulses when hidden."** It already does: hidden pages do not tick, and `:1475` releases the watch and the wake lock.
- **"Each Dollywood export has 2 ungated smooth scrolls."** The park map has 1 reachable. `mapIntoView` (`:1140`) returns at once when `FLAVOR` is `'live'` (`:688-689`).
- **"The smooth-scroll facet relates to P3-DOLLYWOOD-08."** Wrong ID: P3 recorded the Dollywood scrolls in prose (`audits/03-apps/dollywood.md:867, 929`).
- **"Kid Verse shifts 0.163 on the iPhone even on a normal 150 ms network; the story card is inserted above the actions."** At 150 ms it is intermittent, and the mechanism is a collapsing story section with the actions pushed down by content above (GAP-MOTION-1).
- **"The build guide's pulse measured 12.2 %, lower than P3's 15.8-27.7 %."** The re-measure measured 26.5, 27.1 and 32.7 %. The cost is 12-33 % depending on machine load, with 60 style recalcs a second in every run.
- **"Shell press coverage 95-100 %."** Per surface it is 86-100 % (Chat 6/7, Home 12/13); only the aggregate, 65/68, is 96 %.
- **"F260's CLS 0.60 is 3.5× P3's figure."** 0.604 / 0.24 = 2.5×. The iPhone value also depends on the browser date: 0.324 on the real clock, 0.240 on the demo instant.
- **"88 literal durations in F260, Prayer, the Dollywood template and Kid Verse."** 88 is without Kid Verse; the total is 91 with it and 93 with the Larder.
- **"11 hand-written curves."** 6 hand-written cubic-bezier literals exist. 11 is the number of distinct bezier curves in use, counting the three token curves and the three CSS keywords.
- **"The park-map FAB press uses `--ease`."** It uses the literal `cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1)`, the same value but not the token.
- **"On iPad a centred sheet still rises with a grabber."** The grabber is hidden at 720 px and wider (`apps/design.css:587`); only the rise remains.
- **"Shell Apps idles at 0 %."** True for a 10 s window only. It misses the 30 s entrance replay (P4-MOTION-01).

| 7 | other | No loading primitive. hub.js exposes no per-scope "pulled" flag (the shell's `cached()` is private), and `.ds .skeleton` is used by no app. Needs `hub.pulled(scope)` / `hub.onFirstPull(scope, fn)` and skeleton size tokens (`--sk-line`, `--sk-block`, `--sk-card`) that reserve the final heights | `index.html:888-889`; `apps/design.css:539-544`; Table MOTION-5 | shell, f260, leftovers, prayer, tally, timer, dollywood, dollywood-live, kidverse, verses |
| 8 | layout | No stable-height rule: cards, the hero and lists grow after the first pull (shell 218-435 px, F260 405-598 px, build guide 862 px; CLS 0.604 in F260, 0.163 in Kid Verse and 0.159 in the Larder). Needs min-height tokens per card type, and a rule that the loading and loaded states share one box | Table MOTION-6 | shell, tv, f260, prayer, dollywood, kidverse, leftovers |
| 9 | motion | No rule for ambient or infinite animation: `box-shadow` pulses repaint every frame (park map 17-28 %, build guide 12-33 %). Needs a rule that ambient loops animate transform and opacity on HTML layers only, use `--dur-ambient`, and stop after N cycles or when idle (pausing when hidden already happens) | `apps/dollywood-live.html:282, 400-401, 413-414, 546, 561-562`; P4-MOTION-03; P3-DOLLYWOOD-08 | dollywood, dollywood-live |
| 10 | motion | Entrance animations are not tied to first mount: `.stagger` and `.pop-in` replay whenever `innerHTML` is rebuilt. Needs a rule or attribute (for example `data-entered`) so entrance motion runs once per mount | `index.html:380, 706, 1240, 1243`; `apps/design.css:595-599`; P4-MOTION-01 | shell |
| 11 | other | iOS `:active` support is not guaranteed: no document-level `touchstart` listener in hub.js. Needs hub.js to register one passive document `touchstart` listener in every document it loads into | `index.html:664`; `apps/f260.html:2040`; `apps/prayer.html:1716` (the only listeners); GAP-MOTION-3 | shell, tally, timer, verses, kidverse, leftovers, dollywood-live, dollywood |

### Method, scripts and evidence

**Investigator scripts** (`audits/tools/phase4/MOTION/`; evidence in `audits/evidence/p4/MOTION/`):

| Script | What it measures | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `static-motion.mjs` | Every transition and animation declaration (duration, easing, token vs literal), keyframes, `:active` rules, Reduce Motion blocks, JS intervals, rAF, smooth scrolls and `confirm()` in all 11 files | `static-motion.json` |
| `press.mjs` | Chromium; `:active` forced through CDP `CSS.forcePseudoState` on one control per kind per surface; scale, transform, filter, background and shadow deltas, and the transition that carries them | `press.json` |
| `curves.mjs` | Maths on every cubic-bezier in use: overshoot, time to 90 %, press depth after a 60 / 100 / 150 ms tap | `curves.json` |
| `reduced-motion.mjs` | WebKit; each area under no preference and reduce: boots, running and infinite animations, button transitions | `reduced-motion.json` |
| `rm-smooth.mjs` | WebKit and Chromium; F260's own smooth scroll under reduce | `rm-smooth.json` |
| `idle.mjs` | Chromium CDP; main-thread busy %, style and layout per second, rAF per second, live intervals, infinite animations over 10 s idle (`IDLE_MS`, `VARIANT` env) | `idle.json`, `idle-tv-board-typical-60000.json`, `idle-dollywood-live-shell-home-adult-park-10000.json` |
| `park-live.mjs` | Chromium; the park map located and sharing (variant `park`, GPS granted), idle cost under no preference and reduce | `park-live.json`, `park-live-located-{no-preference,reduce}-iphone.png` |
| `cls.mjs lat150 \| held` | Chromium; a cold load of 14 surfaces × iPad and iPhone: CLS, text-keyed block moves, and the loading state at 1.2 s | `cls-lat150.json`, `cls-held.json` |
| `viewer.mjs` | WebKit; viewer open and close animations, taps and hash opens during the 220 ms exit, sheet entry and exit | `viewer.json`, `viewer-open-during-exit-ipad.png` |
| `interrupt.mjs` | Chromium; closing an app during its opening; a retargeted tab indicator | `interrupt.json` |
| `tabswitch.mjs` | Chromium; long tasks and indicator frames per tab tap (iPad bottom bar, desktop sidebar) | `tabswitch.json` |
| `replay.mjs`, `replay-shot.mjs` | WebKit, 65 s idle on `#apps`, `#home` and the TV, listening for `animationstart`; a Chromium still of the Apps grid mid-replay | `replay.json`, `replay-shot.json`, `apps-grid-replay-mid-ipad.png` |

**Skeptic scripts:** `verify-<key>-1.mjs` and `verify-<key>-2.mjs` for each confirmed finding, in the same folder. The keys are `apps-grid-replays-entrance-every-pull`, `viewer-exit-not-interruptible`, `park-map-located-idle-pulses` and `smooth-scroll-ignores-reduced-motion`. Their outputs are the `verify-*.json` and `verify-*.png` files in `audits/evidence/p4/MOTION/`.

**Re-measure** (`audits/tools/phase4/MOTION/remeasure.mjs`; outputs `remeasure-*.json`) used methods different from the investigator's where it could:
- A real pointer press instead of `CSS.forcePseudoState`.
- A close fired in-page at 120 ms, with values read in the same task.
- F260's year-grid jump instead of the Reflect button.
- A capture-phase `animationstart` listener on three devices in parallel.
- Its own style tokenizer.

Result: 17 of 20 agree and 3 disagree (rows 4, 6 and 14). Every disagreement, plus the wording corrections the re-measure raised, is applied above:
- Shell press coverage per surface.
- F260 2.5× and its date dependence.
- 88 vs 91 literal durations.
- 6 literals vs 11 curves.
- The FAB easing label.
- The WebKit frame counts.
- The 10 s window on Apps.

The section writer added three corrections from the raw data and code:
- 12 of 13 idle surfaces, not 11 (`idle.json`).
- The iPad sheet has no grabber (`apps/design.css:587`).
- F260's loading state shows zeros, not a finished page (`cls-held.json`).

**Limits.**
- No physical device was used. Real iOS `:active`, haptics, ProMotion, GPU cost and how the curves feel are unmeasured.
- CPU figures are Chromium-only, and headless WebKit throttles rAF, so WebKit frame samples are sparse.
- A separate session ran parallel browsers throughout, so busy-% figures are load-sensitive. Style and layout rates were stable.
- `press.mjs` sampled controls in the first viewport only.
- The park map's Reduce Motion behaviour was measured standalone: inside the shell it cannot run under reduce (P2-STAB-01).
- The Phase 4 shared measure dataset (`audits/evidence/p4/measure/motion.json`) did not exist during the run, so every number comes from this dimension's scripts.

Every run was local. No script edited app code, and `L.close()` ran in a `finally` block in every script, so no server or browser was left running.

## Dark mode completeness (DARK)

Baseline: the working tree at fe6041d (no app file has changed since). Every number here comes from one of five sources:
- code;
- the rig-v2 themes run (iPad portrait, typical household, WebKit). Its keys are `system-light`, `system-dark`, `hearth-dark` (Hearth on a dark OS), and `parchment`, `frost`, `midnight`, `forest`, the named themes on a light OS;
- the investigator's targeted runs;
- the skeptics' own scripts;
- the independent re-measure.

Scripts are in `audits/tools/phase4/DARK/` and evidence files are in `audits/evidence/p4/DARK/` unless a full path is given. No request went to production, and no PIN or pairing code was read or used.

**One rig caveat changes this section.** The rig's WebKit is the Windows port of Playwright. It paints a `<select>` itself, over any author background: even `background: red !important` comes out `#F4F4F4` on a light OS. Every select figure from that engine therefore describes the port, not an iPad (see Checked and not a bug 1).

**Summary**

- **Four defects confirmed, all adversarially verified: two medium, two low.**
  - **P4-DARK-01 (medium):** the profile colour is used raw as text and as the Timer's progress arc, and no dark theme lifts it. In Midnight, Eli's Prayer Kitchen headings read 2.83:1 and the park map's walk time 2.14-2.57:1 for Eli and David. The Timer arc is 2.1-2.7:1 for them.
  - **P4-DARK-02 (medium):** P2-VIS-03, measured app by app. With Hearth on a dark OS:
    - the park map's inactive pane tabs fall to 2.6-3.3:1 whenever the sheet is open;
    - the build guide's list labels fall to 3.4-3.9:1;
    - F260's destructive Reset and "Replace and restore" fall to 2.61:1.
  - **P4-DARK-03 (low, lowered from medium; 2 of 3 skeptics):** `color-scheme` follows the OS, not the theme. The one failure shown in a real engine is F260's week-note Copy button: 1.01:1 in Midnight on a light OS.
  - **P4-DARK-04 (low):** the `theme-color` meta goes stale whenever a pull, rather than a tap, changes the theme.
- **The select claim did not survive.** The investigator's headline was that the Larder's size select and the Dollywood selects read 1.06:1 in Midnight on a light OS. It is a rig artefact:
  - three skeptics showed that the Windows WebKit port ignores every author background on a select;
  - Chromium paints the token backgrounds at 11.21-15.02:1.
  - What an iPad paints is a device check (Unresolved 1).
- **Dark text is better than light in 8 of 11 areas, not 9.** Examples: F260 64.8% → 15.8% of text failing AA, park map 40.1% → 6.4%, TV 26.3% → 9.6%. The exceptions:
  - the shell is worse (3.5% → 4.9%; the Home hero is P2-VIS-06);
  - the Larder and Tally stay at 0%. The Larder's 3.0% in the rig is the select artefact.
- **Dark's real weaknesses are not text.** They are a shared token base that every design-system app inherits:
  - soft fills only 1.01-1.11:1 from the card (GAP-DARK-1);
  - a raw profile colour under 3:1 for 3 of 9 colours (P4-DARK-01);
  - a flat depth ladder where "sunken" goes darker (GAP-DARK-2);
  - a focus ring under 3:1 in every palette (GAP-DARK-3);
  - toasts that invert to a cream slab (VIS-DARK-1);
  - an illustration set with no dark form (CONS-DARK-1).
- **The foundation holds.**
  - Every named and System-dark block overrides all 46 literal colour, shadow and glass tokens.
  - The three written copies of Midnight and the two of Forest do not drift.
  - No app uses `prefers-color-scheme` in CSS.
  - The five pure-token apps render Hearth on a dark OS exactly as System dark.
- **Re-measure: 17 numbers checked with independent code; 14 agree and 3 disagree.**
  - F260 Reset reads 7.14 in System dark, not 9.2.
  - Midnight is written three times, not four.
  - The focus-ring ranges were wrong.
  - Three sentences in the draft also contradicted the raw data (8 of 11, not 9; the Larder "zero in dark"; the soft-fill chroma framing). All are corrected below.

Two notes for other dimensions:
- **Color & palette (dark).** The house rule that pastels glow in dark is half met:
  - the semantic inks are glowing pastels (L 0.81-0.87, 8.9-10.4:1);
  - the fills are low-chroma in every theme, Hearth included (C 0.014-0.037), so that is a palette issue, not a dark one;
  - in dark the fills also lose their luminance step, and the per-person accent is never lifted.
- **Native feel.** Only the F260 Copy button is shown to paint in the OS scheme, not the theme's (a facet of VIS-F260-5). The select web tell stands as "default control", but its colour in the wrong scheme is unproven.

### Confirmed defects

Each confirmed defect was adversarially verified: independent skeptics re-read the code, wrote their own scripts and re-ran them on the local instance (a third skeptic broke the tie on P4-DARK-03). Severities follow the Phase 2 rule (`audits/02-shell.md:25-37`) and its design-system clause.

#### P4-DARK-01 — The raw profile colour is painted as text and as the Timer arc in dark: Prayer's Kitchen headings 2.83:1 and the park map's walk time 2.14-2.57:1 for Eli and David; the Timer arc 2.1-2.7:1

> **Pointer (merged at assembly) → P4-COLOR-02 for the text, P4-ACCENT-04 for the Timer arc.** The Kitchen headings and the park map's walk times are the same rules and the same cause as P4-COLOR-02, which owns them at medium; this entry keeps its dark-palette measurements and evidence. The Timer arc is the same measurement as P4-ACCENT-04, whose skeptics rated it low on its own; the scorecard's consistency pass also found that the arc is not the only carrier of the time (the digits carry it), so the arc counts at low under P4-ACCENT-04.

- **Severity: medium.** Both skeptics rated it medium; not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** text a household member needs fails WCAG AA on a primary surface, which the design-system clause puts at medium at least.
  - **Why not high:** neither text is the main content or the primary action. The Kitchen items themselves are 24 px in ink. The Nearby row's distance is bold `--text`. The Timer digits use `--accent-strong`.
  - **The arc on its own:** a graphic under 3:1. Phase 2 rated the same failure medium for the shell rings.
  - **Exposure:** wider than choosing a dark theme. System is the default and resolves to Midnight whenever the device is in dark mode, which with iOS Automatic appearance is every evening.
    - Text fails 4.5:1 for 8 of 9 profile colours (Table DARK-4).
    - The arc fails 3:1 for Eli and David. Mae passes at 3.65-3.79.
- **Areas:** prayer, dollywood-live, timer. The shell rings share the cause but are Phase 2's item.
- **What happens.**
  - hub.js sets `--accent` inline from the profile's colour (`apps/hub.js:80`). design.css defines `--accent` only as the `:root` fallback (`apps/design.css:86`), and no theme block redefines it. The dark blocks lift `--accent-deep` instead (`apps/design.css:170`). So `var(--accent)` is the light-palette hue in every theme.
  - Three app rules paint foreground with it:
    - `#kitchen .k-cat { color: var(--accent) }` (`apps/prayer.html:359`);
    - `.lv-item .d small { color: var(--accent) }` (`../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:440`, exported into `apps/dollywood-live.html`);
    - `.dial { --tint: var(--accent) }` with `.dial .ring .fg { stroke: var(--tint) }` (`apps/timer.html:22, 29`).
  - Measured values are in Table DARK-5. In short:
    - Kitchen heading: Eli 2.83 in Midnight and Forest, against 5.75 in Hearth.
    - Walk time: Eli 2.57/2.53, David 2.14/2.11, Mae 3.65/3.60 (Midnight/Forest).
    - Timer arc, computed: Eli 2.57/2.53, David 2.14/2.11.
  - At 13.5 px, antialiasing makes the rendered Kitchen ink weaker still: its darkest pixels reach only 2.12-2.65.
  - The Kitchen failure is limited to a person's own list. On the Family list `body.shared` sets `--accent: var(--teal)` (`apps/prayer.html:39`), and teal is lifted in dark, so the headings pass there at 8.52/8.64.
- **Expected.** The system's own intent is that `--accent-deep`/`--accent-strong` carries the person's colour as text ("text on soft — AA on paper for every family colour", `apps/design.css:89-90`). In dark, `--accent-deep` measures 5.68-8.65 against the Midnight card for all nine colours (Table DARK-4). Text in the person's colour should reach at least 4.5:1, and arcs at least 3:1, in every palette.
- **Why it matters.**
  - The walk time is the fact a Nearby row exists to give at the park.
  - The Kitchen headings organise a person's own list on the counter view.
  - The arc is the Timer's only picture of how much time is left.
  - Under System, Eli and David see these at 2.1-2.8:1 every evening. David's Kitchen figure would be 2.35 by palette math (`--accent` against `--bg`); his seeded list has no categories, so it was not measured live.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/hub.js:80`; `apps/design.css:86, 89-90, 170, 528`; `apps/prayer.html:39, 359`; `apps/timer.html:22, 29`; `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:440` (read-only).
  - Investigator:
    - `accent-fg.json` and `palette-dark.json` (`accents.midnight`, `accents.forest`);
    - `summary.json` darkOnly: `div#kitchenBody > div.k-cat` 2.83 (n=14) and `button.lv-item > span.d > small` 2.57/2.53 (n=24);
    - `nontext-dark.json`: `frame:timer … circle.fg` 2.41 in Midnight, 2.40 in Forest.
  - Skeptics:
    - `verify-raw-accent-foreground-in-dark-1-midnight-eli.json` and `verify-raw-accent-foreground-in-dark-1-midnight-dad_midnight-christian_forest-eli_forest-dad_hearth-eli.json`, with the crops `-1-kcat-midnight-eli.png`, `-1-walk-midnight-eli.png`, `-1-timer-midnight-eli.png` and `-1-timer-midnight-dad.png`;
    - `verify-raw-accent-foreground-in-dark-2.json`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-webkit.json`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `cd "C:/Users/ex_bo/OneDrive/Claude Related/App Hub" && node audits/tools/phase4/DARK/accent-fg.mjs` (about 8 min). It prints `{homeRing, timerArc, kitchenCat, parkWalk}` per theme and profile. Expect Midnight Eli `2.57, 2.57, 2.83, 2.57`, Midnight David timerArc `2.14`, and Hearth Eli kitchenCat `5.75`.
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/DARK/palette-dark.mjs` for Table DARK-4.
  - Skeptics' runs: `node audits/tools/phase4/DARK/verify-raw-accent-foreground-in-dark-1.mjs [theme:profile …]` (about 1.5 min per case) and `… -2.mjs`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** re-read the cited lines and wrote their own WebKit script (park variant, iPad portrait, light OS). It set each theme through `PUT /api/data/hub/theme` and localStorage, and measured the computed colour and the rendered pixels. It used the real Nearby list: "me" placed with the app's `setMe()` beside DP's Celebrity Theater, the sheet at half, then `renderNear()`, which gave 12 real rows. The investigator had used a synthetic element. Six cases were run: Midnight × Eli, David, Mae; Forest × Eli, David; Hearth × Eli.
    - Kitchen: Eli 2.83 in both dark palettes (rendered 2.12-2.65); Hearth 5.75.
    - Walk time: exactly as claimed, and the rendered pixels matched the computed values.
    - Timer arc against the dial just inside the ring: Eli 2.66/2.64, David 2.22/2.20, Mae 3.79.
    - Palette math: all nine values as claimed.
    - The Home ring facet is Phase 2's (`audits/02-shell.md:5840-5846`).
  - **Skeptic 2** re-read the code and design.css's intent (`:89-90`; the park map's own AA step-up at `template.html:216-217`), then wrote an independent WebKit script. It compared each foreground with the alpha-composited ancestor background and sampled the rendered pixels. It used real Nearby rows after "Set my spot", the Kitchen view on both My list and the Family list, and a running timer.
    - Walk time: Eli 2.57/2.53, David 2.14/2.11, Mae 3.65; Hearth 6.27.
    - Kitchen, own list: Eli 2.83/2.83; Hearth 5.75.
    - **Kitchen, Family list: 8.52/8.64.** It passes, because `body.shared` swaps in the lifted teal.
    - Timer arc against the dial: Eli 2.66/2.64, David 2.22/2.20, Mae 3.79.
    - The park sheet in dark and the Kitchen's `--paper` are solid, so blur does not affect these ratios.
  - **Re-measure (independent code):**
    - Kitchen 2.83 (Hearth 5.75).
    - Walk time 2.57 / 2.14 / 3.65. The typical seed has no real walk-time rows, so a synthetic row was used.
    - Timer arc computed 2.57 / 2.14. Rendered against the track under the arc: Eli 2.61, David 2.21.
    - All nine palette values.
    - Agrees. Eli's rendered arc, 2.61 against the rig's 2.41, is just outside the rendered tolerance. The likely cause is that the rig takes a pixel minimum that includes antialiased edges. Every figure is under 3:1.
- **Corrected claim.** The draft is accurate for text, with these corrections:
  - The Kitchen failure is on each person's own list only. The Family list passes at 8.5:1, so "unreadable on the counter" overstated it.
  - Measured against the dial it sits on, the Timer arc reads Eli 2.64-2.66 and David 2.20-2.22, not 2.41. Mae's arc passes (3.79).
  - The Home ring (`apps/design.css:528`) is not new. It belongs to Phase 2's "accent and tile icons are not lifted for dark" (`audits/02-shell.md:5840-5846`, medium), which also owns the root cause at `apps/hub.js:80`.
  - P3-KIDVERSE-14 is a different defect (an override that does not apply) and is not related.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - Phase 2's unnumbered dark deviation above: the shell rings, tile icons and badge.
  - VIS-TIMER-7 (the 1.2:1 track), and the Timer checker's "muddy adult accents" noted without numbers (`audits/03-apps/timer.md:445, 460`).
  - COLOR's raw-accent check ran in parallel and should be merged at consolidation.

#### P4-DARK-02 — Hearth on a dark OS, app by app (a cross-area facet of P2-VIS-03): the park map's inactive pane tabs fall to 2.6-3.3:1 when the sheet is open, the build guide's labels to 3.4-3.9:1, and F260's Reset and "Replace and restore" to 2.61:1

- **Severity: medium.** Both skeptics rated it medium; not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** controls and labels on primary surfaces fail AA: the park map's navigation tabs, the build guide's list labels, and F260's destructive confirmations and Done. That is the design-system medium floor.
  - **Why not high:** the trigger is narrow, and the one daily primary action affected, F260 Done, is already P2-VIS-03 (medium).
  - **Exposure:** only a person who picked Hearth, on a device in dark mode. The choice follows the person to every device, including iOS Automatic appearance after sunset (P2-VIS-03).
- **Areas:** dollywood-live (36 selectors), dollywood (12), f260 (8), tv (2, rig only).
  - Unaffected, with 0 worse selectors in the rig: leftovers, prayer, timer, kidverse, verses.
  - The shell has 0 worse and 5 better. Tally has no text change.
- **What happens.**
  - hub.js deletes `data-theme` for Hearth (`apps/hub.js:77`). On a dark OS, `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root:not([data-theme])` then applies the Midnight tokens (`apps/design.css:176-177`), while hub.js sets `data-scheme="light"` from `hub.THEMES` (`apps/hub.js:66, 79`).
  - Every document measured reads `data-theme` null, `data-scheme` light, `--bg` #1A1512 and `--text` #F3EDE5 (`hearth-dark-os.json` tokens; both skeptics). So only rules keyed on `[data-scheme]` change:
    - F260's `--on-solid` flip (`apps/f260.html:28`);
    - the template's `--dim → --text-2` step-up and denser dark glass (`../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:219`) and its light category inks (`:10`).
  - **Park map, 36 selectors.** Labels take `--dim`, which here is Midnight's `--muted` #A2948A instead of #C9BBAB.
    - The four pane tabs, Nearby, Style, Search and Family, read 3.00, 3.12, 3.14 and 2.86 at the rig's p10, against 6.46-7.12 in System dark.
    - Also: list meta `span.t > span > em` 3.76 (n=92), `.oi .k` 3.30, card `dl.kv dt` 2.62, route meta 2.77, "up to date" 2.92.
    - The sheet keeps the light-branch glass over the map (`crop-hearth-darkos-parkmap-family.png`), so values move with the terrain behind it.
    - Only the inactive tabs fail: the active tab takes `--text` and reads 6.94-6.95.
    - They fail only with the sheet open at half or full. At peek, the state the map opens in, they pass at 4.80-4.91 (System dark 8.33-8.40).
    - Share of text failing: 645/2232 = 28.9% against 142/2232 = 6.4% over all park-map jobs (`summary.json`), and 381/1910 = 19.9% against 48/1910 = 2.5% on the 44 screens `hearth-dark-os.mjs` pairs (`hearth-dark-os.json`). The denominators differ; both show the same jump.
  - **Build guide, 12 selectors.**
    - Listing kind `.oi .k` 3.86 against 6.05. That is 41 groups in `hearth-dark-os.json` and 340 text boxes in `summary.json`.
    - Section headings 3.49 against 5.46; their counts 3.44; "rider height" 3.53.
    - The card's `dl.kv dt`: worst 3.0 in the rig, 3.98-4.47 on the card a skeptic opened (System dark 4.7-7.0).
  - **F260, 8 selectors.**
    - Done, the ring's "5/5" and "week", "Start week 38" and "Got it" are white on #9DC183 at 2.02 (9.2 in System dark). Done is P2-VIS-03; the other four share its token.
    - The Journal tab reads 3.99 (5.55).
    - **New: Reset (`#doConfirm`) and "Replace and restore" (`#restoreOk`) are white on #E28A66 at 2.61**, against 7.14 in System dark and 4.51 in real Hearth. No earlier phase recorded them.
  - **TV kiosk, 2 selectors (rig only; no one re-measured it).** The kiosk Me hero's title reads 1.35 and its kicker 2.34: #17120E on the dark hero, against 6.18 and 5.0. The kiosk never adopts a server theme (`apps/hub.js:98`), so this needs Hearth set on the TV's own device.
- **Expected.** Hearth renders its light palette on any OS, which is P2-VIS-03's expected behaviour (`apps/hub.js:66`; `apps/design.css:113-115`). Until then, no app should add failures beyond what System dark shows.
- **Why it matters.**
  - Someone who picks Hearth and opens the park map on a dark-mode phone cannot read the tabs that switch between Nearby, Search, Family and Style.
  - F260's two irreversible confirmations drop below AA exactly where the words matter.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/hub.js:66, 77, 79, 98`; `apps/design.css:176-177`; `apps/f260.html:28`; `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:10, 219, 426` (read-only).
  - Investigator: `hearth-dark-os.json` (per area: `worse`, `better`, `tokens`), `summary.json`, `crop-hearth-darkos-parkmap-family.png`; `audits/evidence/p4/SCORE/shots/hearth/f260/reset-confirm-typical-ipad-portrait-dark.png`.
  - Skeptics:
