#### P4-DARK-03 — Native controls take their colours from the OS, not the chosen theme: F260's week-note Copy button reads 1.01-1.08:1 in Midnight or Forest on a light OS, and 2.58-2.92:1 in Parchment or Frost on a dark OS

> **Pointer (merged at assembly) → P4-COLOR-04.** The same mechanism (`color-scheme` fixed at `apps/design.css:15`) and the same F260 Copy button, confirmed low in both sections; counted under P4-COLOR-04. This entry keeps the three-skeptic record and the select-artefact analysis.

- **Severity: low (lowered from the investigator's medium).** Of the three skeptics, two confirmed at low and one refuted.
  - **Why lowered:** the investigator rated it medium because of the Larder's daily add bar and the map filters. That part is a rig artefact (Checked and not a bug 1).
  - **Clause:** what survives is a secondary control on a secondary surface, the Copy button inside an unlocked journal's week-note panel. The design-system clause makes secondary failures low.
  - **Exposure:** it fails badly only when the theme's scheme opposes the OS: Midnight or Forest on a light OS, or Parchment or Frost on a dark OS. Forest also just fails when the schemes match, at 4.33:1 (Chromium, with the scheme forced to dark, which is what a dark OS gives).
- **Areas:** f260. The mechanism, `apps/design.css:15`, is shared by every document on design.css.
- **What happens.**
  - `color-scheme: light dark` is declared once, on `:root` (`apps/design.css:15`). It is the only `color-scheme` declaration in `apps/`, design.css or index.html, and no theme block or `[data-scheme]` rule changes it. The used colour scheme is therefore the OS's, and anything the browser paints itself follows the OS: ButtonFace, and by the same mechanism checkboxes, scrollbars and picker popups (those not measured, Unresolved 2).
  - F260's week-note footer builds its Copy button at `apps/f260.html:1297` with no author background.
    - F260's only generic button rule is `button{…color:inherit}` (`:45`).
    - `.jr .jft button{background:none…}` (`:333`) targets the HEAR journal footer, not `.wnbody .jft`.
    - So the button paints ButtonFace under the theme's `--text`.
  - In Chromium it measures (computed / rendered):

    | Theme on OS | Mismatched: ButtonFace, label ratio | Counterfactual: `color-scheme` forced to the theme's scheme |
    |---|---|---|
    | Midnight on a light OS | #F0F0F0 (rendered #EFEFEF), **1.02 / 1.01** | #6B6B6B, 4.58 |
    | Forest on a light OS | #F0F0F0, **1.08 / 1.07** | #6B6B6B, **4.33** |
    | Parchment on a dark OS | #6B6B6B, **2.58** | light, 11.97 |
    | Frost on a dark OS | #6B6B6B, **2.92** | light, 13.53 |
    | Controls: System light / System or Midnight on a dark OS | 13.18 / 4.58 | — |

  - The counterfactual isolates the cause: forcing the scheme lifts three of the four cases to AA. Forest stays under AA (4.33) even when the schemes match, because the dark ButtonFace is a mid grey.
  - The button is 55×32 in Chromium and 55×35 in WebKit, under the 44 px target. VIS-F260-5 already records that.
  - In the rig's WebKit, ButtonFace computes to a constant rgb(192,192,192): 1.56 against Midnight's ink. The Windows port paints #F4F4F4 or #343434 over it (rig 1.06 and 1.11). Those are the port's values, not an iPad's.
- **Expected.** Every native control renders with the theme's surface and ink at 4.5:1 or better, in every theme and on either OS setting.
- **Why it matters.** Anyone who keeps Midnight on a light-mode iPad or desktop, or Parchment on a dark-mode phone, sees a blank grey chip where Copy should be. Beyond this one button, the single `color-scheme` is a trap for any native control added later.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/design.css:15`; `apps/f260.html:45, 333, 346, 1297`.
  - Investigator: `native-button.json` (synthetic `.wnbody .jft button` in the real F260 document) and `native-controls.json`.
  - Skeptics:
    - `verify-native-controls-follow-os-not-theme-1.json` with `-1-chromium-f260copy-midnight-light.png` and `-1-chromium-f260copy-parchment-dark.png`;
    - `verify-native-controls-follow-os-not-theme-2.json` with `-2-chromium-f260-copy-midnight-lightos.png`;
    - `verify-native-controls-follow-os-not-theme-3-chromium.json` and `-3-webkit.json` with `-3-chromium-f260copy-midnight-lightos.png` and `-3-chromium-f260copy-parchment-darkos.png`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-chromium.json`, `remeasure-webkit.json`.
  - Rig roll-up: `summary.json` darkOnly `div.wnbody > div.jft > button` (Midnight 1.06, Forest 1.12, WebKit port values).
- **Reproduction.**
  - `cd "C:/Users/ex_bo/OneDrive/Claude Related/App Hub" && node audits/tools/phase4/DARK/native-button.mjs`. Expect Chromium Midnight on a light OS 1.02, Parchment on a dark OS 2.58, Midnight on a dark OS 4.58.
  - Tie-break run: `node audits/tools/phase4/DARK/verify-native-controls-follow-os-not-theme-3.mjs chromium`, then `… webkit`. It prints each engine × theme × OS mode × control with its computed and rendered ratio, and the red-background probes.
- **Verified: 2/3 skeptics confirmed (1 refuted).**
  - **Skeptic 1 (refuted).** Re-read the code and wrote their own two-engine script (Eli, iPad portrait; System/light, Midnight/light, Midnight/dark, Parchment/dark, Parchment/light). It added a probe setting `background-color: rgb(255,0,0) !important` on the Larder select.
    - In WebKit the red select still rendered #F4F4F4 on a light OS and #343434 on a dark OS, and System light rendered #F4F4F4 instead of the declared #FFFCF8. The port ignores every author select background, so the 1.06-1.25 select figures say nothing about an iPad.
    - Chromium honoured the red (#FF0000) and the token backgrounds (14.16 and 11.21).
    - What they accepted: the F260 Copy button in Chromium, at 1.02 (1.01 rendered), 2.58 and 4.58. They rated it a low facet of VIS-F260-5.
  - **Skeptic 2 (confirmed, low).** Re-read the code and wrote their own script. Cases: System light and dark, Midnight/light, Parchment/dark, Midnight/dark, in both engines. It measured the Larder select and a red-background select plus an `appearance:none` select in the same frame, and the F260 Copy button.
    - WebKit: reproduced 1.06 and 1.11, but the red probe also rendered #F4F4F4, and even System dark painted #343434 over the declared #241E19. The `appearance:none` probe rendered the token #241E19 at 14.16.
    - Chromium: the select read 14.68/14.16/14.16/11.21. The Copy button read 1.02 (1.01) and 2.58, with 13.18 and 4.58 as the controls.
    - Their conclusion: the mechanism is real and engine-independent, and the one casualty in a real engine is the Copy button.
  - **Skeptic 3 (tie-break; confirmed, low).** Re-read the code and wrote their own script, run once per engine. Cases: System/light as the control, Midnight/light, Forest/light, Parchment/dark, Frost/dark, Midnight/dark. It measured the Larder `#size`, the build guide `#bmap`, the Copy button injected with the exact `:1297` markup inside `.wn.on > .wnbody`, and three select probes (red with a border, red without, unstyled), plus a forced-`color-scheme` counterfactual.
    - WebKit painted every select, red or not, as #F4F4F4.
    - Chromium kept the author backgrounds: `#size` 14.16/13.19/11.21/15.02 and `#bmap` 14.16/11.21.
    - Copy: 1.01, 1.07, 2.58 and 2.92, lifting to 4.58, 4.33, 11.97 and 13.53 when the scheme is forced. Forest still fails.
    - Sided with skeptic 2, with the scope cut to the Copy button plus the mechanism.
  - **Re-measure (independent code).**
    - Chromium: Copy at 1.01 (rendered; 1.02 computed), 2.58 and 4.58. The selects honour the author background everywhere (11.21-15.02).
    - WebKit: the investigator's select numbers (1.06, 1.12, 1.11, 1.25; counterfactual 10.7 and 12.51) match. But this is the same Windows port, so the agreement confirms the rig reading, not what an iPad does.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - `apps/design.css:15` never follows `data-scheme`, so browser-painted controls take the OS's scheme.
  - The only failure shown in a real engine is F260's week-note Copy button: 1.01-1.08:1 with a dark theme on a light OS, 2.58-2.92:1 with a light theme on a dark OS, and 4.33:1 in Forest even on a dark OS.
  - The Larder `select#size` and the Dollywood `#bmap`/`#hf`/`#cint` keep their author backgrounds (Chromium 11.21-15.02). Their WebKit readings of 1.06-1.25 are an artefact of the port and are withdrawn.
  - The rig's WebKit Copy figure of 1.06 is the port's paint; its computed ButtonFace ratio is 1.56.
  - A per-`[data-scheme]` `color-scheme` rule depends on P2-VIS-03 first giving `data-scheme` the right value.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - VIS-F260-5, "the week-note … Copy is a default 55×35 grey button" (low; `audits/03-apps/f260.md:713`). This item adds its theme-dependent contrast failure.
  - P2-VIS-03, the prerequisite for the fix.
  - COLOR's native-control check ran in parallel and should be merged at consolidation.

#### P4-DARK-04 — The `theme-color` meta goes stale whenever a pull, not a tap, changes the theme

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low; not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** cosmetic. The page paints correctly. Only the meta that tints the browser chrome is wrong, and no data, flow or readability is affected.
  - **Exposure:** any device whose theme changes by a pull: a new device, a theme picked on another device, or the everyday visibility and 30-second pulls.
- **Areas:** shell.
- **What happens.**
  - `syncThemeColor()` copies `--bg` into both theme-color metas (`index.html:656-658`). Its only callers are:
    - enterShell (`:624`);
    - a frame's `hub:theme` message (`:767`);
    - a theme tap in Me (`:1283`);
    - boot and an OS scheme change (`:1702-1703`).
  - `adoptTheme()` applies the person's server row after a pull (`apps/hub.js:97-105`, called at `:208, 313, 333`). Its `tell()` posts only from inside a frame (`apps/hub.js:35`), and the shell's `onChange` does not call `syncThemeColor` (`audits/00-inventory.md:1698`). Nothing re-syncs the top-level page's metas.
  - Results (iPhone PWA, light OS, WebKit):

    | Case | Metas | Page `--bg` | Match |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | A: new device, server row Midnight, after the first pull | #F7F2EB | #1A1512 | no |
    | A2: after a reload | #1A1512 | #1A1512 | yes |
    | B1: Parchment picked on another device, then `hub.pull()` | #1A1512 | #E7D9BE | no |
    | B2: Forest picked remotely, pull triggered by `visibilitychange` | #1A1512 | #10171A | no |
    | C: System, with the OS flipping to dark | follows | follows | yes (control) |
    | D: a Me tap on Frost | #EDF0F5 | #EDF0F5 | yes (control) |
- **Expected.** The meta always equals the painted `--bg`, as the code's own comment intends: "the browser chrome (iOS status bar, Android address bar) follows the hub's paper colour" (`index.html:655`).
- **Why it matters.** In Safari the toolbar tint, and on the Home Screen app possibly the status-bar strip (Unresolved 3), shows paper over a dark page, or dark over paper. The seam stays at the top of every screen until a reload, an OS appearance change or a theme tap.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `index.html:624, 655-658, 767, 1283, 1702-1703`; `apps/hub.js:35, 97-105, 208, 313, 333`.
  - Investigator: `theme-color.json`. `theme-color-A-iphone-server-midnight.png` and `theme-color-B-iphone-remote-parchment.png` show the page only; the metas are DOM values.
  - Skeptics: `verify-theme-color-stale-after-server-theme-1.json` with `-1-A.png`, and `verify-theme-color-stale-after-server-theme-2.json`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-webkit.json`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `cd "C:/Users/ex_bo/OneDrive/Claude Related/App Hub" && node audits/tools/phase4/DARK/theme-color.mjs` (about 1 min). It prints A `… =#F7F2EB … --bg #1A1512 … match false`, A2 match true, B1 `=#1A1512 … --bg #E7D9BE … match false`, and C match true.
  - Skeptic 1 reported this script missing at the time of their run; it is in the folder now.
  - Skeptics' runs: `node audits/tools/phase4/DARK/verify-theme-color-stale-after-server-theme-1.mjs` and `… -2.mjs`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** re-read the callers and `adoptTheme()`, then wrote their own WebKit script (iPhone PWA, Eli). It set the server row with `PUT /api/data/hub/theme?scope=person`, booted or pulled, and read `data-theme`, `--bg` and both metas.
    - A: metas #F7F2EB against #1A1512. A2 (reload): match.
    - B1: #1A1512 against #E7D9BE.
    - Extra case B2, a `visibilitychange` pull to Forest: #1A1512 against #10171A.
    - Controls D (Me tap on Frost) and C (OS flip) matched.
    - Every number in the draft reproduced.
  - **Skeptic 2** wrote an independent WebKit script with a different profile and different themes (Mae; Forest, Frost), waiting for the SDK's own interval pull instead of calling `hub.pull()`.
    - A′: Forest adopted after 513 ms, metas still #F7F2EB against #10171A.
    - Switching Home → Me → Home left the metas stale. A reload matched them.
    - B′: Frost arrived by the natural interval pull after 27.5 s, with the metas at #10171A against #EDF0F5.
    - A Me tap matched.
    - With an app frame open the metas matched only by coincidence: the frame's hub.js does not declare the `hub|person` scope, so it never adopts or posts `hub:theme`.
  - **Re-measure (independent code):** case A reproduced exactly (metas #F7F2EB, `--bg` #1A1512, `data-theme` midnight). After a reload the metas were #1A1512. Agrees.
- **Corrected claim.** Accurate, with two additions:
  - Any pull that changes the theme leaves the meta stale, including the everyday `visibilitychange` and 30-second pulls, not only the first pull on a new device.
  - It clears on a reload, an OS appearance change or a theme tap in Me.
  - It is not a duplicate of P2-VIS-03, which is Hearth painting Midnight. Phase 2's PWA-OK-5 (`audits/02-shell.md:5189-5190`) exercised only the tap paths.
- **Related:** `audits/00-inventory.md:1698` recorded the gap from reading the code, as prior art but not a defect. The device check is Phase 2's "status bar under Midnight and Forest" (`audits/02-shell.md:5279`).

### Consistency, visual and gap findings

These items were not adversarially verified. Their evidence is the investigator's code scan and measurements, spot-checked by the section writer against the cited lines and raw JSON, with the re-measure's corrections applied. Severities are the investigator's ratings.

#### GAP-DARK-1 — Dark soft fills sit 1.01-1.22:1 from the card, so every soft-filled state goes muddy or vanishes; one token choice explains six per-app Phase 3 findings (investigator rating: medium)

- **What happens.**
  - In Midnight the semantic `-soft` tokens (`apps/design.css:163-168`) against `--surface` #241E19 measure:
    - mocha 1.10, gold 1.08, olive 1.07, teal 1.02, terra 1.01, slate 1.11;
    - Forest 1.02-1.10.
  - `--accent-soft` (`color-mix(accent 14%, surface)`, `apps/design.css:169`) measures 1.08-1.22 (Forest 1.08-1.21).
  - Every chip, disc, dot, rating fill and state pill built on these tokens fades into the card. Table DARK-3 maps the six Phase 3 findings this explains:
    - VIS-LEFTOVERS-3: chips 1.01-1.08;
    - VIS-VERSES-7: Not yet and Almost;
    - VIS-TALLY-1: discs 1.13-1.62;
    - VIS-KIDVERSE-3: badge discs 1.15, and the dots at 1.14;
    - Prayer's kid prayed and unprayed fills 1.06-1.16 (`audits/03-apps/prayer.md:955`);
    - VIS-F260-2, through `--sunk` (see GAP-DARK-2).
  - **Correction (re-measure):** low chroma is not specific to dark. Hearth's own soft fills are just as achromatic (C 0.014-0.037, against the house pastels' 0.057-0.093), so chroma is a palette-wide COLOR issue. What is dark-specific is the luminance step: 1.01-1.11 in Midnight against 1.16-1.21 in Hearth.
  - The inks meanwhile do glow as the house style asks: L 0.81-0.87, 8.9-10.4:1 on their fills.
- **Expected (house style).** Dark mode flips roles: the pastel glows and never goes muddy. Soft fills should read as tints, at about 1.4:1 or more from the card. State shapes that carry meaning should reach 3:1.
- **Why it matters.** Expiry states, rating choices, the tally buttons and the kids' progress dots all rely on the soft fill. For pre-readers the fill is the state cue. Under System, the always-on iPad runs dark every evening.
- **Evidence:** `palette-dark.json` (`semantics.midnight`, `semantics.forest`, `accents.*`, `house`); `remeasure-static.json` (`pal`); `audits/evidence/p4/SCORE/shots/forest/tally/main-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png`; `audits/evidence/p4/SCORE/shots/midnight/leftovers/main-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/DARK/palette-dark.mjs`. It prints `## midnight semantics` with teal 1.02 and terra 1.01, and accent soft 1.08-1.22.
- **Related (not re-filed):** VIS-LEFTOVERS-3, VIS-VERSES-7, VIS-TALLY-1, VIS-KIDVERSE-3, VIS-PRAYER-5 (empty calendar days), VIS-F260-2.

### What works

- **OK-DARK-1 — Complete, drift-free dark token blocks.**
  - Parchment, Frost, Midnight, System-dark and Forest each override all 46 colour, shadow and glass tokens that Hearth sets with a literal (0 missing).
  - The only tokens not overridden are accent-derived or non-colour: `--sheen-x`, `--accent-tint`, `--accent-glow`, `--focus`.
  - Midnight is written three times (`apps/design.css:156` for the named theme and its swatch, `:177` System-dark, `:257` the System swatch's night half) and Forest twice (`:198`, `:218`), with 0 drift. The draft said four Midnight copies; the re-measure counts three. The repetition is a maintenance risk only.
  - No design.css token leaks a light literal into dark. What fails to adapt sits outside the blocks: the inline `--accent`, `color-scheme`, a few component literals (`apps/design.css:423`, the toast `:589`), the art set and the Dollywood category literals. Source: `theme-blocks.json`, `remeasure-static.json`.
- **OK-DARK-2 — Dark is keyed the way CLAUDE.md prescribes.**
  - No app uses `prefers-color-scheme` in CSS.
  - F260, Tally, the Dollywood template and the shell key their own dark rules off `[data-scheme]`.
  - The app-local colour tokens in F260 (15), Prayer (16) and the Larder (3) all adapt (`local-tokens.json`).
  - Larder, Prayer, Timer, Kid Verse and Verses are pure-token and render Hearth on a dark OS exactly as System dark (0 worse selectors).
- **OK-DARK-3 — Dark text beats light in 8 of 11 areas** (Table DARK-1). Examples: F260 64.8% → 15.8%, park map 40.1% → 6.4%, build guide 28.3% → 3.4%, TV 26.3% → 9.6%, Prayer 7.0% → 2.3%. In a real engine the Larder, Timer, Verses and Tally have no failing text in any dark palette.
- **OK-DARK-4 — Pastel inks glow and primaries flip fill and ink** (`palette-dark.json`; Phase 2's "what holds up").
  - The inks are L 0.81-0.87 at 8.9-10.4:1 on their fills.
  - F260 Done becomes #9DC183 with dark ink at 9.2:1, and Kid Verse Done ★ #7FB9B5; Prayer's "Pray now" and Timer's Start flip the same way. This is the house fill/ink flip done right.
- **OK-DARK-5 — `theme-color` follows a Me tap and an OS flip.** The control cases C and D in P4-DARK-04 match.

### Checked and not a bug

1. **The Larder size select and the Dollywood selects at 1.06-1.25:1 (Midnight or Forest on a light OS; Parchment or Frost on a dark OS).**
   - This is an artefact of the rig's Windows WebKit port, which paints every `<select>` itself. All three skeptics showed it:
     - a select with `background: rgb(255,0,0)`, with or without a border, still renders #F4F4F4 on a light OS and #343434 on a dark OS;
     - System light renders #F4F4F4 where #FFFCF8 is declared.

### Unresolved

1. **What iOS and iPadOS Safari paint for a styled select whose theme opposes the OS.** The Larder `#size` and the Dollywood `#bmap`/`#hf`/`#cint` declare an author border and a token background. Apple's WebKit should switch such a select to the styled `menulist-button` look and paint the author background (the skeptics' understanding, not checked on a device). The same check would give iOS's ButtonFace for P4-DARK-03.
   - To settle: on an iPad in light mode with Midnight picked, open the Larder's add bar and the park map's Search and Style panes, and screenshot them. Repeat on an iPhone in dark mode with Parchment. Safari on a Mac with the appearance forced also works.
2. **Other browser-painted parts under the single `color-scheme`**: checkboxes (`label.tog > input`, 572 in the build guide), the range slider, the Larder's date input and picker, and scrollbars. The mechanism predicts they follow the OS; none was measured.
   - To settle: the device check above, plus a Chromium probe of each with the scheme opposed.
3. **Whether the iOS Home Screen status bar repaints when `theme-color` changes at runtime** under `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style: default` (`index.html:12`). This decides whether P4-DARK-04 shows in the installed app, beyond Safari's toolbar. It is Phase 2's device check 10 (`audits/02-shell.md:5279`).
4. **Real backdrop blur on dark glass.** The rig paints none. For the park-map sheet, skeptic 2's mean-backdrop ratio stands in for blur (3.14-3.29, still failing); other dark glass was measured unblurred.
5. **Figures only the investigator measured:**
   - the story-panel luminance (7.8-12.6:1);
   - the TV kiosk Me hero under Hearth on a dark OS (1.35 and 2.34);
   - the build guide's worst card `dt` (3.0);

6. **Coverage the runs did not reach:**
   - Parchment and Frost on a dark OS beyond the native-control probes (the themes run used a light OS for every named theme);
   - hover, active and focus states in dark (only resting states were measured; the focus figures are computed from the token);

7. **Side observation (one skeptic, light mode, not verified).** In Hearth the Family list's Kitchen heading (`--teal` #137F77 on `--bg`) is 4.35:1, just under AA. Passed to COLOR.
8. **Process.** COLOR ran overlapping checks during this run (`verify-native-controls-ignore-theme-1.mjs`, `verify-raw-accent-ink-no-dark-lift-1.mjs`). P4-DARK-01 and P4-DARK-03 may duplicate them, and should be merged at consolidation with one ID each.

### Token gaps for the proposal

The fixes are written in the Phase 4 token proposal. These are the gaps this dimension found.

1. **`color-scheme` per resolved scheme** (color): `:root[data-scheme="light"]{color-scheme:light}` and `:root[data-scheme="dark"]{color-scheme:dark}`, after P2-VIS-03's fix makes `data-scheme` right. With it, ButtonFace, checkboxes, range, pickers and scrollbars follow the theme. Pair it with an author background on every button and `appearance:none` plus a token chevron on selects, since Forest's dark ButtonFace fails even when the schemes match (4.33). Evidence: `apps/design.css:15`; P4-DARK-03. The select numbers are not evidence (Checked and not a bug 1).
2. **An explicit Hearth block** (color): `:root[data-theme="hearth"]`, or hub.js keeping `data-theme="hearth"`, so that tokens and `data-scheme` always agree. Evidence: `apps/hub.js:77, 79`; `apps/design.css:176-197`; P4-DARK-02.
3. **A dark-lifted profile foreground** (color): `--accent-fg`, which is `--accent-deep` in light and a lifted mix in dark. It must guarantee 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for graphics against the card, for all eight family colours, the kiosk and guest colours, in every palette. Add a lint rule that `var(--accent)` is never used for text or strokes. `--accent-deep` already reaches 5.59-8.65 in dark (Table DARK-4). Evidence: `apps/hub.js:80`; P4-DARK-01.
4. **Dark soft fills that read as tints** (color): `--*-soft` and `--accent-soft` at about 1.4:1 or more from the card in dark (for example, ink at 20-24% over the surface), plus `--*-fill` for state shapes that must reach 3:1. Chroma of 0.05 or more is a palette-wide need, Hearth included. Evidence: `apps/design.css:163-169`; GAP-DARK-1.
5. **A dark elevation ladder and a separate fill token** (color, shadow):
   - a page-to-card step of about 1.2:1 or more;
   - a lighter-than-card `--fill` for wells, tracks and skeletons in dark, separate from `--surface-2`;
   - dark elevation expressed as a surface step plus a top hairline, instead of black `--e1`…`--e4` (the glass tokens already have `--glass-spec` for this).
   Evidence: `apps/design.css:157, 173-174, 540`; GAP-DARK-2.
6. **A focus token at 3:1 in every palette** (color): a solid ring in `--accent-fg` with an offset. Evidence: `apps/design.css:102`; GAP-DARK-3.
7. **A toast/HUD material per scheme** (color): `--toast-bg` and `--toast-ink`, used by the shared toast and Prayer's own. Evidence: `apps/design.css:588-589`; `apps/prayer.html:254-260`; VIS-DARK-1.
8. **A theme-applied hook** (other): hub.js dispatches a same-window theme event from `applyTheme`, or syncs the theme-color metas itself, so the shell re-syncs whenever a theme is applied, not only on taps. Evidence: `apps/hub.js:35, 97-105`; `index.html:656-658`; P4-DARK-04.
9. **Dark art** (other): `scripts/make-art.mjs` emits dark variants (or inline SVG with token fills), plus one shared dark rule for spot, empty and story art. Evidence: `art-dark.json`; `index.html:203`; CONS-DARK-1.
10. **Dollywood category and water literals** (color): `--cat-attr` #FF6B4A, `--cat-shop` #5B8DEF, `--cat-dine` #F2A44A, `--cat-ink` #1C1714, `--water` #3E9BC4 and the wait-band fills are identical in light and dark. They need dark pastel pairs or a documented map exemption. Changes go in the sibling template. Evidence: `local-tokens.json`; `summary.json` nonAdaptText (`span.wt`, `span.n`).
11. **A `--placeholder` token applied to every `::placeholder`** (color): the UA's #A9A9A9 shows in the build guide, F260 and Prayer inputs, the same in both schemes (2.13-2.3:1 in light). Evidence: `summary.json` nonAdaptText (`input#q`, `input#pass1`, `input#f-newcat`).

## Per-profile accent use (ACCENT)

Baseline: the working tree at fe6041d (no app file has changed since). Every number here comes from one of five sources:
- the investigator's token maths (`tokens.mjs`): 11 colours × 7 theme keys, re-derived with sRGB `color-mix()` and matched to WebKit's resolved values;
- a runtime pass signed in as every profile in every theme key (`runtime.mjs`: 896 jobs on the iPad portrait in WebKit, plus a park-day pass), and the Phase 4 rig dataset (`dataset-scan.mjs`);
- the investigator's targeted runs (`recolour.mjs`, `app-vs-person.mjs`, `cvd-strip.mjs`);
- two skeptics per defect, each with their own script;
- an independent re-measure of 20 key numbers (`remeasure.mjs`), which imports no investigator code.

Everything ran on the local instance. No request went to production, and no PIN or pairing code was read or used.

**The colours.** The eight seeded household colours (`worker/seed.sql:4-11`) are Eli #4F5D8C, Mae #BC5A38, Ezra #137F77, Kiara #B4861B, Elizabeth #8A6A4B, David #3D5A3D, Mea #5B8143 and the Downstairs TV #4C4C58. The token maths also covers the two guest-only swatches (plum #8C4F7A, sage #4C7B6A, `index.html:449`) and the overflow guest Theo (#1F6FB2). "Household cells" means 8 colours × 7 keys = 56.

**The 7 theme keys.**
- System light (the Hearth tokens by day).
- Parchment and Frost (light OS).
- Midnight and Forest (light OS).
- System dark (the Midnight tokens).
- Hearth on a dark OS ("Hearth-dark"). It takes the dark tokens while reporting `data-scheme=light`. That is the P2-VIS-03 / P2-PWA-07 state, not a palette of its own, but it is one of the 7 keys in every count below. So 8 of every 32 "dark" household cells are this state.

**How contrast is reported.** A rendered figure is the computed ink against the median painted background under the element, taken with the text or graphic hidden (skeptics, re-measure). Figures marked p10 come from the runtime pass or the dataset. Figures marked "token" are maths. Text is judged at 4.5:1 (3:1 at 24 px, or 18.66 px bold), and information-bearing graphics at 3:1.

**Summary**

- **Six defects confirmed, each 2/2: three medium and three low.**
  - **Selection by hue (P4-ACCENT-01, medium) is new.** The tab bar, Prayer's nav and Timer's presets mark the selected item only with a 1.0-1.35:1 fill and a hue shift, at the same weight and with the same icon. For David in the dark palettes and Kiara in the light ones, the selected label's luminance differs from its neighbours' by 1.02-1.08:1. This settles U-TOK-1: the tab bar's selected state fails.
  - **Two mediums are the Colour section's defects measured per person.** They are the raw profile colour as small text (P4-ACCENT-02 = P4-COLOR-02) and Me → Switch in dark (P4-ACCENT-03 = P4-COLOR-03). Phase 5 should keep one ID for each. This section adds the per-adult matrices and one structural proof: no single hex can be AA text on both the Hearth card and the Midnight page.
  - **Three lows, two lowered from the investigator's medium:**
    - Person-coloured rings in the apps and in Kiara's light palettes (P4-ACCENT-04).
    - An admin recolour never reaches a signed-in session (P4-ACCENT-05).
    - The pressed north-up compass, whose "N" sits at 1.0-2.45:1 on the person's fill for every profile, with the needle at 1.0-1.5:1 in dark (P4-ACCENT-06).
- **The cause is one line.** `apps/hub.js:80` writes the profile's raw hex as `--accent` in every scheme. Only the derived tokens adapt (`apps/design.css:87-89`; dark `:170, 191, 212`).
  - `--accent-deep` passes for every colour in every theme: 0/77 cells fail, 4.72-12.01:1 (OK-ACCENT-1).
  - Every use of the raw hex as ink or as a thin graphic fails for some colour in some scheme: 39/56 household cells as text on a card, 43/56 as text on the page, and 13/56 as a graphic.
- **The person colours are neither pastel nor distinct as fills.**
  - They sit at OKLCH L 0.42-0.65. Their soft fills are near-grey: C 0.004-0.026 in Hearth, against 0.057-0.093 for the house pastels.
  - As fills, 6 of 21 household pairs are under ΔE00 5 even with normal vision (David/Mea 2.43).
  - One hue means a person, an app and a status at once. 5 of 9 app colours are exactly a person's colour, and Mae's colour is `--danger` in Hearth (VIS-ACCENT-1, CONS-ACCENT-2).
- **Colour as identity mostly holds.** Every place that identifies a person pairs the colour with a face and a name (OK-ACCENT-2). The exceptions are the Timer and Tally, where the owner is shown by hue (P3's).
  - Signed out, the PIN pad paints its dots and Continue in Elizabeth's colour, whoever is signing in (CONS-ACCENT-1).
  - A recolour leaves the old colour on open sessions (P4-ACCENT-05).
- **Apps use the accent unevenly.** Prayer, Timer, Verses and the park map put it on primaries and selection. F260, the Larder and the build guide keep it off their content, and Tally uses it only as a wash (CONS-ACCENT-4). Two of the three apps that override the accent locally forget to re-derive `--accent-deep` (CONS-ACCENT-3).
- **The re-measure checked 20 numbers: 17 agree and 3 do not.** All three disagreements are non-text or park-map values, and all are corrected below:
  - Kiara's Kids-chip ring passes in Hearth and Frost.
  - The park tab-icon ranges change.
  - The ride-card distance reads 2.08 dark and 4.17 light.

  It also corrected six statements in the draft: the Kitchen pair, Mae's Kitchen, "Hearth-dark" as a palette, the wording on the house fills, and the two counts built on the "vsDecl" background model.

### Confirmed defects

Six defects, each confirmed by both skeptics. They are ordered by severity, and then by how many people and screens they reach.

#### P4-ACCENT-01 — The selected tab, Prayer nav item and Timer preset are marked only by a 1.0-1.35:1 fill and a shift in hue: for David in the dark palettes and Kiara in the light ones, the selected tab's label differs from its neighbours by 1.02-1.08:1

- **Severity: medium.** Both skeptics rated it medium; it is not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** a measurable accessibility failure on the primary navigation.
    - The only indicator of the current section is non-text below 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11).
    - The selected and idle colours differ by less than 3:1, with no second cue (1.4.1).
  - **Why not high:**
    - The page content and the tab's position still show where you are.
    - The label text itself passes (4.70+).
    - `aria-current` is set (`index.html:640`; Prayer's `aria-current="true"`), so VoiceOver announces the state.
  - **Exposure:** every person, in every theme, on every screen with the tab bar or Prayer's nav. The kiosk hides the tab bar (`index.html:78`). The worst cases are David in System dark, Midnight and Forest (1.05-1.08; System is Midnight at night), and Kiara in Hearth, Parchment and Frost (1.02-1.06).
- **Areas:** shell (the tab bar, and the desktop sidebar, which uses the same classes), prayer (bottom nav), timer (presets). The park map's sheet tabs are a weaker form: the fill is 1.12-1.30, but the label also changes luminance.
- **What happens.** In each component, selection changes only the ink hue and adds an `--accent-soft` fill:
  - **Tab bar.**
    - `.ds .tab` is `--muted` at weight 600 (`apps/design.css:559-560`), and `.tab.on` changes only the colour, to `--accent-deep` (`:564`).
    - The indicator `.tab-ind` is `--accent-soft`, 14 % of the accent into `--surface` (`:566-567`, `:87`).
    - The icon is the same `<use>` in both states (`index.html:396-399`), and `showTab` toggles only `.on` and `aria-current` (`:640`).
  - **Prayer nav.** `nav button` is `--muted` at 600; the current item gets `--accent-deep` on `--accent-soft` (`apps/prayer.html:276-281`).
  - **Timer presets.** `.presets .btn.on` gets an `--accent-soft` fill, a 45 % accent border and `--accent-deep` ink (`apps/timer.html:44`).
  - **Park sheet tabs.** An 18 % accent fill, the label changed from `--dim` to `--text`, and the icon in the raw accent (template `:428-429`).
  - **Measured** (skeptics, rendered):

    | Component | Fill against its neighbours or bar | Selected ÷ idle ink | Other cue | Below 3:1 |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | Tab bar | 1.09-1.25 (token 1.10-1.24, 56/56) | 1.02-2.03 (Table ACCENT-5) | none: weight 600, same icon | 49/49 and 42/42 |
    | Prayer nav, personal list | 1.11-1.23 | 1.05-2.03 (David dark 1.05-1.06) | none | 35/35 and 30/30 |
    | Prayer nav, Family list (`--teal-soft`) | 1.03-1.04 (runtime, heuristic) | teal, the same for everyone | none | — |
    | Timer preset `.on` | 1.09-1.24 against the idle chips (skeptic 2); 1.00-1.35 against the page, Kiara in Parchment 1.00 (skeptic 1) | 1.15-2.70 | a 45 % accent border, 1.10-1.58 (skeptic 1; skeptic 2 read 1.00-1.35) | 49/49 and 42/42 |
    | Park sheet tab | 1.12-1.30 | label `--dim` → `--text`: 2.75 light, 1.62 dark | raw-accent icon (P4-COLOR-02) | fill only |

- **Expected.** A selected state that can be seen without hue: an indicator of at least 3:1 against the bar or card, or a second cue such as weight, a filled icon or an underline. The house style asks for "Hierarchy through weight and size, not color alone" (`audits/HUB-AUDIT-PROMPT.md:50`) and says "Never rely on hue alone" (`:71-73`).
- **Why it matters.**
  - The tab bar is the navigation on every screen for every person.
  - A colour-blind adult, someone reading the kitchen iPad across the room, or a pre-reader relying on shape cannot tell which tab is current.
  - For David in dark, the selected and idle inks are also almost the same hue for a deuteranope (ΔE00 1.43), so neither luminance nor hue separates them.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/design.css:87, 559-567`; `index.html:78, 396-399, 640`; `apps/prayer.html:276-281`; `apps/timer.html:44`; `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:428-429` (read-only).
  - Investigator: `tokens.json` (`selection.rows`), `runtime-summary.json` (timer presets 84/84; Prayer nav 56/56 and 35/35), `tabbar-selected-dad-kiara.png`.
  - Skeptics:
    - `verify-selection-by-hue-only-1.json`, `-1-park.json`, `-1-shots.json`, `-1-system-dark-dad-shell.png`, `-1-system-light-kiara-shell.png`
    - `verify-selection-by-hue-only-2-{shell,timer,prayer}.json`, `-2-shell-dad-system-dark.png`, `-2-timer-kiara-parchment.png`
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-tokens.json` (indicator 56/56; ink 1.02-2.17 over 11 colours; David dark 1.06, deuteranopia ΔE00 1.43).
- **Reproduction.** All from `cd "C:/Users/ex_bo/OneDrive/Claude Related/App Hub"`:
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/tokens.mjs --selection` prints the David row at 1.06 in the dark columns.

#### P4-ACCENT-05 — An admin recolour never reaches a person who is already signed in: their chrome and every open app keep the old colour until they next sign in

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low; this section lowers it from the investigator's medium.
  - **Clause:** cosmetic, and triggered by a rare admin edit. No data is lost or misattributed, and no flow breaks.
  - **Exposure:** anyone who stays signed in after an admin changes their colour.
    - On a personal phone it lasts until they sign out.
    - On the shared iPad, the next sign-in fetches the new profile (skeptic 2), but the session also never returns to the picker by itself (P2-PROF-09, skeptic 1).
- **Areas:** shell, and every app through hub.js.
- **What happens.**
  - **Where the colour comes from.** `--accent` is `hub.profile.color` (`apps/hub.js:80`). `hub.profile` is read only from the stored session (`:105-111`).
  - **What refreshes the session:**
    - login and createPin (`:169, 173`);
    - a photo change (`:482, 488`);
    - an admin editing their own profile on the same device (`index.html:1684`).
  - **What does not.** No client calls `GET /api/me` (`worker/src/index.js:270`). Pulls never touch the session (`apps/hub.js:286-320`), and the frames' `storage` listener ignores `hub.session` (`:350-364`).
  - **Run** (investigator, Mae → #8C4F7A). The admin PUT returns 200 and the server's `/api/me` returns #8C4F7A. On Mae's iPad:
    - `--accent` stays #BC5A38 after a reload and after 35 s of pulls;
    - the Tally frame stays #BC5A38;
    - a fresh picker shows #8C4F7A.
- **Expected.** A colour change reaches every open session and frame within one pull, as other shared data does.
- **Why it matters.** The person's own chrome, hero and buttons show a colour the rest of the household no longer associates with them. After a reload, the feed on the same page already shows the new one.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/hub.js:80, 105-111, 169, 173, 286-320, 350-364, 482, 488`; `index.html:1684`; `worker/src/index.js:270, 453-475`; `audits/00-inventory.md:457-458`.
  - Investigator: `recolour.json`, `recolour-mae-home-after.png`, `recolour-mae-tally-after.png`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-recolour-not-propagated-1.json`, `-1-home.png`, `-1-tally.png`; `verify-recolour-not-propagated-2.json`, `-2-home.png`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-recolour.json`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/verify-recolour-not-propagated-1.mjs` runs Mae on the iPad in WebKit. It prints `--accent` as #BC5A38 at every step, 0 client `/api/me` requests, and the picker `--tint` as the new colour.
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/verify-recolour-not-propagated-2.mjs` runs David on the iPhone in Chromium.
  - Both change a profile colour on the local instance only.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** (Mae, iPad, WebKit, a different swatch #5B6FA8) read `--accent` inline and computed, `hub.profile.color`, the stored session, `hub.people()` and the feed `--tint` at six points: after `hub.pull()`, a visibilitychange, a reload, 35 s of pulls, `hub.profiles()`, and in the Tally frame.
    - The accent stayed #BC5A38 throughout, with 0 `/api/me` calls.
    - The feed changed after the reload (the server joins the colour), while `hub.people()` changed only when `hub.profiles()` was called.
    - A pre-signed rig device turned out to be a stale control (`lib/local.mjs:113`), so the picker was used instead.
  - **Skeptic 2** changed the person (David), device (iPhone PWA), engine (Chromium) and colour (#2E7D5B) and got the same pattern. The selected tab kept the old colour, and so did the Timer frame. They noted that name and kind come from the same stale session (U-ACCENT-3).
- **Corrected claim.**
  - **"`hub.people()` and the feed do refresh" is half true.** The feed takes the new colour on the next reload. `hub.people()` changes only when something calls `hub.profiles()`. On a signed-in device, that is the picker, Add a guest, admin remove or purge, or a photo upload (`index.html:524, 1421, 1628, 1634`; `apps/hub.js:483, 489`).
  - **The investigator's "after a profiles refresh" step was forced by its own script.**
  - **"Two colours on one screen":** they are on the same page, but not in the same iPad viewport.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - P2-PROF-09: the shared iPad never returns to the picker.
  - The Phase 0 gap at `audits/00-inventory.md:457-458` (no ID).

#### P4-ACCENT-06 — With north-up pressed, the compass fills with the person's `--accent-deep`: its 9 px red "N" drops to 1.0-2.45:1 for every profile, and its red needle to 1.0-1.5:1 in dark

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** a secondary label and graphic on an optional map toggle. The compass shape, the ring and the rotation still show which way is north, and the button is unpressed by default (template `:620`, `aria-pressed="false"`).
  - **Exposure:** only while north-up is on, but then for every household profile in every theme (41 skeptic cases, all below 3:1).
- **Areas:** dollywood-live (from the sibling template).
- **What happens.**
  - **The fill wins on specificity.** `[data-flavor=live] button[aria-pressed=true]{background:var(--accent-deep)}` (template `:225`, specificity 0,2,1) beats `.lv-north`'s glass (`:417`, 0,1,0) once the button is pressed (`:1595`).
  - **The glyphs are fixed red.** The "N" is `.lv-north b{font-size:9px;font-weight:800;color:var(--danger)}` (`:418`), and the needle is a literal `fill="#FF6B4A"` (`:620`).
  - **Neither changes with the person's colour, while the fill does.** Rendered, the pixel ratio equals the token ratio within 0.02 (Table ACCENT-6):

    | Glyph | Dark | Light |
    |---|---|---|
    | "N" | 1.01-1.37 (Eli 1.01, Kiara 1.37) | 1.28-2.45 (Kiara 1.28, David 2.45) |
    | Needle | 1.01-1.48 | Mae, Elizabeth, Mea, Ezra and Kiara 2.05-2.97; Eli and David pass at 3.44-4.27 |

- **Expected.** The north indicator stays at least 4.5:1 for the label, or 3:1 as a graphic, whatever the person's colour. The pressed state should not put a person-coloured fill under semantic glyphs.
- **Why it matters.** North-up is the orientation aid on a rotated park map. When it is switched on, its own label all but vanishes.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:225, 417-418, 620, 1595` (read-only; the same lines are in `apps/dollywood-live.html`).
  - Investigator: `dataset-accent.json` (`button#lv-north.lv-north > b`, 13/13).
  - Skeptics:
    - `verify-park-north-n-on-accent-1.json`, `-1-eli-system-dark.png`, `-1-eli-system-light.png`
    - `verify-park-north-n-on-accent-2.json`, `-2-eli-system-dark.png`, `-2-eli-system-light.png`, `-2-dad-system-light.png`
- **Reproduction.** `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/verify-park-north-n-on-accent-2.mjs --profiles=eli,kiara --themes=system-dark,system-light` prints `tokenRatioN` 1.01 / 2.15 for Eli and 1.37 / 1.28 for Kiara, with `tokenRatioArrow` alongside.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** confirmed the specificity chain and ran 15 cases: 5 adults in System light and dark, and Eli in five palettes. It resolved the computed background and N colours through a canvas.
    - 15/15 were below 3:1, at 1.01-2.45.
    - A pixel pass was contaminated by the needle overlapping the N's box, so the exact-paint ratios are reported.
  - **Skeptic 2** ran 26 cases: 7 profiles in System light and dark, plus Eli, Mae and David in four palettes. It hid the N and took the pixel median under its box, and checked that the glyph lies 100 % inside the 44 px circle.
    - 26/26 were below 3:1.
    - It added the needle facet.
    - It noted that the disc also rotates on the first tap (P3-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-09).
- **Corrected claim.**
  - **It is broader than stated.** The draft had Eli only; it is every profile.
  - **Eli's light values are 1.88-2.15 in exact paint,** not the dataset's p10 1.39-1.45.
  - **The needle on the same fill is new here.** P4-ICON-04 covers the needle on the unpressed glass in light, and notes the N at 4.37-4.77 there.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - P4-ICON-04: the needle, unpressed.
  - P3-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-09: the compass behaviour.
  - Table COLOR-3 row "Compass N", which defers the pressed state to this section.

### Consistency, visual and gap findings

These were not put to skeptics. They rest on the investigator's evidence, and the re-measure reproduced every number quoted here.

#### CONS-ACCENT-1 — Signed out, the accent falls back to Elizabeth's colour, so every PIN pad fills its dots and Continue in #8A6A4B (Midnight #CBA77E), whoever is signing in (investigator rating: low)

- **The rule.** `.pin-dots i.on` is painted with `--accent` (`index.html:58`). hub.js removes `--accent` while nobody is signed in (`apps/hub.js:81`), so `--accent: var(--mocha)` applies (`apps/design.css:86`). That is Elizabeth's exact hex.
- **The pad knows the person but does not use it.** It sets the person's `--tint` (`index.html:553`), but only the avatar ring reads it. The rig's own note expects "dots fill in the person's colour" (`audits/tools/areas/shell.mjs:165`).
- **The same hex is the default everywhere:** `FALLBACK` (`index.html:450`), `hub.avatarHtml`'s fallback (`apps/hub.js:461`), and the Worker's guest default (`worker/src/index.js:182`).
- **Rendered on Eli's pad.** The avatar ring is rgb(79,93,140). The filled dots are rgb(138,106,75) in System light and rgb(203,167,126) in Midnight (`remeasure-pin.json`, exact).
- **Expected.** The pad, dots and Continue in the person's colour. Defaults and fallbacks in a neutral that is nobody's colour.
- **Evidence and reproduction.** `pin-pad-mocha-dots-eli.png`. Run `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/runtime.mjs --profiles signed-out --only shell:pin-entry --themes system-light,midnight --force`, then read `runtime/system-light/signed-out/shell--pin-entry.json`, or run `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/remeasure.mjs pin`.

#### CONS-ACCENT-2 — One hue means a person, an app and a status at once: 5 of 9 app colours are a household member's exact colour, and Mae's running Timer ring is `--danger` (investigator rating: low)

- **App colours.** They are painted through the same `--tint` as people (`index.html:700, 1165-1188`); see Table ACCENT-8.
  - F260 = Eli, Larder = David, Prayer = Elizabeth, Kid Verse = Kiara, Verses = Mea.
  - Tally is the sage swatch, and the park map is the overflow guest's colour.
  - Timer is ΔE00 3.2 from Mae.
  - On David's Home, the F260 card, ring and tile are Eli's slate (`home-david-system-dark.png`).
- **Semantic colours.** Six of the eight household colours equal a hue or semantic token. P2 recorded the four semantic ones (`audits/02-shell.md:5786`), and CONS-COLOR-4 records the semantic confusion.
- **New facet.** Mae's accent equals `--danger` exactly in Hearth, since `--danger: var(--terra)` = #BC5A38 (`apps/design.css:77, 82`). The Timer paints the running ring in her colour and "time's up" in `--danger` (`apps/timer.html:22, 36-38`). For Mae the two states are the same colour; UX-TIMER-4 measured Elizabeth at 1.1.
- **Guest colours.** 3 of the 4 seeded guests reuse a household hex exactly (`audits/tools/seed/story.mjs:32, 36, 38`).
- **Expected.** Person colours reserved for people, and app and semantic colours drawn from a set no profile can take.
- **Evidence and reproduction.** `app-vs-person.json`; `worker/seed.sql:4-11`; `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/app-vs-person.mjs` prints 6 rows marked identical, plus Timer → Mae at 3.2.
- **Related:** the P2 deviation "Profile colours double as the semantic colours" (`audits/02-shell.md:5786`), UX-TIMER-4, CONS-COLOR-4, and the tile glyphs' contrast in P4-ICON-01.

#### CONS-ACCENT-3 — A local accent override does not re-derive the tokens that paint: Kid Verse and Prayer's Family list get it wrong, Verses gets it right (investigator rating: low)

- **Why it breaks.** `--accent-soft`, `--accent-tint` and `--accent-deep` are computed once on `:root` (`apps/design.css:87-89`).
- **Kid Verse** sets only `--accent: var(--gold)` (`apps/kidverse.html:55, 137`), so Done ★ keeps the kid's deep (P3-KIDVERSE-14).
- **Prayer's Family list** sets `--accent` and `--accent-soft` to teal but not `--accent-deep` (`apps/prayer.html:39`). The pressed chips, Pray now and the nav label stay in the person's deep on a teal page (VIS-PRAYER-4).
- **Verses** re-declares all three tokens on its rating buttons (`apps/verses.html:56-58`) and works.
- **Expected.** One mechanism that re-derives every accent token wherever `--accent` changes.
- **Related:** GAP-TOK-6 (the Tokens section's system gap), P3-KIDVERSE-14, VIS-PRAYER-4.

#### CONS-ACCENT-4 — Three apps never put the person's colour on their content and Tally uses it only as a wash, while Prayer, Timer, Verses and the park map carry it on primaries and selection (investigator rating: low)

The runtime pass covered every profile.
- **F260:** 0 contrast-bearing accent groups, 3 glass groups, and 13 hue collisions. Its `.btn.primary` is `--slate` for everyone (`apps/f260.html:208`), which is Eli's colour on every person's F260.
- **Larder:** the add-bar glass only (`apps/leftovers.html:39`).
- **Build guide:** pressed chips and tools only; progress is olive and gold.
- **Tally:** 15 decor groups, the page wash.

The house style asks for the accent "applied consistently (profile chip, selection states, progress, activity feed)" (`audits/HUB-AUDIT-PROMPT.md:71-72`).

- **Evidence and reproduction.** `runtime-summary.json` (`areas`); `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/recount.mjs` prints the area table.
- **Related:** VIS-F260-11, VIS-LEFTOVERS-4, OK-DOLLYWOOD-4, VIS-TALLY-8.

#### VIS-ACCENT-1 — The profile colours are neither pastel nor distinct enough as fills: the soft fills are near-grey, and 6 of 21 household pairs sit under ΔE00 5 as fills (investigator rating: medium)

- **The colours are mid-tones.** Every profile colour sits at OKLCH L 0.42-0.65: too dark to be a fill, too light and too grey to be an ink.
  - The house style's pastel fills are L 0.876-0.953 and C 0.057-0.093 (`audits/HUB-AUDIT-PROMPT.md:55-63`).
  - design.css's own `-soft` fills are only C 0.014-0.037 in Hearth (VIS-COLOR-1).
- **The derived `--accent-soft` is near-grey:** C 0.004-0.026 in Hearth (Eli's is #E6E6E9 at C 0.004), 0.005-0.019 in Frost, 0.024-0.047 in Parchment and 0.006-0.036 in Midnight (`tokens.json` `rows[].softChroma`).
- **The dark "glowing" ink is muddy.** `--accent-deep` in dark is C 0.031-0.086 (Elizabeth #BBA997 at 0.033, David #8E9F8E at 0.031); Timer's visual check saw the same (`audits/03-apps/timer.md:445`).
- **As fills, people run together.** 6/21 household pairs are under ΔE00 5 in Hearth even with normal vision (David / Mea 2.43, Mae / Elizabeth 4.1). Under colour-blindness the raw colours collide too: deuteranopia Elizabeth / Mea 2.1, protanopia Mae / Elizabeth 4.8 (Table ACCENT-7).
- **The picker offers only these ten mid-tones** (`index.html:449`).
- **Expected.** Each profile gets a distinct, vibrant pastel accent (fill + deep ink of one hue) that stays vibrant in dark (`audits/HUB-AUDIT-PROMPT.md:69-73`).
- **Evidence.** `tokens.json` (`lc`, `house`, `rows[].softChroma`, `pairs`), `cvd-strip.png`, `worker/seed.sql:4-11`.
- **Reproduction.** `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/tokens.mjs` prints `lc` and the closest pairs; `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/cvd-strip.mjs` draws the strip.
- **Related:** the P2 deviation "The earthy Hearth palette, not the house pastels" (`audits/02-shell.md:5778`), and VIS-COLOR-1 (the whole palette's chroma). This item is the person-colour facet.

#### GAP-ACCENT-1 — The colour picker cannot keep people apart: swatches are named by hex, duplicates are allowed, and nothing checks lightness, contrast or colour-blind distance (investigator rating: low)

- **The swatches are unnamed.** Each carries `aria-label="#4F5D8C"` and so on (`index.html:1398, 1666`). The selected swatch is shown only by a `--text` border and a scale (`index.html:308`).
- **Nothing stops two people sharing a colour.**
  - A new guest defaults to Ezra's teal (`index.html:1393`).
  - 3 of the 4 seeded guests share a household hex.
  - The Worker checks only the `#rrggbb` format (`worker/src/index.js:183, 469`).
- **The slate swatch reads 2.62-2.69 against the dark sheet** (`dataset-accent.json` → `graphics.shell`).
- **Expected.** Named, unique, pre-validated pastel choices, with duplicates blocked or flagged.
- **Related:** the P2 deviation at `audits/02-shell.md:5788`.

### What works

- **OK-ACCENT-1 — The derived ink `--accent-deep` is AA for every profile colour in every theme.** It keeps the promise in `apps/design.css:89`, in dark too.
  - **Token maths (the re-measure reproduced it exactly):** deep on surface 5.34-11.57, deep on soft 4.72-9.29, on-accent on deep 5.64-12.01, with 0/77 cells failing.
  - **Rendered for every person:**
    - Timer Start 5.89+; Verses Show and Kid Verse Done ★ 4.74+;
    - tab and preset labels 4.70+;
    - Prayer Pray now 6.64+; the timer-pill digits 4.91+;
    - build-guide chips 0/105 failing.
  - **The one dip** is Kiara's gradient top stop (4.35 Hearth, 4.45 Frost), and her rendered label still passes.
  - **Related:** OK-COLOR-3 (the same result from the Colour section), OK-VERSES-3, OK-TIMER-3.
- **OK-ACCENT-2 — Wherever a person is identified, the colour is paired with a face and a name.** This covers the picker, feed, Kids card, park list, TV faces and lines, Prayer's asker and prayed-today faces, Kid Verse rows, the Verses who-pill and the park map markers (`index.html:533, 899, 916, 955, 1045, 1070`; `apps/hub.js:461`; Table ACCENT-7). The hue-only owner cues are the Timer and Tally, both already in Phase 3. Related: OK-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-2.
- **OK-ACCENT-3 — Verses shows how a local accent should work.** Its rating buttons re-declare `--accent`, `--accent-soft` and `--accent-deep` together, taking the deep value from each hue's AA `-ink` token (`apps/verses.html:56-58`). So Not yet, Almost and Got it each read in one consistent hue, whoever is signed in. It is the pattern CONS-ACCENT-3 asks the other apps to follow.

### Checked and not a bug

- **"The Prayer initials are painted in the viewer's accent" (the draft's raw-on-soft, 48/56).** They are not. `.init` renders only for a name `hub.people()` does not know (`apps/prayer.html:1551-1555`), and only on the Family list (`:1558, 1571`), where `--accent` is teal (`:39`). 0 initials rendered in 10 runs (P4-ACCENT-02 skeptic 2).
- **"Kiara's earned stars are 2.78" as an accent failure.** The star is `--gold` on `--gold-soft` for every kid (`apps/kidverse.html:67-68`); Ezra's reads the same 2.78. It is P4-COLOR-01's.
- **Kiara's Kids-chip ring in Hearth and Frost.** It passes, at 3.22 and 3.19, against the card it sits on. The draft's 2.96 and 2.89 were against `--bg` (re-measure; both P4-ACCENT-04 skeptics).
- **The TV's selected tab (1.02-1.04).** The kiosk has no tab bar (`index.html:78`).
- **The TV's Me → Switch (2.59).** It cannot be reached through the UI: `enterShell` sends the kiosk to Home whatever the hash (`index.html:626`), and it switches with its own `#kiosk-switch`.
- **"The park sheet tab is selected by hue only."** Its label also changes from `--dim` to `--text` (2.75:1 light, 1.62:1 dark). Its fill is still below 3:1 (P4-ACCENT-01).
- **The signed-out PIN "Continue" at 1.42 in the runtime pass.** That is the disabled state: the button starts `disabled` (`index.html:564`), and disabled buttons are drawn at opacity .45 (`apps/design.css:360`) until four digits are in. WCAG exempts inactive controls. The enabled button's colour is CONS-ACCENT-1.
- **The Family-list Kitchen headings.** They are teal, not a person's colour: 8.52-8.64 in dark, 4.35-4.37 in light (P4-ACCENT-02 skeptic 2). The light-palette teal-as-text failure belongs to P4-COLOR-01.
- **Failing text groups in Table ACCENT-2 that are not this dimension's:**
  - the Home and Me hero text (P2-VIS-06, P2 VIS);
  - album captions over photos (P2 VIS);
  - the "shared" pill (VIS-PRAYER-1);
  - Kid Verse day letters (VIS-KIDVERSE-1).

### Unresolved

- **U-ACCENT-1 — Why Prayer's More → Kitchen cannot be opened for Mae in the rig.**
  - The seed writes her personal list (`audits/tools/seed/prayer.mjs:170-172`; `audits/tools/areas/prayer.mjs:66` lists `christian` in `HAS_OWN_LIST`).
  - `#moreBtn` is in her DOM, yet the tap timed out in 7 runtime jobs, in the re-measure (`remeasure-prayer-mae.json`), and for the Colour skeptics. For David and Mea there is no list, so More is hidden as designed.
  - **To settle it:** open Prayer as Mae on the local rig, screenshot before the tap, and read `document.elementFromPoint` at `#moreBtn`'s centre. If something covers it in the real UI, that is a new defect.
- **U-ACCENT-2 — The park map's Find-me FAB icon on the raw-accent gradient** (template `:412`).
  - By token maths, `--on-accent` on the raw colour is 2.90 for Eli and 2.42 for David in every dark key: 12/56 household cells, 4 of them the TV's colour, which cannot open the park map.
  - It was not rendered, and the gradient's lighter centre may lift it.
  - **To settle it:** render the park seed as Eli and David in Midnight and sample the icon against the gradient under it.
- **U-ACCENT-3 — Rename and kind changes probably do not reach open sessions either.** `hub.profile.name` and `.kind` come from the same stale session (P4-ACCENT-05 skeptic 2). A kind change would affect `hub.isKid` and `hub.canWrite` on the client. The server re-reads the profile per request (`worker/src/auth.js:89`).
  - **To settle it:** extend `verify-recolour-not-propagated-2.mjs` to PUT a name and a kind, then read `hub.profile`, `hub.isKid` and `hub.canWrite` after a reload.
- **U-ACCENT-4 — Real devices.** WebKit on Windows paints no backdrop blur, so the tab indicator, pills and glass-backed labels were measured against unblurred glass. Display P3 and True Tone shifts were not modelled.
  - **To settle it:** iPad and iPhone screenshots of the tab bar for David in Midnight and Kiara in Parchment, and of Me → Switch for Mea in Forest.
- **U-ACCENT-5 — The build guide's north button.** The same pressed rule covers `[data-flavor=hub]` (template `:225`), and the Colour rig counted 102 build-guide "N" occurrences at 1.0-1.45. But P4-ICON-04 reports the build guide's compass hidden below 700 px and dead above it.
  - **To settle it:** tap `#lv-north` in `apps/dollywood.html` on the iPad landscape and read `aria-pressed` and the computed background.
- **U-ACCENT-6 — What was not modelled.**
  - Colour-blind simulation is Machado 2009 at severity 1.0 (dichromacy); no anomalous trichromat and no real user.
  - Whether production profiles still use the seeded colours (production was not read).
  - The park map's you-dot, route and family markers against the illustrated map (maps are excluded from the graphics heuristics).
  - Hover, focus and active states (focus is P4-TOK-01), sheets other than Me → appearance, and the empty, overflow, loading and offline states per profile.

### Method, scripts and evidence

- **Scripts** (all in `audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/`; run from the repo root):
  - Investigator:
    - `tokens.mjs`: token maths, colour-blind distances, and the `--selection` matrix.
    - `code-uses.mjs`: static inventory of accent uses.
    - `dataset-scan.mjs`: accent texts and graphics in the Phase 4 dataset.
    - `runtime.mjs` (+ `png.mjs`): per-profile runtime, with `--park`.
    - `aggregate.mjs`: builds `runtime-summary.json`.
    - `matrix.mjs`: profile × theme for one selector.
    - `recolour.mjs`, `app-vs-person.mjs`, `cvd-strip.mjs`, `crop.mjs`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-selection-by-hue-only-{1,2}.mjs`, `verify-raw-accent-as-text-{1,2}.mjs`, `verify-hero-button-dark-every-adult-{1,2}.mjs`, `verify-raw-accent-graphics-light-and-apps-{1,2}.mjs`, `verify-recolour-not-propagated-{1,2}.mjs`, `verify-park-north-n-on-accent-{1,2}.mjs`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure.mjs` (parts: tokens, apps, prayer, park, me, kids, timer, pin, recolour).
  - Section writer: `recount.mjs`, which reads `runtime-summary.json` only and prints Table ACCENT-2.
- **Evidence** (all in `audits/evidence/p4/ACCENT/`):
  - Investigator JSON: `tokens.json`, `code-uses.json`, `dataset-accent.json`, `runtime-summary.json`, `recolour.json`, `app-vs-person.json`.
  - Investigator PNGs: `cvd-strip.png`, `tabbar-selected-dad-kiara.png`, `prayer-kitchen-raw-accent-eli-midnight-mom-parchment.png`, `park-nearby-raw-accent-eli-dad-dark.png`, `pin-pad-mocha-dots-eli.png`, `home-david-system-dark.png`, `me-hero-dark-switch-mea-eli.png`, `kids-chip-kiara-parchment.png`, `recolour-mae-home-after.png`, `recolour-mae-tally-after.png`.
  - Skeptics' `verify-*.json` and `verify-*.png`, as cited per defect.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-*.json`.
  - `runtime/` and `runtime-shots/` are regenerated by `runtime.mjs` and git-ignored.
- **Rig.** Everything used the local instance through `audits/tools/lib/local.mjs`, mostly WebKit on the iPad portrait. Skeptics also used the iPhone PWA, the TV device and, for P4-ACCENT-05, Chromium. Themes were set through `PUT /api/data/hub/theme?scope=person` as each profile, plus localStorage `hub.theme`. `L.close()` ran in every script, and no server or browser was left running. The recolour scripts changed a profile colour on the local instance only; the re-measure restored Mae to #BC5A38.
- **Re-measure result: 20 numbers checked, 17 agree and 3 disagree.**
  - **Tolerances:** text and token contrast ±0.05, non-text ±0.1, ΔE00 ±0.1; hex values and counts exact.
  - **Agree:**
    - token derivation, max 0.5/255 over 231 checks;
    - raw-on-surface 39/56, 1.92-8.27, no colour passing all 7 keys;
    - the Prayer Kitchen headings;
    - the park walk time (27/35 adult cells = 54/70);
    - Me → Switch per adult (largest gap 0.03) and 32/32 token dark cells;
    - the timer-pill ring (within 0.07);
    - the selection indicator 56/56 and ink 1.02-2.17;
    - soft chroma, soft-pair minimum, and the colour-blind pairs;
    - app colours 5 of 9;
    - the recolour behaviour, the PIN dots, `--accent-deep` 0/77, and the 896-job coverage.
  - **Disagree, corrected in place:**
    - **Kiara's Kids-chip ring:** 2.69 / 3.19 / 3.22, not 2.37 / 2.89 / 2.96 (P4-ACCENT-04).
    - **The park selected tab icon:** David 1.52, Eli 1.75, Mae 3.15 in Hearth (passes), Kiara 2.43-2.50 (Table ACCENT-6).
    - **The ride-card distance:** 2.08 / 4.17, not 1.63-2.00 / 3.34-3.77 (P4-ACCENT-02). It still fails in both.
    - **The cause of the first two:** the draft's "vsDecl" metric (`matrix.mjs:21`, `aggregate.mjs:47`) measures against the nearest declared background, often the page, not the pixels next to the graphic. The investigator's own `vsOutside` field matched the re-measure.
  - **Draft statements corrected:**
    - the Kitchen headings sit on `--bg`, weight 700;
    - Mae's Kitchen was not measured because a tap timed out, not because her list is empty (U-ACCENT-1);
    - "Hearth-dark" is the P2-PWA-07 / P2-VIS-03 state, counted in the dark cells;
    - "house pastel fills" means the HOUSE STYLE target (C 0.057-0.093), not design.css's own soft fills (C 0.014-0.037);
    - the per-case non-text counts based on vsDecl are not used for severity.

## The web tells, everywhere (TELL)

This section checks the house style's twelve web tells in all eleven areas: the shell (`index.html` with `apps/design.css`), the TV board (the kiosk branch of `index.html`) and the nine apps. Baseline: the working tree at fe6041d; no app file has changed since. Everything ran on the local instance. No request went to production, and no PIN or pairing code was read or used: the pairing-code rotation button was never clicked, and every native dialog was dismissed. Measurements are taken in each area's own document: the page for the shell and the TV, the app frame inside the shell viewer for apps. The committed rig aggregate (`audits/evidence/p4/measure/tells.json`) mixes the shell page behind the viewer into every app area, so `from-raw.mjs` re-cuts the rig-v2 raw files per document. Scripts are in `audits/tools/phase4/TELL/` and evidence in `audits/evidence/p4/TELL/`.

What the rig cannot show, and this section does not claim: the iOS long-press loupe and callout, real rubber-banding, the iOS focus zoom itself, Safari's scrollbar rendering, the TV's own browser, and any timing on a real iPad (Unresolved lists them).

**Summary**

- **Four tells pass everywhere, and they are the ones design.css sets on `body` or gets free from the viewport.**
  - Tap highlight is transparent on 343/343 visible controls (re-measure: 346/346).
  - Tap latency is 0-2 ms, and every document has `width=device-width` and `touch-action: manipulation`.
  - No area paints a focus ring after a touch tap.
  - There are no blue underlined links.
  - Everything else fails in exactly the places design.css leaves it: rules scoped to `.ds`, a rule on an element that cannot carry it, a rule at a specificity the components beat, or a capability that does not exist (Table TELL-2).
  - Worst areas: the build guide (5 FAIL), then the park map and F260 (4 each), all among the five apps that never use `.ds`. Cleanest: Tally (0 FAIL) and Timer (1).
- **Two medium defects, each confirmed 2/2.**
  - **P4-TELL-01:** keyboard focus is invisible on every `.ds .btn`. 26 of 26 Tab stops in the shell, TV, Tally, Timer, Kid Verse and Verses change 0 pixels when focused, in Chromium and WebKit, light and dark. P2 filed only the shell; the cross-area reach is new.
  - **P4-TELL-07 (added after the completeness critic):** the same holds for all 9 Apps-grid tiles and all 9 picker cards, whose own shadows beat the shared ring, and the chat composer removes its ring outright.
- **Five low defects, each confirmed 2/2.**
  - **P4-TELL-02:** 12 reachable form fields are under 16 px, so iOS zooms on focus. That includes the park map's Search (15 px) and rider-height select (12.5 px).
  - **P4-TELL-03:** with Midnight chosen on a light-OS device, all nine Hearth-based documents paint paper-white Hearth until `hub.js` runs, for as long as `hub.js` is late. `apps/hub.js:59` says the theme is applied synchronously "so there is no flash".
  - **P4-TELL-04:** with classic scrollbars, 10-15 px OS bars paint on the hub's scrollers. Under Midnight on a light OS the track is a white stripe.
  - **P4-TELL-05:** the build guide first paints an empty section-chip strip, then its map drops 44-48 px.
  - **P4-TELL-06:** the only overscroll reset is set on `body`, where it has no effect.
- **Earlier phases got three tells wrong, because of rig limits or an untested case.**
  - P2 #9 ("0 px on `#views`") and P3's F260 and build-guide scrollbar rows came from Playwright's `--hide-scrollbars` flag. The chip bar is 10 px, not 6.
  - P2 #7 passed rubber-banding "in code" on a declaration that is inert.
  - P2 #6's white-flash pass is right for the case it ran (System on a dark OS). It never ran a named dark palette on a light OS.
- **Consistency, visual and gap findings (not adversarially verified).**
  - **CONS-TELL-1:** chrome is selectable in 100 % of controls in the five apps without `.ds`, and in 0 % of Tally's and Timer's. No file sets `-webkit-touch-callout`.
  - **CONS-TELL-2:** there are three confirmation idioms, and 14 of 20 native `confirm()`/`alert()` call sites are reachable.
  - **VIS-TELL-1:** light themes open the build guide on a near-black frame.
  - **GAP-TELL-1:** no app uses a skeleton. This is the same gap as MOTION's CONS-MOTION-4.
- **Re-measure.** 15 key numbers were re-measured with independent code, and 13 agree. Two disagree, and both are corrected here:
  - There are 20 native-dialog call sites, not 17.
  - Flash durations track the injected `hub.js` delay (about 0.4-0.5 s at +400 ms); they are not per-area constants.

Prior scores: P2 for the shell (`audits/02-shell.md:5426`), and the P3 scorecard (`audits/03-apps.md:51-62`).

| Area | Prior Native feel | Suggested | Inputs from this dimension |
