- **Related (not re-filed):** P2 UX "The reminder and chat inputs are labelled only by placeholders" (low; `audits/02-shell.md:5802-5805`); the pairing-code sheet's placeholder-only fields (`audits/02-shell.md:1063-1064`); `#chat-in` (`audits/02-shell.md:3640, 4435`).

#### P4-COLOR-06 — `--muted` is validated only on paper and cards: 4.45:1 on Hearth wells, 4.37 on Parchment wells, 4.49 on F260's New Testament paper, and about 4.0-4.2 on its New Testament wells

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low; it is not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** every affected string is secondary (blurbs, counts, captions, hints, a step pill) and misses AA by 0.01-0.13. The rule makes a secondary failure low.
  - **Control labels:** Prayer's unpressed Mine/Family segment and F260's 11 px HEAR buttons are control labels. They are already covered at medium by VIS-PRAYER-1 and VIS-F260-1.
  - **What this defect adds** is the shared token cause.
- **Areas:** shell, kidverse, prayer, dollywood, f260.
- **What happens.**
  - **The token and its validation.** `--muted` is annotated "AA on paper and cards (4.9:1)" (`apps/design.css:47`). The system itself puts it on `--surface-2`, documented as "sunken wells, inputs" (`:43`).
  - **The style guide's check misses these pairs.** Its contrast list checks muted on bg and on surface, and text on surface-2, but not muted on surface-2 or any `color-mix()` surface (`docs/design.html:291-293`). `scripts/test-design.mjs:109-110` therefore cannot catch it.
  - **On wells:**
    - theme-card blurbs; Kid Verse badge hints ("prayed on 5 days", Ezra); Prayer's category counts and unpressed "Family" segment; the build guide's "step 8 of 9" pill;
    - they read 4.45 in Hearth and 4.37 in Parchment, and pass in Frost at 4.55.
  - **On F260's New Testament paper.** `body.nt` mixes 7 % teal into `--bg` (`apps/f260.html:30-33`), switched on from week 31 (`:1500`, so it is on at the demo date).
    - Hearth captions read 4.49 on #E7EAE3: ".sub", day labels, ring numbers, HEAR buttons. Skeptic 2 found 58 of 68 undimmed `--muted` items failing.
    - Parchment (4.56-4.58) and Frost (4.54) pass.
    - The New Testament wells (`--sunk`, `:32`) come to about 4.10 / 4.00 / 4.20 by token maths, the worst pair. The reflection field did not render in the skeptics' runs.
  - **Kid Verse "Also this week"** reads 4.46 p10 / 4.53 median only when scrolled into the top band of the fixed gold wash (`apps/kidverse.html:13-18`). Unscrolled it reads 4.85-4.90 and passes.
  - **Rig:** muted-on-well 476 occurrences, theme-card blurbs 456, F260 NT captions 2,874.
- **Expected.** Every text token is validated against every surface it can sit on, wells and `color-mix()` surfaces included, and holds at least 4.5:1.
- **Why it matters.** Each instance is small, but it is one token pair repeated across five areas. On F260 in Hearth it is the single largest cause of failing captions.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/design.css:43, 47`; `apps/f260.html:30-33, 1500`; `apps/kidverse.html:13-18`; `docs/design.html:291-293`; `scripts/test-design.mjs:109-110`.
  - Investigator: `palette.json` (`themes.*.mutedOnSurface2`), `components.json` (muted-well, theme-blurb, f260-nt-muted).
  - Skeptics: `verify-muted-on-wells-and-derived-surfaces-1.json`, `-1-kidverse-hearth-also-desktop-scrolled-viewport.png` (4.46), `-1-kidverse-hearth-also-desktop-viewport.png` (4.9), `verify-muted-on-wells-and-derived-surfaces-2.json`, `-2-f260-hearth.png`.
  - Phase 1: `audits/screens/f260/behind-pace-typical-desktop-light.png`, `audits/screens/kidverse/kid-reading-typical-desktop-light.png`.
- **Reproduction.** From `cd "C:/Users/ex_bo/OneDrive/Claude Related/App Hub"`:
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/palette.mjs | grep 'muted on bg'` prints system-light … s2 4.45 and parchment … s2 4.37.
  - `node -e "import('./audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/palette.mjs').then(m=>console.log(m.cr('#75675B', m.mix('#F7F2EB','#137F77',.93))))"` prints 4.49.
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/verify-muted-on-wells-and-derived-surfaces-2.mjs` prints the rendered values.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** wrote their own token parser and WebKit run, taking text-hidden 1x screenshots with p10 and median per element. It covered the shell theme cards (Hearth, Parchment, Frost), F260 as Eli in Hearth, Kid Verse as Ezra on the iPad and desktop (scrolled and unscrolled), and Prayer's counts. They also sampled pixels straight from the Phase 1 capture.
    - The blurbs read 4.45 / 4.37 / 4.55, Prayer's counts 4.45 / 4.37 and F260 in Hearth 4.49.
    - Kid Verse read 4.90 unscrolled and 4.46 / 4.53 scrolled; the Phase 1 capture's pixels read 4.45-4.53.
    - They found every per-surface instance already filed, and corrected the `body.nt` line numbers.
  - **Skeptic 2** wrote their own parser with float WCAG maths and a WebKit run in the three light palettes. It walked every visible, undimmed text whose computed colour equals `--muted`, and composited the background chain.
    - Its values match skeptic 1's.
    - It attributed about 59 of VIS-F260-1's 150 Hearth items to the NT paper, from P3's `contrast.json`: 150 in Hearth against 91 in Parchment and Frost.
    - It found the gap in the style guide's check list.
    - It could not reproduce Kid Verse's 4.45, because its DOM composite ignores gradients; a 10 % gold mix gives 4.45.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - The `body.nt` rule is at `apps/f260.html:30-33`, not `:24-27`.
  - The NT paper accounts for about 59 of VIS-F260-1's 150 Hearth items, not "most". The rest fail in every light palette, from opacity dimming and gold ink.
  - Kid Verse's 4.45 depends on scroll position.
  - The NT wells, not the paper, are the worst pair.
  - Every per-surface instance is already filed. New here: the shared token cause, the `body.nt` attribution and the style guide's missing pairs.
- **Related (not re-filed):** the P2 VIS table's 4.45 theme-card-blurb row (`audits/02-shell.md:5814`), VIS-KIDVERSE-1, VIS-PRAYER-1, VIS-DOLLYWOOD-5 and VIS-F260-1 (whose checker already noted that the 4.49 items overstate how the page looks, `audits/03-apps/f260.md:707-708`).

### Consistency, visual and gap findings

These items were not adversarially verified. The evidence is the investigator's rig aggregation, token maths and code reading, spot-checked by the section writer against the cited lines and JSON, with the re-measure's corrections applied. Severities are the investigator's ratings.

#### CONS-COLOR-1 — "Past", "done" and "not yet" are shown by dimming text with opacity, differently in every app: 1.46-3.5:1 (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens.** There is no AA-safe tertiary or "done" ink, so each app dims text with its own opacity:

  | Where | How | Measured |
  |---|---|---|
  | F260 past weeks | opacity .6 (`apps/f260.html:235`) | 2.21-2.88; their check discs (white on 60 % olive) 2.24-2.81 |
  | F260 unearned milestones | opacity .55 (`apps/f260.html:193`) | 2.01-2.59 |
  | Build guide done steps | opacity .55 plus strike-through (`apps/dollywood.html:101`) | 1.99-3.5 |
  | Park map rows filtered out for a kid's height | `.lv-item.noride{opacity:.55}` (template `:508`) | the 20 px/800 wait minutes at 1.46-1.54, below 3:1 even as large text (new); ride numbers at opacity .75, 1.73-1.79 p10 (median 3.2-3.36) |
  | TV board | "not read yet" faces | 2.05-3.1 |
  | Timer | time's-up 0:00 blinks to opacity .65 (`apps/timer.html:38-39`, `steps(2)`) | 2.42, under 3:1 even as large text (new) |
  | Home hero kicker | opacity .85 (`apps/design.css:417`) | P2 |

- **Expected.** One tertiary or "done" ink that passes AA, and no opacity on text. A state change shows through ink plus a glyph (a check, a strike-through), not through transparency.
- **Why it matters.** Dimmed states are most of the hub's failing text occurrences (F260's past weeks alone are 16,277), and each app picked its own value.
- **Evidence:** `components.json` (f260-past, f260-milestone, dw-done, dw-min, tv-dim, timer-blink); `remeasure-raw.json` (the Timer's 0:00 in `devices/timer/done-typical-desktop-light-system`); `audits/screens/dollywood-live/waits-kid-typical-desktop-light.png`; `audits/screens/f260/behind-typical-desktop-light.png`; `audits/screens/timer/done-typical-desktop-light.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/components.mjs | grep -i 'opacity\|wait tiles\|not read'`.
- **Related:** VIS-F260-1, VIS-DOLLYWOOD-1, VIS-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-8.

#### CONS-COLOR-2 — "Today" is a ring in three apps, drawn three ways; it is below 3:1 in Hearth in all three, and in every theme in Kid Verse (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens.**

  | App | Recipe | Hearth | Parchment | Frost | Dark |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | F260 heatmap | gold ring | 2.62-2.71 | 2.83 | 3.09 | 8.45-9.55 |
  | Prayer calendar | gold 2 px box-shadow (`apps/prayer.html:165`) | 2.96 | 3.24 | 3.47 | 9.0-9.2 |
  | Kid Verse | `--focus` ring (`apps/kidverse.html:69`) | 1.29-1.86 in every theme | | | |

- **Correction.** The draft's "all below 3:1" holds only in Hearth, plus F260 in Parchment and Kid Verse everywhere. The draft gave Kid Verse's range as 1.29-1.70 in one place and 1.29-1.66 in another; the re-measure finds 1.29-1.86.
- **Expected.** One today-marker token, a ring or fill of at least 3:1 against `--surface` and `--surface-2` in both schemes, used by every calendar, grid and strip.
- **Why it matters.** "Today" anchors every progress strip, and for pre-readers it is the only cue.
- **Evidence:** `nontext-summary.json`; `remeasure-raw.json` (`rings`); `verify-mid-tone-semantic-as-ink-2.json` (F260 ring by palette).

- **Related:** VIS-KIDVERSE-2.

#### CONS-COLOR-3 — The person's colour becomes ink through four recipes, and only `--accent-deep` is guaranteed (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens** (Table COLOR-6):
  - **Raw `--accent` / `--tint`** fails in both schemes: 1.49-2.93 in dark, and 2.25-4.41 in light for four colours (P4-COLOR-02; P2 for the shell).
  - **`--accent-deep`** passes on every surface, and fails only on the hero's fixed white fill (P4-COLOR-03).
  - **`--tint-ink` = 70 % colour + `--text`** (`index.html:955, 1070`) gives feed names at 4.22 for David in dark, 4.04 in Forest, 3.85-4.01 for the TV, and 4.03 for Kiara in Parchment (new; P2 recorded David).
  - **The app-tile `--tint`** reads 1.95-2.81 (VIS-COLOR-1).
- **Expected.** One per-scheme person-ink pair, derived in one place and contrast-checked, used by every area.
- **Why it matters.** Profile colours are editable in the admin panel, and guests pick from swatches. Only an ink derived with a contrast floor can guarantee that a new colour passes. Today, whether a colour passes depends on which recipe an area happened to use.
- **Evidence:** `palette.json` (`profiles.*.themes.*`); `parchment-home-feed-names.png`; `audits/evidence/p4/measure/failing-pairs/shell.json` (`div.fwho` Parchment #8F6A1B 4.03).
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/palette.mjs | grep -A11 '^Profiles'`.

#### CONS-COLOR-4 — Semantic colours are neither consistent between areas nor unmistakable (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens** (Table COLOR-7):
  - **The aliases reach four files only:** the shell, the Larder, the Timer (`--danger` only) and the Dollywood template (`--ok`, `--danger`). The draft's "only the Larder and the shell" was corrected by a grep.
  - **F260 and Prayer map meaning to hue families their own way.** The template adds a literal traffic-light set: #1E8A4C / #C77A00 / #C8391F / #6A6259.
  - **A finished Timer shows the destructive red.** Mae's running ring is the same hex as `--danger` in Hearth.
  - **Success against destructive** (olive against terra) has a luminance ratio of 1.00 in all three light palettes. Under deuteranopia they are ΔE 4.0-5.1 apart (the re-measure gets 4.2 in Hearth, a difference in the simulation variant). Success against info is only ΔE 8.0-8.7, even with normal vision.
  - **The soft chip fills** are within ΔE 6.5 of each other, and the park map's green and red bands are 1.18:1 in luminance.
  - **Four household colours are semantic colours:** Mae = `--danger`, Ezra = `--info`, Kiara = `--warn`, Mea = `--ok` (P2 VIS, `audits/02-shell.md:5786-5790`).
  - **The house pastels do not solve it alone:** Mint against Bubblegum is deutan ΔE 3.4 as fills and 2.0 as inks.
- **Expected.** One semantic set used everywhere, drawn from the pastel family with AA inks:
  - success, warning, destructive and info;
  - separated by lightness (success against destructive at a luminance ratio of 1.3 or more);
  - always paired with a glyph;
  - never reused as a profile colour.
- **Why it matters.** The house style requires semantic colours that stay unmistakable. Today their meaning changes from app to app, and red against green is carried by hue alone.
- **Evidence:** `semantic.json`; `apps/design.css:80-83`; `apps/f260.html:11-12`; `apps/prayer.html:106, 230, 311`; `apps/timer.html:36-38`; template `:495-496, 501`; `worker/seed.sql:4-11`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/semantic.mjs`.
- **Related:** VIS-PRAYER-10; P2 VIS "Profile colours double as the semantic colours".

#### VIS-COLOR-1 — The fills and tiles sit at about a third of the house chroma in all five palettes, two house hues are missing, and dark cards barely lift off the page (investigator rating: medium)

- **What happens** (Table COLOR-8):
  - **Soft fills.** They sit at the pastels' lightness (L 0.87-0.94, against 0.876-0.953) but at about a third of their chroma (C 0.008-0.070, against 0.057-0.093). Parchment's gold-soft, at 0.070, is the only exception. `--accent-soft` for the ten swatches is 0.004-0.047.
  - **Tiles.** They run pale to paler, a 22 % → 8 % tint over the surface (`apps/design.css:606-608`), instead of pastel to saturated. The icon ink is the raw app colour: Kid Verse's gold is 2.39-2.81 in light (new), and the Larder's and F260's are 1.95-2.33 in dark (P2).
  - **Hues.** Six earth families span hues 42-274°. Bubblegum (354°) and Lavender (303°) have no counterpart, and Sky (252°) and Periwinkle (278°) collapse into one slate.
  - **Other gradients.**
    - The hero runs within one hue, from 70 % white through the accent to `--accent-deep` (`apps/design.css:412`), and stays pale in dark (P2-VIS-06).
    - The page wash mixes two hues, the accent at 10 % and gold at 6 % (`:70-71`; the draft cited `:67-68`).
    - The `.bar` fill starts at 75 % tint + white (`:534`). That is why the bars read 2.27-2.99 against their tracks.
  - **Neutrals.**
    - Hearth's page is warm paper (H 77, C 0.011) at the lightness of iOS #F2F2F7 (H 286). Parchment is tan (L 0.89, C 0.039). Frost alone matches iOS.
    - In dark, the card-to-page step is 1.10-1.12, against iOS's 1.23, and the well is darker than the page (1.04).
- **Expected (house style).**
  - Pastel fills at C ≈ 0.055-0.095, with a deep ink of the same hue.
  - Tiles running pastel to saturated within one hue, with an AA ink.
  - All eight house hues available for profiles and chips.
  - Grouped grey with white cards in light; near-black with a card elevated 1.2:1 or more in dark.
- **Why it matters.** This is the house style's central colour rule, and the main reason every area scores 3-5 on Colour & palette.
- **Evidence:** `palette.json` (`themes.*.softChroma`, `houseFillChroma`, `neutrals`), `tiles.json`, `audits/evidence/p4/measure/nontext/shell.json` (`span.app-icon.ticon > svg.icon`), `audits/screens/shell/apps-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png`, `audits/screens/shell/home-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/palette.mjs | grep 'soft C\|house fill chroma'; node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/tiles.mjs`.
- **Related:** P2 VIS "The earthy Hearth palette, not the house pastels" (`audits/02-shell.md:5778-5785`), which measured Hearth and Midnight only. This extends it to Parchment, Frost and Forest and to the tiles.
  - **Merge note:** the ACCENT draft's ACC-10 covers the profile-colour side.

### What works

- **OK-COLOR-1 — All eight house pastel pairs pass AA as given; no ink has to be darkened** (Table COLOR-9).
  - Ink on fill 5.04 (Peach) to 5.86 (Periwinkle, Lavender); inks on white 6.58-8.63, and on #F2F2F7 5.90-7.74.
  - As dark-mode inks, the pastels read 11.5-14.9 on #1C1C1E and 9.99-12.0 on a deep tint of their own ink.
  - The thinnest margins are Peach (5.04) and Mint (5.24): never place these chips on glass or under opacity.
  - 7:1 variants that keep hue and chroma exist for small captions and the TV.
  - Caveat for dark chips: a 28 % ink tint stands only 1.14-1.24:1 from the card, so a dark chip needs a stronger fill step or a ring.
  - The re-measure reproduces every pair exactly.
- **OK-COLOR-2 — The `-ink` tokens pass everywhere, and four apps are essentially AA-clean.**
  - `-ink` on its soft fill reads 5.37-10.35 in every theme.
  - Tally: 0 failing text in all 7 keys.
  - Verses: one pair ("Got it", 4.4 in Hearth).
  - Larder: text clean in the light palettes; the 12 px error line is P3-LEFTOVERS-15.
  - Timer: its text passes everywhere except the blinking 0:00.
  - Kid Verse and Verses use `-ink` for kickers, chips and labels (`apps/kidverse.html:35-108`, `apps/verses.html:29-94`), and the Larder uses it for chip text. The pattern to copy already exists in the codebase.
- **OK-COLOR-3 — `--accent-deep`, the derived person ink, passes on every surface for every colour in every theme.**
  - It reads 5.34 or more on `--bg` and `--surface` in light, and 5.60-8.62 on the surface in dark.
  - The one sub-AA pair is Kiara on the Parchment well, at 4.12.
  - It is used correctly by the shell's buttons and selection, Prayer's `#pray .cat` and six template rules.
  - Evidence: skeptic 2 of P4-COLOR-02 (`verify-raw-accent-ink-no-dark-lift-2.json`); skeptic 1's 6.25-9.48 on the dark page.
- **OK-COLOR-4 — The dark palettes lift every mid tone to 6.2-9.2:1, and the dark chips reach 8.9-10.4.** Dark mode's failures come from the person's colour, opacity and white-on-fill, not from the hue families.

### Checked and not a bug

No filed finding was refuted: all six bug findings survived both skeptics. The claims below were checked and corrected or dropped.

- **"Switch on the TV: 2.59" (P4-COLOR-03).** The kiosk cannot reach Me: `index.html:626` sends it to Home, and `index.html:78` hides its tab bar. The TV profile's Switch was measured only by opening the hash directly in the rig.
- **"Native controls: shell" (P4-COLOR-04).** The shell's only select is `appearance: none` (`apps/design.css:448`).
- **"The guest name, guest PIN and Prayer fields are unlabelled" (P4-COLOR-05).** Each has a visible label (`index.html:1396, 1399`; `apps/prayer.html:480-489`).
- **"F260 has no `::placeholder` rule."** It has two, both `--muted` (`apps/f260.html:182, 359`); only the passcode fields fall back to the UA grey.
- **"`#chat-in` boundary 1.0."** The input is borderless and transparent by design (`index.html:263`). Its visible boundary is the composer bar, at 1.07-1.12 (provisional).
- **"`design.css:48` says `--muted-decor` is decorative only, yet it is the placeholder colour."** The comment lists placeholders as an intended use. The defect is the assumption that a placeholder is never the only label.
- **"No person-ink token exists" (P4-COLOR-02).** `--accent-deep` is that token and it passes (OK-COLOR-3). The defect is six rules that bypass it.
- **"The route glyph lacks a dark lift."** It is a cascade bug (template `:464` over `:458`) and fails in light too, at 1.52.
- **"The F260 NT paper accounts for most of VIS-F260-1's 150 Hearth failures."** About 59 of them.
- **"`apps/f260.html:24-27`" for `body.nt`.** The rule is at `:30-33`.
- **"Kid Verse 'Also this week' 4.45."** Only when scrolled into the gold wash; unscrolled it reads 4.85-4.90.
- **"Light themes fail more than dark ones everywhere except the shell."** The Timer and the Larder fail more in dark too (Table COLOR-2).
- **"Today markers: all below 3:1."** Prayer's ring passes in Parchment (3.24), Frost (3.47) and dark; F260's passes in Frost (3.09) and dark (CONS-COLOR-2).
- **"The Timer's own text passes AA everywhere."** The time's-up 0:00 at opacity .65 reads 2.42 (Table COLOR-10).
- **"F260 60.6 % against Parchment 35.2 %."** Not like-for-like. On the same run set the Hearth figure is 57.9 %, and the park map's is 40.5 %, above the quoted 21.5-36 % range (Table COLOR-2). The conclusions hold.
- **"Hero token range 1.63-2.48."** It is 1.76-2.56 over the seeded colours. The TV's colour is the maximum, at 2.56.
- **"Raw colour in light: Kiara only."** Mae and Mea fail in every light palette (4.35-4.41 on the surface, 3.67 in Parchment), and Ezra (3.95) and Elizabeth (4.03) fail in Parchment.
- **"Me hero kicker and name, dark 2.21-2.33."** The rig's p10 reaches 2.47. P2's 2.72 / 2.79 are medians (rig medians 2.74-2.98), so "rig confirms" holds once p10 and median are told apart.
- **"Only the Larder and the shell use the semantic aliases."** The Timer and the Dollywood template use them too (CONS-COLOR-4).
- **F260 "Set passcode" at 1.03-1.19.** Read inside the `.side` scroller's clip. Rig v2 counts an ancestor hit as uncovered, so this is an artefact. It is not filed and was not checked on screen.
- **Checkboxes painting in the OS scheme (P4-COLOR-04).** Cosmetic: the box stays visible.
- **"VIS-VERSES-3 is the same pattern" (P4-COLOR-01).** It is white text on an olive fill, a different pair; it is only loosely related.

**States sweep (after the completeness critic; measured, not adversarially verified).** `audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/states-sweep.mjs` ran once per theme key (System light and dark, Hearth on a dark OS, Parchment, Frost, Midnight, Forest) on the desktop (1440×900, Chromium, as Eli; Kid Verse as Ezra) over 13 documents: the shell's Home, Apps, Me and picker, and every app. In each document it clones every author rule that uses `:hover`, `:active`, `:focus` or `:focus-visible` into a class, applies the state the way the browser does (hover and press on the element and its ancestors, focus on the element), keeps the targets whose state changes a text colour, an opacity or a background under their text, and samples each text pair at rest and in the state with the text hidden (median against AA). It also lists every `::before` / `::after` with string or `attr()` content. Per theme key: 300 state rules cloned, 352 targets whose text pair changes (2,464 over the seven keys), 5 pseudo-elements. Because some state rules paint with the person's colour, two per-person runs were added (the same script with a profile argument): Kiara in Parchment (shell Home and Me, Tally, Timer, Kid Verse, Verses; `states/parchment-light-kiara.json`) and Elizabeth in Hearth (shell Home and Me, Verses, Prayer; `states/system-light-mom.json`). Results (`audits/evidence/p4/COLOR/states-summary.json`; per key `audits/evidence/p4/COLOR/states/<theme>-<os>.json`; summariser `audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/states-summary.mjs`):
- **Nothing new fails in the `.ds` areas.** The shell (32 state-changing targets per key, e.g. `.ds .btn-soft:hover` at 6.5:1 in Hearth), Tally, Timer, Kid Verse, Verses, Prayer, the Larder, the park map (none of its state rules changes a text pair) and every focus state (focus changes rings, never a text pair) keep AA in every key.
- **Pseudo-element text passes:** F260's "now" pill (`apps/f260.html:247`, 11 px slate on slate-soft) 5.19-7.10 across the seven keys; the build guide's toolbar group labels (`content: attr(data-l)`, 10.5 px `--dim`, template `:156`) 5.24-8.97. The 10.5 px size is TYPE's concern, not colour's.

### Method, scripts and evidence

**Primary dataset.** The rig-v2 summaries in `audits/evidence/p4/measure/`: `pairs.json`, `failing-pairs/<area>.json`, `nontext/<area>.json`, `tokens-resolved.json` and `coverage.json`. They cover 3,662 jobs: every Phase 1 screen on the iPad portrait in 7 theme keys, plus the devices and states runs in System light and dark.

**Investigator scripts** (`audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/`; evidence in `audits/evidence/p4/COLOR/`):

| Script | What it does | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `table.mjs` | Area × theme table from `pairs.json` and `failing-pairs/*` | `table.json` |
| `components.mjs` | Groups every non-suspect failing text group by cause | `components.json` (98 KB) |
| `nontext-summary.mjs` | Non-text contrast per area. svg icons only; emoji and images are informational | `nontext-summary.json` (84 KB) |
| `palette.mjs` | Token maths: house pairs, OKLCH, per-theme families, per-profile recipes, neutrals | `palette.json` (66 KB) |
| `semantic.mjs` | Semantic distances (OKLab ΔE, luminance ratio) under simulated colour-vision deficiency (Machado 2009) | `semantic.json` |
| `tiles.mjs` | App-tile gradients against the house recipe | `tiles.json` |
| `native-controls.mjs [webkit\|chromium\|both]` | Harness experiment on the Larder frame: default button, select, checkbox under each theme and OS mode | `native-controls.json`, `native-controls-*.png` |
| `spot.mjs` | Independent spot-check with its own PNG decoding and blending | `spot.json`, `spot-*.png` |
| `crop.mjs` | Crops the cited screenshots (1x CSS) | `midnight-*.png`, `parchment-home-feed-names.png` |

The investigator's spot-checks agreed with the rig within 0.07 on every value.

The two largest cited PNGs are under 1 MB: `midnight-park-nearby-raw-accent.png` (925 KB) and `midnight-build-guide-view-menu-selects.png` (810 KB).

**Skeptic scripts** (`audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/verify-<key>-{1,2}.mjs`, outputs `audits/evidence/p4/COLOR/verify-<key>-*.json` and `.png`):

Every skeptic closed its instance with `L.close()` in a `finally` block. Several saw WebKit or Playwright processes afterwards that belonged to parallel sessions and left them alone. The verdict records are in the session scratchpad (`p4/verify/COLOR/*.json`).

**Re-measure** (`audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/remeasure.mjs tokens | raw | live [webkit|chromium]`). It shares no code with the investigator's scripts or the rig page-lib:
- its own `design.css` parser, with WCAG, `color-mix`, OKLab and Machado maths;
- its own re-aggregation of the 3,662 raw job files, with its own AA threshold;
- WebKit and Chromium runs on the local instance, through its own probe: text hidden, a 1x CSS screenshot, its own PNG decoder, per-pixel contrast.

Outputs: `remeasure-tokens.json`, `remeasure-raw.json`, `remeasure-live-webkit.json`, `remeasure-live-chromium.json`. Tolerances:
- ±0.05 on rendered ratios;
- ±0.02 on token ratios;
- ±0.2 percentage points on shares;
- ±0.002 on chroma;
- ±0.5 on ΔE.

**Not verified in this dimension:**
- iOS rendering of selects and placeholders;
- real blur;

- the 10-foot TV and sunlight;
- font fallback: the rig renders Segoe UI, Palatino and Manrope, so glyph coverage and p10 may differ slightly on an iPad; background colours do not.

Against the hero pixels beside it the coherence verifier measured 1.23-1.40 in light and 1.28-1.33 in dark, in both engines; only the `--e2` shadow, about a 0.5 px hairline, outlines it. A deep-tint capsule with a pastel label is also the variant D15 rejects for primary buttons; the pastel capsule with its dark label (`--accent-strong` / `--accent-on`) would read ≥ 8.67. It is not a WCAG failure, because the text label identifies the button, but the section should note it or choose deliberately (for example `--accent-fill-strong` or a ring). Both verifiers raised it.

Only `contrast.mjs`'s static order check proves the order; the coherence verifier's in-place probe confirmed that it holds in both engines, so this is a gap in the harness, not a failing claim.

> **What the decisions changed in the tokens**

That covers the Add-a-guest sheet's default #137F77, the Worker's no-colour default and both guest swatches (#8C4F7A, #4C7B6A). In batch 0d the Worker writes `hue = 'sky'` for every new guest (revision 6b, verify-rev6 issue 3). **Amended 2026-09-26** (`05-decisions.md`, "Admin-assigned colours"): sky is only the default. A stored hue from the 18 names wins for everyone, guests included, and a guest falls back to sky only when no valid hue is stored.
> - **D5, app colours: separate app hues.** The nine app families are coral, apricot, honey, pistachio, leaf, seafoam, lagoon, cornflower and orchid.
>   - **How they were made.** `audits/tools/phase5/app-hues.mjs` places each app at a maximin slot between two house pastels. It interpolates each of the eight roles in OKLCH from those two neighbours, then nudges lightness until every rule a person family meets holds with a 0.03 margin.

>   - **What the gate holds them to.** Each family sits in both scheme blocks, carries a `[data-accent]` block, and joins the ink and 7:1 solid swaps. The gate runs every accent-context check for them too (18 families, not 9).
>   - **How distinct they are** (CIEDE2000, all gated):
>     - app vs app is ≥ 13.2 in light and ≥ 9.9 in dark on the tile end (floor 8), and ≥ 10.3 on the mark (floor 10);
>     - **app vs person, in every role** (revision 6d, after round 3 found Kid Verse's dark honey fill, glyph and label on Mae's peach at 1.79 / 2.18 / 1.58):
>       - the floor per role and scheme is half the people's own closest spacing, and never under 4 on the tile end or 5 on the mark;
>       - lowest in light: wash 1.89 (floor 1.6), fill 4.38 (3.9), tile end 5.32 (5.0), strong 5.44 (4.6), mark 7.60 (7.3), ink 4.22 (3.9), ink-hi 4.34 (3.7);
>       - lowest in dark: wash 3.91 (3.2), fill 4.03 (3.6), tile end 4.77 (4.3), strong 5.31 (5.0), mark 6.98 (6.6), ink 4.49 (4.1), ink-hi 3.42 (3.1), on 3.23 (2.9);
>       - apricot's light wash is no longer the peach wash (round 3 issue 6);
>     - **app vs status colour** (revisions 6b-6c): in **every** role (wash, fill, fill-strong, graphic, strong, on, ink, ink-hi), no app sits closer to success, warning or danger than the closest person already does, per scheme.
>       - The mark is held to the people's own gate of 10 and measures ≥ 10.46 in light and ≥ 10.35 in dark (coral vs danger).
>       - In dark, the glyph (ink) is ≥ 3.79 (people 3.44), the solid (strong) ≥ 5.59 (people 5.13) and its label (on) ≥ 2.93 (people 2.62).

>       - Kid Verse's dark honey tile, glyph and solid no longer match the warning chip.
>       - **Status by status (reported; round 3 issue 2).** The rule is "no closer than the closest person to *any* status colour". Taken status by status it is looser for four apps, because they sit in the status hues' own neighbourhoods: coral (Timer) and apricot (Prayer) by danger, in every role, honey (Kid Verse) by warning, and leaf (the Larder) by success. Pistachio and seafoam are looser than the people only on the mark vs success, trivially (16.07 and 19.61, where the people are at 21.24). The whole table is reported per app, status, role and palette in `contrast.json` → `appHues`.
>         - In dark, coral's glyph is 3.7 from danger's text, where no person comes closer than 9.7.
>         - A tile always carries its glyph and name, and a status always carries its ✓ / ! / ✕ glyph, so neither is read by colour alone. But a red-pink Timer tile beside a danger chip is the closest pair in the house, and the owner should see it in the preview.
>     - **Rounding.** The generator measures the 8-bit hex it writes, not the unrounded colour. Round 2 found a distance that held unrounded and failed on the hex: 3.71 against 3.38.
>   - **Colour vision.** Deficiency simulations of the apps are reported, not gated: a tile is its glyph and name.
>   - **The retired mapping.** The "each app takes the house hue nearest its colour" list under D5 is replaced by this one.
> - **D8, glass: four levels.** A person preference, `hub.prefs.glass`, written by the bootstrap as `data-glass`:
>   - **Clear:** 40 % pills and buttons, 48 % bars and sheets.
>   - **Current:** today's look, 64 % / 84 %.
>   - **Frosted:** the default, 78-80 % / 90 %.
>   - **Solid:** this is `data-transparency="reduce"`.
>
>   How the levels behave:
>   - **Precedence.** The level chosen in Me is the source of truth once the person has chosen: the bootstrap writes `data-glass` and `data-transparency="full"`, so an OS Reduce Transparency setting no longer applies. That holds for an explicit Frosted too; Safari cannot report that setting anyway, and Solid is one tap away. A person who never chose follows the OS.
>   - **Old rows.** `hub.prefs.glass` supersedes the older `transparency` key. Batch 1b migrates `transparency: 'reduce'` to `glass: 'solid'` and deletes the old key, and until then `glass` wins.
>   - **The TV.** The TV ignores a stored glass level: its panels are the photo panel and the opaque look. OS Reduce Transparency still makes them solid unless the TV's own device-local switch was set to "full" (that is an explicit choice on the TV). The bootstrap applies a glass level only for a signed-in person, so nothing is applied before anyone is picked (verify-rev6 issues 4-5, round 2 issue 5).
>   - **The halo, as first proposed and as fixed.** Clear and Current paint a text halo, `--glass-text-shadow`.
>     - Revision 6 made it a blurred glow and gated it as one flat layer. The independent verifier rendered it and measured the pixels beside the strokes: text-2 on Clear over a black photo read 2.9-4.2, not the modelled 5.7 (verify-rev6 issue 1, blocking).
>     - Revision 6b makes it an **outline**: eight 1 px offsets at 0 blur in the card colour (`--glass-halo-edge`, solid), then one soft 8 px glow.
>     - Revision 6c:
>       - **Icons.** `text-shadow` does not paint on SVG, so icons get their own outline, `--glass-icon-filter`: four chained 1 px drop-shadows, applied by batch 1b to every `svg` on glass. Before this, an icon on Clear over a photo read 1.60 (round 2 issue 2).
>       - **Frosted pays nothing.** Both outlines are `none` by default, so Frosted and Solid paint and cost nothing.
>     - Revision 6d (round 3 issue 3): a nested palette re-points both outlines to its own card colour. A theme preview or a `data-scheme` island inside another palette therefore outlines in its own `--surface`, not the root's. `browser-check.mjs` probes this both ways, in both engines (`nestedOutline`); `contrast.mjs` does not model descendant selectors.
>   - **How the halo is proved.** It is measured **as rendered**, in WebKit and Chromium, by `audits/tools/phase5/halo-check.mjs` → `audits/evidence/p5/halo-check.json`.
>     - **The method (revision 6c; round 2 issue 3).** Device scale 2, under the full sheen and pickup, over the page, a card, #767676 and a black or white photo, in all six palettes.
>       - What is measured: regular text at 11, 13 and 15 px, and a 1.75 px stroke icon.
>       - The **inner ring** is 0.5-1 CSS px round each glyph core: outside the anti-aliased fringe, inside the outline. Its **p10** is gated, not the median, because a median over a ring that is mostly outline passes by construction. The thresholds are text 7, text-2 4.5, text-3 4.5 and icons 3.
>       - Text-3 is never gated over a photo or on pills; it is a lint row there.
>       - The **outer ring** (1.5-3 CSS px) is what lies behind the outline, and is reported.
>       - The ring is defined at device scale 2, and the check always renders at 2 (round 3 issue 4). At scale 1 a fixed 2-device-px ring would fall outside the 1 px outline. The verifier's scale-aware ring passes at 1, 2 and 3 (lowest at scale 1: text-2 6.70, icons 4.82).
>     - **Lowest inner-ring p10.**
>       - Clear: text 10.28, text-2 7.89, text-3 5.98, icons 7.05.
>       - Current: text 11.44, text-2 8.72, text-3 6.09, icons 7.05.
>       - The same text on an opaque card reads 13.42 / 9.08 / 6.14.
>     - **Outer ring, reported.** On Clear over a photo the glass itself reads down to 1.59 for text-2 and 1.26 for an icon. That is what the outline is for.
>     - **How it looks** (the verifier's crops). The outline reads as one continuous contour, with no doubling. Strokes look heavier, and in dark slightly embossed; at 11 px the counters narrow. A 1.5 px icon in dark reads as a dark icon with a light hairline inside, and a selected tab's accent reads mostly as outline; filled glyphs and 2 px strokes look fine. All of it is legible, but it departs from iOS's vibrancy, and **the owner should judge it in the preview**.
>     - The gate refuses to pass unless `halo-check.json` was made from the current token file (sha-256) and passed.
>     - **Reported: Frosted, the default, with no halo, on the same inner-ring p10.** Over a black or white photo text reads 6.62, text-2 4.91 and icons 4.22. The flat WCAG figures the gate holds Frosted to stay ≥ 7 and ≥ 4.5; this pixel measure is stricter than WCAG (it samples the thinnest 11 px strokes). Real screens remain a device check.
>   - **Increase Contrast and Solid** both beat a see-through level (gated).
> - **D15, dark primary buttons.** The Me hero's Switch capsule in dark is now the glowing pastel solid with its dark label (`--accent-strong` / `--accent-on`). This also closes round-6 item 19: the capsule's edge against both hero stops is ≥ 5.26 in dark (gated ≥ 3) and 1.02 in light (reported: a white capsule with a shadow; the regenerated light app washes are nearer white). The label reads ≥ 8.65 in dark in both engines.

This is the complete token set that closes the Phase 4 gaps. It is a proposal for Phase 5's design preview, not app code: nothing ships until Phase 6 is approved.

**Files**
- **The token set:** `audits/tools/phase4/tokens/proposed-tokens.css`, 672 lines of plain CSS custom properties. It needs no build step, no framework and no web font.
- **The GLASS-7 component rule:** `audits/tools/phase4/tokens/glass7-component.css`, the 30-line batch-1b rule §7 quotes. The engine cross-check loads it over today's `.ds` components.
- **The person and app identity rules:** `audits/tools/phase4/tokens/identity-component.css`, the batch-1a avatar rule and the batch-2 app-icon rule that §1 and the migration table quote. The engine cross-check loads it over today's `.ds` components.
- **The pre-paint bootstrap:** `audits/tools/phase4/tokens/bootstrap.js`, the exact snippet §1 shows. The gate runs it.
- **The gate:** `audits/tools/phase4/tokens/contrast.mjs` writes `audits/evidence/p4/tokens/contrast.json`.
- **The engine cross-check:** `audits/tools/phase4/tokens/browser-check.mjs` writes `audits/evidence/p4/tokens/browser-check.json`.
- **The runtime check on the local rig:** `audits/tools/phase4/tokens/rev2-runtime.mjs` writes `audits/evidence/p4/tokens/rev2-runtime.json` and `rev2-tv-1920-proposed.png`. It serves `apps/design.css` with lines 14-289 swapped for the token file, and checks six things in WebKit: the TV board fit, F260's theme buttons, kid-mode fonts, big numerals, the text floor, and (round 4) the Dollywood pair's text as rendered. For the last three it runs every document twice: with app code as it is, and with the batch rows this section names injected as CSS.
- **The legacy read count:** `audits/tools/phase4/tokens/legacy-reads.mjs` writes `audits/evidence/p4/tokens/legacy-reads.json`. It follows app-local aliases transitively and counts reads by property.

**Verification in one line.** 1,728 check kinds and 102,583 evaluations, with **0 failing**. All 26 planted faults make the gate fail. WebKit 26.6 and Chromium 154 each resolve 7,560 token values with **0 mismatches**; the largest channel difference is 0.5/255. Both engines also agree that a dark root without `data-theme` equals Midnight in every mode (531 tokens each), that the GLASS-7 component rule keeps today's components working, that a face wears its own person's family inside any page (the TV's included), that Prayer keeps exactly one `theme-color` meta with its id, and (revision 5) that the Me hero's Switch button, with its batch-1a row, paints `--hero-btn-bg` / `--hero-btn-ink` at ≥ 6.58 (≥ 6.86 in dark) in 162 contexts each. On the local rig, the TV board at 1920 × 1080 fits exactly as it does today (grid bottom 1064). With the named batch rows applied, every rendered big numeral is ui-rounded for an adult, a kid and the kiosk; kid mode is 100 % rounded on Home and every kid-visible app, the park map included; no adult or kiosk text is under 11 px, the build guide and the park map included (SVG labels measured as rendered); and no kid text is under 16 px.

**How the numbers are rounded.** Every "≥ x" and every table minimum is the true minimum **rounded down** to the shown precision (`fl()` in `contrast.mjs`). A stated bound is therefore never above the measured value, and a few figures read 0.01 lower than a round-to-nearest reading would (for example 7.01 for a true 7.019).

### How the set was assembled

Three competing proposals were written and ranked by three judges (each scored six criteria out of 10, so 60 at most).

**How the base was chosen.**
- **The judges were split.** The totals were migration 142 (48, 48 and 46), fidelity 140 (47, 46 and 47) and access 133 (45, 44 and 44). Judges 1 and 3 ranked migration first; judge 2 ranked fidelity first and advised building on fidelity with migration's alias layer and delivery.
- **The synthesiser was told the wrong winner.** The orchestration script matched each proposal to the judges' rankings by name. The names did not match, so every total read 0, and the script handed the synthesiser the first proposal, fidelity, as the winner. The synthesiser did receive all three judges' full rankings and graft lists.
- **What was built.** Fidelity is the base, with migration's whole compatibility and delivery layer grafted on. That is judge 2's recommendation, and the migration strengths judges 1 and 3 named are all in it. The two-point lead was therefore not honoured as a choice of base.
- **The record.** The judges' records are in the session scratchpad (`p4/proposals/rounds-1-2.json`). Phase 5 may revisit the base.

**Base: "fidelity"** (Apple first-party fidelity in the house pastels). The synthesis keeps:
- the eight-role colour families;
- the house pastels and inks unchanged;
- the lightness-tiered identity tones;
- ink-hi 7:1 swaps for the kiosk and Increase Contrast;
- prefers-* media mirrors of every attribute block;
- the iPad type tier on touch devices only;
- concentric-by-construction radii;
- the springs.

**Grafted from "migration"** (judges: 48, 46, 48):
- **Complete compatibility.** Every one of the 121 names `apps/design.css` defines still resolves; `--dur` was retired after a scan found 0 readers.
- **Legacy values kept.** Legacy radii, line heights and tracking keep today's values, including the kid radius overrides.
- **Stale-scheme guard.** Hue blocks are keyed on `:root`'s theme as well as on `data-scheme`, so a stale scheme cannot repaint a theme.
- **Theme aliases.** `light` and `dark` stay as aliases of Hearth and Midnight.
- **One block per palette.** Each palette is a single block that the theme cards reuse.
- **Graphite.** An iOS near-black palette is added as a named theme.
- **Overlay scale.** `--hi-*` and `--shade-*`.
- **Delivery.** The inline `<head>` bootstrap and the `hub:theme` event.
- **Verification.** The mutation test and the two-engine cross-check.

**Grafted from "access"** (judges: 45, 44, 44):
- graded text thresholds (7 / 6 / 4.5), with glass measured over the worst backdrop;
- the check that every semantic colour is at least 10 ΔE00 from every person colour (access's F4);
- the TV photo panel and the title-safe TV margins;
- kiosk body text at medium weight;
- the glance type roles for reading the iPad at 2-3 m;
- 52 px list rows, and targets that grow with the person's text size;
- the kids'-star outline check;
- `--art-plate`;
- a focus ring drawn as an outline;
- a masked, themed select chevron;
- the named material roles.

**Fixed while synthesizing:**
1. **Legacy `--accent` as text.** The person `-strong` tones were darkened so they reach ≥ 4.5:1 as text on every light surface, including Parchment's page. With fidelity's tones, the 14 existing `color: var(--accent)` reads measured 3.91-4.49 there (judge 2's computation). Now the minimum is 4.58.
2. **Missing aliases.** `--font-sans`, `--font-display`, `--lh*`, `--ls-tight`, `--ease-out`, `--ease-in-out` and `--accent-glow` are now defined. Fidelity dropped them.
3. **Warning too close to Peach.** The warning graphic moved from #9F6400 to #BC6D00, because it sat 9.5 ΔE00 from Peach.
4. **Aqua solid too grey.** The Aqua solid became #006B87, to keep chroma ≥ 0.09.
5. **Hero button in nested scopes.** The dark hero button now re-derives inside a nested scope. The gate found this bug.
6. **Kiosk text size.** The kiosk now ignores the text-size preference.
7. **Reduce Transparency beats the kiosk look.** The reduce-transparency block comes after the kiosk block, and a check enforces this. Access had this in the wrong order.

### 1. How it switches

hub.js and a pre-paint `<head>` bootstrap write every mode as an attribute on `<html>`. CSS keys off those attributes only; no app uses `prefers-color-scheme`.

| Attribute | Values | Set from | Replaces |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data-theme` (on `<html>` only) | hearth, parchment, frost, midnight, forest, graphite. `light` and `dark` are aliases. | The person's theme (`app_data(person,'hub','theme')`, mirrored in `hub.theme`). **System resolves here** to Hearth (OS light) or Midnight (OS dark), and the choice is kept in `data-theme-choice="system"`. hub.js never deletes the attribute. **Only `:root[data-theme=…]` is a palette scope.** A `data-theme` on any other element is data (F260's theme buttons, `apps/f260.html:2028`; the Me theme cards, `index.html:1259`) and keeps the document's palette (gated). | Today, `data-theme` is deleted for Hearth and System (`apps/hub.js:77`), which is why Hearth can pick up dark tokens (P4-DARK-02). A root that still arrives with `data-scheme="dark"` and no `data-theme` (a document on today's hub.js) now resolves to Midnight's grounds, not Hearth's, **in every mode**. The guard is `:root:where([data-scheme="dark"]:not([data-theme]))`, specificity (0,1,0), so the kiosk, Increase Contrast and Reduce Transparency blocks (0,2,0) still apply on that root. Both scripts compare it with Midnight in every mode, every declared token included. |
| `data-theme-preview` (any element) | the same palette ids | A theme swatch: the Me theme cards (`index.html:1260`) and `docs/design.html`. It carries `data-theme-preview`, `data-scheme` and `data-accent`, and paints itself in that palette, at its **adult** values (see §2.2a). **Every element that carries `data-scheme` or `data-theme-preview` also carries `data-accent`**, including the System card's night half. The `--accent-*` roles are declared only on `:root` and `[data-accent]`, so a half without the attribute inherits the swatch's light-scheme accent (#FFC8DD fill on Midnight's #211F1D). Gated: a nested half with `data-accent` equals the real palette, and a static check holds the shipped markup to the rule. | The `.tp[data-preview=…]` blocks (`apps/design.css:116, 136, 156, 218, 238, 257`) |
| `data-scheme` | light, dark | Derived from the theme. If the two ever disagree, the theme wins: `:root[data-theme=…]` has specificity (0,2,0) and `[data-scheme]` has (0,1,0). The gate checks this. | — |
| `data-accent` | bubblegum, peach, butter, mint, aqua, sky, periwinkle, lavender, graphite | The person's hue **name**, from a new profile `hue` field. Sessions stored before the deploy carry only a hex, so the bootstrap and hub.js map it through a fallback table. **Any element** may carry the attribute: avatars, feed rows, kids' cards and app tiles re-derive every `--accent-*` role inside it. | The inline `--accent` hex (`apps/hub.js:80`), the inline `--tint` / `--tint-ink` hexes (`index.html:683, 955, 1070`) and the 168 `color-mix` recipes. |
| `data-kind` | adult, kid, kiosk | The profile | (already set) |
| `data-text-size` | xs, s, m (the default, no attribute), l, xl, xxl | A new person preference (storage below) | F260's `body.big` zoom; see "F260 text size" below |
| `data-contrast` | `more`, or `standard` to opt out | A person switch (storage below). The `@media (prefers-contrast: more)` mirror applies the same values with no JS. | — (no prefers-contrast support today) |
| `data-transparency` | `reduce`, or `full` to opt out | A person switch in Me > Appearance (storage below), plus an `@media (prefers-reduced-transparency)` mirror. Safari has no such media feature, so **the switch is the working path on iPad and iPhone**. | — |
| `data-motion` | `reduce`, or `full` to opt out | The `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)` mirror, applied live, plus an optional switch (storage below). The bootstrap applies the switch before first paint. | The OS-only global kill at `apps/design.css:611-613`, which batch 1b **re-keys, and keeps until every app's literal durations read the tokens** (§8) |
| `data-tv-scale` | `10ft`, or absent (the default) | **Opt-in**, kiosk only. The Phase 6 batch that re-lays out the TV grid sets it. It has an effect only at 1600 px and wider. | — (§3: the TV keeps today's sizes until then) |

**Pre-paint bootstrap (Phase 6).** This is `bootstrap.js` exactly. It goes inline in `<head>` of `index.html`, every app and the Dollywood template (P4-TELL-03), **right after `<meta charset>` and the viewport meta and before any stylesheet** (in Prayer, right after its own `theme-color` meta at `:9`, below). It reads only keys hub.js already writes (`hub.theme`, `hub.session`, both JSON-encoded, `apps/hub.js:27, 32`), plus the proposed `hub.prefs` mirror (below):

```html
<script>(function(d){try{var g=function(k,f){try{var v=localStorage.getItem(k);return v==null?f:JSON.parse(v)}catch(e){return f}},
```

- **`B` is the `theme-color` map:** each palette's v3 `--bg`. The snippet writes it into every `<meta name="theme-color">` and drops the `media` attribute, so the status bar follows the **chosen** palette, not the OS. Midnight on a light OS therefore gets a dark bar from the first paint. If the document has no such meta, the snippet creates one. In batch 1a the shell's two static metas at `index.html:8-9` go away; they carry today's Hearth and Midnight pages (#F7F2EB / #1A1512), which no longer match v3. After the first paint, the shell's `syncThemeColor()` (`index.html:656-658`) keeps the meta current on each `hub:theme` event.
- **Prayer keeps its own meta, and its id.** Prayer has a static `<meta name="theme-color" id="themeColor" content="#F7F2EB">` at `apps/prayer.html:9`, and `applyTheme()` reads it by that id (`el('themeColor')`, `:1534`). CLAUDE.md keeps Prayer's ids, so the meta stays. A meta later in `<head>` is not seen by a snippet that runs before it: with the bootstrap in its standard place, Prayer would end up with two metas, the bootstrap's #0B0A09 and then the stale #F7F2EB (measured in both engines). So **in Prayer only, the bootstrap goes immediately after line 9**, still before `design.css` (`:10`) and before any stylesheet. It then finds that meta, writes the palette's `--bg` into it, drops nothing but a `media` attribute (it has none) and creates no second one. `applyTheme()` keeps `el('themeColor')` and changes only its `t === 'dark'` test and its #1C1714 / #F7F2EB fallbacks: it writes the computed `--bg`, falling back to the bootstrap's `B` value (migration table). **Gated** in the sandbox (Prayer on System and on Midnight: exactly one `theme-color` meta, `id="themeColor"` kept, the palette's `--bg`, no `media`; a bootstrap mutation that ignores the meta is caught) and in both engines on Prayer's real lines 1-9 with the bootstrap after them (System light and dark, Midnight, Forest: `browser-check.json` → `prayerMeta`).
- **`H` is the hex-to-hue fallback** for a session stored before the `hue` field existed. It covers every hex in `worker/seed.sql:4-11` and in `SWATCHES` (`index.html:449`). An unknown hex falls back to graphite, never to another person.

The gate runs this exact file against a stub `document` (with today's two media-keyed metas, or none), `localStorage` and `matchMedia` in 12 cases, then feeds what it wrote back through the cascade. The cases are:
- System on a light OS (no static meta) and on a dark OS;
- Hearth on a dark OS, which stays Hearth;
- the `dark` alias;
- Forest and Graphite;
- an unknown stored theme;
- a legacy adult session and a legacy kid session, each with a hex and no `hue`;
- a new session that carries its `hue`;
- an unknown hex;
- all four preferences, motion included.

Each case must set the right attributes. The inline `colorScheme` must equal the CSS `color-scheme`, and `--accent-strong` must be the expected family. **Every `theme-color` meta must carry the resolved palette's `--bg`, computed through the cascade, with no `media` attribute.** All 12 pass. The theme list gate also checks `B[id]` against each palette's `--bg`, and a mutation (Midnight left at #1A1512) is caught.

**hub.js in batch 1a:**
- **`hue` in the profile.** `publicProfile()` (`apps/hub.js:60`) whitelists fields, so it gains `hue`. Without it `hub.profile.hue` is always undefined.
- **`hub.avatarHtml` carries the person's family (round 4).** `apps/hub.js:459-462` writes `style="--tint:<hex>"` on every avatar today, with Elizabeth's #8A6A4B as the fallback. In batch 1a it emits `data-accent="${p.hue || H[color] || 'graphite'}"` **instead of** the inline `--tint`. Every face in the hub comes from it: the shell's `avatar()` (`index.html:455`, 16 calls), Kid Verse (2), Verses (1) and Prayer (1). This lands in the same commit as the `.ds .avatar` rewrite (batch 1a, `identity-component.css`), because that rewrite reads `--accent-*` from the nearest `data-accent`. Without it, Mae's avatar in Eli's page filled with Eli's periwinkle while its ring kept Mae's hex, and every face on the TV turned graphite (round 4, both engines). Any reader of `--tint` inside the avatar (Prayer's faces, `apps/prayer.html:110`) then gets that person's `--accent-strong` through the scope. A record with no colour and no hue is graphite, never another person (ACCENT-6).
- **`hub.THEMES`** (`apps/hub.js:64-71`): Hearth's blurb "Warm paper" (`:66`) becomes "Warm grouped neutrals", and the graphite entry is added if D2 is accepted.
- **The session refresh (ACCENT-9).** hub.js refreshes the stored session profile from `/api/me` (or `hub.people()`) on pull, and re-applies it in frames through the storage listener. Until then, sessions from before the deploy resolve through the same `H` table that hub.js carries.
- **`applyTheme()`** (`apps/hub.js:74-82`):
  - always writes `data-theme` (the resolved palette) and `data-theme-choice`;
  - writes `data-accent` (`hub.profile.hue`, else `H[color]`, else graphite) and stops writing `--accent`;
  - **sets `root.style.colorScheme` to the resolved scheme on every call.** The bootstrap's inline value would otherwise go stale after `adoptTheme` (`apps/hub.js:97-104`), `setTheme` or an OS change under System.
- **Live preferences.** It re-resolves on the OS `prefers-color-scheme`, `prefers-reduced-motion` and `prefers-contrast` changes; today reduce-motion is read once, at `apps/hub.js:442`. It mirrors the person preferences into `hub.prefs`.
- **`hub:theme`.** It dispatches a same-window `hub:theme` event from `applyTheme`, so the shell can re-sync `theme-color` (P4-DARK-04).
- **The sheen (GLASS-7).** It writes `--sheen-x` on the **visible tab bar and top bar** only (also through `hub.sheenFrom` for a scroller's own bars), never on `:root`. Those two bars are the only elements with a drifting layer (§7). It skips the drift entirely in a document with no visible bar, under Reduce Motion, and on the kiosk. Today the write goes to `:root` (`apps/hub.js:445`).

**Person preferences: storage and adoption (GLASS-1, TYPE-9, D11).** Only the theme's storage exists today. The four new preferences follow the same pattern:
- **Storage.** One person-scope row per preference, beside `theme`, so two devices changing different settings never overwrite each other under last-write-wins:
  - `app_data(person,'hub','textSize')`: `xs` … `xxl` (`m` or unset is the default);
  - `app_data(person,'hub','contrast')`: `more` / `standard` / unset (unset = follow the OS);
  - `app_data(person,'hub','transparency')`: `reduce` / `full` / unset;
  - `app_data(person,'hub','motion')`: `reduce` / `full` / unset.
- **Device mirror.** `localStorage` `hub.prefs` = `{textSize, contrast, transparency, motion}`. The bootstrap reads it before first paint, like `hub.theme`.
- **Adoption.** `adoptPrefs()` works exactly like `adoptTheme()` (`apps/hub.js:97-104`). After the person's hub row set is pulled, **the server row wins** over the mirror. If the scope was pulled before and a key is unset, the mirror is cleared to the default. It re-applies the attributes and dispatches `hub:theme`.
- **The kiosk.** Its preferences are **device-local, exactly like its theme**. On the display profile each setter writes the `hub.prefs` mirror and applies the attribute, as `hub.setTheme` does there (`apps/hub.js:88-93`), and **skips the server row** (the `hub.canWrite` guard). It shows no `hub.kioskNudge()` toast and never throws, because nothing is refused: the setting is the TV's own. `adoptPrefs` returns early for `hub.isKiosk`, as `adoptTheme` does, so no person's rows reach it. The CSS also ignores the text size on the kiosk.
- **API** (each validates, writes the mirror, applies the attribute, and writes the row when `hasPrefs() && hub.canWrite`, like `hub.setTheme`, `apps/hub.js:88-93`):
  - `hub.setTextSize(size)`;
  - `hub.setContrast('more' | 'standard' | null)`;
  - `hub.setTransparency('reduce' | 'full' | null)`;
  - `hub.setMotion('reduce' | 'full' | null)`;
  - `hub.prefs()` returns the resolved set.
- **`scripts/test-prefs.mjs` gains these cases:**
  1. text size set on device A shows on device B for the same person, and not for another person;
  2. the Reduce Transparency switch sets `data-transparency="reduce"` on both devices, and the computed tab-bar background is opaque;
  3. Increase Contrast and motion follow the person the same way;
  4. a stale mirror loses to the server row after the first pull;
  5. the display profile: each setter writes the device mirror and applies its attribute, writes **no** server row, shows no toast and does not throw; a reload keeps the setting (the bootstrap reads the mirror), and a person's rows never adopt onto it;
  6. **conditional on D17:** F260's `f260.big` migrates to `textSize: 'l'` once, or, under D17's alternative, F260 keeps `f260.big` and the hub size does not override it (below).

**F260's theme buttons (batch 1a, JS only).** Once `<html>` always carries `data-theme`, F260's handler `e.target.closest('[data-theme]')` (`apps/f260.html:2031`) climbs to `<html>` from a tap in the 8 px gap of `#themeSeg`. It then calls `hub.setTheme('hearth')` for a person on System, which turns System into Hearth in their `app_data` and loses automatic dark mode. The fix changes the selector to `e.target.closest('#themeSeg button')` and nothing else, so the markup, layout and ids stay. The shell's handler already uses `closest('button')` (`index.html:1283`). The token side is already safe: a bare `data-theme` is not a palette scope, so the buttons keep the document's palette (gated; measured in the running F260, `rev2-runtime.json` → `B`, every button identical to the document in Hearth and in Midnight).

**Other `data-theme` used as data** (grep of the repo, to recheck before batch 1a lands):
- the tests click `#theme [data-theme=…]` (`scripts/screens-themes.mjs:67, 78, 89`, `scripts/test-prefs.mjs:76, 86, 94`); they keep working;
- the Dollywood template's reference flavour defaults `<html data-theme="dark">` and keys `:where([data-theme=light])` (`template.html:2, 11`). In the hub flavour hub.js overwrites it. `dark` is an alias of Midnight, so nothing changes there;
- `scripts/screens-apps.mjs:47, 50` assert that no app CSS keys on `[data-theme=`; that stays true.

**Role rules** (the Phase 6 lint enforces them):

| What | Token | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Text and icons on a hue | `--X-ink` | Never `-fill`, `-fill-strong`, `-graphic`, `--success-strong` or `--warning-strong` as small text (the lint's never-as-text list). |
| A solid fill | `--X-strong`, with `--X-on` as its label | A **person** `-strong` is also ≥ 4.58 as text, so legacy `color: var(--accent)` stays AA. A **semantic** `-strong` is a fill only: as text, success is 3.70 and warning 3.79 on Parchment's page (4.76 and 4.88 on white; round-6 item 18: rounded down, as every bound here), so semantic text is `--X-ink` (`--ok`, `--warn` and `--danger` alias it). Danger's strong happens to read 7.42, but the rule is the same. |
| **The pairing rule** | A background on an element that sets a label (`--on-accent`, `--on-solid`, white/#fff) maps to the family's `-strong`, and the label to that family's `-on`, **in the same commit**. Only unlabelled tints go to `-fill` or `-wash`. | White on `--mint-fill` is 1.26:1 and white on `--butter-fill` is 1.14:1. The lint refuses `-on` or white on any `-fill`, `-wash` or `-fill-strong`. |
| Identity marks (avatar ring, today ring, map marker) | `--X-graphic` | ≥ 3:1, and separated by lightness for colour-blind viewers |
| The selected tab (icon and label) | `--accent-ink`, the icon in `currentColor` | As the shell paints it today (`.ds .tab.on`). The ink is text-grade: ≥ 5.97 under the full sheen (gated) and ≥ 4.52 under the full pickup over any backdrop (reported). Under the full sheen the graphic tone falls to 2.75 (Lavender, Reduce Transparency), and the desktop sidebar's tabs sit under the sheen (§7). |
| Tiles | `var(--tile-bg)` | `linear-gradient(160deg, --X-fill, --X-fill-strong)` with an `--X-ink` glyph |
| Semantic states | colour + glyph | Never a person's family |
| People | colour + face or initial | Always. Every face carries its **own** family: `hub.avatarHtml` writes the person's `data-accent` on the avatar (batch 1a), so the fill, ink and ring are that person's inside any page, the TV's graphite included (gated in the script and both engines) |
| Content cards | `--material-solid-bg` | Glass only on the navigation and control layer (§7) |
| Press feedback | `.pressable`, a **global** opt-in class (not scoped to `.ds`) | The same press everywhere, including the apps that keep their own CSS (§8) |
| Theme swatches | `data-theme-preview` + `data-scheme` + `data-accent`, on **every** swatch and half | A bare `data-theme` is data, never a palette scope; an element with `data-scheme` but no `data-accent` keeps its parent's resolved accent. A swatch shows its palette's **adult** values (the kiosk and Increase Contrast swaps do not reach inside it) and carries **no text**: the theme name and blurb sit outside it, in the document's palette (as `index.html:1261` does today) |

### 2. Colour

#### 2.1 The eight house pastels (and Graphite): fill/ink pairs with computed ratios

#### 2.2 Semantic colours (from the pastel family, and unmistakable)

| Role | Light: fill / ink (ratio) / strong / graphic | Dark: fill / ink (ratio) / strong / graphic | Glyph | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Success | #C4F7CA / #005D22 (6.76) / #008533 / #008533 | #214B29 / #B0E6B7 (7.06) / #84E093 / #84E093 | ✓ (`--success-glyph`, or Lucide `check`) | Also the switch "on" (#269143 in dark, where a white knob stays ≥ 4.02:1) |
| Warning | #FFDCB6 / #724600 (6.23) / #9F6400 / **#BC6D00** | #5A390A ↑ / #FACD98 (7.03) / #FFBB69 / #FFBB69 | ! (`alert-triangle`) | `--attention` and `--attention-fill` for "use it up" |
| Danger (destructive) | #FFC8C3 / #9B1E25 (5.48) / #900017 / #900017 | #64312E ↑ / #FFC6C1 (6.97) / #F07E79 / #F07E79 | ✕ (`x`) | Badges: `--badge-bg` = danger-strong with `--badge-ink` (6.42). **Badge vs card ≥ 6.00 (true minimum 6.004, Forest); vs sheet ≥ 5.28 (Graphite's #2C2C2E sheet); vs page ≥ 7.35.** |

**A semantic `-strong` is a fill, never text.** Success #008533 and warning #9F6400 are solids for a white label (≥ 4.76). As text they are 3.70 and 3.79 on Parchment's page (4.76 and 4.88 on white; round-6 item 18: rounded down, as every bound here), under 4.5 on every light page, and they are not swapped in the 7:1 modes. So a "Saved" or "Use soon" label reads `--success-ink` / `--warning-ink`; `--success-strong` and `--warning-strong` are on the lint's never-as-text list. The gate holds a semantic `-strong` to 3:1 as a graphic (lowest 3.70, success on Parchment's page, the same pair as its text figure above) and reports its text figure (`contrast.json` → `semanticCvdInfo`). The lowest semantic graphic of any role is 3.06: the warning `-graphic` #BC6D00 on Parchment's page.

What the gate checks for the semantic colours:
- **Luminance ratios.** Success vs danger and warning vs danger each have a strong-tone luminance ratio ≥ 1.3; the lowest is 1.57. So the states differ in lightness, not only in hue.
- **Distance from people (access's F4).** Every semantic graphic is **≥ 10.74 ΔE00 from every person graphic** in both schemes; the closest is success vs Mint in light. No profile may take a semantic hue.
- **Time's up** is the timer owner's colour plus motion and sound (`--timer-done: var(--accent-strong)`), never danger (CONS-COLOR-4).
- **Colour-blind separation is reported, not gated.** Success vs warning is 3.9 under protanopia (light), and success vs danger is 8.6 under deuteranopia (dark). The glyph carries the state, which is why glyph tokens exist and the lint requires them.

#### 2.2a The 7:1 modes (kiosk and Increase Contrast): what is 7:1, and what stays AA

The kiosk block and `[data-contrast=more]`, with its `@media (prefers-contrast: more)` mirror, swap these:
- `--text-2` and `--text-3` → `--text-2-hi`;
- the 12 `--X-ink` → `--X-ink-hi`;
- the **9 person `--X-strong` → `--X-ink-hi`, in the light palettes only** (Hearth and its `light` alias, Parchment, Frost, and a root with no theme and no dark scheme). In dark the pastel solid stays: its `-on` label is already ≥ 8.67 and it reads ≥ 7.06 as text on every dark surface, so the swap would only turn it near-white (Bubblegum #FF9BC4 → #FFE0EB) with nothing gained. *Design change in revision 4.* Gated: light roots swap, dark roots keep the adult pastel, in the kiosk, Increase Contrast and its media mirror; a mutation that applies the swap in dark is caught;
- `--badge-bg` → `--danger-ink-hi`;
- `--toast-ink-2` → `--toast-ink`;
- `--glass-inverse` → `--glass-inverse-hi` (.76 light, .86 dark; new in revision 3).

The TV photo panel needs no swap: `--tv-panel` is `.74` in every mode, which holds both TV lines at 7:1 by itself (new in revision 3; it was `.66`).

The semantic solids are deliberately not swapped. Swapping them to ink-hi collapses warning against danger to a luminance ratio of 1.00, and the gate requires ≥ 1.3, so the states would differ by hue alone. Semantic solid labels are therefore AA in every mode and gated at 4.5 under their own check id.

**In the kiosk and Increase Contrast, every text pair the gate measures is ≥ 7:1, with two exceptions, both by design:**
- **semantic solid labels**, AA at ≥ 4.76 (above);
- **large numerals drawn in a person's `-graphic` tone**, gated as large text at ≥ 3.13. No numeral reads the graphic tone today: the Timer digits read `--accent-strong` (≥ 7.06 in these modes) and the Tally digits read `--accent-ink`.

That includes the TV board's secondary line and the inverse glass, each gated at 7 here since revision 3.

**Theme swatches are the one scope the swaps do not reach, by design.** A swatch (`[data-theme-preview]` + `data-scheme` + `data-accent`) re-declares its palette's hue families and neutrals on itself, so inside it the adult values apply: measured on a Hearth swatch under Increase Contrast, `--text-3` on `--surface` is 6.66 and the Mint ink on its fill 5.23. That is harmless because **a swatch carries no text**: the Me cards (`index.html:295-304`) paint blocks only, and the theme name and blurb sit outside the swatch, in the document's (swapped) palette. The rule is in the role table: any label goes outside the swatch. Adult dark mode does not claim 7:1: the dark ink on its own chip is 6.86-6.94 for Bubblegum, Peach and Lavender, and the dark hero button uses that same pair.

### 3. Type

The face is always the system stack: `system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif`. No font is fetched and SF Pro is never embedded.

| Token | Adult | Kid (`data-kind="kid"`) |
|---|---|---|
| `--font-text` | The system stack above | `--font-rounded` |
| `--font-rounded` | `ui-rounded`, then the system stack | same |
| `--font-ui` (and the legacy `--font-sans`) | `--font-text` | `--font-rounded` |
| `--font-display` (legacy alias; large titles) | `--font-text`, bold (D6) | `--font-rounded` |
| `--font-serif` | Reading and scripture only (F260 passages, prayer text) | `--font-rounded` |
| `--font-numeral` | Rounded, with `--numeral-features: tabular-nums` | Rounded |
| `--font-mono` | Unchanged | **`--font-rounded`** (the Larder's counts, `apps/leftovers.html:24, 69`) |

**Kid mode is rounded everywhere.** The kid block sets `--font-text`, `--font-ui`, `--font-display`, `--font-serif` and `--font-mono` to the rounded face. At specificity (0,2,0) it beats the `:root` aliases in §9, so every legacy read follows. Two kid surfaces need more than a token:
- **Prayer** sets Manrope and Instrument Serif as literals (`apps/prayer.html:45, 148, 338`), so no token reaches it. The Prayer batch adds a kid rule that holds **whatever D13 decides**: `:root[data-kind="kid"] body { font-family: var(--font-ui) }` and `:root[data-kind="kid"] :is(.ansnote, #pray .last) { font-family: var(--font-serif) }`. Both resolve to ui-rounded for a kid. If D13 is accepted, Prayer reads the tokens for everyone and the rule becomes redundant.
- **The Larder's counts** read `--font-mono`, which the kid block now rounds.

Measured on the local rig as Ezra (iPhone PWA and iPad portrait), token file swapped in (`rev2-runtime.json` → `summary.C_*`, `E`). "Planned" means the batch rows this section names are injected as CSS:

| Kid-visible read | Today | Proposed, app code as it is | Proposed + planned rows |

| Kid Verse `.ref h1`, `.stars .count`, `.rewards .bank b`, `.story-head h2` (`apps/kidverse.html:36, 62, 78, 127`) | ui-serif | ui-rounded | ui-rounded |
| The Larder body (`apps/leftovers.html:16`) and its counts `.tally`, `.group h2 small` (`:24, :69`, `--font-mono`) | ui-serif / monospace | ui-rounded | ui-rounded |
| Tally `.count` (`apps/tally.html:58`) | ui-serif | ui-rounded | ui-rounded |
| Verses `.trainer .text` and `.trainer h1` (`apps/verses.html:43, 38`) | ui-serif | ui-rounded | ui-rounded |
| **Prayer**, all visible text | Manrope (0 % rounded) | Manrope (0 %) | **ui-rounded (100 %)**, the Prayer batch's kid rule |

| **Share of visible text in ui-rounded**: Home and the seven kid-visible apps, on both devices | 0-95 % | 100 % except Prayer (0 %) and the park map's badge | **100 % everywhere** |

The gate checks that every font token (`--font-text`, `-ui`, `-sans`, `-display`, `-serif`, `-mono`, `-numeral`) starts with `ui-rounded` in kid mode. For adults it checks that display and body start with `system-ui`, the serif with `ui-serif`, and numerals with `ui-rounded`.

**Big numerals are rounded for everyone, through a batch-1a move.** Legacy `--font-sans` now aliases the text face (TYPE-1), so a numeral that reads `--font-sans` or inherits the body font leaves ui-rounded unless it moves. Measured with app code as it is: the adult Timer's "10:00" went from ui-rounded 76.5 px to system-ui 76.5 px, and the TV clock from ui-rounded 172.8 px to system-ui 172.8 px. So **batch 1a moves every numeral read to `--font-numeral`**:
- the `--font-display` numerals: Tally `.count` (`apps/tally.html:58`), Kid Verse `.stars .count`, `.rewards .bank b` and the week stepper `.stepper .wk` (`apps/kidverse.html:62, 78, 99`), and Verses `.done .big` (`apps/verses.html:64`);
- the Timer digits `.time` (`apps/timer.html:32`, today `--font-sans`);
- the Home clock `.home-hero .clock` (`index.html:100`) and the TV clock `.tv-hero .clock` (`:142`);
- the timer pill `#timer-pill .tp-time` (`:350`) and the in-app countdown `#pill #pill-timer` (`:360`);
- the kids' star counts, `.kid-chip b` on Home (`:206`) and `.tv-face b` in the TV stars pane (`:156`);
- the park wait times `.park-list .pt` (`:196`), and Verses `.boxes .n` and `.queue .when` (`apps/verses.html:83, 90`).

The rule is simple: **every read set in `tabular-nums` reads `--font-numeral`**. `rev2-runtime.mjs` (`D`) checks it statically: every `tabular-nums` rule in the shell and the apps is on the list, and none is missing. With the move applied, every numeral the demo household renders resolves to ui-rounded:
- adult: the star counts, timer pill, Tally, Timer, Verses and the Kid Verse stepper;
- kid: the Kid Verse stars and balance, Tally and Timer;
- kiosk: the TV clock at 172.8 px and the TV star counts.

Four selectors are not rendered by the demo household (the Home clock, the park list, the in-app countdown and Verses "done"). They are on the same list and read the same token.

Size = the role's base × `--ts`, and never below `--fs-floor`. `--ts` is the product of three multipliers:
- **`--ts-width`:** 1.12 at ≥ 744 px **with a coarse pointer**, so the iPad gets the tier and a desktop window keeps 1.
- **`--ts-user`:** the text-size preference: xs .88, s .94, m 1, l 1.12, xl 1.25, xxl 1.5. The kiosk ignores it.
- **`--ts-kind`:** kid 1.2 (floor 16). The kiosk is 1.3 with an 18 px floor **at every width**. The 10-foot scale (1.9, floor 28) exists only behind the opt-in `data-tv-scale="10ft"` at 1600 px and wider.
