| `--fs-field` | max(16 px, body) | | | | | | | |

These are the resolved px at text size m, from `typeTable` in `contrast.json`. Both engines resolve the same lengths. **Today the TV board reads none of these role tokens**; it reads the legacy sizes below.

**Why the kiosk keeps today's sizes at every width (D16).** The TV board (`index.html:103-176`) reads the legacy `--fs-*` and `--sp-*` inside a fixed grid: `.tv` is `1fr 1fr` below 1200 px and `5fr 4fr 4fr` above (`:134, :136`), `.tv-face` is a fixed 104 px (`:153`) and `.when` is nowrap (`:163`). It fits 1080 px only at today's values. Revision 1 grew them 15-58 % at 1600 px and wider. The verifier measured that on the local rig (`audits/evidence/p4/tokens/verify-constraints-1.json` → `A['1920x1080-proposed']`; screenshots `verify-constraints-1-tv-today.png` and `-tv-proposed.png`):
- the `.tv` grid grew from 1,040 px (bottom y = 1064) to 1,434 px (bottom y = 1470);
- the Reminders pane (`.tv-rem`), which is what the board exists to show, ended at y = 1470, off the screen;
- the bottom of the feed ended at 1096, and the document cannot scroll.

So the kiosk block now:
- **pins the legacy sizes to today's kiosk values** (`apps/design.css:287`);
- **keeps today's spacing** (`--space-k: 1`);
- keeps the normal margin;
- at every width, unless the opt-in is on.

| Legacy size | Kiosk, every width (= today) | TV 10-foot opt-in at 1920 |
|---|---|---|
| `--fs-sm` / `--fs-md` / `--fs-lg` | 18 / 22 / 26 | 28.5 / 32.3 / 38 |
| `--fs-xl` / `--fs-2xl` / `--fs-3xl` | 32 / 40 / 56 | 41.8 / 53.2 / 64.6 |
| `--fs-4xl` / `--fs-hero` | 84 / clamp(56px, 8vw, 96px) | 121.6 / clamp(64, 5vw, 96) |
| `--fs-xs` | **18** (the kiosk floor; today 12). The board does not read it: `.tv-rem .rem-by` uses `--fs-sm` (`:172`) | 28 |
| `--sp-4` / `--sp-6`, `--margin` | 16 / 24, normal (28 at 1024, 32 at 1920) | 24 / 36, 96 |

Measured with the token file swapped in (`rev2-runtime.mjs` → `rev2-runtime.json`, `A`; screenshot `audits/evidence/p4/tokens/rev2-tv-1920-proposed.png`):

| Viewport | Today | Proposed (default) | Proposed + `data-tv-scale="10ft"` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1920 × 1080 (the real TV) | fits: grid 1,040 px, bottom 1064 | **fits, identical: grid 1,040 px, bottom 1064**, no clipped text, no horizontal scroll | does not fit: bottom 1470, the Reminders pane off screen |
| 1024 × 768 | does not fit today either: bottom 1232 | bottom 1240 (+8 px; the pinned sizes and spacing are identical, so it comes from another role change, most likely the display face leaving the serif, D6; not isolated) | inert below 1600 px: 1240, same as the default |

The 1024 × 768 case is pre-existing and not a regression: the board already overflows a landscape 1024 kiosk today. It is noted for Phase 5; the TV is 1920 × 1080.

**The 10-foot scale is an opt-in** (`:root[data-kind="kiosk"][data-tv-scale="10ft"]` inside `@media (min-width: 1600px)`). It re-aliases the legacy sizes to the roles (none shrinks below today, gated) and sets floor 28, body 32.3, × 1.5 spacing and the 96 px title-safe margin. It is turned on **only by the Phase 6 batch that re-lays out the `.tv` grid** (`index.html:134-166`: the fixed 104 px `.tv-face`, the nowrap `.when`), with `scripts/test-tv.mjs` passing at 1920 × 1080 and a fit check (grid bottom ≤ 1080, no clipped text) passing too. **Phase 5 should record the real TV's CSS viewport.** A TV browser that reports under 1600 CSS px (a device pixel ratio above 1) would never reach the 10-foot scale, and the re-layout batch would then key it on the attribute alone.

Also:
- **Weights:** `--fw-light` 300 (numerals only), `--fw-regular` 400, `--fw-medium` 500, `--fw-semibold` 600, `--fw-bold` 700 and `--fw-heavy` 800 (numerals only). The audit found seven weights in use, 300-900.
- **Key/value pair:** `--text-label` (footnote + `--text-3`) and `--text-value` (subheadline semibold + `--text`).
- **Caps:** `--ls-caps` .06em.

**Gates** (90 contexts: 3 kinds × 5 widths × 6 text sizes, × 15 roles):
- every role ≥ 11 adult, ≥ 16 kid, ≥ 18 kiosk, at every width;
- **the kiosk keeps today's legacy sizes and spacing exactly, at every width** (both bounds: `--fs-sm … --fs-4xl`, `--fs-hero`, `--sp-2/-4/-6`), with the normal margin;
- the opt-in at 1600 px and wider: floor 28, every role ≥ 28, body ≥ 32, margin 96, and no legacy size below today;
- the opt-in is inert under 1600 px;
- fields ≥ 16;
- a desktop window at 1440 keeps body 17;
- the iPad lifts body to ≥ 19;
- kid mode is rounded in every font token (mono included), and adults keep the text face for display.

**The floor reaches only what reads a role.** `--fs-floor` binds the role tokens and the legacy `--fs-*` aliases. It does not bind a px literal, so literals under the floor still render. They predate the proposal; this is not a regression. Measured on the rig with the token file swapped in and app code as it is (`rev2-runtime.json` → `summary.E_*`):
- **Under 11 px for an adult:** F260's ring caption `.tring .rn small` (9.5 px, `apps/f260.html:133`), and Kid Verse's day letters `.kids .days span` (10 px, `apps/kidverse.html:110`; 12 visible in the parent's view of the kids' weeks). Kid Verse's badge captions `.badges li small` (10 px, `:86`) are the same literal size, and a kid sees them.
- **Under 16 px for a kid:**
  - Kid Verse's badge captions (10 px, 6 visible to Ezra: "Sep 8", "50 stars earned", "prayed on 5 days");
  - Prayer's date line `.date` (14 px);
  - nine Larder literals, from 11 to 14 px (`.tally`, `.lede`, `.alert`, `.group h2`, `.group h2 small`, `.meta`, `.status`, `.hearth p`, `.copy`).

- **The Dollywood pair** (round 4; the park map is kid-visible, because `apps.json` gives it no `visibleTo`). Measured **as rendered**: HTML at its computed size, SVG `<text>` at its computed size × √|det(getScreenCTM())| (the map scales its labels), and `::before` text (`rev2-runtime.json` → `F`: the build guide's map, cross-section and steps as Eli; the park map's map, whole park and waits as Eli; the kid's map, whole park and Family as Ezra; the view-only map, Nearby and a ride card as Kiara; iPhone PWA and iPad portrait):
  - **under 11 px for an adult:** the build guide's cross-section axis (4.46 px on the iPhone, 9.1 on the iPad), section names (6.14 / 10.23), listing numbers (6.82) and contour heights (9.5), all SVG; the toolbar group labels (10.5, `::before`); the compass N (9) in both exports; the park map's wait tile MIN (9.5). These are P4-TYPE-01 and Table TYPE-5, now on named rows;
  - **under 16 px for a kid** on the park map: the compass N, the wait chip, the family and meeting-point labels (11), and 11-15.5 px literals across the location line, the sheet tabs, the meeting-point bar, the Family and Nearby panes and the ride card.

Each of these is a **named row** in the migration table. The three sub-11 literals in the hub (F260, Kid Verse) move to `--fs-caption2` in batch 1a, which is 11 px for an adult and 16 px for a kid. The Prayer and Larder literals move to the nearest role in their own app batch. The Dollywood rows land in the template batch (`../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html`, rebuild, `verify.py`, export): its three sub-11 HTML literals move to `--fs-caption2`; its SVG labels are sized `max(--fs-floor, design px) / screen scale`, the rule the family labels already follow; and, for the kid floor, every `font-size` literal under 16 px in its CSS moves to its nearest role (109 rules in the park-map export). With every named row applied, the rig measures **no adult or kiosk text under 11 px** on Home and every app, the build guide and the park map included, and **no kid text under 16 px** on Home and the seven kid-visible apps, the park map included, on both devices. It also checks that every text under the floor in the unplanned run is on a named row. The SVG label rule is JS in the template's `apply()`, so the check **emulates** it per named selector (it sets each label's size as the rule would); the template batch re-runs this check on the real code. TYPE-6 and TYPE-11 are therefore T+R, and the TYPE-12 lint (no px font sizes) keeps new literals out.

### 7. Glass (the navigation and control layer only)

**The role rule.** Glass sits on the navigation and control layer only: the tab bar, top bar, sheets, floating buttons, the profile switcher, and toolbars over content. **Every content card and list uses `--material-solid-bg`**, in scrollers and on the TV. The TV board's panes (`<section class="tv-pane glass-strong …">`, `index.html:1121-1127`) are content, so they leave `.glass-strong` in the shell batch (migration table); only the `.kiosk-switch` control keeps glass. `--material-look-*` is **deprecated**. It is kept only as the migration target for today's `.ds .card.glass` (`apps/design.css:400`) and for a panel floating over a photo where `--tv-panel` does not apply. The Phase 6 lint flags `.glass` or the look material on a content card.

| Token | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--glass` / `--glass-strong` | `color-mix(--surface α, transparent)`, α = 78/90 % light, 80/90 % dark | Raised from .62-.66 / .84-.86. **The fill alone**, over the worst unblurred backdrop (a white photo under dark glass, black under light glass), keeps primary text ≥ 7.01 and secondary ≥ 5.23. Decision D8. |
| `--glass-bg` / `--glass-bg-strong` | The specular sheen + the fill. **No `var(--sheen-x)` and no pickup** (GLASS-7, below) | The recipe in one token (CONS-GLASS-1); replaces 17 hand copies and the template's `--lv-glass*`. The two bars paint it under their drifting layer. |
| `--glass-bg-tinted` / `--glass-bg-strong-tinted` | The sheen + the person pickup painted in place + the fill (the layer order of today's recipe) | Every glass surface except the two bars: sheets, pills, buttons, `.glass` / `.glass-strong`, the chat composer. `--material-chrome-bg` is the strong one. |
| `--glass-pickup-layer` | A radial (90 % × 70 % at 50 % −10 %, clear by 62 %) of the person's **tile-end tone, `--accent-fill-strong`**, at `--glass-pickup` | Painted in place by the `-tinted` recipes, and on the two bars by a drifting `::after` layer (below). Re-derived in every `data-accent` scope. It was the strong tone until revision 3; in dark that is a light pastel, which lightened dark glass under light text (sheet titles 5.91 over a white photo). |
| `--glass-spec` | White at .60-.75 in light; **.06 in dark** (was .12-.14) | The dark cap keeps sheet titles 7:1 over a white photo |
| `--glass-shadow` | Inner highlight, refracted edge, inner bottom shadow, outer ring, e2 | |
| `--glass-filter` / `--glass-filter-strong` | blur(20) / blur(32) + saturate(1.8) | `--blur-sm` 8, `--blur` 20, `--blur-lg` 32 |
| `--blur-photo` | 24 px | The TV album backdrop (`index.html:131`, today a literal `filter: blur(24px)` on two full-screen images that crossfade over 2.5 s all day). **On the kiosk it is applied once per photo, not live:** the board draws the album's 256 px rendition into a canvas once with `ctx.filter = 'blur(24px)'` (scaled to the screen) and crossfades two static bitmaps, so the crossfade animates only opacity. Elsewhere, where the photo does not animate, the live filter may stay. A server-side blurred rendition is the alternative if the canvas step proves slow on the TV. |
| `--scrim-blur` | 0 | Scrims never blur: one live glass layer at a time |
| `--glass-look` | `--surface` 90 % over `--bg`, no filter | The kiosk paints its chrome with it; otherwise deprecated (above) |
| `--glass-solid` / `--glass-strong-solid` | `--surface` / `--surface-raised` | Reduce Transparency |
| `--material-chrome-bg/-filter`, `--material-solid-bg`, `--material-look-bg/-filter` | Chrome = live glass on the control layer (`--glass-bg-strong-tinted`); solid = every content card; look = deprecated | Named roles the lint can check. The component half gets `.mat-chrome` / `.mat-solid` (and a deprecated `.mat-look`), **scoped to `.ds` or opt-in** (not global element rules). |

CIEDE2000 of the full pickup from the bare pane, for the eight hues over Hearth's and Frost's white card and over Midnight's and Graphite's card: 6.2-12.9 light and 8.2-14.3 dark, against 5.5-10.7 and 8.9-16.1 with the strong tone (floored). |

**The sheen (GLASS-7): option (b), a compositor-only layer on the two bars.** A custom property's `var()` is substituted where the property is declared. So revision 1's `--glass-bg`, declared on `:root` with `var(--sheen-x)` inside, froze the sheen at the `:root` value. The verifier measured that writing `--sheen-x` on a glass element left its `--glass-bg` unchanged in both engines (`audits/evidence/p4/tokens/verify-scope-probe.json`). Only a per-frame `:root` write moved it, and that is the cost P4-GLASS-01 flags.

Revision 2 moved the drift onto a `::before` layer on every glass class, with `position: relative; overflow: hidden` on the host. The third verification loaded that rule over today's `.ds` components in both engines (`verify-coherence-3.json` → R3). It broke three of them:
- `.ds .sheet::before` is the sheet's grabber (`apps/design.css:584`), and the layer replaced it;
- `.ds .sheet` scrolls (`overflow: auto`, `:580`), and `overflow: hidden` stopped a tall sheet from scrolling;
- `.ds .tabbar` is `position: fixed` (`:556`), and `position: relative` un-pinned it. (The shell's timer pill `#timer-pill`, a `.pill`, is `position: fixed` too, `index.html:344`.)

**Revision 3 splits the job.** The component rule is `audits/tools/phase4/tokens/glass7-component.css`, batch 1b, quoted exactly:

```css
.ds :is(.glass, .btn-glass, .pill) { background: var(--glass-bg-tinted); }
.ds :is(.glass-strong, .sheet) { background: var(--glass-bg-strong-tinted); }
.ds :is(.tabbar, .topbar) { background: var(--glass-bg-strong); }
.ds :is(.tabbar, .topbar)::after {
  content: ""; position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; left: 25%; right: 25%; z-index: -1; pointer-events: none;
  background: var(--glass-pickup-layer);
  transform: translateX(calc((var(--sheen-x) - 50%) / 2)); will-change: transform;
}
.ds .tabbar::after { bottom: 67%; }
@media (min-width: 1024px) { .ds .tabbar.sidebar::after { content: none; } }
```

- **Every glass surface but the two bars paints the pickup in place**, centred and still, through the `-tinted` recipes. That covers sheets, pills, buttons, `.glass` / `.glass-strong` and the chat composer. **No pseudo-element is used and nothing sets `position` or `overflow`.** The sheet keeps its `::before` grabber and its scrolling, and the fixed timer pill stays fixed.
- **Only the tab bar and the top bar carry the drift**, on `::after` (no `.ds` component uses `::after` on them). Both are already positioned stacking contexts (`fixed` / `sticky`, `z-index: 20`), so `z-index: -1` paints the layer over the bar's own background and under its content. The layer is the bar's middle half and drifts at most 25 % of its own width, which is 12.5 % of the bar. **It never leaves the bar**, so neither bar gets an `overflow` or a `clip-path`.
- **The bottom tab bar** keeps the layer on its top third. The radial's colour ends 70 % × 62 % − 10 % = 33 % down the layer, 11 % down the bar: 7.9 px of a 72 px bar, above the icons at 13.8 px in WebKit and 14.3 px in Chromium.
- **The desktop sidebar** (`class="tabbar sidebar"`, `index.html:393`; `apps/design.css:570`, at 1024 px and wider) **carries no drifting layer**. Its tabs start at the top of a full-height bar: revision 2's top-third clip ended at y = 271 px, and the first three tabs (y 24-176) sat under it. The person's colour stays in the selected tab. The class is on the element at every width, so the phone-width bottom bar keeps its layer, and the check covers that case too.
- **hub.js** writes `--sheen-x` on the visible tab bar and top bar only (§1). A frame therefore re-resolves one layer's `transform`, which the compositor moves without a repaint.
- **The template's glass classes** adopt the same split in their batch (the sibling repo).

**Gated, in both engines** (`browser-check.json` → `glass7`). The rule is loaded after today's component half of `apps/design.css`, at 390 × 844 with the bottom bar, at 1180 × 820 with the sidebar, and at 390 with the sidebar class, each at `--sheen-x` 0 %, 30 % and 100 %. It checks that:
- the sheet's `::before` is still the grabber, a static solid bar, below 720 px (above 720 px design.css hides it);
- the sheet still scrolls and paints the pickup;
- the tab bar stays `fixed`, the top bar `sticky` and the timer pill `fixed`;
- the document and the sheet have no horizontal overflow at either end of the drift;
- each bar's layer stays inside its bar, at `z-index: -1`;
- the pickup's colour ends above every tab's icon and label;
- the sidebar has no layer.

All three cases pass in WebKit 26.6 and Chromium 154. The token side is gated in `contrast.mjs`:
- **no token contains `var(--sheen-x)`**, checked statically; a mutation that puts it back is caught;
- a child and a grandchild that write `--sheen-x: 80%` on themselves leave `--glass-bg`, `--glass-bg-strong`, both `-tinted` recipes, `--material-chrome-bg` and `--glass-pickup-layer` unchanged;
- the `::after` transform resolved at that element reads 80 %.

**Measured with its layers.** The white sheen is full at the top edge and gone by 34 % of the height. The pickup radial has faded to nothing by 33 % of the height of the box that paints it.
- **Gated: text under the full sheen on `--glass-strong`** (sheets, top bar, tab bar), every palette, person and mode. Primary is ≥ 8.22 and secondary ≥ 6.15, both over the worst backdrop. The dark `.06` cap is what makes this pass.
- **Gated (new in revision 3): text under the full sheen and the full pickup**, which is what a sheet title or the top of a pill sits under.
  - On `--glass-strong` over every backdrop, a white photo included: primary ≥ 7.52, secondary ≥ 5.56.
  - On `--glass` over the page, a card and #767676: primary ≥ 7.98, secondary ≥ 5.89.
  - Both are ≥ 7 in the 7:1 modes (primary 9.79, secondary 8.93).
  - With the strong tone this failed at 5.91 for a sheet title over a white photo. That failure is why the tone changed, and the mutation that puts it back is caught.
- **Gated: text under the full sheen on `--glass`** (buttons, pills) over the page, a card and #767676: primary ≥ 8.89, secondary ≥ 6.62 (≥ 7 in the 7:1 modes).
- **Gated (new in revision 3): the tabs under the full sheen** on `--glass-strong` over the page, a card and #767676. ### 8. Motion

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `--spring-snappy` + `--dur-snappy` | A damped spring as `linear()`, 240 ms, 0.8 % overshoot | Presses (the release), toggles, the tab indicator; legacy `--spring` aliases it |
| `--spring-gentle` + `--dur-gentle` | 290 ms, no overshoot | Sheets sliding up, pages, layout |
| `--spring-bouncy` + `--dur-bouncy` | **340 ms**, 9 % overshoot (ζ 0.608, ω 26.7 rad/s, within 0.5 % of rest at 340 ms; was 460 ms) | Celebrations only: stars, badges (D10) |
| `--ease-standard` / `--ease-exit` | cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1) / (.4,0,.8,.2) | Colour and opacity / things leaving |
| `--dur-fast` / `-base` / `-slow` / `-exit` | 200 / 280 / 350 / **200** ms | Legacy `--dur-1` and `--dur-2` → fast (120 → 200 and 220 → 200), `--dur-3` → slow (360 → 350) |
| `--dur-progress` | **`var(--dur-slow)`, 350 ms, on `--spring-gentle`** (was 800 ms) | A progress fill or ring moving to its new value |
| `--dur-press` | **0**: the press-in is an instant `:active` state with no transition | The release animates on `--dur-snappy` / `--spring-snappy`. So every **UI** transition token is inside 200-350 ms. |
| `--dur-shimmer` / `-pulse` / `-ambient` | 1400 / 1200 / 2400 ms | Keyframe loops, not transitions (Table MOTION-1) |
| `--dur-crossfade` | 2500 ms | **The one ambient transition outside 200-350 ms**: the TV album crossfade, a CSS opacity transition on the kiosk only (`:root[data-kind="kiosk"] .tv-bg-img { transition: opacity 2.5s … }`, `index.html:131`). An owner-approved exception, decision **D18**. Under Reduce Motion the kept global kill makes it a 150 ms opacity change. Gated as the named exception (2500 ms, adult and kiosk). |
| `--pulse-scale` | 0.94 (1 under Reduce Motion) | The chat mic's listening pulse (`index.html:265-266`, `@keyframes pulse { 50% { transform: scale(.94) } }`). The keyframes read the token, so under Reduce Motion the pulse no longer scales. |
| `--ambient-iterations` | 3 | Ambient loops stop, and use transform/opacity only |
| `--press-scale` / `--press-scale-sm` / `--press-dim` | 0.97 / 0.94 / brightness(.94) light, (1.14) dark | Press state with a brightness shift |
| `--enter-distance` | 16 px | Sheet and toast entry |
| **Reduce Motion** (attribute + mirror) | Springs → linear 150 ms (opacity crossfade), scale 1, distance 0, ambient 0, pulse scale 1, shimmer and progress 0 | Gated |

**The press rule (MOTION-3).** `.pressable` is a **global opt-in class, not scoped to `.ds`**, so the apps that keep their own CSS can use it:

```css
.pressable { transition: transform var(--dur-snappy) var(--spring-snappy), filter var(--dur-snappy) var(--ease-standard); }
.pressable:active { transform: scale(var(--press-scale)); filter: var(--press-dim); transition-duration: var(--dur-press); }
.pressable.is-small:active { transform: scale(var(--press-scale-sm)); }
```

The `.ds .btn` family gets it in batch 1b. The non-`.ds` apps adopt it in their own batches: F260 (its `.btn`, chips and week cells), Prayer (`.chip`, `button.act`, the "Pray now" controls), the Larder (the add bar and rows), and the Dollywood template (its buttons, chips and FABs, changed in the sibling repo).

**The global Reduce Motion kill is kept, re-keyed (MOTION-6).** The tokens neutralise every duration and distance that reads a token. But F260, Prayer, the Dollywood pair and the shell still animate with literal durations and curves until their own batches (for example `apps/f260.html:137, 258` and `apps/prayer.html:98`). So batch 1b does not delete today's OS-only kill (`apps/design.css:611-613`). It re-keys it to the switch and its mirror, and makes it an opacity-only substitute rather than a hard stop:

```css
:root[data-motion="reduce"] *, :root[data-motion="reduce"] *::before, :root[data-motion="reduce"] *::after {
  animation-duration: .01ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;
  transition-property: opacity, color, background-color, border-color !important; transition-duration: 150ms !important;
  scroll-behavior: auto !important; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  :root:not([data-motion="full"]) *, :root:not([data-motion="full"]) *::before, :root:not([data-motion="full"]) *::after { /* the same */ } }
```

So the in-app switch (`data-motion="reduce"`) also stops literal animations, and `data-motion="full"` opts out of the OS kill. The kill is retired only when the Phase 6 lint finds no literal duration or curve left.

**The reduced-motion test moves with it (batch 1b).** `scripts/test-design.mjs:91-94` asserts today's hard stop: `.btn`'s `transition-duration` under 0.02 s. The re-keyed kill is an opacity-only substitute at 150 ms, measured at 0.15 s in both engines under the OS setting and under `data-motion="reduce"` (round 4). So in the same commit the test asserts instead:
- `animation-duration` ≤ 0.01 ms (`:90-91`, unchanged in substance);
- `.btn`'s `transition-property` lists only `opacity`, `color`, `background-color` and `border-color`, and its `transition-duration` is ≤ 150 ms (`:92-93`);
- the Midnight switch at `:94-96` waits for the 150 ms body-background fade (≥ 200 ms, or `transitionend`) before it reads the colour, which today it reads after 150 ms with no transition at all.

CLAUDE.md's test table changes with it ("reduced motion" becomes "reduced motion: animations off; transitions opacity and colour only, ≤ 150 ms").

**Gated:** every UI transition token is within 200-350 ms (snappy, gentle, bouncy, fast, base, slow, exit, progress, and the legacy `--dur-1/-2/-3`); `--dur-crossfade` is the one ambient exception, at 2500 ms (D18); the press-in is 0; each spring ends at 1, snappy and gentle overshoot ≤ 2 %, bouncy ≤ 10 %; Reduce Motion removes travel, scale and the pulse. A mutation that puts `--dur-progress` back to 800 ms is caught.

**Adding a theme** (the corrected CLAUDE.md wording for Phase 6). A theme named X of scheme S needs these steps.

In the token file:
1. a neutral block keyed `:root[data-theme="X"], [data-theme-preview="X"]` in §3;
2. `:root[data-theme="X"]` in scheme S's hue-family selector list (§2);
3. the same selector in scheme S's role selector list (§4). Leaving it out breaks the stale-scheme guard for glass, toast and elevation.
3a. **for a light theme only:** `:root[data-kind="kiosk"][data-theme="X"]`, `:root[data-contrast="more"][data-theme="X"]` and `:root:not([data-contrast="standard"])[data-theme="X"]` in the three light-only person-solid swap lists (§7-§8 of the file; revision 4). A dark theme is in none of them (gated both ways).
4. `:root[data-theme="X"]` and `[data-theme-preview="X"]` on scheme S's `color-scheme` line (the end of §3; the neutral blocks do not declare it).

In the bootstrap and hub.js:

5. `X:'S'` in the bootstrap's `S` map, and X's `--bg` in its `B` (`theme-color`) map;
6. an entry in `hub.THEMES` (`apps/hub.js:64-71`), with its blurb. Batch 1a also rewrites Hearth's blurb, "Warm paper" (`:66`), to "Warm grouped neutrals", since v3 re-tunes Hearth to a grouped page with white cards.

In the tests, which hard-code today's five palettes and their page colours:

7. `scripts/test-design.mjs:102` (each palette's page rgb) and `:112` (`t === 'midnight' || t === 'forest'` → dark). As written, a seventh theme fails this test. The same file hard-codes two more page colours, `:45` and `:96`, and `scripts/test-apps.mjs:221` and `scripts/test-prefs.mjs:98, 104` do too (batch 1a, step 4 below).
8. `scripts/screens-themes.mjs:32` (the palette → page rgb and scheme map) and `:77` (the light/dark pair it switches between);
9. `scripts/screens-apps.mjs:32` (the same map);
10. `scripts/test-dollywood-themes.mjs:30-37` (the theme list it walks).

In the docs and the park map:

11. `docs/design.html`: the theme segmented control (`:74`), the swatch row (`:270`) and the `DARK` map (`:312`);
12. the Dollywood template (`../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html`) keys its hub flavour on `data-scheme` only (`:212`, `:219`), so it needs no theme list. Re-run its `verify.py` and `scripts/test-dollywood-themes.mjs` after the change.

The gate reads the `hub.THEMES` ids from `apps/hub.js`, adds graphite, and checks every id against steps 1-5, including `B[X]` = X's `--bg` and step 3a. `color-scheme` is also checked per theme under a stale `data-scheme`, in the script and in both engines.

**Theme swatches.** The `.tp[data-preview=…]` copies go away. A swatch is any element carrying `data-theme-preview`, `data-scheme` and `data-accent`. **`data-preview="<id>"` stays on the swatch as data**, so the shell's own rule that hides the System card's second half-card (`.theme-swatch[data-preview="system"] > .tp-card + .tp-card { display: none }`, `index.html:304`) keeps working with no change; the System swatch then carries `data-preview="system" data-theme-preview="hearth"`. A swatch shows its palette's adult values and carries no text (§2.2a), and **every element that carries `data-scheme` also carries `data-accent`**, the System card's night half included. Without it, the half keeps the swatch's resolved light-scheme accent: in both engines its `--accent-fill`, `--accent-ink` and `--sel-fill` read #FFC8DD / #A3134F / #FFC8DD on Midnight's #211F1D, where they should read #613146 / #FFC2D9 / #613146 (`browser-check.json` → `nestedHalf`; `contrast.json` → `nestedPreviewWithoutAccent`). The gate proves a nested half **with** `data-accent` resolves like the real palette, in both engines, and a static check holds every `data-scheme` / `data-theme-preview` element in the shipped markup to the rule. It holds vacuously today: 0 such elements; batch 1a adds them. The gate proves a swatch inside another theme resolves exactly like the real palette, and both engines confirm it. It also proves the converse: a **bare** `data-theme` on an element that is not the root is data, and it keeps the document's palette. Every palette selector is either `:root[data-theme=…]` or `[data-theme-preview=…]`. The mutation "a bare `[data-theme="midnight"]` put back" is caught.

**The adoption changes CLAUDE.md in these places** (Phase 6 edits them in the batch that lands each change):
- **"Themes"** (CLAUDE.md line 27). The palette count becomes six if D2 adds Graphite, and Hearth is "warm grouped neutrals", not "warm paper" (the `hub.THEMES` blurb at `apps/hub.js:66` changes with it). The sentence "Each is a complete token block under `:root[data-theme=…]`" is no longer true: the hue families are per scheme and only the neutrals are per palette. It becomes: "Each is one neutral block under `:root[data-theme=…]` (plus `[data-theme-preview=…]`); the nine hue families are per scheme." The last sentence becomes: "Adding a theme = the steps above; swatches carry `data-theme-preview`" (no `.tp[data-preview=…]` copy).
- **"`apps/design.css`"** (line 30). "`--accent` is the signed-in person's colour, set by hub.js" becomes: "the person's family is `data-accent`, set by hub.js and the pre-paint bootstrap; `--accent` is an alias of `--accent-strong`, and any element carrying `data-accent` (an avatar, a tile) re-derives every `--accent-*` role". hub.js stops writing `--accent`.
- **"Preferences"** (line 28). **Conditional on decision D17.** If D17 is accepted, the sentence "F260 keeps text size and autolock in its own person scope" becomes: "the text size, contrast, transparency and motion preferences are hub person-scope rows beside `theme`; F260 keeps autolock". If D17's alternative is chosen, it becomes: "the contrast, transparency and motion preferences and the hub text size are hub person-scope rows beside `theme`; F260 keeps its own text size (`f260.big`) and autolock, and applies the hub size only when `f260.big` is unset". See "F260 text size" and "Person preferences".
- **"Liquid glass"** (line 29). Today it says every glass surface shares one recipe with the person's colour caught in the pane, that `--sheen-x` drifts the highlight in every glass surface (written by hub.js), and that `.card.glass` in a scroller and `.glass-lite` paint the look without `backdrop-filter`. v3 changes each of those. The new paragraph: "Glass is the navigation and control layer only: tab bar, top bar, sheets, floating buttons, pills and toolbars over content. **Every content card is solid** (`--material-solid-bg`). The recipe is tokens: `--glass-bg` / `--glass-bg-strong` (the specular sheen along the top plus the fill), `--glass-filter` (blur 20 px, `saturate(1.8)`, was 1.4), `--glass-shadow` (inner highlight, refracted edge, inner bottom shadow, outer ring, e2), and per theme `--glass-spec/-edge/-ring/-inner/-pickup`. The person's colour is `--glass-pickup-layer`, in the tile-end tone. Most surfaces paint it in place (`--glass-bg-tinted`, `--glass-bg-strong-tinted`). Only the tab bar and the top bar drift it, on an `::after` layer that hub.js moves by writing `--sheen-x` on those two bars, never on `:root` (`glass7-component.css`; off under Reduce Motion and on the kiosk). The look without blur (`--glass-look`, `.card.glass`, `.glass-lite`) is **deprecated**: the kiosk's chrome uses it, and the lint flags it on content. Reduce Transparency (`data-transparency`, Me > Appearance) makes every glass solid; Increase Contrast raises its opacity to 96/98 %."
- **"Adding an app", step 3** (line 58). The `apps.json` entry gains `"hue": "<family>"`, which drives the tile's `data-accent` (batch 2; the nine apps' hues are in D5). `"color"` stays only as a fallback until every tile reads `hue`.
- **The test table** (line 105). `test-design.mjs` covers "all six palettes" and "the nine families", and its "reduced motion" becomes "reduced motion: animations off; transitions opacity and colour only, ≤ 150 ms" (§8).
- **"Profiles"** (line 24) and **"Admin operations → Schema changes"** (line 94). A profile gains `hue`; see the migration below.

**The profile `hue` column** (batch 1a, back up D1 first). The procedure CLAUDE.md requires (line 94):
- **A new migration, `006-profile-hue.sql` in `worker/migrations/`.** It follows the pattern of `005-guests.sql`: SQLite has no `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, so the runner guards on `PRAGMA table_info(profiles)` having no `hue` column.
  - `ALTER TABLE profiles ADD COLUMN hue TEXT;`
  - then one `UPDATE profiles SET hue = '<family>' WHERE id = '<id>' AND hue IS NULL;` per seeded profile, using the D3 assignment. Guests get the first unused hue. The updates are idempotent because they only fill a `NULL`.
  - Run with `npx wrangler d1 execute house-hub --remote --file migrations/006-profile-hue.sql`.
- **`worker/schema.sql`** gains `hue TEXT` beside `color` (`:8`).
- **`worker/seed.sql`** (`:4-11`) gains the `hue` column in its `INSERT OR IGNORE`, so a fresh local D1 matches.
- **The Worker** accepts only the 18 family names (the nine people's and the nine app colours; amended 2026-09-26, `05-decisions.md` "Admin-assigned colours"; the admin sets them, guests included) in `POST /api/profiles` and the admin edit, and returns `hue` in the profile. **A profile created without a hue gets `hue = null`, which means graphite** (revision 6b: except a guest, which gets `hue = 'sky'` by default, D4; the admin may change it, and the bootstrap lets a valid stored hue win), and without a colour it gets graphite's #4C4C58, not Elizabeth's #8A6A4B (`worker/src/index.js:182` today). Otherwise `p.hue || H[p.color]` would map the default hex to Peach, Elizabeth's family (ACCENT-6).
- **`publicProfile()`** passes it through (§1). Until a session is refreshed, the bootstrap's `H` table maps the stored hex.

**F260 text size (decision D17).** CLAUDE.md and `scripts/test-prefs.mjs` say F260 keeps its text size in its own person scope (`app_data(person,'f260','f260.big')`, a boolean behind a 1.15 zoom). Retiring that reverses a standing project rule, so it is a household decision, not a migration detail.

**If D17 is accepted** (the recommendation: one text size for every app), in the same Phase 6 batch:
1. **Migration.** On F260's first open under v3, an adult whose hub `textSize` is unset and whose `f260.big` is true gets `hub.setTextSize('l')` (1.12, the nearest step to the 1.15 zoom). Until an adult opens F260, hub.js reads `f260.big` as a fallback.
2. **Ownership.** After that, the hub preference owns text size for every app, and F260's Normal/Large control (`apps/f260.html:649-650`) writes it.
3. **Compatibility.** `body.big` keeps working until the migration has run.
4. **Docs and tests.** `test-prefs.mjs` case 6 and the CLAUDE.md line ("F260 keeps text size and autolock in its own person scope") change together. Autolock stays in F260's scope.

**If D17's alternative is chosen,** F260 keeps `f260.big` in its own scope, and its Normal/Large control keeps writing it. The hub size applies to every other app. F260 applies the hub size only while `f260.big` is unset. CLAUDE.md keeps its sentence, with one addition: "the hub text size applies to the other apps". `test-prefs.mjs` case 6 becomes "F260 keeps `f260.big`; the hub size does not override it".

**Batch 1a pre-pass (required).** Some reads change meaning the moment the file lands. `legacy-reads.mjs` counts them by property and **follows app-local aliases transitively**. The shell, design.css (component half) and the apps are counted below; the two Dollywood exports repeat the template, so the template is counted once.

| What changes | Text reads | Surface (background / border / outline / shadow) | SVG stroke / fill | Other |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bare legacy hues, read directly | 80 (become AA inks: the point) | **114** | 7 | 4 |
| Bare hues through local aliases: F260 NT paper and `--gc` | 2 | **77** | 2 | — |
| Prayer `--d0…--d7` and `body.shared` | 5 | **19** | — | — |
| The template's `--ochre` / `--moss` | 7 | **13** | 7 | 4 (accent-color) |
| Kid Verse, Verses, Timer and the shell re-pointing `--accent` / `--tint` at a hue | — | 6 | 2 | 1 (filter) |
| `--muted-decor` | 3 by property: the placeholder and the Kid Verse day letters (both move to text tokens), and the unearned badge glyphs (a 3:1 mark, left on `--track-info`) | 4 (PIN rings, sync dots, the sheet grabber) | — | — |

So batch 1a runs in this order, **in one commit, deployed as one push together with batch 1b** (the `.ds` component half):
1. **The pre-pass.** Every non-text read above moves to `-graphic`, `-strong`, `-fill` or `-wash` by the **pairing rule**:
   - a background that carries a label goes to the family's `-strong`, with the label on its `-on`;
   - an unlabelled tint goes to `-fill` or `-wash`;
   - bars, borders, dots and SVG marks go to `-graphic`;
   - the local aliases are retargeted at their definitions (F260 `--g-*` and `body.nt`, Prayer `--d*` and `body.shared`, the template's `:212`, Kid Verse, Verses, Timer, `index.html:1256`).
   - The template change is rebuilt, run through `verify.py` and exported **in the same commit**.
2. **The labelled backgrounds.** The gate reads all 37 legacy backgrounds that carry a label, **exactly as the shipped CSS writes the label and the background**, under the new tokens in every palette × person:

   | Result | Rules |
   |---|---|
   | Fail as written | 4 |
   | Pass as written, and the pairing rewrite still applies | 22 |
   | Tints carrying a text colour, passing as written: icons ≥ 3.86 (`.ds .app-icon`, `apps/design.css:607`) and 5.03 (`.feed .ficon`, `index.html:210`), both gated at 3; text ≥ 6.20 (`.ds .person-chip`, `apps/design.css:501`) | 6 |
   | Layered backgrounds, skipped | 3 |
   | Map-category badges (D12), exempt | 2 |

   The four that fail as written, with their batch-1a rewrite:

   | Rule | As written | Rewrite | After |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `.ds .badge` (`apps/design.css:516`) | white on danger-ink, 1.48 in dark | `--badge-bg` / `--badge-ink` | 6.42 |
   | `.ds .hero` (`:412`) | 3.09 | `--hero-bg` (wash → fill) with `--accent-ink`: a surface, so it becomes the **deep tint** in dark, not a pastel slab | 5.03 |
   | `.ds .avatar` (`:493`) | 3.56 | `--accent-fill` with `--accent-ink`, the ring on `--accent-graphic` (`identity-component.css`), **with `hub.avatarHtml` writing the person's `data-accent` on the avatar in the same commit** (§1) | 5.03 |
   | the template's `.fab-primary` (`:412`) | 2.55 | `--accent-strong` / `--accent-on` | 5.90 |

   Every rewrite passes (≥ 4.76, the success solid's label), and the pairing lint (no `-on` or white on a `-fill`, `-wash` or `-fill-strong`) is gated.
3. **Surfaces and buttons.**
   - **Surfaces become deep tints in dark:** the chat bubble (`index.html:249`) moves to `--accent-fill` with `--accent-ink`, and `.hero` as above.
   - **The hero button moves onto its pair (revision 5).** `.ds .hero .btn-primary` (`apps/design.css:423`, the Me hero's Switch) is today `{ background: rgba(255,255,255,.92); color: var(--accent-deep); box-shadow: var(--e2); }`. Its background is not a legacy hue, so the labelled-background pass above does not read it. Once `--accent-deep` is the glowing dark ink, the rule reads 1.19:1 in dark. It becomes exactly:

     ```css
     .ds .hero .btn-primary { background: var(--hero-btn-bg); color: var(--hero-btn-ink); box-shadow: var(--e2); }
     ```

     That is the white capsule with the person's ink in light, and the person's deep fill with the glowing ink in dark. The rule stays where it is, after `.ds .btn:hover` and `.ds .btn-primary:hover` (`:373-374`, the same specificity), so hovering keeps the capsule. `contrast.mjs` gates the pair over both hero stops in every palette × person × mode, at ≥ 6.58 light, ≥ 6.86 dark, and ≥ 9.37 / ≥ 8.35 in the 7:1 modes. It also checks that the shipped rule is still the one this row replaces, and that the order holds. `browser-check.mjs` renders the button with the row in both engines (`heroButton`).
   - **Buttons become the glowing pastel capsule with a dark label** (decision D15). Today's `--accent-deep` backgrounds with `--on-accent` labels move to `--accent-strong` / `--accent-on`: `.btn-primary` (`apps/design.css:361`), Prayer's solid chips and buttons (`apps/prayer.html:191, 193, 350, 422`) and seven template controls (`template.html:225, 244, 453, 458, 472, 503, 556`).
4. **The token file lands** (`apps/design.css:14-289` replaced), with the bootstrap in every document. In the same commit:
   - the shell's Me theme cards and `docs/design.html` move to `data-theme-preview` (the migration table above);
   - the shell's static theme-color metas go (`index.html:8-9`). **Prayer's stays** (`apps/prayer.html:9`, with its id); in Prayer the bootstrap goes right after it, and `applyTheme()` keeps `el('themeColor')`, dropping only its `dark` test and hex fallbacks;
   - F260's theme-button handler becomes `closest('#themeSeg button')`;
   - **every numeral read moves to `--font-numeral`** (the list in §3: the `--font-display` numerals, the Timer digits, the Home and TV clocks, the timer pill and countdown, the star counts, the park times and the Verses counts);
   - the three sub-11 literals move to `--fs-caption2` (`apps/kidverse.html:86, 110`, `apps/f260.html:133`);

     - `scripts/test-design.mjs:102` (the palette map);

     - `scripts/screens-themes.mjs:32`;
     - `scripts/screens-apps.mjs:32`.

     The new values are hearth `rgb(244, 241, 236)`, parchment `rgb(236, 226, 205)`, frost `rgb(242, 242, 247)`, midnight `rgb(11, 10, 9)` and forest `rgb(7, 15, 13)`, plus graphite `rgb(0, 0, 0)` if D2 is accepted. `scripts/test-dollywood-themes.mjs` compares the body with the live `--bg` token (`:66, :75`), so it needs no colour change, only Graphite in its theme list (`:30-37`) under D2.
5. **hub.js** (§1):
   - `hue` in `publicProfile`;
   - **`hub.avatarHtml` emitting `data-accent="${p.hue || H[color] || 'graphite'}"` instead of the inline `--tint`** (`apps/hub.js:459-462`), in the same commit as the `.ds .avatar` rewrite;

6. **Profiles** gain the `hue` column through a new migration, `006-profile-hue.sql` in `worker/migrations/`, with `schema.sql` and `seed.sql` in sync and the Worker validating the name (back up D1 first; the procedure is under "Adding a theme" above). A new profile without a hue gets `null` (graphite) and without a colour graphite's #4C4C58, not #8A6A4B (`worker/src/index.js:182`).

**Sequence after that:**
1. **Batch 1b** (same push as 1a): the `.ds` component half moves onto roles:
   - capsule `.btn` with press scale + dim through the **global** `.pressable` rule (§8);
   - focus as an outline;
   - the switch, select chevron and a global `::placeholder`;

   - (**`.app-icon` is not in 1b.** Its rewrite reads the nearest `data-accent`, and until batch 2 no tile or icon carries one: every tile and pane icon would take the signed-in person's family, and on the TV graphite. It moves to batch 2; until then `.ds .app-icon` keeps today's `--tint` recipe, which the gate passes as written, glyph ≥ 3.86.)
   - **GLASS-7 exactly as `glass7-component.css`** (§7): the pickup painted in place on every glass surface, and the drifting `::after` layer on the tab bar and the top bar only (none on the desktop sidebar), with no `position` or `overflow` set on a bar, a sheet or a pill. Batch 1b re-runs `browser-check.mjs`, which loads that file over the component half;
   - tab, segmented and chip selection with `--sel-weight` + a ≥ 3:1 indicator (ACCENT-3);
   - base chrome rules (user-select, touch-callout, `overscroll-behavior` on `html`, scrollbars, `--fs-field`);
   - pulse keyframes reading `--pulse-scale`;
   - **the global Reduce Motion kill, re-keyed** to `data-motion` and its mirror as an opacity-only substitute (§8). It stays until the lint finds no literal duration left. **`scripts/test-design.mjs:91-96` changes in the same commit** (§8): transitions opacity and colour only, ≤ 150 ms; animations ≤ 0.01 ms; the Midnight switch read after the 150 ms fade.
2. **Batch 2:** the shell: `data-accent` everywhere (and Kid Verse's per-kid `--tint`, `apps/kidverse.html:372`, if its own batch has not landed), **in one commit with the `.app-icon` rewrite** (`identity-component.css`: `--tile-bg`, the glyph in `--accent-ink`, the corner `calc(var(--icon-box) * var(--r-icon-ratio))`, the five literal radii at `index.html:109, 139, 167, 188, 247` set only `--icon-box`), a `"hue"` on every `apps.json` entry (D5) and a `data-accent` on every tile, glance card and icon (`index.html:700, 894, 904, 913, 1118, 1153, 1165, 1176, 1188, 1203, 1206, 1256, 1257, 1272`); the PIN pad painted from the person's `data-accent` (ACCENT-6), `FALLBACK` as the hue name `'graphite'`, the registry picker, the sidebar tab on `--tap`, and **the TV board's `.tv-pane` sections off `.glass-strong` onto `--material-solid-bg`** (the `.kiosk-switch` keeps glass).
3. **Then one app per batch.** Each batch deletes that app's local aliases, adopts `.pressable` (F260, Prayer, the Larder, the Dollywood template), moves its named literal rows to roles (Prayer's kid rule and `.date`, the nine Larder literals), and turns on its lint row. `rev2-runtime.mjs` (`C`, `E`) injects exactly those rows today: with them, kid mode is 100 % rounded and no kid text is under 16 px.
4. **The TV re-layout batch** re-lays out the `.tv` grid (`index.html:134-166`) and only then sets `data-tv-scale="10ft"`, with `scripts/test-tv.mjs` passing at 1920 × 1080 and the fit check of `rev2-runtime.mjs` passing (§3, D16).

### Verification result

**Run:** `node audits/tools/phase4/tokens/contrast.mjs`, which exits 0. The runtime is about 34 s, the mutation runs included. Its output is in `audits/evidence/p4/tokens/contrast.json`. Every minimum below is rounded down.

**Method.** The script runs the cascade itself:
- specificity and order, `:where()` (which adds no specificity) included;
- `@media` for width, pointer and prefers-*;
- custom-property and `color-scheme` inheritance into nested `data-accent` and `data-theme-preview` scopes;
- inline element styles (for the `--sheen-x` write);
- `var()` with fallbacks;
- `color-mix` and alpha compositing.

It covers 6 palettes × 9 people × 6 modes (adult, kid, kiosk, Increase Contrast, Reduce Transparency, and kiosk + Reduce Transparency). It also:
- runs `bootstrap.js` in a sandbox, `theme-color` metas included;
- reads the shipped CSS of the shell, the apps and the Dollywood template for the labelled-background pass, and `apps/design.css:423` for the hero button's batch-1a row (revision 5);
- reads `apps/hub.js` for the theme list;
- reads the shipped markup for the `data-scheme` / `data-accent` rule.

**Not verified:**
- **The apps are not rendered with the whole v3 system.** The runtime check swaps the token half and injects only the named batch rows. The rest of the component half (batch 1b), hub.js and the bootstrap are not in it; the GLASS-7 rule is checked on a probe page in both engines, not in the running apps. Batch 1b must re-run the gate and the capture rig.
- **The 10-foot TV scale's layout.** It does not fit today's grid, by design; the TV re-layout batch must prove the new grid with `scripts/test-tv.mjs` and the fit check at 1920 × 1080. **Phase 5 should record the real TV's CSS viewport** (a TV reporting under 1600 CSS px never reaches the opt-in's width condition).
- **Glass is measured unblurred.** This is conservative. `--glass` over a white photo is reported, not gated (5.94 / 4.42). Identity marks under the full pickup or sheen are reported as upper bounds (2.30-3.32). The selected tab reads the ink, and its geometry is gated clear of the pickup. Phase 5 measures the bars on screen.
- **The Dollywood rows are emulated.** The SVG label rule lives in the template's `apply()`, so `rev2-runtime.mjs` sets each named label's size as the rule would, and it generates the kid-floor rows from the export's CSS. The template batch runs the real code through `verify.py` and this check.
- **The labelled-background pass reads only single-layer backgrounds and a label in the same rule.** A label inherited from a parent rule, and layered backgrounds (3 skipped), are not measured; the Phase 6 lint covers them.
- **The bootstrap is tested in a sandbox and on a probe page**, not in Safari with a real `localStorage` and a real status bar.
- **The rig's WebKit on Windows is not iOS Safari.** `ui-rounded`, real blur and the feel of the springs need a device.
- **The household's iOS versions are unknown.** `linear()` needs iOS 17.2+, `color-mix()` needs 16.2+ and `:where()` needs 14+.
- **Colour-blind separation is a model** (Machado 2009), not a test with people.
- **Display P3 and True Tone are not modelled.**
- **Whether the fills read as "vibrant" to the household** is visual, and belongs to Phase 5's preview. So is the new pickup tone.

## Not verified — device checks, grouped

Everything in this report ran on the local instance in Playwright WebKit (and Chromium where stated) on Windows. What that cannot show is listed in `audits/01-capture.md` §3 (line 103). Each item below names the section whose "Unresolved" list holds the detail and says what would settle it. None of them would remove a confirmed defect. The items that could change a severity or a score are marked **(severity)** or **(score)**; the device results also decide whether Typography and Shape stop being provisional.

**On a real iPad and iPhone**
- **Selects and other browser-painted controls when the theme's scheme opposes the OS.** The Windows WebKit port paints every `<select>` over its author background; Chromium honours it. Open the Larder add bar, the park map's Search and Style panes and the build guide's view menu with Midnight chosen in light Appearance, and Parchment in dark. **(severity)** P4-COLOR-04 rises to medium if the Larder select is unreadable (COLOR Unresolved 1; DARK Unresolved 1-2).
- **Real backdrop blur.** Text and icons on glass bars, tabs and sheets were measured over the unblurred fill (Chromium's with-blur re-measure covered the tab bar and Prayer's nav only); the look of the blur is not scored, so Shape stays provisional (COLOR Unresolved 3; GLASS; ACCENT U-ACCENT-4).
- **Apple faces.** SF Pro, SF Pro Rounded, New York and SF Mono: their fit, wrapping and tracking, and what the generic `serif` and `sans-serif` resolve to on iOS; Apple Color Emoji and the SF text glyphs (✓ ★ ⚑). Typography stays provisional (TYPE Unresolved 3; ICON Unresolved).
- **Touch.** Whether `:active` press states fire where no document registers a `touchstart` listener (GAP-MOTION-3, plausible, not scored); the long-press loupe and image callout on chrome; rubber-banding of the app iframes; the iOS focus zoom on the 12 fields under 16 px, and whether it zooms the whole shell; real finger hit-testing (MOTION, TELL Unresolved 1-3, 11; SHAPE Unresolved 6).
- **Accessibility settings.** Whether Safari 26 reports `prefers-reduced-transparency` and `prefers-contrast` from Settings (GLASS Unresolved); iOS Larger Text never reaching the hub rests on code only (TYPE Unresolved 4).
- **Status bar and launch.** Whether the Home Screen status bar repaints when `theme-color` changes at runtime, which decides whether P4-DARK-04 shows in the installed app (DARK Unresolved 3; Phase 2 device check 10); how long a cold launch takes to start the service worker, which decides P4-TELL-03's real exposure (TELL Unresolved 7).
- **Performance on the device.** The `--sheen-x` restyle while scrolling F260 (P4-GLASS-01), Tally's glass under real taps (P4-GLASS-05), the park map's pulses where WebKit does not composite SVG transform animations (P4-MOTION-03), GPU cost, ProMotion, and haptics (`navigator.vibrate` is not exposed on iOS) (GLASS and MOTION Unresolved).
- **Display.** Continuous-corner rendering, safe-area insets in standalone mode, Display P3 and True Tone (SHAPE Unresolved 6; ACCENT U-ACCENT-4). The household's iOS versions decide whether the proposal's `linear()` springs (iOS 17.2+) and `color-mix()` (16.2+) are safe (Proposed token set, Verification result).

**On the TV**
- The set's diagonal and the sofa distance, which decide VIS-TYPE-1's severity; the real TV's CSS viewport, which decides whether the proposal's opt-in 10-foot tier can ever apply **(score: Glanceability of the shell row rests on GLA-5/GLA-6)** (TYPE Unresolved 5; COLOR Unresolved 11; Proposed token set).
- The TV's own browser: its scrollbars, how a remote moves keyboard focus, its dark rendering, `color-scheme` and `theme-color`, and the cost of the Switch's blur (TELL Unresolved 8; DARK Unresolved 6; GLASS Unresolved).

**With the household**
- Colour-vision results are Machado 2009 simulations, not tests with people (COLOR Unresolved 9; ACCENT U-ACCENT-6).
- Whether production profiles still use the seeded colours; production was not read (ACCENT U-ACCENT-6).
- The park phones in sunlight (COLOR Unresolved 11), and whether the proposal's fills read as "vibrant" (Phase 5's preview).

**Rig follow-ups (no device needed)**
- **Mae's Prayer Kitchen view could not be opened in the rig**: the tap on `#moreBtn` timed out in 7 runtime jobs, the re-measure and the Colour skeptics. If something covers it in the real UI, that is a new defect (ACCENT U-ACCENT-1; COLOR Unresolved 5).
- **Rename and kind changes** probably do not reach open sessions either, like a recolour (P4-ACCENT-05); a kind change would affect `hub.isKid` and `hub.canWrite` on the client (ACCENT U-ACCENT-3).
- The park map's Find-me FAB icon on the raw-accent gradient (2.42-2.90 by token maths in dark; not rendered) (ACCENT U-ACCENT-2); the build guide's pressed north button (U-ACCENT-5).
- Phase 3's "about 6 px" park-map labels on the aerial basemap, which the default illustrated basemap hides; the wait markers' 9 px unit (TYPE Unresolved 1-2).
- Non-text in hover, press and focus states (their text was swept on the desktop after the completeness critic, which found five state-only failures still to verify), SVG `<text>`, canvas text, sheets and dialogs, guest and Kiara variants, and the named light palettes on a dark-OS device were swept only partly (COLOR Unresolved 7-8; TYPE Unresolved 6-9; ICON Unresolved; SHAPE Unresolved 7-9; TELL Unresolved 9-10).
- The exact concentric totals per corner (the rig skips pills and judges every corner by its top-left radius), so VIS-SHAPE-1's 58 of 99 is a floor (SHAPE Unresolved 1).
- Figures one party measured and nobody re-measured: the story-panel luminance, the TV Me hero under Hearth on a dark OS, Tally's discs, several occurrence totals and the reminder field boundary (DARK Unresolved 5; COLOR Unresolved 10).
- The token proposal's component half, hub.js and the bootstrap were not rendered as a whole system; the runtime check swapped only the token half of design.css, and revision 5's hero-button check and round 6's two probes added only the one hero-button row (Proposed token set, Verification result and assembler's note).

## Scripts and evidence

Every script runs from the repo root against the local instance (`audits/tools/lib/local.mjs`), closes its browser and server with `L.close()` in a `finally` block, and sends nothing to production. Each dimension section ends with its own "Method, scripts and evidence" table, which lists every script, what it measures, its output, the skeptics' `verify-<key>-1.mjs` / `-2.mjs` (and `-3.mjs` for a tie-break) and the re-measure with its agreement table.

| Folder (`audits/tools/phase4/…`) | What it holds | Evidence (`audits/evidence/p4/…`) |

- **Scorecard evidence.** The named-theme screenshots the scorecard and the sections cite from the git-ignored rig folders are copied, unchanged and each under 1 MB, into `audits/evidence/p4/SCORE/` with the same sub-path (`SCORE/shots/<theme>/<area>/…`; nine files), so every cited file can be committed.
- **Evidence size and scale** (re-checked after the completeness critic with `node audits/tools/phase4/HYGIENE/evidence-hygiene.mjs`, output `audits/evidence/p4/HYGIENE/evidence-hygiene.json`; it parses the `.gitignore` files itself, since the phase uses no git). The assembly note ("about 700 files and 50 MB", one file over 1 MB) checked size only. The re-check also checks citation and scale:
  - **Scale.** Three cited screenshots had been saved at device scale, against the 1x rule: `audits/evidence/p4/DARK/theme-color-A-iphone-server-midnight.png` and `audits/evidence/p4/DARK/theme-color-B-iphone-remote-parchment.png` (1290×2796, 3x) and `audits/evidence/p4/GLASS/verify-guard-misses-glass-strong-1-pairform-ipad.png` (1640×2360, 2x; it is cited at GLASS, P4-GLASS-02, as `-1-pairform-ipad.png`). `audits/tools/phase4/HYGIENE/rescale-1x.mjs` re-saved them in place at 430×932 and 820×1180. No other PNG is wider than 1920 or at a 2x/3x device width.
  - **Citation.** An exact pass (path, basename, brace expansion, the report's `-suffix.png` shorthand, and wildcards only when specific) found 89 committed PNGs cited nowhere (34 in DARK, 15 in COLOR, 15 in TELL, 11 in ICON, 8 in CRIT, 4 in RIGCHECK, 1 in ACCENT, 1 in TOK), fewer than the critic's heuristic estimate of about 110 because the report cites many shots by suffix. Each is now listed in its folder's `.gitignore` (kept on disk, out of git). 32 committed summaries in `measure/` are cited through the folder and `measure/*.json`, not by name, and stay.
  - **Totals.** Outside the ignored files, `audits/evidence/p4/` now holds 675 files and 48 MB (byte sum), with 294 PNGs, every one cited and at 1x. No file is over 1 MB; the one that was, `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/verify-kid-targets-own-css-2-dollywood-live.png` (1.47 MB, uncited), stays in `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/.gitignore`. The critic's "about 30 MB by `du -ch`" counted a different file set; the byte sum here is the script's.
- **Verdict records** of the skeptics sit in the session scratchpad, outside the repo, as the sections note; each confirmed finding's section carries both skeptics' scripts, outputs and conclusions.
- **Citations.** `node audits/tools/phase3/check-citations.mjs audits/04-design-system.md` checks every repo path and file:line cited in this report. At assembly it checked 2,149 citations and found 0 broken; after the completeness critic's patch, 2,215 citations and 0 broken. The register's section line numbers were re-synced to the headings after the new sections were inserted.
- **Process notes.** While building rig v1, the rig's author ran `taskkill /F /IM node.exe /T` once (about 21:21 UTC), which may have ended other investigators' node runs then in progress (for example `ICON/measure.mjs` and `MOTION/cls.mjs`). It is recorded here so the owner knows; whether any run was cut short was not established. The same agent also ran `git status --short audits/` once, read-only, to confirm nothing outside `audits/` had changed; the phase's rules said no git, and it changed nothing.
